5:1: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Na'im bin Hammad told us, Abdullah bin Mubarak told us, Mis'ar told us, Ma'n and Awf told me, or one of them, that a man came to Abdullah bin Mas'ud and said: Give me a testament. He said: When you hear God say, O you who believe, then listen to it, for it is either good that He commands or evil that He forbids. And he said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Abdul Rahman bin Ibrahim Dahim told us, Al-Walid told us, Al-Awza'i told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said: When God says, O you who believe, then do so, for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is one of them. Ahmad bin Sinan told us, Muhammad bin Ubaid told us, Al-A'mash told us on the authority of Khaithamah, who said: Everything in the Qur'an that says, O you who believe, is in the Torah, O you poor people. As for what he narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Ismail al-Sayegh al-Baghdadi, he told us, Muawiyah, meaning Ibn Hisham, on the authority of Isa bin Rashid, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: There is no verse in the Qur’an that says O you who believe, except that Ali is its master, its nobleman, and its leader, and there is no one from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, except that he was rebuked in the Qur’an except Ali bin Abi Talib, for he was not rebuked in any of it, so it is a strange trace, and its wording is strange, and there is doubt in its chain of transmission. Al-Bukhari said: This Isa bin Rashid is unknown, and his report is rejected. I said: And Ali bin Badhima, even if he was trustworthy, he was an extremist Shiite, and his report in such a case is suspected and not accepted. And his saying: So no one of the companions remained except that he was reprimanded in the Qur’an except Ali, he is referring to the verse commanding charity before secret conversation, for more than one person has mentioned that no one acted upon it except Ali, and his saying was revealed: Did you fear to offer alms before your secret conversation? Then since you did not, God has forgiven you 1:13. And there is a view on whether this is a reprimand, for it has been said that the command was a recommendation, not an obligation, then it was abrogated from them before the action, so no one of them issued a contradiction. And his saying: On the authority of Ali that he was not reprimanded in anything in the Qur’an is also questionable, for the verse in Al-Anfal in which there is reprimand for taking the ransom, included all those who advised taking it, and no one was spared from it except Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, so it is known from this and what preceded that this narration is weak, and God knows best. And Ibn Jarir: Al-Muthanna told me, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, Al-Layth told us, Yunus told me, he said: Muhammad bin Muslim said: I read the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which he wrote to Amr bin Hazm when he sent him to Najran, and the letter was with Abu Bakr bin Hazm in it, This is a statement from God and His Messenger, ‘O you who believe, fulfill your contracts,’ and he wrote the verses from it until he reached, Indeed, God is swift in account. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed told us, Yunus bin Bakir told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, Abdullah bin Abi Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm told me on the authority of his father, who said: This is the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with us, which he wrote to Amr bin Hazm when he sent him to Yemen to teach its people the Sunnah and collect their alms. So he wrote him a letter and a covenant, and ordered him in it with his order, so he wrote: “In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This is a letter from God and His Messenger. ‘O you who believe, fulfill your contracts.’ A covenant from Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Amr bin Hazm when he sent him to Yemen. He ordered him to fear God in all his affairs, for God is with those who fear Him and those who do good.” God the Almighty said: Fulfill contracts. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and more than one said: By contracts, he means covenants. Ibn Jarir narrated the consensus on that. He said: Covenants are what they used to agree on, such as oaths and other things. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: O you who have believed, fulfill contracts, meaning covenants, meaning what God has permitted and forbidden and imposed and what has been set in the entire Quran. Do not betray or break them. Then He emphasized that, saying: And those who break the covenant of God after ratifying it and sever that which God has ordered to be joined, until His statement: the worst home. Ad-Dahhak said: Fulfill contracts, meaning what God has permitted and forbidden, and what God has taken from the covenant from those who acknowledge faith in the Prophet and the Book, that they should fulfill what God has taken from them of obligations, from what is lawful and what is unlawful. Zayd bin Aslam said: Fulfill contracts, he said: They are six: the covenant of God, the covenant of an oath, the contract of partnership, the contract of sale, the contract of marriage, and the contract of an oath. Muhammad bin Kaab said: There are five of them, including the pre-Islamic oath and the negotiation partnership. Some of those who said that there is no option in the sale session have used this verse as evidence: Fulfill contracts. He said: This indicates the binding nature of the contract and its validity, which necessitates the negation of the option in the session. This is the school of thought of Abu Hanifa and Malik, but Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad and the majority disagreed with them on this. The evidence for this is what was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The two parties to a sale have the option so long as they have not parted. And in another wording by Al-Bukhari: If two men enter into a sale, each of them has the option so long as they have not parted. This is explicit in proving the option in the session following the sale contract, and this does not contradict the binding nature of the contract, rather it is one of its requirements in the Shari’ah, so its commitment is part of the completion of the fulfillment of contracts. And the Almighty’s saying: Lawful to you are the beasts of grazing livestock means camels, cows, and sheep. This was stated by Abu al-Hasan, Qatadah, and more than one person. Ibn Jarir said: This is also the case among the Arabs. Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, and more than one person used this verse as evidence for the permissibility of the fetus if it is found dead in its mother’s womb if she is slaughtered. A hadith was reported in the Sunan on this matter, narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Abu al-Wadak, Jubayr ibn Nawfal, on the authority of Abu Saeed, who said: We said: O Messenger of God, we slaughter the she-camel and slaughter the cow or sheep with the fetus in its belly. Should we throw it away or eat it? He said, Eat it if you wish, for its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother. Al-Tirmidhi said: A good hadith. Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Faris told us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, Atab ibn Bashir told us, Ubayd God ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qaddah al-Makki told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, The slaughter of the fetus is the slaughter of its mother. Abu Dawud alone transmitted it. And His statement, Except what is recited to you, Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means by that dead meat, blood, and pork. Qatada said: He means by that dead meat and that over which the name of God has not been mentioned. It appears - and God knows best - that what is meant by that is His statement, “Forbidden to you are dead meat, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than God, and that which has been strangled, or that which has been beaten, or that which has fallen from a fall, or that which has been gored, and that which has been eaten by a wild animal,” for even though these are from the livestock, they are forbidden by these factors. For this reason He said, Except what you have slaughtered and that which has been slaughtered on stone altars, meaning from them, for it is forbidden and cannot be remedied or followed up. For this reason God the Almighty said, Lawful to you are the beasts of grazing livestock, except what is recited to you, meaning except what will be recited to you of the prohibition of some of them in some circumstances. And the Almighty’s saying: Except for the game while you are in a state of ihram. Some of them said: This is in the accusative case as a state, and what is meant by livestock is what includes humans such as camels, cows, and sheep, and includes wild animals such as gazelles, cows, and donkeys. So He excluded from humans what was mentioned above, and He excluded from wild animals hunting during the state of ihram. It was said: What is meant is that We have made livestock lawful for you, except what was excluded from it for those who committed themselves to the prohibition of hunting, and it is forbidden according to His saying: But if someone is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [it], then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. That is, We have permitted the consumption of dead animals for the one who is forced, on the condition that he is neither desiring nor transgressing [it], and so it is here, that is, just as We have made livestock lawful in all states, then they have forbidden hunting during the state of ihram, for God has ruled this, and He is the Wise in all that He commands and forbids. For this reason, God the Almighty said: Indeed, God judges what He wills. Then He the Almighty said: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of God. Ibn Abbas said: By that he meant the rituals of Hajj. Mujahid said: Al-Safa and Al-Marwah, the sacrificial animals and the sacrificial animals are among the symbols of God. It was said: The symbols of God are His prohibitions, meaning do not make permissible the prohibitions of God that He has prohibited. For this reason, God the Almighty said: nor the sacred month, meaning by that its prohibition and recognition of its greatness, and leaving what God has forbidden to do in it, such as initiating fighting and emphasizing avoiding the prohibitions, as God the Almighty said: “They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein. Say: Fighting therein is great.” And God the Almighty said: Indeed, the number of months with God is twelve months. And in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Abu Bakrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said during the Farewell Pilgrimage: “Time has returned to its original state on the day God created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, of which four are sacred, three consecutive: Dhul-Qadah, Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram, and Rajab Mudar, which is between Jumada and Sha’ban.” This indicates that it will continue to be prohibited until the end of time, as is the doctrine of a group of the Salaf. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, regarding the Almighty’s statement: nor the sacred month, meaning do not consider fighting permissible in it. Muqatil bin Hayyan and Abdul Karim bin Malik Al-Jazari said the same, and Ibn Jarir also chose it. The majority of scholars held that this was abrogated and that it is permissible to initiate fighting in the sacred months. They cited as evidence the statement of God Almighty: So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them, meaning the four months of travel. They said: He did not exclude a sacred month from the others. Imam Abu Jaafar narrated the consensus that God has permitted fighting the polytheists in the sacred months and other months of the year. He said: They also agreed that if a polytheist were to hang the bark of all the trees of the sanctuary around his neck or arms, this would not be a guarantee for him from being killed if he had not previously received a covenant of protection from the Muslims or a guarantee of safety. This issue has another discussion that has a more detailed place than this. And the Almighty’s saying: nor the offerings nor the garlands means do not leave the offering to the Sacred House, for in it is the glorification of the symbols of God, and do not leave garlanding them around their necks to distinguish them from other livestock, and let it be known that they are offerings to the Kaaba so that those who want to harm them will avoid them, and it will prompt those who see them to bring something similar, for whoever calls to an offering will have a reward like the rewards of those who follow him without anything being diminished from their rewards. For this reason, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed Hajj, he spent the night in Dhu’l-Hulayfah, which is the valley of Al-‘Aqiq, and when morning came, he went around to his wives, who were nine, then he washed himself, perfumed himself, and prayed two rak’ahs, then he marked his offering and garlanded it, and prepared for Hajj and ‘Umrah, and his offering was many camels, more than sixty, of the most beautiful shapes and colors, as God, the Almighty, said: “That is so. And whoever honors the symbols of God, indeed, it is from the piety of the hearts.” And some of the predecessors said that honoring them means appreciating them and making them fat. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded us. God’s prayers and peace be upon him, that we should look into the eyes and ears, narrated by the people of Sunnah. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: His statement, nor necklaces, do not consider them permissible. When the people of the Age of Ignorance left their homes outside of the sacred months, they would garland themselves with hair and fur. The polytheists of the Sacred Sanctuary would garland themselves with the bark of its trees, and they would feel safe with it. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Then he said: Muhammad ibn Ammar told us, Saeed ibn Sulayman told us, Ibad ibn al-Awwam told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Husayn, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: Two verses were abrogated from this Surah: the verse of necklaces and His statement, But if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them. Al-Mundhir ibn Shadhan told us, Zakariya ibn Adi told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Adi told us, on the authority of Ibn Auf, who said: I said to al-Hasan: Has anything been abrogated from al-Ma’idah? He said: No. Ata’ said: They would garland themselves with trees from the Sacred Sanctuary, and they would feel safe, but God forbade cutting down its trees. Mutraf ibn Abdullah said the same. God the Almighty said: nor those who are at the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and approval. That is, do not consider it permissible to fight those who intend to go to the Sacred House of God, whoever enters it is safe. Likewise, whoever intends to go to it seeking the bounty of God and desiring His approval, do not turn them away, prevent them, or incite them. Mujahid, Ata’, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Mutraf bin Abdullah, Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Qatadah, and more than one said that regarding His statement, seek bounty from their Lord, he meant by that trade. This is as mentioned previously in His statement, There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord. And his saying, And pleasure. Ibn Abbas said: They seek to please God with their pilgrimage. Ikrimah, Al-Suddi, and Ibn Jarir mentioned that this verse was revealed about Al-Hatim bin Hind Al-Bakri, who had raided the herds of Medina. Then, the following year, he performed the minor pilgrimage to the House. Some of the Companions wanted to intercept him on his way to the House, so God Almighty revealed, And those who enter the Sacred House, seeking bounty from their Lord and approval. Ibn Jarir narrated the consensus that it is permissible to kill a polytheist if he does not have security, even if he is heading to the Sacred House or the Holy House, and that this ruling has been abrogated in their case, and God knows best. As for the one who intends to commit heresy and polytheism in it and disbelieve in it, then this is forbidden. God Almighty said: O you who believe, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs. For this reason, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Ali in the year nine when he ordered the pilgrims to declare innocence on behalf of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ordered him to call out, as a deputie, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that no polytheist should perform the Hajj after this year, and no one should circumambulate the House naked. Ibn Abi Talhah said: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying nor those who are at the Sacred House means whoever heads towards the Sacred House, so the believers and polytheists would perform the Hajj, so God forbade the believers from preventing anyone, whether a believer or a disbeliever. Then God revealed after that: The polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs. The verse, and God Almighty said: It is not for the polytheists to build mosques. God said: The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day. So he banished the polytheists from the Sacred Mosque. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: nor garlands or those entrusted with the Sacred House, he said: It is abrogated. When a man in the Age of Ignorance left his house intending to perform Hajj, he would wear a necklace of wood and no one would interfere with him. When he returned, he would wear a necklace of hair and no one would interfere with him. At that time, the polytheist would not be prevented from entering the House. So they were ordered not to fight in the sacred month or at the House, so it was abrogated by his statement: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. Ibn Jarir chose that what was meant by his statement: nor garlands means that if they wear a necklace from the Sacred Sanctuary, then they would be safe. He said: The Arabs have always reproached those who neglected that. The poet said: Did you not kill the two blind men who passed by you with their braided bark? And the Almighty’s saying: And when you have finished your state of ihram, then hunt. That is, when you have finished your state of ihram and have finished it, then We have permitted you what was forbidden to you in terms of hunting while in ihram. This is a command after the prohibition. The correct view that is proven in practice is that the ruling is returned to what it was before the prohibition. If it was obligatory, then it is obligatory. If it was recommended, then it is recommended, or permissible, then it is permissible. Whoever says that it is obligatory is refuted by many verses. Whoever says that it is permissible is refuted by other verses. What organizes all the evidence is what we have mentioned, as some scholars of the principles of jurisprudence have chosen, and God knows best. And His statement, And let not the hatred of a people because they prevented you from the Sacred Mosque prevent you from transgressing. Some of the reciters read that they prevented you with the opening of the alif of an, and its meaning is clear, that is, do not let the hatred of a people who prevented you from reaching the Sacred Mosque in the year of Hudaybiyyah cause you to transgress God’s judgment regarding them and take retribution from them unjustly and aggressively. Rather, rule with what God has commanded you of justice with regard to everyone. This verse, as will come from His statement, “And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness.” That is, do not let the hatred of a people cause you to abandon justice, for justice is obligatory upon everyone with regard to everyone in every situation. And some of the predecessors said: You have not treated someone who disobeyed God in you with anything more than obeying God in him. And justice is what the heavens and the earth were established by. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Sahl ibn Affan told us, Abdullah ibn Ja`far told us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was at Al-Hudaybiyah with his companions when the polytheists prevented them from entering the House, and that was very difficult for them. Then some polytheists from the East passed by them wanting to perform Umrah, so the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We will prevent these people as their companions prevented us. Then God revealed this verse. Hatred is hatred, as Ibn Abbas and others said. It is a source of hatred from shanatuhu, ashnuhu shanan with the fat-ha, like their saying jamzan, daraj, and raqalan from jamz, daraj, and raqal. Ibn Jarir said: Some Arabs omit the fat-ha in shanaan and say shanan, and I do not know anyone who recited it with it. And from it is the saying of the poet: Life is nothing but what you love and desire, even if the one who has hatred and dislikes it criticizes and denies it. God the Almighty says: And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression. God the Almighty commands His believing servants to cooperate in doing good deeds, which is righteousness, and to abandon evil deeds, which is piety. He forbids them from supporting one another in falsehood and from supporting one another in sins and forbidden acts. Ibn Jarir said: Sin is abandoning what God has commanded to be done, and aggression is going beyond what God has set in your religion and going beyond what God has imposed upon you in yourselves and in others. Imam Ahmad said: Hisham told us, Ubaydullah bin Abi Bakr bin Anas told us, on the authority of his grandfather Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Support your brother, whether he is a wrongdoer or wronged. It was said: O Messenger of God, this is supporting him when he is wronged, but how do I support him if he is a wrongdoer? He said: You restrain him and prevent him from injustice, and that is supporting him. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it from the hadith of Hisham, with a similar chain of transmission. They both transmitted it from the path of Thabit on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Support your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed. It was said: O Messenger of God, this is supporting him when he is oppressed, but how do I support him when he is an oppressor? He said: You prevent him from oppression, and that is your support of him. Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Sufyan ibn Sa`id told us, on the authority of Al-A`mash, on the authority of Yahya ibn Waththab, on the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The believer who mixes with people and is patient with their harm has a greater reward than the one who does not mix with people and is not patient with their harm. Ahmad also narrated it in the Musnad of Abdullah ibn `Umar. Hajjaj told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Al-A`mash, on the authority of Yahya ibn Waththab, on the authority of a sheikh from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The believer who mixes with people and is patient with their harm is better than the one who does not mix with them and is not patient with their harm. This is how Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Shu`bah, and Ibn Majah from the path of Ishaq ibn Yusuf, both of them from Al-A`mash with it. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Muhammad Abu Shaiba Al-Kufi told us, Bakr bin Abdul Rahman told us, Isa bin Al-Mukhtar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Fadil bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The one who guides to good is like the one who does it. Then he said: We do not know of it being narrated except with this chain of transmission. I said: And it has a corroborating report in the Sahih: “Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward like the rewards of those who follow him until the Day of Resurrection, without diminishing anything from their rewards. And whoever calls to misguidance will have a sin like the sins of those who follow him until the Day of Resurrection, without diminishing anything from their sins.” Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani said: Amr bin Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Zuraiq Al-Himsi told us, my father told us, Amr bin Al-Harith told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Salim, on the authority of Al-Zubaidi, Abbas bin Yunus said: Abu Al-Hasan Nimran bin Sakhr told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever walks with an oppressor to help him, knowing that he is… He is an oppressor who has left Islam.

So he wrote him a letter and a covenant, and ordered him in it with his order, so he wrote: “In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This is a letter from God and His Messenger. ‘O you who believe, fulfill your contracts.’ A covenant from Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Amr bin Hazm when he sent him to Yemen. He ordered him to fear God in all his affairs, for God is with those who fear Him and those who do good.” God the Almighty said: Fulfill contracts. He said: This indicates the binding nature of the contract and its validity, which necessitates the negation of the option in the session. This is the school of thought of Abu Hanifa and Malik, but Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad and the majority disagreed with them on this. The evidence for this is what was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The two parties to a sale have the option so long as they have not parted. And in another wording by Al-Bukhari: If two men enter into a sale, each of them has the option so long as they have not parted. This is explicit in proving the option in the session following the sale contract, and this does not contradict the binding nature of the contract, rather it is one of its requirements in the Shari’ah, so its commitment is part of the completion of the fulfillment of contracts. And the Almighty’s saying: Lawful to you are the beasts of grazing livestock means camels, cows, and sheep. This was stated by Abu al-Hasan, Qatadah, and more than one person. Ibn Jarir said: This is also the case among the Arabs. Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, and more than one person used this verse as evidence for the permissibility of the fetus if it is found dead in its mother’s womb if she is slaughtered. A hadith was reported in the Sunan on this matter, narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Abu al-Wadak, Jubayr ibn Nawfal, on the authority of Abu Saeed, who said: We said: O Messenger of God, we slaughter the she-camel and slaughter the cow or sheep with the fetus in its belly. Should we throw it away or eat it? He said, Eat it if you wish, for its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother. Al-Tirmidhi said: A good hadith. Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Faris told us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, Atab ibn Bashir told us, Ubayd God ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qaddah al-Makki told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, The slaughter of the fetus is the slaughter of its mother. Abu Dawud alone transmitted it. And His statement, Except what is recited to you, Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means by that dead meat, blood, and pork. Qatada said: He means by that dead meat and that over which the name of God has not been mentioned. It appears - and God knows best - that what is meant by that is His statement, “Forbidden to you are dead meat, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than God, and that which has been strangled, or that which has been beaten, or that which has fallen from a fall, or that which has been gored, and that which has been eaten by a wild animal,” for even though these are from the livestock, they are forbidden by these factors. For this reason He said, Except what you have slaughtered and that which has been slaughtered on stone altars, meaning from them, for it is forbidden and cannot be remedied or followed up. For this reason God the Almighty said, Lawful to you are the beasts of grazing livestock, except what is recited to you, meaning except what will be recited to you of the prohibition of some of them in some circumstances. And the Almighty’s saying: Except for the game while you are in a state of ihram. Some of them said: This is in the accusative case as a state, and what is meant by livestock is what includes humans such as camels, cows, and sheep, and includes wild animals such as gazelles, cows, and donkeys. So He excluded from humans what was mentioned above, and He excluded from wild animals hunting during the state of ihram. It was said: What is meant is that We have made livestock lawful for you, except what was excluded from it for those who committed themselves to the prohibition of hunting, and it is forbidden according to His saying: But if someone is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [it], then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. That is, We have permitted the consumption of dead animals for the one who is forced, on the condition that he is neither desiring nor transgressing [it], and so it is here, that is, just as We have made livestock lawful in all states, then they have forbidden hunting during the state of ihram, for God has ruled this, and He is the Wise in all that He commands and forbids. For this reason, God the Almighty said: Indeed, God judges what He wills. Then He the Almighty said: O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of God. Ibn Abbas said: By that he meant the rituals of Hajj. Mujahid said: Al-Safa and Al-Marwah, the sacrificial animals and the sacrificial animals are among the symbols of God. It was said: The symbols of God are His prohibitions, meaning do not make permissible the prohibitions of God that He has prohibited. For this reason, God the Almighty said: nor the sacred month, meaning by that its prohibition and recognition of its greatness, and leaving what God has forbidden to do in it, such as initiating fighting and emphasizing avoiding the prohibitions, as God the Almighty said: “They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein. Say: Fighting therein is great.” And God the Almighty said: Indeed, the number of months with God is twelve months. And in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Abu Bakrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said during the Farewell Pilgrimage: “Time has returned to its original state on the day God created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, of which four are sacred, three consecutive: Dhul-Qadah, Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram, and Rajab Mudar, which is between Jumada and Sha’ban.” This indicates that it will continue to be prohibited until the end of time, as is the doctrine of a group of the Salaf. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, regarding the Almighty’s statement: nor the sacred month, meaning do not consider fighting permissible in it. Muqatil bin Hayyan and Abdul Karim bin Malik Al-Jazari said the same, and Ibn Jarir also chose it. The majority of scholars held that this was abrogated and that it is permissible to initiate fighting in the sacred months. They cited as evidence the statement of God Almighty: So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them, meaning the four months of travel. They said: He did not exclude a sacred month from the others. Imam Abu Jaafar narrated the consensus that God has permitted fighting the polytheists in the sacred months and other months of the year. He said: They also agreed that if a polytheist were to hang the bark of all the trees of the sanctuary around his neck or arms, this would not be a guarantee for him from being killed if he had not previously received a covenant of protection from the Muslims or a guarantee of safety. This issue has another discussion that has a more detailed place than this. And the Almighty’s saying: nor the offerings nor the garlands means do not leave the offering to the Sacred House, for in it is the glorification of the symbols of God, and do not leave garlanding them around their necks to distinguish them from other livestock, and let it be known that they are offerings to the Kaaba so that those who want to harm them will avoid them, and it will prompt those who see them to bring something similar, for whoever calls to an offering will have a reward like the rewards of those who follow him without anything being diminished from their rewards. For this reason, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed Hajj, he spent the night in Dhu’l-Hulayfah, which is the valley of Al-‘Aqiq, and when morning came, he went around to his wives, who were nine, then he washed himself, perfumed himself, and prayed two rak’ahs, then he marked his offering and garlanded it, and prepared for Hajj and ‘Umrah, and his offering was many camels, more than sixty, of the most beautiful shapes and colors, as God, the Almighty, said: “That is so. And whoever honors the symbols of God, indeed, it is from the piety of the hearts.” And some of the predecessors said that honoring them means appreciating them and making them fat. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded us. God’s prayers and peace be upon him, that we should look into the eyes and ears, narrated by the people of Sunnah. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: His statement, nor necklaces, do not consider them permissible. When the people of the Age of Ignorance left their homes outside of the sacred months, they would garland themselves with hair and fur. The polytheists of the Sacred Sanctuary would garland themselves with the bark of its trees, and they would feel safe with it. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Then he said: Muhammad ibn Ammar told us, Saeed ibn Sulayman told us, Ibad ibn al-Awwam told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Husayn, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: Two verses were abrogated from this Surah: the verse of necklaces and His statement, But if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them. Al-Mundhir ibn Shadhan told us, Zakariya ibn Adi told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Adi told us, on the authority of Ibn Auf, who said: I said to al-Hasan: Has anything been abrogated from al-Ma’idah? He said: No. Ata’ said: They would garland themselves with trees from the Sacred Sanctuary, and they would feel safe, but God forbade cutting down its trees. Mutraf ibn Abdullah said the same. God the Almighty said: nor those who are at the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and approval. That is, do not consider it permissible to fight those who intend to go to the Sacred House of God, whoever enters it is safe. Likewise, whoever intends to go to it seeking the bounty of God and desiring His approval, do not turn them away, prevent them, or incite them. Mujahid, Ata’, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Mutraf bin Abdullah, Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Qatadah, and more than one said that regarding His statement, seek bounty from their Lord, he meant by that trade. This is as mentioned previously in His statement, There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord. And his saying, And pleasure. Ibn Abbas said: They seek to please God with their pilgrimage. Ikrimah, Al-Suddi, and Ibn Jarir mentioned that this verse was revealed about Al-Hatim bin Hind Al-Bakri, who had raided the herds of Medina. Then, the following year, he performed the minor pilgrimage to the House. Some of the Companions wanted to intercept him on his way to the House, so God Almighty revealed, And those who enter the Sacred House, seeking bounty from their Lord and approval. Ibn Jarir narrated the consensus that it is permissible to kill a polytheist if he does not have security, even if he is heading to the Sacred House or the Holy House, and that this ruling has been abrogated in their case, and God knows best. As for the one who intends to commit heresy and polytheism in it and disbelieve in it, then this is forbidden. God Almighty said: O you who believe, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs. For this reason, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Ali in the year nine when he ordered the pilgrims to declare innocence on behalf of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ordered him to call out, as a deputie, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that no polytheist should perform the Hajj after this year, and no one should circumambulate the House naked. Ibn Abi Talhah said: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying nor those who are at the Sacred House means whoever heads towards the Sacred House, so the believers and polytheists would perform the Hajj, so God forbade the believers from preventing anyone, whether a believer or a disbeliever. Then God revealed after that: The polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs. The verse, and God Almighty said: It is not for the polytheists to build mosques. God said: The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day. So he banished the polytheists from the Sacred Mosque. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: nor garlands or those entrusted with the Sacred House, he said: It is abrogated. When a man in the Age of Ignorance left his house intending to perform Hajj, he would wear a necklace of wood and no one would interfere with him. When he returned, he would wear a necklace of hair and no one would interfere with him. At that time, the polytheist would not be prevented from entering the House. So they were ordered not to fight in the sacred month or at the House, so it was abrogated by his statement: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. Ibn Jarir chose that what was meant by his statement: nor garlands means that if they wear a necklace from the Sacred Sanctuary, then they would be safe. He said: The Arabs have always reproached those who neglected that. The poet said: Did you not kill the two blind men who passed by you with their braided bark? And the Almighty’s saying: And when you have finished your state of ihram, then hunt. That is, when you have finished your state of ihram and have finished it, then We have permitted you what was forbidden to you in terms of hunting while in ihram. This is a command after the prohibition. The correct view that is proven in practice is that the ruling is returned to what it was before the prohibition. If it was obligatory, then it is obligatory. If it was recommended, then it is recommended, or permissible, then it is permissible. Whoever says that it is obligatory is refuted by many verses. Whoever says that it is permissible is refuted by other verses. What organizes all the evidence is what we have mentioned, as some scholars of the principles of jurisprudence have chosen, and God knows best. And His statement, And let not the hatred of a people because they prevented you from the Sacred Mosque prevent you from transgressing. Some of the reciters read that they prevented you with the opening of the alif of an, and its meaning is clear, that is, do not let the hatred of a people who prevented you from reaching the Sacred Mosque in the year of Hudaybiyyah cause you to transgress God’s judgment regarding them and take retribution from them unjustly and aggressively. Rather, rule with what God has commanded you of justice with regard to everyone. This verse, as will come from His statement, “And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness.” That is, do not let the hatred of a people cause you to abandon justice, for justice is obligatory upon everyone with regard to everyone in every situation. And some of the predecessors said: You have not treated someone who disobeyed God in you with anything more than obeying God in him. And justice is what the heavens and the earth were established by. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Sahl ibn Affan told us, Abdullah ibn Ja`far told us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was at Al-Hudaybiyah with his companions when the polytheists prevented them from entering the House, and that was very difficult for them. Then some polytheists from the East passed by them wanting to perform Umrah, so the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We will prevent these people as their companions prevented us. Then God revealed this verse. Hatred is hatred, as Ibn Abbas and others said. It is a source of hatred from shanatuhu, ashnuhu shanan with the fat-ha, like their saying jamzan, daraj, and raqalan from jamz, daraj, and raqal. Ibn Jarir said: Some Arabs omit the fat-ha in shanaan and say shanan, and I do not know anyone who recited it with it. And from it is the saying of the poet: Life is nothing but what you love and desire, even if the one who has hatred and dislikes it criticizes and denies it. God the Almighty says: And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression. God the Almighty commands His believing servants to cooperate in doing good deeds, which is righteousness, and to abandon evil deeds, which is piety. He forbids them from supporting one another in falsehood and from supporting one another in sins and forbidden acts. Ibn Jarir said: Sin is abandoning what God has commanded to be done, and aggression is going beyond what God has set in your religion and going beyond what God has imposed upon you in yourselves and in others. Imam Ahmad said: Hisham told us, Ubaydullah bin Abi Bakr bin Anas told us, on the authority of his grandfather Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Support your brother, whether he is a wrongdoer or wronged. It was said: O Messenger of God, this is supporting him when he is wronged, but how do I support him if he is a wrongdoer? He said: You restrain him and prevent him from injustice, and that is supporting him. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it from the hadith of Hisham, with a similar chain of transmission. They both transmitted it from the path of Thabit on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Support your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed. It was said: O Messenger of God, this is supporting him when he is oppressed, but how do I support him when he is an oppressor? He said: You prevent him from oppression, and that is your support of him. Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Sufyan ibn Sa`id told us, on the authority of Al-A`mash, on the authority of Yahya ibn Waththab, on the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The believer who mixes with people and is patient with their harm has a greater reward than the one who does not mix with people and is not patient with their harm. Ahmad also narrated it in the Musnad of Abdullah ibn `Umar. Hajjaj told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Al-A`mash, on the authority of Yahya ibn Waththab, on the authority of a sheikh from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The believer who mixes with people and is patient with their harm is better than the one who does not mix with them and is not patient with their harm. This is how Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Shu`bah, and Ibn Majah from the path of Ishaq ibn Yusuf, both of them from Al-A`mash with it. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Muhammad Abu Shaiba Al-Kufi told us, Bakr bin Abdul Rahman told us, Isa bin Al-Mukhtar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Fadil bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The one who guides to good is like the one who does it. Then he said: We do not know of it being narrated except with this chain of transmission. I said: And it has a corroborating report in the Sahih: “Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward like the rewards of those who follow him until the Day of Resurrection, without diminishing anything from their rewards. And whoever calls to misguidance will have a sin like the sins of those who follow him until the Day of Resurrection, without diminishing anything from their sins.” Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani said: Amr bin Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Zuraiq Al-Himsi told us, my father told us, Amr bin Al-Harith told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Salim, on the authority of Al-Zubaidi, Abbas bin Yunus said: Abu Al-Hasan Nimran bin Sakhr told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever walks with an oppressor to help him, knowing that he is… He is an oppressor who has left Islam.
5:3: God Almighty informs His servants of report that includes the prohibition of consuming these forbidden things from dead animals, which are animals that died a natural death without slaughtering or hunting, and that is only because of the harm in them due to the congested blood in them, so they are harmful to religion and the body, and for this reason God Almighty forbade them, and the exception from dead animals is fish, which is permissible whether it died by slaughtering or otherwise, based on what was narrated by Malik in his Muwatta’, and Al-Shafi’i and Ahmad in their Musnads, and Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah in their Sunans, and Ibn Khuzaymah and Ibn Hibban in their Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about seawater, and he said, Its water is pure and its dead is permissible. And so is locusts, based on what will come in the hadith. And his saying, and blood, means spilled, like his saying, or spilled blood, as Ibn Abbas and Sa’id ibn Jubayr said. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Kathir ibn Shihab told us. Al-Madhhaji, Muhammad bin Saeed bin Sabeq told us, Amr, meaning Ibn Qais, told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he was asked about the spleen, so he said: Eat it, so they said: It is blood, so he said: Only spilled blood is forbidden to you, and Hammad bin Salamah narrated it likewise on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Al-Qasim! On the authority of Aisha, she said: He only forbade the shedding of blood. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Idris Al-Shafi’i said: Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Two dead things and two types of blood have been made lawful for us. As for the two dead things, they are fish and locusts, and as for the two types of blood, they are the liver and the spleen.” This is how Ahmad bin Hanbal, Ibn Majah, Ad-Darqutni and Al-Bayhaqi narrated it on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam, and it is weak. Al-Hafiz Al-Bayhaqi said: Ismail bin Abi Idris narrated it on the authority of Usamah, Abdullah and Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: All three of them are weak, but some of them are more authentic than others. Sulayman bin Bilal, one of the trustworthy narrators, narrated it on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ibn Umar, and some of them attributed it to him. Al-Hafiz Abu Zur’ah Al-Razi said: It is more authentic. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hasan told us, Muhammad bin Abd Al-Malik bin Abi Al-Shawarib told us. Bashir bin Shuraih narrated to us on the authority of Abu Ghalib, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who is Siddi bin Ajlan, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me to my people to call them to God and His Messenger, and to present to them the laws of Islam. So I came to them, and while we were like that, they brought a bowl of blood, and they gathered around it to eat it. They said: Come, Siddi, and eat. I said: Woe to you, I have only come to you from someone who forbids this to you. So they turned to him and said: What is it? So I recited to them this verse: Forbidden to you are dead animals and blood al-Baqarah 2:177. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Abi al-Shawarib with his chain of transmission similarly, and he added this chain of transmission after it. He said: So I began to call them to Islam, but they refused me. So I said: Woe to you, give me a drink of water, for I am very thirsty. He said: And I am wearing my cloak. They said: No, but we will leave you until you die of thirst. He said: So I became upset and hit my head on the cloak, and I slept on the hot sand in intense heat. He said: Then someone came to me in my dream with a glass cup, the most beautiful of which people had never seen, and in it was a drink the most delicious of which people had never seen. He gave it to me, so I drank it. When I finished my drink, I woke up, and by God, I was neither thirsty nor naked after that drink. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Ali bin Hammad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal, Abdullah bin Salamah bin Ayyash Al-Amiri told me, Sadaqah bin Harm told us on the authority of Abu Ghalib, on the authority of Abu Umamah, and he mentioned something similar, and he added after his saying: After that drink, I heard them say: A man from the elite of your people came to you and you did not fill him with a sip, so bring me a sip, and I said: I have no need of it, God fed me and gave me drink, and I showed them my stomach, so they converted to Islam, all of them, and how beautiful is what Al-A’sha recited in his poem that Ibn Ishaq mentioned: And beware of dead animals, do not approach them, and do not take an iron bone and bleed it. That is, do not do the actions of the Age of Ignorance, which is that when one of them was hungry, he would take a specific thing from a bone or the like, and bleed his camel or any animal of any kind with it, and collect the blood that came out of it and drink it. For this reason, God forbade blood to this nation. Then Al-A’sha said: And do not go to this erected idol, nor worship idols, but worship God. And his saying: and the flesh of swine means its domestic and wild, and the flesh includes all its parts even the fat, and there is no need for the cleverness of the Zahiris in their rigidity here, and their arbitrariness in citing as evidence his saying: for it is an abomination or a transgression, meaning the saying of God Almighty: unless it be a dead animal or blood poured forth or the flesh of swine, for it is an abomination. They returned the pronoun in what they understood to be to the pig so that it includes all its parts, and this is far-fetched in terms of language, because the pronoun only refers to the noun and not the noun it is added to. What is more apparent is that the flesh includes all the parts as is understood from the language of the Arabs, and from the prevailing custom, and in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Buraydah ibn al-Khasib al-Aslami, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever plays with backgammon, it is as if he dipped his hand in the flesh and blood of a pig. So if this repulsion is merely due to touch, then how can there be a threat and a definite warning against eating it and nourishing oneself with it, and in it is evidence that the flesh includes all its parts, from fat and other things? In the two Sahihs, it is narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has forbidden the sale of wine, dead animals, pork, and idols. It was said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of the fat of dead animals, for it is used to coat ships, grease hides, and people use it for lighting lamps? He said: No, it is forbidden. In Sahih al-Bukhari, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Sufyan that he said to Heraclius, the king of al-Rum 30:He forbade us from dead animals and blood. His saying, And that which is dedicated to other than God means that which is slaughtered and the name of other than God is mentioned over it, then it is forbidden, because God Almighty has made it obligatory that His creations be slaughtered in His great name. So whenever it is deviated from that and the name of other than Him is mentioned over it, such as an idol, a tyrant, a statue, or any other of the other creations, then it is forbidden by consensus. The scholars differed about the omission of the name of God either intentionally or by forgetfulness, as will be explained in Surat Al-An’am. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hasan Al-Sinjani told us, Naim bin Hammad told us, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Al-Walid bin Jami’, on the authority of Abu Al-Tufayl, who said: Adam revealed the prohibition of four things: dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than God. These four things were never permissible, and they have remained forbidden since God created the heavens and the earth. When the Children of Israel were there, God prohibited for them good things that were made permissible for them because of their sins. When God sent Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, He revealed the first command that Adam brought and made permissible for them everything else, but they denied him and disobeyed him. This is a strange trace. Ibn Abi Hatim also said: My father told us, Ahmad bin Yunus told us, Rib’i told us, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: I heard Al-Jarud bin Abi Sabra, who said: He is my grandfather, who said: There was a man from Banu Rabah called Ibn Wa’il, and he was a poet. He often competed with Abu Al-Farazdaq at a watering place in the back of Kufa on the condition that this one would hamstring a hundred of his camels and this one would kill a hundred of his camels. A hundred of his camels when they came to the water. When they came to the water, they went to them with their swords and began to uncover their heels. He said: So the people went out on the red camels and mules seeking meat. He said: And Ali was in Kufa. He said: So Ali went out on the white mule of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was calling: O people, do not eat from its meat, for it has been sacrificed to other than God. This is a strange narration, and what testifies to its authenticity is what Abu Dawud narrated: Harun bin Abdullah told us, Ibn Hammad bin Mas`adah told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Abu Rayhanah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade drinking from the Bedouins. Then Abu Dawud Muhammad bin Ja`far said, he is Ghandar: He stopped it from Ibn Abbas, Abu Dawud is the only one who narrated it. Abu Dawud also said: Harun bin Zaid bin Abi Al-Zarqa’ told us, my father told us, Jarir bin Hazim told us, on the authority of Al-Zubayr bin Harith, who said: I heard `Ikrimah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade eating the food of the competitors. Then Abu Dawud said: More Whoever narrated it other than Ibn Jarir does not mention Ibn Abbas in it, and he is also the only one who narrated it. His saying: And the strangled one is the one who dies by strangulation, either intentionally or by accident, so that she is confused in her bonds, and dies from it, so it is forbidden. As for “the one who is beaten with a heavy, unsharpened object until she dies, as Ibn Abbas and more than one said: It is the one who is beaten with wood until it wakes her up and she dies. Qatada said: The people of the Age of Ignorance used to beat her with sticks until she died, then they would eat her. In Sahih, it is narrated that Adi bin Hatim said: I said: O Messenger of God, I shoot with a spear at game and I hit it. He said: “If you shoot with a spear and it pierces it, then eat it, but if it hits its side, then it is a dead animal, so do not eat it.” So he differentiated between what was hit by an arrow or a spear or the like with its sharp edge, which is permissible, and what was hit with its side and made a dead animal, which is not permissible. This is agreed upon by the jurists, and they differed concerning what happens when the spear strikes the game and kills it with its weight, and does not wound it, according to two opinions, which are the opinions of Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him. The first is that it is not permissible, as in the case of an arrow, and the general opinion is that each of them dies without wounding, so it is a dead animal. The second is that it is permissible because he ruled that what a dog hunts is permissible and did not elaborate, so this indicates the permissibility of what we mentioned, because it is included in the generality. I have decided a chapter for this issue, so let it be written here. [Chapter] - The scholars, may God have mercy on them, differed as to whether a dog is sent after a game animal and kills it with its weight without wounding or hitting it: Is it permissible or not? There are two opinions one of them that it is permissible due to the generality of the Almighty’s statement: Then eat of that which they catch for you, and also the generalities of the hadith of Adi bin Hatim. This is a statement that the companions narrated from Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, and some of the later scholars among them authenticated it, such as Al-Nawawi and Al-Rafi’i. I say: This is not apparent from the words of Al-Shafi’i in Al-Umm and Al-Mukhtasar, as he said in both places: It has two possible meanings, then he explained each of them, and the companions carried that from him, so they issued two opinions on the issue from him, except that in his discussion of the opinion of permissibility, he mentioned it a little, and did not state either of them explicitly, nor was he certain of it, and the opinion of that - I mean permissibility - was transmitted by Ibn Al-Sabbagh from Abu Hanifa from the narration of Al-Hasan bin Ziyad from him, and he did not mention anything else. As for Abu Jaafar bin Jarir, he narrated it in his interpretation on the authority of Salman al-Farsi, Abu Hurairah, Saad bin Abi Waqqas, and Ibn Umar. This is very strange, and it is not found explicitly stated on their authority, except that it is from his own interpretation, may God have mercy on him and be pleased with him. [The second opinion] - that this is not permissible, and it is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, and it was chosen by Al-Muzani, and it appears from the words of Ibn Al-Sabbagh that it is also preferable, and God knows best. Abu Yusuf and Muhammad narrated it on the authority of Abu Hanifa, and it is the well-known opinion on the authority of Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, may God be pleased with him. This opinion is more likely to be correct, and God knows best, because it is based on the fundamental principles and is closer to the principles of Islamic law. Ibn Al-Sabbagh provided evidence for it with the hadith of Rafi’ bin Khadij, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, we will meet the enemy tomorrow, and we do not have knives, so should we slaughter with reeds? He said: Whatever the blood flows and the name of God has been mentioned over it, eat it. The hadith in full, and it is in the two Sahihs. And even if this was mentioned for a specific reason, the meaning is the generality of the wording according to the majority of scholars in the principles and branches, as he, peace be upon him, was asked about the bit, which is honey wine, and he said, Every drink that intoxicates is forbidden. So can a jurist say: This wording is specific to honey wine? And so it is with this, as they asked him about something related to slaughtering, and he said to them general words that include that which was asked about and others because he, peace be upon him, had been given comprehensive words. If this is established, then what the dog struck or overwhelmed with its weight is not something that caused its blood to flow, so it is not permissible according to the meaning of this hadith. If it is said: This hadith is not of this type at all, because they only asked him about the tool with which it is slaughtered, and they did not ask him about the thing that is slaughtered, and for this reason he excluded from that the tooth and the nail where he said: It is not the tooth and the nail, and I will tell you about that, as for the tooth it is a bone and as for the nail it is the scales of the Abyssinians. And the exception indicates the type of the exception, otherwise it would not be connected, so it indicates that the tool is the tool, so there is no indication in it for what You mentioned, so the answer to this is that there is something in the statement that is also difficult for you, as he says, Whatever blood flows and the name of God is mentioned over it, eat it, and he did not say, Then slaughter with it. So both rulings are taken from this together, the ruling of the instrument with which it is slaughtered is taken, and the ruling of the slaughtered animal is taken, and that its blood must flow with an instrument that is neither a tooth nor a fingernail. This is the approach. [The second path]: Al-Muzani’s method, which is that the arrow was explicitly stated that if it kills with its width, then it is not to be eaten, and if it pierces, then it is to be eaten. The dog came in general, so it is carried on what was restricted there from piercing because they share in the reason, which is hunting, so it must be carried here even if the reason differs, just as it is necessary to carry the generality of emancipation in zihar on its restriction to faith in killing, rather this is more appropriate, and this is directed to him who accepts the origin of this rule as it is, and there is no disagreement among the companions in general, so they must have an answer to this, and he can say: This was killed by the dog with its weight, so it was not permissible by analogy to what the arrow killed with its width, and the common denominator is that each of them is a hunting tool, and it died with its weight in both of them, and this is not contradicted by the generality of the verse, because analogy takes precedence over generality, as is the doctrine of the four imams and the majority, and this is also a good path. [Another approach] - which is that the Almighty’s saying: Then eat of what they catch for you is general in what is killed by wounding or otherwise, but this killed in this disputed manner is either by being gored or in the same ruling, or by being strangled or in the same ruling, and whatever it was, this verse must be presented in these aspects: One of them is that the Lawgiver considered the ruling of this verse in the case of hunting, where he said to Adi bin Hatim: And if it strikes it with its side, then it is only a wound, so do not eat it, and we do not know of any of the scholars who distinguished between one ruling and another from this verse, and said: The wound is considered in the case of hunting, and the gored is not considered, so saying that the disputed matter is permissible is a breach of consensus, and no one says it, and it is forbidden according to many scholars. Second That verse, So eat of what they catch for you, is not general by consensus, but rather is specific to the edible animals that are hunted. The non-edible animals are excluded from the generality of its wording by consensus, and the preserved generality takes precedence over the unpreserved. [The other path] - This hunt, in this case, is considered dead, because blood and the moisture that follows it have congealed in it, so it is not permissible by analogy to dead meat. [The other path] - The verse of prohibition, I mean His saying: Forbidden to you are dead animals to the end, is decisive and has not been abrogated or specified. And so the verse of permission should be decisive, I mean the Almighty’s saying: “They ask you, what is lawful for them. Say: Lawful for you are good things” Al-Maslah Al-Kahf 2:17. So there should be no contradiction between them at all, and the Sunnah came to explain that. And the evidence for that is the story of the arrow, for it mentioned the ruling of what was included in this verse, which is if the arrow pierces it, then it is lawful, because it is from the good things, and what was included in the ruling of that verse, the verse of prohibition, which is if it struck it accidentally, then it is not eaten, because it is a wound, so it is one of the individuals of the verse of prohibition. And so the ruling of this should be the same whether the dog wounded him, then it is included in the ruling of the verse of permission, and if it did not wound him but rather struck him or killed him with its weight, then it is a goring or in its ruling, so it is not lawful. If it is said: Why did he not separate the ruling of the dog, and said: What you mentioned, if it wounded him, then it is lawful, and if it did not wound him, then it is forbidden. [The answer] is that this is rare, because it is the nature of a dog to kill with its claw or its fang or both, but its collision with the prey is rare, as is its killing it with its weight, so there is no need to take precautions against this because of its rarity or because its ruling is clear to those who know that dead animals, strangled animals, animals that have been beaten to death, animals that have fallen from a fall, and animals that have been gored are forbidden. As for the arrow and the projectile, sometimes it misses because of the poor aim of its archer, or for fun or something similar, rather its miss is more than its hit, so he mentioned each of its rulings in detail, and God knows best. And because the dog is likely to eat from the game, he mentioned the ruling on what happens if it eats from the game, so he said, If it eats, do not eat, for I fear that it has caught it for itself. This is correct and proven in the two Sahihs, and it is also specific to the general verse of permissibility according to many, so they said: What a dog has eaten is not permissible. This was narrated from Abu Hurayrah and Ibn Abbas, and this is what Al-Hasan, Al-Sha’bi and Al-Nakha’i said, and Abu Hanifa and his two companions went to it, and Ahmad Ibn Hanbal and Al-Shafi’i in the well-known opinion from him, and Ibn Jarir narrated in his interpretation from Ali, Sa’id, Salman, Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas: The game may be eaten even if a dog eats from it, until Sa’id, Salman, Abu Hurayrah and others said: It may be eaten even if nothing remains of it except a piece, and this is what Malik and Al-Shafi’i went to in his old opinion, and he indicated in his new opinion to two opinions, this was said by Imam Abu Nasr Ibn Al-Sabbagh. And other companions from him. Abu Dawud narrated with a good and strong chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Tha’labah Al-Khushani on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said regarding hunting with a dog: If you send your dog and mention the name of God, then eat even if it eats from it, and eat whatever your hand returns to you. Al-Nasa’i also narrated it on the authority of Amr ibn Shu’ayb on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather: That a Bedouin called Abu Tha’labah said: O Messenger of God, and he mentioned something similar. Muhammad ibn Jarir said in his interpretation: Imran ibn Bakkar Al-Kila’i told us, Abd Al-Aziz ibn Musa - he is Al-Lahouni - told us, Muhammad ibn Dinar - he is Al-Tahi - told us on the authority of Abu Iyas - he is Mu’awiyah ibn Qurra - on the authority of Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab - on the authority of Salman Al-Farsi - on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: If a man sends his dog to hunt and it catches up with it and it has eaten from it, then let him eat what is left. Then Ibn Jarir explained it as a reason by saying that Abu Qatadah and others narrated it on the authority of Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Salman, as a continuation of the hadith. As for the majority, they preferred the hadith of Adi over that, and they sought to weaken the hadith of Abu Tha’laba and others. Some scholars have interpreted it to mean that if he ate after waiting for his companion and the separation was long and he did not come, and he ate from it because of his hunger or something similar, then there is nothing wrong with that, because in this case it is not feared that he only held back for himself, unlike if he ate from it at first glance, then it appears from it that he held back for himself, and God knows best. As for birds of prey, Al-Shafi’i stated that they are like dogs, so what they eat is forbidden according to the majority of scholars, but not forbidden according to others. Al-Muzani among our companions chose that it is not forbidden to eat what birds and birds of prey eat, and this is the view of Abu Hanifa and Ahmad. They said: Because it is not possible to teach them as dogs are taught by beating and the like. Also, they do not learn except by eating from the game, so that is excused. Also, the text was only mentioned regarding dogs, not birds. Sheikh Abu Ali said in Al-Ifsah: If we say that what dogs eat is forbidden, then there are two views regarding the prohibition of what birds eat. Judge Abu Al-Tayyib rejected this branching and arrangement due to the text of Al-Shafi’i may God have mercy on him on the equality between them, and God Almighty knows best. As for the one who falls: it is the one who falls from a high place or a high place, and dies as a result, so it is not permissible. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The one who falls is the one who falls from a mountain. Qatada said: it is the one who falls into a well. Al-Suddi said: it is the one who falls from a mountain or falls into a well. As for the one who was gored: it is the one who died because of someone else butting her, so it is forbidden even if the horn wounded her and blood came out of her, even from her slaughterhouse. The one who was gored is a fa’ilah with the meaning of maf’ulah, meaning she was gored. This structure is most often used in the speech of the Arabs without the feminine ta’, so they say: ‘ayn khayl’ and ‘kaf khadib’, but they do not say: ‘kaf khadiba’ or ‘ayn khahila’. As for this, some grammarians said: the feminine ta’ was used in it because it is treated like nouns, as in their saying: ‘tariqat ta’ilah’. Some of them said: the feminine ta’ was used in it to indicate the femininity from the first glance, unlike ‘ayn khayl’ and ‘kaf khadib’ because the femininity is understood from the beginning of the speech. And the Almighty’s saying: And what a wild animal has eaten means that a lion, leopard, tiger, wolf, or dog has attacked it and eaten some of it, causing it to die. It is forbidden, even if blood has flowed from it, even if it was from its slaughterhouse. It is not permissible by consensus. The people of the Age of Ignorance used to eat what a wild animal left over from a sheep, camel, cow, or something similar, so God has forbidden that to the believers. And his saying, except what you slaughter, refers to what can be referred to, of what caused its death, so it was possible to remedy it by slaughtering it and in it there is a stable life. This only refers to his saying, and the strangled, and the beaten, and the fallen, and the gored, and that which a wild beast has eaten. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his saying, except what you slaughter, he said: except what you slaughter from these and in it there is life, so eat it, for it is slaughtered. And this is how it was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and Al-Suddi. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Hafs bin Ghiyath told us, Jaafar bin Muhammad told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali regarding the verse, he said: If it stabs with its tail or kicks with its foot or blinks with its eye, then eat. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us: Al-Husayn told us: Hisham and Ibad told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, who said: If you find the slaughtered animal that has been struck by a blow, or fallen, or gored, and it is moving its hand or leg, then eat it. And this is what was narrated from Tawus, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ubayd ibn Umair, Al-Dahhak and others: that when the slaughtered animal moves with a movement that indicates that life is still in it after slaughter, then it is permissible. This is the view of the majority of jurists, and Abu Hanifa, Al-Shafi’i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said the same. Ibn Wahb said: Malik was asked about a sheep whose stomach has been pierced by a wild beast until its intestines come out, Malik said: I do not think that it should be slaughtered. What part of it should be slaughtered? And Ashhab said: Malik was asked about a hyena that attacks a ram and crushes its back. Do you think that it should be slaughtered before it dies and eaten? He said: If it has reached the witches, I do not think it should be eaten, but if it has affected its extremities, I do not see anything wrong with that. It was said to him: Did it jump on him and break his back? He said: I do not like that, he cannot live from it. It was said to him: What if a wolf attacks a sheep and pierces its stomach but does not pierce its intestines? He said: If it rips open its stomach, I do not think it should be eaten. This is the school of Malik, may God have mercy on him. The apparent meaning of the verse is general in what Malik, may God have mercy on him, excluded from the cases in which the animal reached a state from which it could not live, so there needs to be evidence specific to the verse, and God knows best. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Rafi’ ibn Khadij, he said: I said: O Messenger of God, we will meet the enemy tomorrow and we do not have a knife, so should we slaughter with a reed? He said: “Whatever makes the blood flow and the name of God has been mentioned over it, then eat it, except the tooth and the nail. I will tell you about that: The tooth is a bone, and the nail is the knife of the Ethiopians.” In the hadith narrated by Ad-Daraqutni with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, which is questionable, and narrated on the authority of Umar with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, which is more authentic: Slaughter is in the throat and the core, and do not hasten souls to perish. In the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and the Sunan scholars on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah on the authority of Abu Al-Ashra Ad-Darimi on the authority of his father, he said: I said: O Messenger of God, is slaughtering only from the core and the throat? He said: If you were to stab it in the thigh, it would suffice for you. It is a sahih hadith, but it is interpreted as referring to what cannot be slaughtered in the throat and core. And his saying, And what was slaughtered on the altars, Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj said: The altars were stones around the Kaaba. Ibn Jurayj said: They were three hundred and sixty altars. The Arabs in their pre-Islamic period used to slaughter at them, and sprinkle whatever came to the House from them with the blood of those sacrifices, and they would cut up the meat and place it on the altars. This was also mentioned by more than one person. So God forbade the believers from this action, and He forbade them to eat these sacrifices that were done at the altars, even if the name of God was mentioned over them in the slaughter at the altar, from the polytheism that God and His Messenger forbade. And this should be interpreted as such, because the prohibition of what was dedicated to other than God has already been mentioned. And the Almighty said: And that you seek lots with arrows meaning, it is forbidden for you, O believers, to seek lots with arrows, the singular of which is zalam, and the zay may be opened, so it is said: zalam. The Arabs in their ignorance used to do that, and it is a set of three arrows, on one of which is written: Do, and on the other: Do not do, and the third is empty and nothing is due on it. Some people said: It is written on one: My Lord commanded me, and on the other: My Lord forbade me, and the third is empty and nothing is due on it. So if he turns it and the arrow of command appears, he does it, or the arrow of prohibition, he leaves it, and if it appears empty, he repeats it. And seeking lots is taken from seeking a share from these arrows, this is how Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir decided, and Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabah told us, Al-Hajjaj ibn Muhammad told us, Ibn Jurayj and Uthman ibn Ata’ told us on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas And that you seek lots with arrows he said: And the arrows are arrows that they used to seek lots with in matters, and this is how it was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ibrahim al-Nakha`i, al-Hasan al-Basri and Muqatil. Ibn Hayyan. Ibn Abbas said: They were arrows that they used to draw lots for matters. Muhammad bin Ishaq and others mentioned: The greatest idol of the Quraysh was an idol called Hubal, erected over a well inside the Kaaba, in which gifts were placed, and the money of the Kaaba was in it.
