It had seven arrows in which were written what they would seek judgment on that was unclear to them. Whatever came out of it, they would return to it and not turn away from it. It was proven in the two Sahihs that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered the Kaaba, he found Abraham and Ishmael depicted in it, and in their hands were arrows, so he said: “May God kill them. They knew that they had never drawn lots for matters.” In Sahih: When Suraqa bin Malik bin Ja'sham went out in pursuit of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and Abu Bakr, and they were going to Madinah as emigrants, he said: So I cast lots with arrows, will I harm them or not? The one I was forced to cast out would not harm them. He said: So I disobeyed the arrows and followed them, then he cast lots with them a second and third time, each time the one I was forced to cast out would not harm them, and that was the case. Suraqa had not converted to Islam at that time, but he converted to Islam after that. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ibrahim bin Yazid on the authority of Ruqayyah, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, on the authority of Raja bin Haywah, on the authority of Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: He who practices divination or casts lots or returns from a journey flying will not ascend to the ranks. Mujahid said about His statement: And that you cast lots with arrows, he said: They are the arrows of the Arabs, and the arrows of the Persians and Romans, they used to gamble. What was mentioned by Mujahid about the arrows being used for gambling is questionable, unless it is said that they used them for seeking guidance sometimes and for gambling other times, and God knows best. God the Almighty has linked them to gambling, which is maysir, as He said at the end of the Surah: “O you who have believed, indeed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone alters [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful. Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of God and from prayer. So will you not desist?” And likewise He said here: And that you cast lots with arrows - that is grave disobedience, meaning engaging in it is grave disobedience, error, misguidance, ignorance and polytheism. God has commanded the believers, if they are hesitant in their affairs, to seek His guidance by worshipping Him and then asking Him for the best in the matter they want. Imam Ahmad, Al-Bukhari and the people of Sunan narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Mawali on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught us to seek guidance in matters as he taught us a surah from the Qur’an, and he said: “If one of you intends to do something, let him perform two rak’ahs of prayer other than the obligatory prayer, then let him say: ‘O God, I seek guidance from You by Your knowledge, and I seek Your power by Your power, and I ask You from Your great bounty, for You are able and I am not able, and You know and I do not know, and You are the Knower of the unseen. O God, if You know that this matter - and he mentioned it by its name - is good for me in my religion, my worldly life, my livelihood and the consequences of my affair - or he said: my immediate and deferred affair - then decree it for me, make it easy for me, and bless me in it. O God, if You know that it is bad for me in my religion, my worldly life, my livelihood and the consequences of my affair, then turn me away from it, and turn it away from me, and decree for me what is good wherever it may be, and make me content with it.’” The wording of Ahmad. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good, sound, strange hadith, no. We know it only from the hadith of Ibn Abi Al-Mawali. And His saying, Today those who disbelieved have despaired of [defeating] your religion, Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning they have despaired of returning to their religion, and this is what was narrated on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, Al-Suddi, and Muqatil bin Hayyan. And this meaning is based on the authentic hadith in Sahih: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The devil has despaired of being worshipped by those who pray in the Arabian Peninsula, but by causing dissension among them. It is possible that what is meant is that they have despaired of resembling the Muslims because of the characteristics that distinguish Muslims from these characteristics that are contrary to polytheism and its people. For this reason, God the Almighty said, commanding His believing servants to be patient and steadfast in opposing the disbelievers and not to fear anyone except God, so He said, So do not fear them, but fear Me, meaning do not fear them in opposing them, and fear Me, and I will support you against them and annihilate them, and I will make you victorious over them, and heal your hearts from them, and I will make you above them in this world and the hereafter. And His saying, Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favor upon you, and have approved for you Islam as religion, this is the greatest of God’s blessings. God the Almighty has completed their religion for them, so they do not need any other religion than his, nor any prophet other than their prophet, may the prayers and peace of God be upon him. For this reason God the Almighty made him the Seal of the Prophets and sent him to mankind and the jinn. There is nothing permissible except what He has permitted, nothing is forbidden except what He has forbidden, and there is no religion except what He has legislated. Everything that He has informed us about is true and honest, with no lie or betrayal in it, as God the Almighty said: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice. That is, truth in the report, and justice in the commands and prohibitions. When He completed the religion for them, the blessing was completed for them. For this reason God the Almighty said: This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion. That is, so establish it for yourselves, for it is the religion that God loves and is pleased with, and with which He sent the best of the honorable messengers, and with which He revealed the most honorable of His books. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, This day I have perfected your religion for you, which is Islam, God informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers that He had perfected their faith, so they would never need anything more. God had completed it, so it would never decrease, and God was pleased with it, so He would never be angry with him. Asbat said on the authority of Al-Suddi: This verse was revealed on the Day of Arafah, and after that nothing was revealed about what was lawful or unlawful. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned and died. Asma bint Umays said: I performed Hajj with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that Hajj, and while we were walking, Gabriel appeared to him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, leaned on his mount, but the mount could not bear the weight of the Qur’an on it, so it knelt down. I came to him and covered him with a cloak that I had on. Ibn Jarir and others said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died eighty-one days after the Day of Arafah. Both were narrated by Ibn Jarir. Then he said: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of his father, who said: When the verse, This day I have perfected your religion for you, was revealed, and that was the day of the greater pilgrimage, Umar wept. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him, What makes you weep? He said, I am weeping because we used to have an increase in our religion, but when it is perfected, nothing is perfected without being diminished. He said, You have spoken the truth. This meaning is supported by the authentic hadith, Indeed, Islam began as something strange, and it will return to being strange, so blessed are the strangers. Imam Ahmad said: Jaafar bin Awn narrated to us, Abu Al-Umais narrated to us, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, who said: A Jewish man came to Umar bin Al-Khattab and said: O Commander of the Faithful, you recite a verse in your book, if it had been revealed to us Jews, we would have taken that day as a festival. He said: Which verse? He said: His statement: This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you. Umar said: By God, I know the day on which it was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the hour in which it was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: the eve of Arafah on a Friday. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Al-Sabah, on the authority of Jaafar bin Awn, on his authority. Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, and Al-Nasa’i also narrated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on his authority. Al-Bukhari’s wording when interpreting this verse is on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Tariq, who said: The Jews said to Umar: By God, you recite a verse, if it had been revealed to us, we would have taken it as a festival. Umar said: I know when it was revealed, where it was revealed, and where the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was when it was revealed: the Day of Arafah, and by God I am in Arafah. Sufyan said: I am in doubt, whether it was a Friday or not: This day I have perfected for you your religion verse. Sufyan’s doubt, may God have mercy on him, if it was in the narration, was due to piety, as he doubted whether his sheikh had informed him of that or not. If he doubted whether the standing during the Farewell Pilgrimage was on a Friday, then this is what I think Al-Thawri, may God have mercy on him, would have said, for this is a known and definitive matter, and none of the companions of the battles and biographies, nor the jurists, differed about it. There are many narrations about it, the authenticity of which is not doubted, and God knows best. This hadith has been narrated from Umar through more than one chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Raja ibn Abi Salamah told us, Ubadah ibn Nassi told us, our leader Ishaq told us, Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir - he is Ishaq ibn Harsha - said on the authority of Qubaysah, meaning Ibn Abi Dhi`b, he said: Ka`b said: If this verse had been revealed to any other nation, they would have looked to the day on which it was revealed to them, and taken it as a festival on which they would gather. Umar said: Which verse, O Ka`b? He said: This day I have perfected your religion for you. Umar said: I know the day on which it was revealed and the place in which it was revealed: it was revealed on a Friday and the Day of Arafah, and both of them, praise be to God, are festivals for us. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Bakr told us, Qubaysah told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ammar, who was a client of Banu Hashim: Ibn Abbas recited, This day I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and have chosen for you Islam as your religion. A Jew said: If this verse had been revealed to us, we would have taken that day as a festival. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed on the day of two festivals: a festival day and a Friday. Ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad bin Kamil told us, Musa bin Harun told us, Yahya bin Al-Hammani told us, Qais bin Al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Umar Al-Bazzar, on the authority of Abu Al-Hanafiyyah, on the authority of Ali, who said: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was standing on the eve of Arafah, This day I have perfected for you your religion. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Amer Ismail bin Amr Al-Sakuni told us, Hisham bin Ammar told us, Ibn Ayyash told us, Amr bin Qais Al-Sakuni told us, that he heard Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan on the pulpit reciting this verse, This day I have perfected your religion for you, until he finished it, and he said: It was revealed on the Day of Arafah, on a Friday. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq on the authority of Amr ibn Musa ibn Dihya, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah, who said: This verse, This day I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and have approved for you Islam as your religion, was revealed on the Day of Arafah, while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was standing at the place of standing. As for what Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah on the authority of Khalid ibn Abi Imran, on the authority of Hanash ibn Abdullah al-Sagani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was born on Monday, left Mecca on Monday, entered Medina on Monday, conquered Badr on Monday, and Surah al-Ma’idah was revealed on Monday: This day I have perfected for you your religion, and the remembrance was raised on Monday. It is a strange trace, and its chain of transmission is weak. Imam Ahmad narrated it: Musa bin Dawud told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Abi Imran, on the authority of Hanash al-Sagani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was born on Monday, and he was appointed a prophet on Monday, and he emigrated from Mecca to Medina on Monday, and he arrived in Medina on Monday, and he died on Monday, and the Black Stone was placed on Monday. This is the wording of Ahmad, and he did not mention the revelation of the Table on Monday, and God knows best. Perhaps Ibn Abbas meant that it was revealed on the day of two Eids, as mentioned above, so the narrator was confused, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir said: It has been said: That is not a day known to the people. Then it was narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Today I have perfected your religion for you, he said: That is not a day known to the people. He said: It has been said: It was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on his way to the Farewell Pilgrimage. Then it was narrated on the authority of Abu Ja`far Al-Razi on the authority of Al-Rabi` Ibn Anas. I said: Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Abu Harun Al-`Abdi on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri: That it was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Ghadir Khumm when he said to Ali, Whoever I am his master, then Ali is his master. Then he narrated it on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and in it it is the eighteenth day of Dhul-Hijjah, meaning his return from the Farewell Pilgrimage, and neither of these is correct, rather the truth, in which there is no doubt or uncertainty, is that it was revealed on the Day of Arafah, and it was a Friday, as narrated by the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Ali ibn Abi Talib, and the first king of Islam, Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and the interpreter of the Qur’an, Abdullah ibn Abbas, and Samurah ibn Jundub, may God be pleased with them, and it was sent by al-Sha’bi, Qatadah ibn Di’amah, Shahr ibn Hawshab, and more than one of the imams and scholars, and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari, may God have mercy on him, chose it. And his saying, But if someone is forced by severe hunger, not inclining to sin, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. That is, if someone needs to eat any of these forbidden things that God the Most High mentioned due to a necessity that forced him to do so, then he may eat it, and God is Forgiving and Merciful to him because He the Most High knows the need of His servant who is forced and in need of that, so He overlooks it and forgives him. In Al-Musnad and Sahih Ibn Hibban, on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God loves for His concession to be taken advantage of just as He hates for His disobedience to be committed. This is the wording of Ibn Hibban. And in a wording of Ahmad, Whoever does not accept God’s concession will have a burden of sin like the mountains of Arafat. For this reason, the jurists said: Eating dead meat may be obligatory in some cases, such as if he fears for himself and cannot find anything else, and it may be recommended, or it may be permissible according to the circumstances. They differed as to whether he should eat an amount of it that will satisfy his hunger, or whether he should be satisfied or satisfied and take provisions? According to the statements as stated in the Book of Rulings, and in the case of finding a dead animal and the food of another or game while he is in a state of ihram, does he eat the dead animal or that game and is he obligated to pay the penalty or that food and is he liable for its replacement, according to two statements, which are the statements of Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him. And it is not a condition for the permissibility of eating dead animal that three days pass without finding food as many of the common people and others may imagine, rather when he is forced to do so, it is permissible for him. Imam Ahmad said: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Al-Awza’i told us, Hassan bin Atiyah told us, on the authority of Abu Waqid Al-Laithi, that they said: O Messenger of God, we live in a land where famine afflicts us, so when will it be permissible for us to eat dead meat there? He said: If you do not eat it in the morning, or in the evening, or eat green vegetables there, then do as you please. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this source, and it is a sound chain of transmission according to the conditions of the two Sahihs. Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Abd Al-A’la bin Wasil from Muhammad bin Al-Qasim Al-Asadi from Al-Awza’i with it, but some of them narrated it from Al-Awza’i, from Hassan bin Atiyah, from Muslim bin Yazid, from Abu Waqid with it. And some of them narrated it from Al-Awza’i, from Hassan, from Marthad or Abu Marthad from Abu Waqid with it. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir on the authority of Hannad ibn al-Sarri, on the authority of Isa ibn Yunus, on the authority of Hassan, on the authority of a man who was named and he mentioned him. He also narrated it on the authority of Hannad, on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of al-Awza’i, on the authority of Hassan, without a chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim told us, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, who said: I found Samurah’s book with al-Hasan, so I read it to him. It said: In case of necessity, a morning or evening meal is sufficient. Abu Kuraib narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Khaseeb bin Zaid Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Al-Hasan: A man asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: When will the forbidden be made permissible? He said: He said: Until when will your family be satisfied with milk or will their provisions be provided? Ibn Hamid narrated to us, Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, Umar bin Abdullah bin Urwah narrated to me, on the authority of his grandfather Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, on the authority of his grandmother: A man from the Bedouins came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ask him about what God has forbidden to him and what He has permitted to him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Good things are permissible for you and impure things are forbidden to you, unless you are in need of food, in which case you eat from it until you no longer need it. The man said: What is my poverty that makes it permissible for me and what is my wealth that makes me independent of that? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you hope to be rich and you seek it and you reach some of it, then feed your family whatever you want until you are independent of it. The Bedouin said: What is the wealth that I will leave if I find it? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you provide your family with a late-night meal, then avoid the food of your wealth that God has forbidden you, for it is all within reach and there is nothing forbidden in it. The meaning of his saying, Unless you eat breakfast means lunch, Unless you eat dinner means dinner, Or eat some green vegetables, then do as you please so eat from them. Ibn Jarir said: This word, meaning his saying, Or eat some green vegetables is narrated in four ways: Tahafu’u with a hamza, Tahafu: with a light ya’ and ha’, Tahafu with a shaddah, Tahafu with a ha’ and with a light ya’, and it is possible to eat some green vegetables, this is how it was narrated in the interpretation. [Another Hadith] - Abu Dawud said: Harun bin Abdullah told us, Al-Fadl bin Dukayn told us, Wahb bin Uqbah Al-Amiri told us, I heard my father narrating on the authority of Al-Naji’ Al-Amiri that he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: What is permissible for us of dead meat? He said: What is your food? We said: We eat breakfast and lunch. Abu Nu’aym said: Uqbah explained it to me, a cup in the morning and a cup in the evening. He said: That is it, and my father is hungry, and he made dead meat permissible for them in this state. Abu Dawud is the only one to narrate it, and it seems that they used to eat breakfast and lunch with something that was not enough for them, so he made dead meat permissible for them to be sufficient for them. It may be used as evidence by those who believe that it is permissible to eat it until one is full, and that is not restricted to satiating hunger, and God knows best. [Another hadith] - Abu Dawud said: Musa bin Ismail told us, Hammad told us, Samak told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Samurah: That a man went down to Al-Harrah with his family and children, and a man said to him: My she-camel has gone astray, so if you find her, hold on to her. So he found her but did not find her owner, and she fell ill, and his wife said to him: Slaughter her, but he refused, and she died. His wife said to him: Skin her so that her fat and meat are roasted and we can eat it. He said: No, not until I ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he came to him and asked him, and he said: Do you have enough money to satisfy you? He said: No. He said: Then eat her. So her owner came and told him the story, and he said: Why didn’t you slaughter her? He said: I felt shy before you. This is unique, and it may be used as evidence by those who permit eating to one’s fill and stocking up on her for a period of time when they think they will need her, and God knows best. His saying: not inclined to sin means engaging in disobedience to God, for God has permitted that for him and remained silent about the other, as He said in Surat al-Baqarah 2:“But whoever is forced by necessity, neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limits], there is no sin upon him. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.” This verse has been used as evidence by those who say that the sinner who travels is not permitted to avail himself of any of the concessions for travel, because concessions are not attained through sins, and God knows best.
5:4: When God the Almighty mentioned what He forbade in the previous verse of the harmful impurities for the one who consumes them, either in his body or in his religion or in both, and He excepted what He excepted in the case of necessity, as God the Almighty said: And He has explained in detail to you what He has forbidden you, except for that to which you are compelled, He said after that: "They ask you, what is lawful for them. Say: Lawful for you are the good things," as in Surat Al-A'raf in the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He permitted for them the good things and forbade them the impurities. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah told us, Yahya bin Abdullah bin Abi Bakir told us, Abdullah bin Lahi'ah told me, Ata bin Dinar told me on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Adi bin Hatim and Zaid bin Muhalhil Al-Ta'i, they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: O Messenger of God, God has forbidden dead meat, so what is lawful for us from it? Then the verse was revealed: "They ask you, what is lawful for them. Say: Lawful for you are the good things," Saeed said: He meant the lawful and good slaughtered animals for them. Muqatil said: The good things are what is permissible for them to obtain from everything, and it is the lawful provision. Al-Zuhri was asked about drinking urine for medical treatment, and he said: It is not one of the good things. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Wahb said: Malik was asked about selling birds that people eat, and he said: It is not one of the good things. And the Almighty’s saying: And what you have trained of birds of prey to hunt means that the slaughtering of which the name of God has been mentioned, and the good things of sustenance are lawful for you, and what you hunt with birds of prey is lawful for you, which are dogs, cheetahs, falcons and the like, as is the doctrine of the majority of the Companions, Followers and Imams. Among those who said this is Ali bin Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his saying: And what you have trained of birds of prey to hunt which are trained dogs, hawks, and every bird trained for hunting, and birds of prey, meaning the ferocious dogs, cheetahs, falcons and the like. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, then he said: It was narrated from Khaithamah, Tawus, Mujahid, Makhul, and Yahya bin Abi Katheer something similar to that, and it was narrated from Al-Hasan that he said: The hawk and the falcon are among the birds of prey, and it was narrated from Ali bin Al-Hussain something similar, then it was narrated from Mujahid that he disliked hunting all birds, and he recited His statement: And what you have taught of the birds of prey that are hunting with dogs. He said: It was narrated from Saeed bin Jubair something similar to that, and Ibn Jarir transmitted it from Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi, then he said: Hannad told us, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, Ibn Jurayj told us from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar, he said: As for what the hawks and other birds hunt, then whatever you catch is yours, otherwise do not feed it. I said: What is narrated from the majority is that hunting with birds is like hunting with dogs because they catch the prey with their claws as dogs catch it, so there is no difference, and this is the doctrine of the four imams and others, and Ibn Jarir chose it, and he provided evidence for that with what he narrated from Hannad, Isa bin Yunus told us from Mujalid, from Al-Sha’bi, from Adi Ibn Hatim said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about hunting with a hawk, and he said: Whatever it catches for you, eat. Imam Ahmad made an exception for hunting with a black dog, because in his opinion it is something that must be killed and it is not permissible to keep it, as it was proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Dharr that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A donkey, a woman, and a black dog interrupt prayer. So I said: What is the difference between a black dog and a red dog? He said: The black dog is a devil. In another hadith, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the killing of dogs, then he said, What is wrong with them and dogs? Kill every black, white one. These animals that are hunted are called raptures from the word jarh, which means earning, as the Arabs say: So-and-so wounded his family for good, meaning he earned them good. They also say: So-and-so has no wounder, meaning he has no earner. God the Almighty said: And He knows what you have wounded during the day, meaning what you have earned of good and evil. The reason for the revelation of this noble verse was mentioned in the hadith narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim: Hajjaj bin Hamzah told us, Zaid bin Habbab told us, Yunus bin Ubaydah told me, Aban bin Salih told me, on the authority of Al-Qa’qa’ bin Hakim, on the authority of Salma Umm Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the killing of dogs. I said: Then the people came and said: O Messenger of God, what is permissible for us from this nation that you have been ordered to kill? So he remained silent, then God revealed: “They ask you, [O Muhammad], what is lawful for them. Say: Lawful for you are [all] good things and what you have trained of birds of prey to hunt.” The verse, then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a man sends his dog and says the name of God, then it holds it, then let him eat what it has not eaten. And thus Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Zayd ibn al-Habbab on the authority of Abu Rafi’ who said: Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ask permission to see him, so he gave him permission. He said: You have been given permission, O Messenger of God. He said: Yes, But we do not enter a house in which there is a dog. Abu Rafi’ said: Then he ordered me to kill every dog in Medina until I reached a woman who had a dog that was barking at her, so I left it out of mercy for it. Then I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him, so he ordered me to go back to the dog and kill it. Then they came and said: O Messenger of God, what is lawful for us from this nation that you have been ordered to kill? He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained silent. He said: Then God, the Almighty, revealed: “They ask you, what is lawful for them. Say: Lawful for you.” Good things and what you have taught of the birds of prey. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq on the authority of Abaan ibn Salih, and he said: It is authentic, and they did not include it. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abu Rafi’ to kill dogs until he reached Al-Awali. Then Asim ibn Adi, Sa’d ibn Khaithama, and Uwaim ibn Sa’idah came and said: What is permissible for us, O Messenger of God? So the verse was revealed. Al-Hakim narrated it on the authority of Samak on the authority of Ikrimah, and Muhammad ibn Ka’b Al-Qurazi said the same about the reason for the revelation of this verse: It is about killing dogs. The Almighty’s saying: with dogs may be a state of the subject and it may be a state of the object, which is the birds of prey, meaning that you have learned that birds of prey are dogs for hunting, which is that they seize it with their claws or nails. This is evidence in this case that if the bird of prey kills the prey by striking it and not with its claws or nails, then it is not permissible for it, as is one of the two sayings of Al-Shafi’i and a group of scholars. For this reason he said: You teach them from what God has taught you, which is that if he releases it, it releases it, and if he drags it, it retrieves it, and if he takes the prey, he holds it for its owner until it comes to him, and he does not hold it for himself. For this reason God the Almighty said: So eat of what they catch for you and mention the name of God over it. So whenever the bird of prey is trained and holds it for its owner, and he mentioned the name of God over it at the time of its release, then the prey is permissible even if it kills it, by consensus. The Sunnah has mentioned something similar to what this noble verse indicates, as it was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Adi bin Hatim who said: I said: O Messenger of God, I send out trained dogs and mention the name of God! He said: If you send out your trained dog and mention the name of God, then eat what it catches for you. I said: What if they kill? He said: And if they kill what is not a dog that is not one of them, then you only mentioned the name of God over your dog and did not mention anything else. I said to him: What if I shoot with a spear at game and hit it? He said: If you throw a spear and it pierces it, then eat it. If it hits it with its side, then it is a dead animal, so do not eat it. And in another version of theirs: “And if you send your dog, mention the name of God. If it catches you and you catch it alive, then slaughter it. But if you catch it and it has killed it and has not eaten from it, then eat it. If the dog takes its slaughtering, then eat it.” And in another version of theirs: If it eats, then do not eat, for I fear that it caught it for its own sake. This is evidence for the majority, and it is the correct view of the Shafi’i school, which is that if a dog eats from the game, it is absolutely forbidden. They did not ask for details, as was mentioned in that hadith. It was narrated from a group of the Salaf that they said: It is not absolutely forbidden. Mention the effects of that Ibn Jarir said: Hannad told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Salman al-Farsi said: Eat, even if it eats two-thirds of it - meaning the game - if a dog eats from it. Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba and ‘Umar ibn ‘Amir narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Qatadah, and Muhammad ibn Zayd narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Salman. Ibn Jarir also narrated it on the authority of Mujahid ibn Musa, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Bakr ibn ‘Abdullah al-Muzani, and al-Qasim ibn Salman, who said: If a dog eats, then eat, even if it eats two-thirds of it. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Makhramah ibn Bakir told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Humayd ibn Malik ibn Khaitham al-Du’ali, that he asked Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas about the game that a dog eats from, and he said: Eat, even if nothing remains of it except a shoe, meaning a piece. Shu’bah narrated it on the authority of ‘Abd Rabbih ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Bakir ibn al-Ashja’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: Eat, even if it eats. Two thirds Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Abdul-A’la told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: If you send your dog out, eat from it. If it eats two-thirds of it and there is one-third left, then eat it. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad Ibn Abdul-A’la told us, Al-Mu’tamir told us, he heard Abdullah, and Hannad told us, Abdah told us, on the authority of Ubaidullah Ibn Umar, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Umar, who said: If you send out your trained dog and mention the name of God, then eat whatever it catches for you, whether it eats or not. Ubaidullah Ibn Umar, Ibn Abi Dhi’b, and others narrated it likewise on the authority of Nafi’. These narrations are proven on the authority of Salman, Sa’d Ibn Abi Waqqas, Abu Hurairah, and Ibn Umar. It is narrated on the authority of Ali and Ibn Abbas, and there is disagreement about it on the authority of Ata’ and Al-Hasan Al-Basri. It is the opinion of Al-Zuhri, Rabi’ah, and Malik, and Al-Shafi’i adopted it in the old version and alluded to it in the new version. It was narrated on the authority of Salman al-Farsi, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir said: Imran ibn Bakkar al-Kila’i told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Musa al-Lahouni told us, Muhammad ibn Dinar, who is al-Taji, told us on the authority of Abu Iyas Mu’awiyah ibn Qurra, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Salman al-Farsi, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: If a man sends his dog to hunt and it catches up with it and it has eaten some of it, then let him eat what is left. Then Ibn Jarir said: There is a problem with the chain of transmission of this hadith, and Sa’id is not known to have heard it from Salman, and trustworthy narrators narrate it from the words of Salman, other than with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. What Ibn Jarir said is correct, but this meaning has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from other sources. Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Munhal al-Darir told us, Yazid ibn Zari’ told us, Habib al-Mu’allim told us on the authority of Amr ibn Shu’ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that a Bedouin called Abu Tha’labah said: O Messenger of God, I have dogs with dogs, so give me a fatwa regarding hunting them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you have dogs with dogs, then eat them. “From what they catch for you.” He said: Smart or unsmart, and even if it eats from it? He said: Yes, even if it eats from it. He said: O Messenger of God, give me a fatwa regarding my bow. He said: Eat whatever your bow returns to you. He said: Smart or unsmart? “And even if it disappears from you as long as it does not go astray or you find a trace of it other than your arrow.” He said: Give me a fatwa regarding the vessels of the Magians if we are forced to use them. He said: Wash them and eat from them. This is how Abu Dawud narrated it. An-Nasa’i also included it, and Abu Dawud also narrated it on the authority of Yunus ibn Sayf, on the authority of Abu Idris al-Khawlani, on the authority of Abu Tha’labah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you send your dog and mention the name of God, eat even if it eats from it, and eat whatever your hand returns to you. These two chains of transmission are good. Ath-Thawri narrated on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of Adi, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whatever is a harmful dog that you catch for you, eat. I said: Even if it eats? He said: Yes. Abdul Malik bin Habib narrated: Asad bin Musa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Zaydah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Adi, similarly. These are traces indicating that it is forgiven, even if a dog eats from it. Those who do not forbid hunting by eating a dog and the like have used them as evidence, as we mentioned earlier from those we have narrated from. Others have taken a middle course and said: If he eats after he has caught it, then it is forbidden, based on the hadith of Adi bin Hatim, and the reason to which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, referred: If he eats, then do not eat, for I fear that he caught it for his own sake. But if he catches it and then waits for its owner for a long time and becomes hungry and eats from it because of his hunger, then it does not affect the prohibition. They based the hadith of Abu Tha’labah Al-Khushani on that. This is a good distinction, and combining the two hadiths is sound. Professor Abu al-Ma'ali al-Juwayni wished in his book al-Nihaya that he would have explained this detail, and God fulfilled his wish. A group of companions said this statement and distinction, including them. Others said a fourth statement on the issue, which is the distinction between eating a dog, which is forbidden according to the hadith of Adi, and eating falcons and the like, which is not forbidden because they do not accept training except by eating. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Asbat bin Muhammad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Shaibani told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said about the bird: If you release it and it kills, then eat, because if you hit the dog, it will not return, even if the bird learns to return to its owner and not to hit, so if it eats from the hunt and plucks its feathers, then eat. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, and Hammad bin Abi Sulayman said the same. And evidence for these may be cited by what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Abu Sa'id told us, al-Maharibi told us, Mujalid told us, on the authority of al-Sha'bi, on the authority of Adi bin Hatim, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, we are people who hunt with dogs and falcons, so what is permissible for us from them? He said: It is lawful for you to have trained dogs which you have trained from what God has taught you, so eat of what they catch for you and mention the name of God over it. Then he said: Whatever dog you send and mention the name of God over it, then eat of what it catches for you. I said: Even if it kills? He said: Even if it kills, it does not eat. I said: O Messenger of God, what if our dogs mix with other dogs? He said: Then do not eat until you know that your dog is the one who caught it. I said: We are a people who shoot, so what is lawful for us? He said: Whatever you mention the name of God over and it pierces, then eat. So the evidence for them is that he stipulated that the dog should not eat, but he did not stipulate that in the case of the falcon, so this indicates a difference between them in the ruling, and God knows best.” And the Almighty’s saying: And eat of that which they catch for you, and mention the name of God over it means when you send it out, as the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said to Adi bin Hatim: If you send out your trained dog, and mention the name of God, then eat what it catches for you. And in the hadith of Abu Tha’labah, which is also included in the two Sahihs, If you send out your dog, mention the name of God, and if you shoot your arrow, mention the name of God. For this reason, the imams who stipulated it, such as Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, stipulated, in the well-known opinion from him, the Bismillah when sending the dog and shooting the arrow, for this verse and this hadith. And this opinion is the well-known opinion from the majority, that what is meant by this verse is the command to say the Bismillah when sending it out, as al-Suddi and others said. And Ali bin Abi Talhah said from Ibn Abbas regarding his saying: And mention the name of God over it, he says: If you send out your bird of prey, then say: In the name of God, and if you forget, there is no blame. And some people said: What is meant by this verse is the command to say the Bismillah when eating, as is proven in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, taught his foster son Omar bin Abi Salamah, saying: In the name of God, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is in front of you. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Aisha, they said: O Messenger of God, some people come to us recently converted from disbelief, and we eat meat, and we do not know whether the name of God was mentioned over it or not. He said: Say the name of God yourselves and eat. [Another hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Badil, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair, on the authority of Aisha: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was eating food with six of his companions, and a Bedouin came and ate it in two bites, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If the name of God had been mentioned, it would have been sufficient for you. So when one of you eats food, let him mention the name of God. If he forgets to mention the name of God at the beginning, let him say: In the name of God, its beginning and its end.” And this is how Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Yazid bin Harun, and this is a disconnected chain of transmission between Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair and Aisha, for he did not hear this hadith from her, as evidenced by what Imam Ahmad narrated: Abdul Wahhab told us, Hisham, meaning Ibn Abi Abdullah Al-Dastawai, told us, on the authority of Badil, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair: that a woman among them called Umm Kulthum told him on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was eating food with six of his companions, and a Bedouin came. A hungry Bedouin ate two bites of food and said, “If he mentioned the name of God, it would be enough for you. So when one of you eats, let him mention the name of God. If he forgets the name of God at the beginning, let him say, ‘In the name of God, at the beginning and at the end.’” It was also narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa’i from different sources on the authority of Hisham al-Dastawai, and al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih. [Another hadith] - Ahmad said: Ali bin Abdullah told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, Jabir bin Subh told us, Al-Muthanna bin Abdul Rahman Al-Khuza’i told me and I accompanied him to Wasit, so he used to say Bismillah at the beginning of his food, and at the last morsel he would say: In the name of God, its beginning and its end. So I said to him: You say Bismillah at the beginning of what you eat. What do you think of your saying at the end of what you eat, ‘In the name of God, its beginning and its end?’ He said: I told you that my grandfather Umayyah bin Makhshi, who was one of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, I heard him say: A man was eating and the Prophet was watching, so he did not say Bismillah until the last morsel of his food was a morsel. He said: In the name of God, its beginning and its end. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, the devil continued to eat with him until he said Bismillah, and nothing remained in his stomach until he vomited it. And this is how Abu Dawud and Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Jabir bin Subh Al-Rasibi Abu Bishr Al-Basri, and Ibn Ma’in and Al-Nasa’i authenticated him. Abu Al-Fath Al-Azdi said: It does not constitute proof. [Another hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Khaithamah, on the authority of Abu Hudhayfah - Abu Abd al-Rahman Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad, whose name is Salamah bin al-Haitham bin Suhaib - from the companions of Ibn Mas’ud, on the authority of Hudhayfah, said: When we were present with the Prophet at a meal, we would not put our hands down until the Messenger of God began to put his hand down. We were present with him at a meal, and a girl came as if she was pushing and went to put her hand in the food, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took her hand. A Bedouin came as if he was pushing and went to put his hand in the food, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took his hand. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The devil considers food permissible if the name of God is not mentioned over it. He came with this girl to consider it permissible through her, so I took her hand. He came with this Bedouin to consider it permissible through him, so I took his hand. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, his hand is in my hand with their hands,” meaning the devil. Muslim, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa’i narrated it in the same way, from the hadith of al-A’mash. [Another hadith] - Muslim and the people of Sunan, except Al-Tirmidhi, narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “If a man enters his house and mentions God upon entering and upon eating, Satan says: You have no place to spend the night and no dinner. And if he enters and does not mention the name of God upon entering, Satan says: You have found a place to spend the night. And if he does not mention the name of God upon eating, Satan says: You have found a place to spend the night and dinner.” The wording of Abu Dawud. [Another hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Abd Rabbih told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Wahshi bin Harb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that a man said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We eat but we do not get full. He said: “Perhaps you eat separately. Gather around your food and mention the name of God, and He will bless it for you.” Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Al-Walid bin Muslim.
5:5: When God the Almighty mentioned what He has forbidden to His believing servants, of the impure things, and what He has permitted them of the good things, He said after that, This day have been made lawful for you [all] good things. Then He mentioned the ruling on the slaughtering of the People of the Two Books, of the Jews and Christians, saying, And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you. Ibn Abbas, Abu Umamah, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ikrimah, Ata, Al-Hasan, Makhul, Ibrahim Al-Nakha'i, Al-Suddi, and Muqatil bin Hayyan said: He means their slaughtering, and this is a matter agreed upon by the scholars, that their slaughtering is lawful for the Muslims, because they believe that slaughtering for anyone other than God is forbidden, and they do not mention anything over their slaughtering except the name of God, even if they believe in Him the Almighty that which He is free from, exalted and sanctified. It has been proven in Sahih: On the authority of Abdullah bin Mughaffal, he said: A bag of fat was brought to me on the day of Khaybar, so I embraced it and said: I will not give any of this to anyone today. I turned around and saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, smiling. The jurists used this as evidence that it is permissible to eat what one needs of food and the like from the spoils before the division. This is clear. The Hanafi, Shafi’i and Hanbali jurists used this as evidence against the companions of Malik in their prohibition of eating what the Jews believe to be forbidden from their slaughtered animals, such as fat and the like of what was forbidden to them. The Malikis do not permit Muslims to eat it, because God Almighty said: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you. They said: This is not from their food. The majority used this hadith as evidence against them, and there is a consideration in that, because it is a specific issue. It is possible that it was fat, which they believed to be permissible, such as the fat of the back and the entrails and the like. And God knows best. Better in evidence than this is what has been proven in Sahih, that the people of Khaybar presented to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a roasted sheep, and it has been They poisoned her arm and he liked the arm, so he took it and bit it, then the arm told him that it was poisoned, so he spat it out, and that left an effect on the teeth of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and on his aorta, and Bishr ibn al-Bara’ ibn Ma’rur ate from it with him and died, so he killed the Jewess who had poisoned her, and her name was Zaynab, and the evidence from that is that he decided to eat it and those with him, and he did not ask them whether they had removed from it what they believed to be forbidden from its fat or not. In another hadith: That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, added a Jew to barley bread and rancid oil, meaning rancid ghee. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was read to Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid bin Mazid, Muhammad bin Shuaib told us, An-Nu’man bin Al-Mundhir told me, on the authority of Makhul, who said: God revealed, And do not eat of that upon which the name of God has not been mentioned, then the Lord, the Almighty, abrogated it and had mercy on the Muslims, saying, This day are lawful for you [all] good things and the food of those who were given the Scripture, so He abrogated it thereby, and made the food of the People of the Scripture lawful. In what Makhul, may God have mercy on him, said, there is a consideration, because his permitting the food of the People of the Scripture does not necessarily permit eating that upon which the name of God has not been mentioned, because they mention the name of God over their sacrifices and offerings, and they worship that, and for this reason he did not permit the sacrifices of those other than them from the people of polytheism and those similar to them, because they do not mention the name of God over their sacrifices, and they do not even stop at slaughtering what they eat of meat, rather they eat dead meat, unlike the People of the Book and those similar to them from the Samaritans and the Sabians and those who… He adheres to the religion of Abraham, Seth, and other prophets, according to one of the two opinions of scholars and Arab Christians, such as Banu Taghlib, Tanukh, Bahra, Judham, Lakhm, Amala, and those similar to them. Their sacrifices are not eaten according to the majority. Abu Jaafar bin Jarir said: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ubaydah, who said: Ali said: Do not eat the slaughtered animals of Banu Taghlib, because they only adhere to Christianity through drinking alcohol. This is what more than one person from the predecessors and successors said. Saeed bin Abi Arouba said: on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Al-Hasan, that they saw no harm in the slaughtered animals of the Christians of Banu Taghlib. As for the Magians, even though the jizya is taken from them as a consequence of and incorporation into the People of the Book, their slaughtered animals are not to be eaten and their women are not to be married, contrary to the opinion of Abu Thawr Ibrahim bin Khalid Al-Kalbi, one of the jurists from the companions of Al-Shafi’i and Ahmad bin Hanbal. When he said that and it became well-known about him, the jurists denounced him for it, until Imam Ahmad said about him: Abu Thawr, as his name suggests, meaning in this issue, and it is as if he held on to the generality of a hadith that was narrated without a chain of transmission on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in which he said: Treat them as you would the People of the Book. However, this wording was not proven. Rather, what is in Sahih al-Bukhari, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, is that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the jizya from the Magians of Hajar. Even if the authenticity of this hadith is accepted, its generality is limited to the meaning of this verse: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you. So its meaning indicates the meaning of the opposite that the food of those other than them from the people of religions is not lawful. And the Almighty’s saying: And your food is lawful for them means it is lawful for you to feed them from your slaughtered animals. This is not a statement about the ruling according to them, unless it is a statement about what they were commanded to do, which is to eat from every food on which the name of God is mentioned, whether it is from the people of their religion or not. The first is clearer in meaning, meaning it is lawful for you to feed them from your slaughtered animals as you ate from their slaughtered animals. This is a form of recompense, exchange, and recompense, just as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, dressed Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul in his garment when he died and buried him in it. They said: Because he had dressed Al-Abbas in his garment when he came to Medina, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, rewarded him for that with that. As for the hadith in which it says: Do not accompany anyone but a believer, and do not let anyone eat your food but a pious person, it is interpreted as being recommended and desirable, and God knows best. And his saying: And chaste women from among the believers means, and it is lawful for you to marry free, chaste women from among the believing women. This was mentioned as an introduction to what follows, which is the saying of God Almighty: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you. It was said that he meant by chaste women the free women, not the slave women, as Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid. Rather, Mujahid said: The chaste women are the free women. It is possible that he meant what he narrated from him, and it is possible that he meant by the chaste free woman, as he said in the other narration from him, and it is the saying of the majority here, and it is more likely, so that she does not come together as a dhimmi, and she is also not chaste, so her situation is completely corrupted and her husband gets what is said in the proverb: A bad measure and a bad measure. What appears from the verse is that what is meant by chaste women are those who are chaste from fornication, as God Almighty said in the other verse: Chaste, not fornicators nor taking lovers. Then the commentators and scholars differed regarding the saying of God Almighty: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture from among the believers. Before you, does it include every chaste woman of the Book, whether she is free or a slave? Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of a group of the Salaf, who interpreted the word al-Muhsanah as al-Muhsinah. It was said: What is meant by the People of the Book here are the Israelites, which is the view of al-Shafi’i. It was also said: What is meant by that are the dhimmis, not the warlike women, because of His statement: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day, the verse. Abdullah ibn Umar did not see marriage to a Christian woman, and he said: I do not know of a greater form of polytheism than saying that her Lord is Jesus, and God the Most High said: And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe, the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad bin Hatim bin Sulayman al-Mu’addib told us, al-Qasim bin Malik, meaning al-Muzani, told us, Ismail bin Sami’ told us on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ghifari, who said: This verse was revealed: And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe. He said: So people were prevented from them until the verse that came after it was revealed: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you. So people married women from among the People of the Book. A group of the Companions married Christian women, and they saw no harm in that, taking this noble verse: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you. So they made this a specification for the one in Surat al-Baqarah 2:And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe. If it is said that the People of the Book are included in its generality, otherwise there is no contradiction between it and it, because the People of the Book have been separated in their mention from the polytheists in more than one place, like the Almighty’s saying: Those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists could not separate until there came to them clear proof. And like His saying: And say to those who were given the Scripture and the unlettered Have you submitted? If they submit, then they are guided. The verse. And his saying: If you give them their dowries, meaning their bridal gifts, meaning that as they are chaste and pure, then give them dowries willingly. Jabir ibn Abdullah, Amir al-Sha’bi, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, and al-Hasan al-Basri issued a fatwa stating that if a man marries a woman and she commits adultery before he has intercourse with her, then they should be separated and she should return to him what he gave her as a dowry. Ibn Jarir narrated this from them. And his saying: Chaste, not fornicators nor taking mistresses. Just as he stipulated chastity for women, which is chastity from fornication, he also stipulated it for men, which is that the man should also be chaste and married. That is why he said: Not fornicators, which are the fornicators who do not refrain from sin and do not turn themselves away from those who come to them, nor taking mistresses, meaning those with mistresses who do not act except with them, as was mentioned in Surat An-Nisa’, and that is why Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may God have mercy on him, held that it is not valid to marry a prostitute until she repents, and as long as she is like that, it is not valid to marry her to a chaste man. Likewise, according to him, it is not valid for a wicked man to marry a chaste woman until he repents and stops what he is doing of fornication, due to this verse and the hadith: A flogged fornicator may not marry anyone except his like. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Sulayman ibn Harb told us, Abu Hilal told us on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: Umar ibn Al-Khattab said: I was thinking of not… He asked someone who committed an immoral act in Islam to marry a chaste woman. Ubayy ibn Ka’b said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, polytheism is greater than that, and it may be accepted from him if he repents. We will discuss this issue in detail when he says: “The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress does not marry except an adulterer or a polytheist. And that is forbidden to the believers.” For this reason, God Almighty said here: And whoever disbelieves in faith - his work has become worthless, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers.
5:6: Many of the Salaf said about his statement: If you rise to prayer: meaning while you are in a state of minor ritual impurity. Others said: If you rise from sleep to pray, and both are close. Others said: Rather, the meaning is more general than that, as the verse commands ablution when rising to pray, but it is obligatory for one who is in a state of minor ritual impurity, and recommended for one who purifies himself. It has been said that the command to perform ablution for every prayer was obligatory at the beginning of Islam, then it was abrogated. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Marthad, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Buraydah, on the authority of his father, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to perform ablution for every prayer. When it was the day of the conquest, he performed ablution and wiped over his socks and prayed the prayers with one ablution. Umar said to him: O Messenger of God, you have done something that you did not do before. He said, I did it deliberately, O Umar. This is how Muslim and the people of Sunan narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri on the authority of Alqamah ibn Murthad. It appears in Sunan Ibn Majah on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muharib ibn Dithar instead of Alqamah ibn Murthad, both on the authority of Sulayman ibn Buraydah with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abbad ibn Musa told us, Ziyad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Tufayl al-Bakka’i told us, al-Fadl ibn al-Mubashar told us: I saw Jabir ibn Abdullah praying the prayers with one ablution, and if he urinated or broke his ablution, he would perform ablution and wipe his socks with the remaining water from his ablution. I said: Abu Abdullah, is there something you should do? He said: Rather, I saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, do it, so I do it as I saw the Messenger of God do it. And this is how Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Ismail ibn Tawbah, on the authority of Ziyad al-Bakka’i. Ahmad said: Ya’qub told us, my father told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Haban al-Ansari told me, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: Have you seen Abdullah ibn Umar perform ablution for every prayer, whether he was pure or not? Who is he on the authority of? He said: Asma bint Zaid bin Al-Khattab told him that Abdullah bin Hanzala bin Al-Ghasil told her that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to perform ablution for every prayer, whether one was pure or not. When that was difficult for him, he was commanded to use the siwak for every prayer, and ablution was no longer required except for one who had broken his ablution. Abdullah thought that he had the strength to do that, and he used to do it until he died. This is how Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Awf Al-Himsi on the authority of Ahmad bin Khalid Al-Dhahabi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad bin Yahya bin Habban, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah bin Umar. Then Abu Dawud said: Ibrahim bin Saad narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, and Ubaidullah bin Umar said: It means as mentioned previously in the narration of Imam Ahmad, and whatever it was, it is a sound chain of transmission, and Ibn Ishaq explicitly stated in it that he had heard and transmitted it from Muhammad bin Yahya bin Habban, so the danger of tadlis was removed. However, Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir said: It was narrated by Salamah bin Al-Fadl and Ali bin Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad bin Talhah bin Yazid bin Rukanah, on the authority of... Muhammad bin Yahya bin Habban narrated it, and God knows best. In this action of Ibn Omar and his persistence in performing ablution perfectly for every prayer, there is evidence of the desirability of that, as is the doctrine of the majority. Ibn Jarir said: Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told us, Azhar told us on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibn Sirin: The caliphs used to perform ablution for every prayer. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us, I heard Mas’ud bin Ali Al-Shaibani, I heard Ikrimah say: Ali, may God be pleased with him, used to perform ablution for every prayer and recite this verse: O you who believe, when you rise to prayer (al-Baqarah 2:174). Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Wahb bin Jarir told me, Shu’bah told us on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Maysarah, on the authority of Al-Nazzal bin Sabra, who said: I saw Ali pray the noon prayer, then he sat for the people in the courtyard, then he brought water and washed his face and hands, then he wiped his head and feet, and said: This is the ablution of one who has not broken his ablution. Ya’qub bin Ibrahim told me, Hisham told us on the authority of Mughirah on the authority of Ibrahim: Ali measured a handful of grains and performed ablution in which there was an exaggeration, and he said: This is the ablution of one who has not broken his ablution, and this is… Good ways about Ali strengthen each other. Ibn Jarir also said: Ibn Yasar told us, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab performed a light ablution, and said: This is the ablution of one who has not broken his ablution. This is a sound chain of transmission. Muhammad ibn Sirin said: The caliphs used to perform ablution for every prayer. As for what Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated on the authority of Abu Hilal, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, that he said: Ablution without breaking a ritual impurity is an aggression, this is strange from Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, then it is understood that whoever believes in its obligation is a transgressor. As for its being recommended, the Sunnah has indicated that. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Amir al-Ansari, I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to perform ablution for every prayer. He said: I said: So how did you do it? He said: We used to pray all the prayers with one ablution unless we broke our ablution. Al-Bukhari and the Sunan scholars narrated it from more than one chain of transmission on the authority of Amr ibn Amir. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Saeed al-Baghdadi told us, Ishaq ibn Mansur told us on the authority of Hazim, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad, who is al-Afriqi, on the authority of Atif, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever performs ablution in a state of purity, ten good deeds will be recorded for him. He also narrated it on the authority of Isa ibn Yunus on the authority of al-Afriqi, on the authority of Abu Atif, on the authority of Ibn Umar, and he mentioned it, and there is a story in it. And thus Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of al-Afriqi, with a similar chain of transmission. Al-Tirmidhi said: Its chain of transmission is weak. Ibn Jarir said: Some people said: This verse was revealed as a notification from God that ablution is not required except when standing for prayer and not for other actions, because when the Prophet (peace be upon him) broke his ablution, he refrained from all actions until he performed ablution. Abu Kurayb told us, Muawiyah bin Hisham told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Bakr bin Amr bin Hazm, on the authority of Abdullah bin Alqamah bin Waqqas, on the authority of his father, who said: When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) urinated, we would speak to him but he would not speak to us, and we would greet him but he would not respond to us, until the verse of permission was revealed: O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer al-Baqarah 2:177. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Muslim on the authority of Abu Kurayb with a similar wording, and it is a very strange hadith. This Jabir is Ibn Zayd al-Ju’fi, and they declared him weak. Abu Dawud said: Musaddad told us, Ismail told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Malekah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out of the toilet and food was brought to him. They said: Shall we not bring you water for ablution? He said: I was only commanded to perform ablution when I stand up for prayer. This is how At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Mani’, and An-Nasa’i on the authority of Ziyad bin Ayoub on the authority of Ismail, who is Ibn Ulayyah. At-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan hadith. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Huwayrith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he went to the toilet, then he came back and food was brought to him. It was said: O Messenger of God, will you not perform ablution? He said: I have not prayed, so perform ablution. His saying, Wash your faces. A group of scholars have used the Almighty’s saying, When you rise to prayer, wash your faces, as evidence for the necessity of intention in ablution, because the meaning of the words, When you rise to prayer, wash your faces, is for it, just as the Arabs say, If you see the emir, stand up, meaning for him. It is proven in the two Sahihs that the hadith Actions are by intentions, and each person will have only what he intended. It is recommended before washing the face to mention the name of God the Most High over his ablution, as it was reported in the hadith through good chains of transmission on the authority of a group of the Companions, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: There is no ablution for the one who does not mention the name of God over it. It is recommended to wash his hands before putting them in the vessel, and this is emphasized when getting up from sleep, as it was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When one of you wakes up from his sleep, he should not put his hand in the vessel before washing it three times, because one of you does not know where his hand has been. The definition of the face according to the jurists is between the hairline of the head, and baldness and gray hair are not considered, up to the end of the beard and chin in length, and from ear to ear in width. There is a difference of opinion regarding the two tendrils and the deletion: Are they part of the head or the face? And regarding the one who is extending from the beard about the place of obligation, there are two opinions one of them that it is obligatory to pour water over it because it is facing. It was narrated in a hadith that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man covering his beard, so he said, Uncover it, for the beard is part of the face. Mujahid said: It is part of the face. Haven’t you heard the Arabs say about a young man: When his beard grows, his face will appear? It is recommended for the person performing ablution to comb his beard if it is thick. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Isra’il told us, on the authority of Amir ibn Hamza, on the authority of Shaqiq, who said: I saw Uthman performing ablution, and he mentioned the hadith. He said: He combed his beard three times when he washed his face, then he said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do what you have seen me do. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq, and al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih, and al-Bukhari classed it as hasan. Abu Dawud said: Abu Tobah al-Rabi’ ibn Nafi’ narrated to us, Abu al-Malih narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Zoran narrated to us, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, he would take a handful of water and put it under his chin, combing his beard with it, and he would say, This is how my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, has commanded me. Abu Dawud is the only one to narrate it. This version has been narrated from Anas through more than one chain of transmission. Al-Bayhaqi said: We have narrated about combing the beard from Ammar, Aisha, and Umm Salamah, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then from Ali and others. We have narrated about the permission to leave it, from Ibn Umar and al-Hasan ibn Ali, then from al-Nakha’i and a group of the Tabi’un. It has been proven from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, through more than one chain of transmission in the Sahihs and other books that when he performed ablution, he would rinse his mouth and nose. The imams differed on whether they are obligatory in ablution and ritual washing, as is the view of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may God have mercy on him, or recommended in them, as is the view of al-Shafi’i and Malik, because of what is proven in the hadith narrated by the people of knowledge. Sunan, and Ibn Khuzaymah authenticated it on the authority of Rifa’ah ibn Rafi’ al-Zarqi that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: For the one who prays incorrectly, Perform ablution as God has commanded you. Or they are obligatory in washing but not ablution, as is the view of Abu Hanifa, or it is obligatory to sniff water up the nose but not to rinse the mouth, as is narrated on the authority of Imam Ahmad, because it is proven in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Whoever performs ablution should sniff water up the nose, and in another narration, If one of you performs ablution, let him put water in his nostrils and then blow it out. Sniffing is exaggerating in sniffing water up the nose. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Salamah Al-Khuza’i told us, Sulayman bin Bilal told us, on the authority of Zayd bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he performed ablution and washed his face. He took a handful of water and rinsed his mouth and nose with it, then he took a handful and did this, meaning he added it to his other hand, and washed his face with it. Then he took a handful of water and washed his right hand with it, then he took a handful of water and washed his left hand with it, then he wiped his head. Then he took a handful of water and sprinkled it on his right foot until he washed it, then he took a handful of water and washed his left foot with it, then he said: This is how I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performing ablution. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdul Rahim on the authority of Abu Salamah Mansur bin Salamah Al-Khuza’i on his authority. And his saying, and your hands up to the elbows, meaning with the elbows, as God Almighty said, “And do not consume their wealth along with your wealth. Indeed, it is a great sin.” Al-Hafiz Al-Daraqutni and Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqil, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, he would pour water over his elbows. However, this Al-Qasim is an abandoned hadith narrator, and his grandfather is weak, and God knows best. It is recommended for the person performing ablution to start with the upper arm and wash it along with his forearms, based on what Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from the hadith of Na’im Al-Mujmir, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My nation will be called on the Day of Resurrection with radiant limbs and radiant faces from the traces of ablution. So whoever among you can lengthen his radiance, let him do so.” And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Khalaf bin Khalifa, on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Ashja’i, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: I heard my close friend, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The adornment of the believer reaches where the ablution reaches. And the Almighty’s statement: And wipe over your heads, they differed concerning this baa: Is it for adhesion? Which is more apparent, or for partiality? And there is consideration in it, according to two opinions. Among the scholars of the principles of jurisprudence, there are those who said: This is general, so let it be referred to the Sunnah for its explanation.
