It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Malik on the authority of Amr ibn Yahya al-Mazini, on the authority of his father, that a man said to Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn Asim, who was the grandfather of Amr ibn Yahya, and was one of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Can you show me how the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to perform ablution? Abdullah ibn Zayd said: Yes. So he called for water for ablution and poured it over his hands. He washed his hands twice, then rinsed his mouth and nose three times, washed his face three times, then washed his hands twice up to the elbows, then wiped his head with his hands, moving them forward and backward, starting with the front of his head, then moving them to the back of his neck, then bringing them back until he returned to the place where he started, then washed his feet. And in the hadith of Abd al-Khayr on the authority of Ali regarding the description of the ablution of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar to this, and Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Muawiyah and al-Miqdad ibn Ma’dikarib regarding the description of the ablution of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. So in these hadiths there is evidence for those who hold that it is obligatory to complete wiping the entire head, as is the doctrine of Imam Malik and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, especially according to the opinion of those who claim that it was taken as a statement of what was generalized in the Qur’an. The Hanafis held that wiping a quarter of the head, which is the length of the forelock, is obligatory. Our companions held that only what is called wiping is obligatory and that it is not determined by a limit. Rather, if he wipes some hair from his head, it is sufficient for him. Both groups provided evidence for this with the hadith of Al-Mughira bin Shu’ba, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stayed behind, so I stayed behind with him. When he had finished his need, he said: Do you have water with you? So I brought him a water-tool and he washed his hands and face, then he went to uncover his arms but the sleeve of the cloak became too tight, so he took his hands out from under the cloak and threw the cloak over his shoulders, washed his arms and wiped his forehead, his turban and his socks, and mentioned the rest of the hadith which is in Sahih Muslim and others. The companions of Imam Ahmad said to them: He only wiped the forehead because he completed wiping the rest of the head over the turban, and we say that and that it is permissible in the place, as many hadiths have been reported about that and that he used to wipe over the turban and over the socks, so this is more appropriate, and you do not have in it evidence that it is permissible to limit oneself to wiping the forehead or part of the head without completing it over the turban, and God knows best. Then they differed as to whether it is recommended to repeat wiping the head three times, as is well-known in the Shafi’i school of thought, or is it recommended to wipe it once, as is the school of thought of Ahmad ibn Hanbal and those who followed him, according to two opinions. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yazid al-Laythi, on the authority of Hamran ibn Abaan, who said: I saw Uthman ibn Affan perform ablution, so he poured water over his hands three times, then washed them, then rinsed his mouth and nose, then washed his face three times, then washed his right hand up to the elbow three times, then washed his left hand like that, then wiped his head, then washed his right foot three times, then his left foot three times like that, then said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution similar to my ablution, then he said: Whoever performs ablution similar to my ablution, then prays two rak’ahs in which he does not think about anything, his previous sins will be forgiven. Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim in the two Sahihs on the authority of al-Zuhri, similar to this. In Sunan Abi Dawood, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaidullah bin Abi Malekah, on the authority of Uthman, regarding the description of ablution: And he wiped his head once. And likewise on the authority of Abd Khair on the authority of Ali, similarly. And those who recommended repeating the wiping of the head provided evidence for that by the generality of the hadith narrated by Muslim in his Sahih on the authority of Uthman, may God be pleased with him: That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution three times each. Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, al-Dahhak ibn Mukhallad told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Wardan told us, Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman told me, Hamran told me: I saw Uthman ibn Affan perform ablution and he mentioned something similar, but he did not mention rinsing the mouth and nose. He said: Then he wiped his head three times, then he washed his feet three times and then said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution like this, and he said: Whoever performs ablution like this, it will suffice him. Abu Dawud is the only one to narrate it. Then he said: The hadiths of Uthman in the Sahihs indicate that he wiped the head once. His saying, And your feet to the ankles. It was read, And your feet in the accusative case, in apposition to Wash your faces and your hands. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Abu Salamah told us, Wahib told us on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he read it and your feet, meaning: I returned to washing. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, Urwah, Ata’, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ibrahim, Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Az-Zuhri, and Ibrahim At-Taymi something similar to that. This is a clear reading of the obligation of washing, as the predecessors said. From here, those who went to the obligation of order in ablution went as is the doctrine of the majority, in contrast to Abu Hanifa, who did not stipulate order. Rather, if he washed his feet, then wiped his head, washed his hands, then his face, that would suffice him, because the verse commanded washing these limbs, and the waw does not indicate order. The majority followed different paths in answering this research. Some of them said: The verse indicated the obligation of washing the face initially when standing for prayer, because it is commanded by the fa of following, which requires order. None of the people said that washing the face is obligatory. First, then it is not necessary to arrange it after it, but there are two who say: one of them is that the arrangement is necessary as it is in the verse, and the other says: the arrangement is not necessary at all, and the verse indicated the necessity of washing the face first, so the arrangement is necessary in what comes after it by consensus where there is no difference. Some of them said: We do not accept that the waw does not indicate order, but rather it indicates it, as is the doctrine of a group of grammarians, linguists, and some jurists. Then we say that if we accept that it does not indicate order linguistically, it indicates order according to the Shari’ah in what is meant to be ordered. The evidence for that is that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, circumambulated the House, he exited from the door of Safa while reciting the words of God Almighty: Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God. Then he said: Begin with that with which God began. The wording of Muslim, and the wording of al-Nasa’i: Begin with that with which God began. This is the wording of a command, and its chain of transmission is sound. It indicates the obligation to begin with that with which God began, and this is the meaning of it indicating order according to the Shari’ah, and God knows best. Some of them said that when God Almighty mentioned this description in this verse in this order, He separated the similar from the similar, and included the one who was wiped among the two who were washed, this indicated the intention of order. Some of them said: There is no doubt that Abu Dawud and others narrated on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution once, then said, This is an ablution without which God does not accept prayer. They said: So it is either an orderly ablution, in which case order is required, or an unordered ablution, in which case order is not required, and no one says that, so what we mentioned is required. As for the other reading, which is the reading of those who read: and your feet in the accusative case, the Shiites used it as evidence in their statement that wiping the feet is obligatory, because they believe it is connected to wiping the head. It was narrated from a group of the Salaf what suggests the saying about wiping. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Hamid told us: Musa bin Anas said to Anas while we were with him: O Abu Hamza, Al-Hajjaj delivered a sermon to us in Ahwaz while we were with him, and he mentioned purification and said: Wash your faces and your hands, and wipe your heads and your feet, and nothing among the sons of Adam is closer to its filth than his feet, so wash their insides, their purity and their heels. Anas said: God spoke the truth and Al-Hajjaj lied. God Almighty said: And wipe over your heads and your feet. He said: Anas used to wet them when he wiped his feet, a sound chain of transmission to him. Ibn Jarir said: Ali bin Sahl told us, Muammil told us, Hammad told us, Asim Al-Ahwal told us on the authority of Anas, who said: The Qur’an was revealed about wiping and the Sunnah about washing, and this is also a sound chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Muhammad ibn Qays al-Khurasani told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Ablution is two washings and two wipings. Saeed ibn Abi Arooba narrated this on the authority of Qatada. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Muammar al-Manqari told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, Ali ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Yusuf ibn Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles. He said: It is wiping. Then he said: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, Alqamah, Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn Ali, and al-Hasan in one of the narrations, and Jabir ibn Zayd and Mujahid in one of the narrations, something similar to it. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub told us, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Ayoub told us: I saw Ikrimah wiping his feet. He said: He used to say that. Ibn Jarir said: Abu al-Sa’ib told me, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: Gabriel came down with the wiping. Then al-Sha’bi said: Don’t you see that tayammum is wiping what was washed and nullifying what was wiped? Ibn Abi Ziyad told us, Ismail told us: I said to Aamer: Some people say: Gabriel came down with the washing of the feet? He said: Gabriel came down with the wiping. These are very strange narrations, and they are based on the fact that what is meant by wiping is the light washing, as we will mention from the established Sunnah regarding the obligation of washing the feet. This reading in the accusative case came either for proximity and consistency of speech, as in the Arabs’ saying: A ruined lizard’s stone, and like the Almighty’s saying: Upon them will be green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade. This is widespread and accepted in the language of the Arabs. Some of them said: It is based on wiping the feet if they are wearing socks. This was said by Abu Abdullah Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him. Some of them said that it indicates wiping the feet, but what is meant by that is the light washing as mentioned in the Sunnah. In any case, washing the feet is obligatory and necessary, according to the verse and the hadiths that we will mention. One of the best proofs that wiping refers to light washing is what Al-Hafiz Al-Bayhaqi narrated, where he said: Abu Ali Al-Rawzabadi told us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Hamuyah Al-Askari told us, Ja’far bin Muhammad Al-Qalanisi told us, Adam told us, Shu’bah told us, Abdul Malik bin Maysarah told us, I heard Al-Nazzal bin Sabra narrating on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib that he prayed the noon prayer, then sat in the square of Kufa to attend to the needs of the people until the afternoon prayer came, then he brought a jug of water and took a handful of it, and wiped his face, hands, head and feet with it, then he stood up and drank the rest while standing, then he said: Some people dislike drinking while standing, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did as I did, and said: This is the ablution of one who has not broken his ablution. Narrated by Al-Bukhari in Sahih on the authority of Adam with some meaning. Whoever among the Shiites obligated wiping them as one wipes the socks has gone astray and led others astray. Likewise, whoever permitted wiping them and permitted washing them has also made a mistake. Whoever transmitted from Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir that he obligated washing them because of the hadiths, and obligated wiping them because of the verse, did not verify his doctrine in that, for his words in his interpretation only indicate that he meant that it is obligatory to rub the feet without the rest of the limbs of ablution, because they are in contact with the ground and mud and other things, so he obligated rubbing them in order to remove what is on them, but he expressed rubbing as wiping, so whoever did not contemplate his words believed that he meant the obligation to combine washing the feet and wiping them, so whoever narrated it narrated it in this way, and for this reason many of the jurists find it difficult and he is excused, for there is no meaning to combining wiping and washing, whether it precedes or comes after it because it is included in it, but the man meant what I mentioned, and God knows best. Then I contemplated his words also and I saw that he was trying to combine the two readings in his saying and your feet in the accusative case for wiping, which is rubbing, and in the accusative case for washing, so he obligated them both, taking Combining these and these. Mentioning the hadiths that were reported about washing the feet and that it is necessary The hadith of the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman, Ali, Ibn Abbas, Muawiyah, Abdullah bin Zaid bin Asim, and Al-Miqdad bin Ma’dikarib has been presented, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, washed his feet in his ablution either once, twice, or three times, according to the differences in their narrations. And in the hadith of Amr bin Shu’aib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution and washed his feet, then said, This is an ablution without which God does not accept prayer. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Uwanah, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Yusuf bin Mahak, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was left behind on a journey we took, and he caught up with us and the prayer, the afternoon prayer, had exhausted us, and we were performing ablution, so we began to wipe over our feet, and he called out at the top of his voice, Perform ablution thoroughly, woe to the heels from the Fire. And it is also in the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Aishah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, Perform ablution thoroughly, woe to the heels from the Fire. And Al-Layth bin Sa’d narrated on the authority of Haywah bin Shuraih, on the authority of Uqbah bin Muslim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith bin Haraz that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, Woe to the heels and the soles of the feet from the Fire. Narrated by Al-Bayhaqi and Al-Hakim, and this is a sahih chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, that he heard Sa`id ibn Abi Karb or Shu`ayb ibn Abi Karb say: I heard Jabir ibn `Abdullah, while he was on a mountain, say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Woe to the heels from the Fire. And Aswad ibn `Amir told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Abi Karb, on the authority of Jabir ibn `Abdullah, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man with a mark the size of a dirham that he had not washed, so he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire. And Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Sa`id, with a similar wording. And Ibn Jarir narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri, Shu’bah ibn al-Hajjaj and others, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi’i, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abi Karb, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly. Then he said: Ali ibn Muslim told us, Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith told us, Hafs told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw some people performing ablution but the water did not reach their heels, so he said, Woe to the heels from the Fire. Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf bin Al-Walid told us, Ayoub bin Uqbah told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Mu’aqib, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the heels from the Fire. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Ibn Jarir said: Ali bin Abdul A’la told me, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Mutrah bin Yazid, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Zahr, on the authority of Ali bin Yazid, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to the heels from the Fire. He said: There was no noble or lowly person left in the mosque except that I saw him turning his heels, looking at them. Abu Kurayb told us, Husayn told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Laith, Abd al-Rahman bin Sabit told me, on the authority of Abu Umamah or on the brother of Abu Umamah: That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw some people praying, and on the heel of one of them or the ankle of one of them there was something like the size of a dirham or the size of a fingernail that had not been touched by water, so he said: Woe to the heels from the Fire. He said: So if a man saw something on his heel that had not been touched by water, he would repeat his ablution. The evidence from these hadiths is clear, and that is that if it were obligatory to wipe the feet, or that it was permissible to do so, then he would not have been threatened for not doing so, because wiping does not include the entire foot, rather what applies to wiping the sock applies to it. This is how this evidence is presented to the Shiites by Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him. Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of `Umar ibn al-Khattab: A man performed ablution and left out a place the size of a fingernail on his foot, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him and said, Go back and perform your ablution well. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz informed us, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Ya’qub informed us, Muhammad bin Ishaq Al-San’ani informed us, Harun bin Maruf informed us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Jarir bin Hazim informed us that he heard Qatada bin Di’amah say: Anas bin Malik informed us that a man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, after performing ablution and leaving a spot the size of a fingernail on his foot. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him, Go back and perform your ablution properly. This is how Abu Dawud narrated it from Harun bin Maruf and Ibn Majah from Harmalah bin Yahya, both from Ibn Wahb with it. This is a good chain of transmission, all of its men are trustworthy. However, Abu Dawud said: This hadith is not well-known, only Ibn Wahb narrated it. Musa bin Ismail informed us, Hammad informed us, Yunus and Hamid informed us from Al-Hasan: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, in the same sense as the hadith of Qatada. Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim bin Abi Al-Abbas told us, Baqiyah told us, Yahya bin Saad told me, on the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan, on the authority of one of the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: He saw a man praying, and on the back of his foot there was a spot the size of a dirham that the water had not reached, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to repeat the ablution. Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Baqiyah, and he added: and the prayer. This is a good, strong, authentic chain of transmission, and God knows best. In the hadith of Hamran on the authority of Uthman regarding the description of the Prophet’s ablution, may God bless him and grant him peace, he interlocked his fingers. The people of Sunnah narrated from the hadith of Ismail bin Katheer on the authority of Asim bin Laqeet bin Sabra, on the authority of his father, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, tell me about ablution. He said: Perform ablution thoroughly, interlock your fingers, and be thorough in rinsing your nose, unless you are fasting. Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Yazid Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Muqri narrated to us, Akram bin Ammar narrated to us, Shaddad bin Abdullah Al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Abu Umamah narrated to us, Amr bin Abasa narrated to us, he said: I said: O Messenger of God, tell me about ablution. He said: “There is none among you who performs ablution, then rinses his mouth, sniffs water in his nose, and blows it out except that his sins will come out of his mouth and nostrils, along with the water when he blows it out. Then he washes his face as God has commanded him, except that the sins of his face will come out from the edges of his beard with the water. Then he washes his hands up to the elbows, except that the sins of his hands will fall out from the tips of his fingers. Then he wipes his head, except that the sins of his head will fall out from the ends of his hair with the water. Then he washes his feet up to the ankles as God has commanded him, except that the sins of his feet will fall out from the tips of his fingers with the water. Then he stands and praises God and extols Him as He deserves, then he bows two rak’ahs, except that he will emerge from his sins as on the day his mother bore him.” Abu Umamah said: O Amr, think about what you are saying. I heard this from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Will this man be given everything in his position? Amr ibn Abasa said: O Abu Umamah, I have grown old, my bones have become weak, and my end is near. I have no need to lie about God and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, if I had only heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, once, twice, or three times. I heard it seven times or more than that. This is a sound chain of transmission. It is in Sahih Muslim from another chain of transmission, and in it: Then he washes his feet as God commanded him, so this indicates that the Qur’an commands washing. And thus Abu Ishaq al-Sabi’i narrated on the authority of al-Harith, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Wash the feet up to the ankles as you have been commanded, and from here it becomes clear to you what is meant by the hadith of Abd al-Khayr on the authority of Ali that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sprinkled water on his feet while they were in their shoes, and rubbed them, but he only meant a light washing while they were in their shoes, and there is nothing wrong with performing the washing while the foot is in its shoes, but in this there is a response to those who delve too deeply and are too extreme among the obsessive. And thus the hadith which Ibn Jarir narrated on his own authority, and it is from his narration on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to the courtyard of a people, and urinated while standing, then he called for water, performed ablution and wiped over his shoes. It is a sound hadith, and Ibn Jarir responded to it by saying that the trustworthy preservers of hadith narrated it on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: So he urinated while standing, then he performed ablution and wiped over his socks. I said: It is possible to combine the two, that he had socks on his feet and sandals on them. And thus the hadith which Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated: Yahya told us on the authority of Shu’bah, Ya’la told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aws ibn Abi Aws, who said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution and wipe over his shoes, then he stood up to pray. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Musaddad and Ibad bin Musa, both on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ya`la bin Ata`, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aws bin Abi Aws, who said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, come to the courtyard of a people, urinate, perform ablution, and wipe over his shoes and feet. Ibn Jarir narrated it through Shu’bah and through Hisham, then he said: This is based on the fact that he performed ablution in this way and he was not in a state of ritual impurity, since it is not permissible for the obligations of God and the Sunnahs of His Messenger to be contradictory and conflicting. It has been authentically reported from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he ordered the general washing of the feet in ablution with water, by a widespread transmission that is conclusive and an excuse for whoever reached it and received it. Since the Qur’an commands the washing of the feet, as in the accusative reading, and as is obligatory in interpreting the genitive reading as such, some of the Salaf thought that this verse abrogates the permission to wipe over the socks. This has been narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, but its chain of transmission is not authentic, and what is proven from him is the opposite, and it is not as they claimed, since it has been proven that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wiped over the socks after the revelation of this noble verse. Imam Ahmad said: Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, Ziyad bin Abdullah bin Alatha told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim bin Malik Al-Jazari, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Jarir bin Abdullah Al-Bajali, who said: I converted to Islam after the revelation of Al-Ma’idah, and I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wiping after I converted to Islam. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Hammam, he said: Jarir urinated, then performed ablution and wiped over his socks. It was said: Do you do this? He said: Yes, I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, urinate, then performed ablution and wiped over his socks. Al-A’mash said: Ibrahim said: So they were amazed by this hadith because Jarir converted to Islam after the revelation of Al-Ma’idah. The wording of Muslim. It has been proven by continuous chain of transmission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that wiping over the socks is permissible, in word and deed, as is stated in the book Al-Ahkam Al-Kabir, along with what needs to be mentioned there about the timing of wiping or not, or the details thereof, as is explained in detail in its place. The Rafidis have disagreed with this without any evidence, but rather out of ignorance and misguidance, even though it is proven in Sahih Muslim from the narration of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, as it is proven in the two Sahihs from him from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the prohibition of temporary marriage, although they consider it permissible. Likewise, this noble verse indicates the obligation of washing the feet, along with what has been proven by continuous transmission of the action of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in accordance with what this noble verse indicates. They disagree with all of this and do not have a sound evidence in the matter itself, praise be to God. Thus, they disagreed with the imams and the predecessors regarding the two heels on the feet, for they believe that they are on the back of the foot, so they believe that there is a heel on each foot, and the majority believe that the two heels are the two protruding bones at the joint of the leg and the foot. Al-Rabi’ said: Al-Shafi’i said: I do not know of anyone who disagrees that the two heels that God mentioned in His Book regarding ablution are the two protruding ones, and they are the joint of the shin and the foot. This is his wording. According to the imams, may God have mercy on them: On each foot are two heels, as is well-known among the people, and as indicated by the Sunnah. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Hamran, on the authority of Uthman, he performed ablution and washed his right foot up to the ankles, and the left likewise. Al-Bukhari narrated a definitive comment, as did Abu Dawud and Ibn Khuzaymah in his Sahih, on the authority of Abu al-Qasim al-Husayni ibn al-Harith al-Jadali, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned to us and said, Straighten your rows three times. By God, you must straighten your rows, or God will cause discord among your hearts. He said: I saw a man sticking his heel to the heel of his companion, his knee to the knee of his companion, and his shoulder to his shoulder. This is the wording of Ibn Khuzaymah. It is not possible for his heel to stick to the heel of his companion, except that what is meant by it is the protruding bone in the leg until it is level with the heel of the other. This indicates what we mentioned, that they are the two protruding bones at the joint of the leg and the foot, as is the doctrine of the people of the Sunnah. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ismail ibn Musa told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, meaning al-Khabar, who said: I looked at the dead of Zayd’s companions, and I found the heel above the back of the foot. This is a punishment with which the Shi’a were punished after they were killed, as a form of humiliation. And the Almighty said: And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the relieving himself or you have contacted women and you find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it. All of that has been discussed previously in the interpretation of the verse of women, so there is no need for us to repeat it so as not to make the discussion too long. We have already mentioned the reason for the revelation of the verse of tayammum there, but Al-Bukhari narrated here a hadith specifically for this noble verse, so he said: Yahya bin Sulayman told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr bin Al-Harith told me that Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Qasim told him on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, who said: My necklace fell in Al-Baida’ while we were entering Madinah, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped and dismounted, and bent his head in my lap while sleeping, so Abu Bakr came and gave me a strong shove and said: You have detained the people with a necklace, so I wished for death because of the position of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with me, and it hurt me, then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, woke up, and the dawn prayer came. He looked for water but could not find it, so the verse was revealed: O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces until the end of the verse. Asid bin Al-Hudayr said: God has blessed the people in you, O family of Abu Bakr. You are nothing but a blessing to them. And the Almighty said: God does not want to make any difficulty for you meaning that is why He made it easy and simple for you and did not make it difficult. Rather, He permitted tayammum when sick and when there is no water, as an expansion for you and a mercy to you, and He made it for those for whom it was prescribed to take the place of water, except in some ways, as was explained above, and as is established in the Book of Great Rulings. And the Almighty said: But He intends to purify you and to complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful meaning that you may be grateful for His favors upon you in what He prescribed for you of expansion, compassion, mercy, facilitation, and tolerance. The Sunnah has been reported urging supplication after ablution that the one who does it be made among those who purify themselves and enter into compliance with this noble verse, as narrated by Imam Ahmad, Muslim, and the people of the Sunnah on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir, who said: We were in charge of tending camels, and my turn came, so I went to them in the evening, and I found the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, standing and talking to the people, and I realized from his saying: There is no Muslim who performs ablution and does it well, then stands and prays two rak’ahs facing them. “With his heart and face, except that Paradise is obligatory for him.” He said: I said: How good this is! Then a speaker came before me saying: The one before it is better than it. So I looked and it was Umar, may God be pleased with him, and he said: I saw you come just now. He said: “There is none among you who performs ablution and completes it or perfects it, saying: I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, except that the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him, and he enters from whichever one he wishes.” The wording of Muslim. Malik narrated on the authority of Nahshal ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When a Muslim or believing slave performs ablution and washes his face, every sin he looked at with his eyes will come out of his face with the water or with the last drop of water. When he washes his hands, every sin his hands committed will come out of his hands with the water or with the last drop of water. When he washes his feet, every sin his feet walked on will come out with the water or with the last drop of water, until he comes out pure of sins.” Narrated by Muslim on the authority of Abu al-Tahir, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Malik, on his authority. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Muawiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of Ka`b ibn Murrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no man who performs ablution and washes his hands or arms, except that his sins come out of them. When he washes his face, his sins come out of his face. When he wipes his head, his sins come out of his head. When he washes his feet, his sins come out of his feet.” This is the wording. Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ja`far, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Murrah ibn Ka`b or Ka`b ibn Murrah al-Sulami, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When a servant performs ablution and washes his hands, his sins come out from in front of him. When he washes his face, his sins come out from his face. When he washes his arms, his sins come out from his arms. When he washes his feet, his sins come out from his feet.” Shu`bah said: He did not mention wiping the head, and this is a sound chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Shammar ibn Atiyah on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab on the authority of Abu Umamah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever performs ablution and does it well, then stands up to pray, his sins will be removed from his hearing, sight, hands and feet. Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer on the authority of Zayd ibn Salam on the authority of his grandfather Mamtur on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash’ari that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Purity is half of faith, and ‘al-Hamdulillah’ fills the scale, and ‘Subhan God’ and ‘God is Great’ fills what is between heaven and earth, and fasting is a shield, and patience is light, and charity is proof, and the Qur’an is an argument for or against you. Every person goes forth in the morning selling his soul, either freeing it or destroying it.” In Sahih Muslim on the authority of Samak ibn Harb on the authority of Mus’ab ibn Sa’d on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God does not accept charity from ill-gotten gains, nor does He accept prayer without purification. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu’bah told us on the authority of Qatadah, I heard Abu al-Malih al-Hudhali narrating on the authority of his father, he said: I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a house and I heard him say: God does not accept a prayer without purification, nor charity from stolen property. And this is how Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Shu’bah.
5:7: God Almighty says, reminding His believing servants of His blessings upon them in His law for them of this great religion. And sending them this noble Messenger and what he took from them of the covenant and pledge in pledging allegiance to him to follow him, support him and assist him, and to carry out his religion and convey it from him, and to accept it from him, so God Almighty said: And remember the favor of God upon you and His covenant which He bound you with when you said, “We hear and obey.” This is the pledge that they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, upon their conversion to Islam, as they said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pledged us to hear and obey in our ease and our difficulty and in giving preference to us, and that we would not dispute the matter with those in authority. God Almighty said: And what is the matter with you that you do not believe in God while the Messenger calls you to believe in your Lord and He has taken your covenant, if you are believers. It was said: This is a reminder to the Jews of what he took from them of covenants and pledges to follow Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and submit to his law, narrated by Ali bin Abi Talha on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said: It is a reminder of what God Almighty took from the descendants of Adam when He extracted them from his loins and made them testify about themselves, Am I not your Lord? They said, Yes, we testify. This was said by Mujahid and Muqatil bin Hayyan. The first statement is more apparent, and it is what was narrated from Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Then God the Almighty said: And fear God as an emphasis and encouragement to persevere in piety in every situation. Then He informed them that He knows what is in the hearts of secrets and thoughts, so He said: Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts. And the Almighty said: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for God meaning be persistently standing firm for the sake of God the Almighty, not for the sake of people and reputation, and be witnesses with justice meaning with fairness and not with injustice. It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of An-Nu’man ibn Bashir that he said: My father gave me a gift, so my mother, Amrah bint Rawahah, said: I will not be satisfied until you have the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, bear witness to it. So he came to him to have him bear witness to my charity, so he said: Have you given the like of it to all of your children? He said: No. So He said: Fear God and be just with your children. And he said: I do not bear witness to injustice. He said: So my father returned and returned that charity. And the Almighty said: And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. That is, do not let the hatred of a people lead you to abandon justice towards them. Rather, practice justice towards everyone, whether they are friends or enemies. For this reason, He said: Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. That is, your justice is nearer to righteousness than abandoning it. The verb indicates the source to which the pronoun refers, as in its counterparts in the Qur’an and elsewhere, as in His statement: And if you are told, ‘Go back,’ then go back; that is purer for you. And his saying: It is closer to piety from the aspect of using the comparative in a place where there is nothing on the other side of it, as in the saying of the Most High: The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be better in settlement and better in resting place. And like the saying of some of the female companions to Omar: You are ruder and harsher than the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then the Most High said: “And fear God. Indeed, God is Acquainted with what you do.” That is, He will reward you for what He knows of your actions that you have done, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. For this reason, He said after it: God has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness for them, that is, for their sins, and a great reward, which is Paradise, which is from His mercy to His servants. They do not attain it through their actions, but through His mercy and grace. Even though the reason for the mercy reaching them is their actions, He, the Most High, is the One who made them reasons for attaining His mercy, grace, pardon, and pleasure. So all is from Him and for Him, so to Him be praise and thanks. Then He said: And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs - those are the companions of Hellfire. This is from His justice, wisdom and judgment in which He does not act unjustly, rather He is the just, wise, and powerful judgment. And the Almighty said: O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when a people intended to stretch out their hands against you, but He withheld their hands from you. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of al-Zuhri, he mentioned it on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Jabir: That the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped at a place, and the people dispersed among the wild trees to seek shade under them, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, hung his weapon on a tree, and a Bedouin came to the sword of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it and drew it, then he turned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Who can protect you from me? He said: God Almighty. The Bedouin said, two or three times: Who can protect you from me? And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God. He said: The Bedouin drew the sword, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called his companions and told them the story of the Bedouin, while he was sitting next to him, and he did not punish him. Muammar said: Qatada used to mention something like this, and he mentioned that some Arabs wanted to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they sent this Bedouin, and he interpreted Remember the favor of God upon you when a people intended to stretch out their hands against you the verse, and the story of this Bedouin, who is Ghawrath bin Al-Harith, is established in the Sahih. Al-Awfi said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse: O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when a people intended to extend their hands against you, but He withheld their hands from you. That is because a group of Jews prepared food for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions in order to kill them, so God revealed to him about them, but he did not bring the food and ordered his companions to bring it. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Abu Malik said: It was revealed about Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf and his companions when they intended to betray Muhammad and his companions in the house of Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar, Mujahid, Ikrimah and others mentioned that it was revealed regarding Banu Nadir when they wanted to throw a millstone on the head of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), when he came to them seeking their help in the blood money of the two ‘Amiris. They assigned Amr bin Jahash bin Ka’b to do that, and they ordered him to throw that millstone from above if the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sat under the wall and they gathered around him. God revealed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) what they had conspired to do, so he returned to Medina and his companions followed him, so God revealed this verse regarding that. God the Almighty said: And upon God let the believers put their trust meaning whoever puts his trust in God, God will suffice him in what concerns him, and will protect him from the evil of the people and safeguard him. Then He ordered the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to go to them, so he besieged them until he brought them down and expelled them.

5:12: When God Almighty commanded His believing servants to fulfill His covenant and pledge that He took from them through the tongue of His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and commanded them to stand up for the truth and bear witness to justice, and reminded them of His apparent and hidden blessings upon them in what He guided them to of truth and guidance, He began to explain to them how He took covenants and pledges from those who came before them from the People of the Book: the Jews and the Christians. So when they broke His covenants and pledges, He followed that with a curse from Him upon them, and expulsion from His door and His side, and a veil over their hearts from reaching guidance and the religion of truth, which is beneficial knowledge and righteous deeds. So God Almighty said: And God had already taken a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We raised from among them twelve leaders, meaning leaders over their tribes to pledge allegiance and to listen and obey God, His Messenger, and His Book. Ibn Abbas mentioned on the authority of Ibn Ishaq and more than one that this was when Moses, peace be upon him, set out to fight the tyrants, so he was commanded to establish From each tribe there was a chief. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: From the tribe of Reuben was Shamon the son of Reckon, and from the tribe of Simeon was Shaphat the son of Hari, and from the tribe of Judah was Caleb the son of Jophun, and from the tribe of Atin was Michael the son of Joseph, and from the tribe of Joseph, which is the tribe of Ephraim, was Joshua the son of Nun, and from the tribe of Benjamin was Paltham the son of Daphon, and from the tribe of Zebulun was Gidi the son of Shura, and from the tribe of Manasseh the son of Joseph was Gidi the son of Moses, and from the tribe of Dan was Camalel the son of Hamal, and from the tribe of Asher Sathor the son of Malkiel, and from the tribe of Naphtali was Bahr the son of Waksi, and from the tribe of Issachar was Lael the son of Maked. I saw in the fourth book of the Torah the enumeration of the captains over the tribes of the children of Israel and names different from what Ibn Ishaq mentioned, and God knows best. He said in it: Over the children of Reuben was Eliezer son of Sadon, over the children of Simeon was Shemual son of Zurishki, over the children of Judah was Al-Hashun son of Ammiadab, over the children of Issachar was Sheal son of Zaon, over the children of Zebulun was Eliab son of Halub, over the children of Ephraim was Manasseh son of Amnhur, over the children of Manasseh was Hamliel son of Jerzon, over the children of Benjamin was Abidan son of Gideon, over the children of Dan was Geider son of Ammishaddi, over the children of Asher was Nahael son of Ajran, over the children of Kan was El-Sief son of Dau'iel, and over the children of Naphtali was Agda son of Amminan. Thus, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pledged allegiance to the Ansar on the night of Aqaba, there were twelve leaders among them: three from the Aws: Asid ibn al-Hudayr, Sa`d ibn Khaythama, and Rafa`ah ibn `Abd al-Mundhir, and it is said that Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayhan, may God be pleased with him, replaced him, and nine from the Khazraj: Abu Umamah As`ad ibn Zura`ah, Sa`d ibn al-Rabi`, `Abdullah ibn Rawahah, Rafi` ibn Malik ibn al-`Ajlan, al-Bara` ibn Ma`rur, `Ubadah ibn al-Samit, Sa`d ibn `Ubadah, `Abdullah ibn `Amr ibn Haram, and al-Mundhir ibn `Umar ibn Hunaish, may God be pleased with them. Ka`b ibn Malik mentioned them in one of his poems, as Ibn Ishaq, may God have mercy on him, mentioned. 5:15: God the Almighty says, informing about His noble self that He sent His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with guidance and the religion of truth to all the people of the earth: Arabs and non-Arabs, illiterate and People of the Book, and that He sent him with clear proofs and the difference between truth and falsehood. So God the Almighty said: O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture and overlooking much. That is, He makes clear what they have changed, distorted, and interpreted, and fabricated against God in it, and He is silent about much of what they have changed and there is no benefit in explaining it. Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Al-Husayn bin Waqid from Yazid Al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: Whoever disbelieves in stoning has disbelieved in the Qur’an without expecting it. His saying: O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture. So stoning was among what they concealed. Then he said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, and they did not include it. Then God Almighty informed us about the great Qur’an that He revealed to His noble Prophet, saying, “There has come to you from God a light and a clear Book. With it God guides those who pursue His pleasure to the ways of peace,” meaning the paths of salvation and safety and the paths of righteousness, and brings them out from darkness into the light by His permission and guides them to a straight path, meaning He saves them from destruction, and makes clear to them the clearest paths, thus turning away from them what is forbidden, and obtaining for them the most beloved of things, and removing from them misguidance, and guiding them to the most upright state.

5:17: God Almighty says, informing and narrating the disbelief of the Christians in their claim that the Messiah, son of Mary, who is a servant of God and a creation of His creation, is God. God is far above what they say, far above. Then He says, informing about His ability to do things and that they are under His control and authority, “Say: Who has any power over God if He willed to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on the earth?” That is, if He wanted that, who would have prevented Him from doing so or who would have the power to divert Him from doing so? Then He says, “And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills.” That is, all existence is His dominion and His creation, and He is able to do whatever He wills. He is not questioned about what He does by His ability, authority, justice, and greatness. This is a response to the Christians, upon them be the curses of God that continue until the Day of Resurrection. Then God Almighty said, responding to the Jews and Christians in their lies and slander: And the Jews and Christians say, ‘We are the sons of God and His beloved,’ meaning, we are related to His prophets and they are His sons, and He cares for us and He loves us. They narrated from their book that God Almighty said to His servant Israel: You are My firstborn son. They interpreted this in a way other than its meaning and distorted it. More than one of their wise men who converted to Islam responded to them and said: This is used by them to mean honor and respect, just as the Christians narrated from their book that Jesus said to them: I am going to my father and your father, meaning my Lord and your Lord. It is known that they did not claim for themselves the prophethood that they claimed for Jesus, peace be upon him, but rather they wanted to gain their respect and favor with Him. For this reason they said: We are the sons of God and His beloved. God Almighty said, responding to them: Say, ‘Then why does He punish you for your sins?’ meaning, if you were as you claim, His sons and beloved, then why would He not have prepared for you the fire of Hell for your disbelief, lies, and slander? Some Sufi sheikhs said to some jurists: Where do you find in the Qur’an that the beloved does not punish his beloved? He did not respond to him, so the Sufi recited to him this verse: “Say: Then why does He punish you for your sins?” What he said is good, and there is evidence for it in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad where he said: Ibn Abi Uday told us on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by with a group of his companions, and there was a child on the road. When his mother saw the people, she feared that her child would be trampled on, so she came running and said: My son, my son. She ran and took him, and the people said: O Messenger of God, this woman would not throw her child into the fire. He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, protected them and said: No, by God, He will not throw His beloved into the Fire. Ahmad alone reported it. Rather, you are human beings among those He created. That is, you have an example like your peers among the children of Adam. He, glory be to Him, is the judge over all of His servants. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. That is, He does what He wills, and there is no objection to His judgment. He is swift to take account. And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them. That is, all of them are His dominion and are under His control and authority. And to Him is the final destination. That is, the return and destination to Him. So He judges His servants as He wills, and He is the Just One who does not act unjustly. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad on the authority of Ikrimah or Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Nu`man ibn Asa, Bahri ibn `Amr, and Shas ibn `Adi came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and spoke to him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke to them and called them to God and warned them of His wrath. They said: What are you frightening us with, O Muhammad? By God, we are the sons of God and His beloved, as the Christians say. So God revealed about them: And the Jews and the Christians say, ‘We are the sons of God and His beloved,’ to the end of the verse. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. They also narrated on the authority of Asbat on the authority of al-Suddi regarding God’s statement: And the Jews and the Christians say, ‘We are the sons of God and His beloved,’ as for their saying: We are the sons of God. They said: God revealed to Israel that your son is the firstborn of the children, so He will put them in the fire, and they will be in it for forty nights until He purifies them and consumes their sins. Then a caller will call out: Bring out every circumcised person from the children of Israel, so bring them out. That is what they said: The fire will not touch us except for a few days.

5:19: God the Almighty says, addressing the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, that He has sent to them His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the Seal of the Prophets, after whom there is no prophet or messenger, but he is the successor to all of them. That is why He said: After a period of messengers, meaning after a long period between his sending and Jesus, son of Mary. They differed about the length of this period, how long it was. Abu Uthman al-Nahdi and Qatadah said in a narration from him: It was six hundred years. Al-Bukhari narrated it from Salman al-Farsi, and from Qatadah: Five hundred and sixty years. Muammar said, from some of his companions: Five hundred and forty years. Al-Dahhak said: Four hundred and thirty-some years. Ibn Asakir mentioned in the biography of Jesus, peace be upon him, on the authority of al-Sha'bi that he said: From the ascension of Christ until the migration of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, nine hundred and thirty-three years, and the most famous opinion is the first opinion, which is that it was six hundred years. Some of them say: six hundred and twenty years, and there is no contradiction between them, because the first speaker meant six hundred solar years, and the other meant lunar years, and between every hundred solar years and the lunar years there are about three years, and for this reason the Almighty said in the story of the People of al-Kahf 18:And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and added nine, meaning lunar years to complete the three hundred solar years that were known to the People of the Book, and the period was between Jesus, son of Mary, the last of the prophets of the Children of Israel, and Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets from the Children of Adam, as proven in Sahih al-Bukhari on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people who are most deserving of the son of Mary are those who have no prophet between me and him. This is a response to those who claimed that a prophet was sent after Jesus, called Khalid ibn Sinan, as narrated by al-Quda’i and others. What is meant is that God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, during a period of time without messengers, and the obliteration of paths, and the change of religions, and the increase in the worship of idols, fires, and crosses, so the blessing of him was the most complete blessing, and the need for him was a matter of great importance. Generally speaking, corruption had spread throughout the country, and tyranny and ignorance had appeared among all the servants except for a few who adhered to the remnants of the religion of the ancient prophets, from some of the Jewish rabbis and the Christian and Sabian worshippers. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told us, Hisham told us, Qatada told us on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Iyad bin Hammad Al-Majashi’i, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon one day, and he said in his sermon: “And my Lord has commanded me to teach you what you do not know of what He has taught me on this day. All the wealth that I have given to My servants is lawful, and I have created all of My servants as monotheists, but the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, and prohibited for them what I had permitted for them, and commanded them to associate with Me that for which I had not sent down any authority. Then God Almighty looked at the people of the earth and hated them: their Arabs and their non-Arabs, except for a remnant of the Children of Israel, and said: I have only sent you to test you and to test you, and I have sent down to you a book that water cannot wash away, which you read while asleep and while awake. Then God commanded me to burn the Quraysh, so I said: O Lord, then they will cut off my head and call it a loaf of bread. He said: Extract them as they extracted you, and attack them.” We will attack you, and spend on them, and We will spend on you, and send an army, and We will send five times its size, and fight with those who obey you against those who disobey you. The people of Paradise are three: a just ruler, successful, and charitable; a merciful man who is tender-hearted toward all his relatives and Muslims; a chaste, poor man with dependents who gives charity. The people of Hell are five: the weak who has no religion; those who are among you followers or followers - Yahya doubted - who do not seek family or wealth; the traitor whose desires, no matter how small, are not hidden from him except that he betrays them; a man who does not wake up or go to bed except that he deceives you about your family and wealth. He mentioned the miser or the liar, and the obscene liar. Then Imam Ahmad, Muslim and al-Nasa’i narrated it from more than one chain of narration on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Mutraf ibn Abdullah ibn al-Shakheer. In the narration of Shu’bah on the authority of Qatadah, it is explicit that Qatadah heard this hadith from Mutraf. Imam Ahmad mentioned in his Musnad that Qatadah did not hear it from Mutraf, but rather heard it from four people on his authority. Then he narrated it on the authority of Ruh, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Hakim al-Athram, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: Mutraf told me on the authority of ‘Ayadh ibn Hammad, and he mentioned it. And al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Ghundar on the authority of Awf al-A’rabi on his authority. The purpose of citing this hadith is his saying: And God looked at the people of the earth and hated them, both their non-Arabs and their Arabs, except for the remnants of the Children of Israel. And in Muslim’s wording: From the People of the Book. And the religion had become confused for all the people of the earth until God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he guided the creation and God brought them out of darkness into the light, and left them on the white path and the pure Shari’ah. For this reason, God the Almighty said: lest you say, ‘No bearer of good tidings or warner has come to us.’ That is, lest you argue and say, O you who have changed and altered their religion, no messenger has come to us to bring good tidings and warn against evil. Indeed, a bearer of good tidings and a warner has come to you, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And God is over all things competent. Ibn Jarir said: Its meaning is that I am able to punish whoever disobeys Me and reward whoever obeys Me. And remember when Moses said to his people, "O my people, remember the favor of God upon you when He made among you prophets and made you kings and gave you that which He had not given to anyone else in the worlds. * O my people, enter the Holy Land which God has assigned to you and do not turn back [from the religion] and [thus] become losers. They said, O Moses, indeed within it is a people of tyrants, and we will never enter it until they leave it. But if they leave it, then we will enter. Two men from among those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favor, said, Enter upon them through the gate, and when you have entered it, you will be predominant. And upon God rely, if you should be believers. They said, O Moses, indeed we will never enter it as long as they are within it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we will remain right here. He said, My Lord, indeed I do not control except myself and my brother, so separate us from the defiantly disobedient people. He said, Indeed, it is forbidden to them for forty years while they wander throughout the land, so do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people." God the Almighty says, informing about His servant, messenger, and interlocutor, Moses, son of Imran, peace be upon him, in what he mentioned to his people of God’s blessings upon them and His favors upon them in gathering for them the best of this world and the next: If they had remained steadfast on their straight path, God the Almighty says: “And when Moses said to his people, ‘O my people, remember the favor of God upon you when He made among you prophets. ’” That is, whenever a prophet died, another prophet arose among you from your father Abraham to those after him. And thus the prophets continued to call to God and warn against His wrath until they were sealed with Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him. Then God revealed to the Seal of the Prophets and Messengers, Muhammad, son of Abdullah, who is attributed to Ishmael, son of Abraham, peace be upon him, and he is more honorable than all of those who came before him, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. And his saying, And made you kings, Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of al-Hakam or someone else, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his saying, And made you kings, he said: the servant, the woman, and the house. Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak from the hadith of al-Thawri also on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: the woman and the servant. And gave you that which He had not given to anyone in the worlds, he said: those who were among them at that time. Then al-Hakim said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it. Maymun ibn Mihran narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: If a man from the Children of Israel had a wife, a servant, and a house, he was called a king. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Abu Hani’ told us that he heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hanbali say: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-Aas, and a man asked him, saying: Are we not among the poor emigrants? Abdullah said: Do you have a wife to whom you can take refuge? He said: Yes. He said: Do you have a home to live in? He said: Yes. He said: Then you are one of the rich. He said: I have a servant. He said: Then you are one of the kings. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Is a king anything but a mount, a servant, and a house? Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Then something similar to this was narrated by Al-Hakam, Mujahid, Mansur, and Sufyan Al-Thawri. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Maymun bin Mihran. Ibn Shawdhab said: If a man from the Children of Israel had a house and a servant and was asked permission to enter, he was a king. Qatada said: They were the first to have servants. Al-Suddi said about his statement, And made you kings, he said: A man among you owns himself, his wealth, and his family. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Diraj, on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: When one of the Children of Israel had a servant, an animal, and a wife, he was written down as king. This is a strange hadith from this aspect. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Zubayr bin Bakkar told us, Abu Damrah Anas bin Ayyad told us, I heard Zaid bin Aslam say: And made you kings. I do not know except that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has a house and a servant is a king. This is a strange mursal. Malik said: A house, a servant, and a wife. It was mentioned in the hadith, Whoever among you wakes up healthy in his body, safe in his home, and has his daily sustenance, it is as if the entire world has been given to him. And His saying, And He has given you what He has not given to anyone in the worlds, means the scholars of your time, for they were the most honorable people of their time, among the Greeks, Copts, and all other kinds of the children of Adam, as He said, And We had certainly given the Children of Israel the Scripture and wisdom and prophethood, and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over the worlds, and the Most High said, informing about Moses when they said, Make for us a god as they have gods. He said, “Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly. Indeed, what these people are in is ruined, and what they have been doing is futile.” He said, Should I seek for you a god other than God, while He has preferred you over the worlds? What is meant is that they were the best of their time, otherwise this nation is more honorable than them, and better in the sight of God, and more perfect in law, and more upright in method, and more honorable in prophethood, and greater in kingdom, and more abundant in provisions, and more in wealth and children, and more extensive in kingdom, and more lasting in glory. God Almighty said: And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people. We have mentioned the successive hadiths about the virtue of this nation, its honor and its generosity with God when He Almighty said: You are the best nation produced for mankind from Surat Al Imran. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Abu Malik, and Saeed bin Jubair that they said about His statement, And He has given you what He has not given to anyone in the worlds, meaning the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So it is as if they intended that this address in His statement, And He has given you what He has not given to anyone, is to this nation. The majority are of the view that it is an address from Moses to his people, and it is understood to refer to the people of their time, as we have mentioned. It was said that what is meant is, And He has given you what He has not given to anyone in the worlds, meaning by that what God Almighty had sent down to them of manna and quails, and what He had shaded them with of clouds and other things that God Almighty had singled them out with of extraordinary things. And God knows best. Then the Almighty said, informing about Moses’s (peace be upon him) incitement of the Children of Israel to jihad and enter the Holy House, which was in their hands during the time of their father Jacob, when he and his sons and family traveled to the land of Egypt during the time of Joseph (peace be upon him). They remained there until they went out with Moses, and found there a people of the giant giants who had taken control of it and owned it. The Messenger of God, Moses (peace be upon him), ordered them to enter it and fight their enemies and gave them good report of victory and triumph over them, but they refused and disobeyed and disobeyed his command. They were punished by going into the wilderness and continuing their journey, confused and not knowing how to head towards a destination, for a period of forty years as punishment for their negligence in the command of God Almighty. Then the Almighty said, informing about Moses that he said: O my people, enter the Holy Land, meaning the purified one. Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Enter the Holy Land, he said: It is Mount Tur and what is around it. Mujahid and others said the same. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Baqqal, on the authority of `Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: It is Jericho. This was also mentioned on the authority of more than one of the commentators, and there is a consideration in this, because Jericho was not what was intended by the conquest, nor was it on their way to Jerusalem. They had come from the land of Egypt when God destroyed their enemy Pharaoh, unless what was meant by Jericho was the land of Jerusalem, as al-Suddi said in what Ibn Jarir narrated on his authority, and not that what was meant by it was this well-known town on the edge of the mountain to the east of Jerusalem. And the Almighty’s saying: Which God has ordained for you meaning which God promised you through your father Israel that it is the inheritance of those among you who believed, and do not turn back meaning do not refrain from jihad or you will become losers. They said, “O Moses, indeed within it is a people of tyrants, and we will never enter it until they leave it. But if they leave it, then we will enter.” That is, they made an excuse that in this town that you ordered us to enter and fight its people are a people of tyrants, meaning of formidable character and strong strength, and we are not able to resist them or confront them, and we cannot enter it as long as they are within it. So if they leave it, we will enter it, otherwise we will have no power over them. Ibn Jarir said: Abdul Karim bin Al-Haitham told me, Ibrahim bin Bashar told us, Sufyan told us, Abu Saeed said: Ikrimah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Moses was commanded to enter the city of the giants. He said: Moses and those with him went until they stopped near the city, which is Jericho, so he sent to them twelve spies, one from each tribe, to bring him report of the people. He said: So they entered the city and saw a great matter in their appearance, body and size, so they entered a garden belonging to one of them, so the owner of the garden came to pick the fruits from his garden, so he started picking the fruits and looking at their traces, so he followed them and whenever he found one of them he took him and put him in his sleeve with the fruit, until he picked up all twelve of them, so he put them in his sleeve with the fruit, and went with them to their king and scattered them before him, so the king said to them: You have seen our situation and our matter, so go and inform your master. He said: So they returned to Moses and told him what they had seen of their situation, and in this The chain of transmission is considered. Ali bin Abi Talha said: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, when Moses and his people descended, he sent twelve men from among them, and they were the leaders whom God mentioned. He sent them to bring him report of them. They set out and were met by a man from the tyrants, who put them in his cloak and carried them until he brought them to the city. He called out to his people and they gathered around him. They said, Who are you? They said: We are the people of Moses, we were sent to bring him report of you, so they gave them a grape that would suffice for a man, and they said to them: Go to Moses and his people, and tell them this is the size of their fruit, so they returned to Moses and told him what they saw, and when Moses, peace be upon him, ordered them to enter upon them and fight them, they said: O Moses, go you and your Lord and fight, we are sitting here, narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, then he said: My father told us, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, Yahya bin Ayoub told us, on the authority of Yazid bin al-Hadi, Yahya bin Abd al-Rahman told me, he said: I saw Anas bin Malik, he took his staff and measured with it something, I do not know how many, then he measured with it on the ground fifty or fifty-five, then he said: This is the height of the Amalekites, and many of the commentators have mentioned here report of the status of the Children of Israel in the greatness of the creation of these giants, and that among them was Og bin Anq, the son of the daughter of Adam, peace be upon him, and that his height was three thousand cubits and three hundred and thirty-three cubits A third of an arm, the liberation of the account, and this is something that is embarrassing to mention, then it is contrary to what was proven in the two Sahihs, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God created Adam and his height was sixty cubits, then creation continued to decrease until now. Then they mentioned that this man was a disbeliever, and that he was the son of fornication, and that he refused to board Noah’s ark, and that the flood did not reach his knee, and this is a lie and slander, for God the Most High mentioned that Noah called upon the people of the earth from the disbelievers, and he said: My Lord, do not leave on the earth from the disbelievers a single dweller. And God the Most High said: “So We saved him and those with him in the laden ark. Then We drowned after him the rest.” And God the Most High said: There is no protector this day from the decree of God except for him on whom He has mercy. And if the son of Noah, the disbeliever, drowned, then how could Awj bin Anq remain while he was a disbeliever and the son of fornication? This is not permissible in reason or law. Then there is a consideration regarding the existence of a man called Awj bin Anq, and God knows best. And the Almighty said: Two men from among those who feared, upon whom God had bestowed favor, said. That is, when the Children of Israel refused to obey God and follow the Messenger of God, Moses, peace and blessings be upon him, two men from among those who feared God’s command and dreaded His punishment, urged them on. Some of them read: Two men from among those who feared, that is, from those who had awe and a place among the people. It is said that they were Joshua bin Nun and Caleb bin Yuqana. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Atiyah, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and more than one of the early and later generations, may God have mercy on them, said: “Enter upon them through the gate, and when you have entered it, you will be victorious. And upon God rely, if you are believers.” That is, if you rely upon God, follow His command, and agree with His Messenger, God will grant you victory over your enemies, support you, and make you triumph over them, and you will enter the country that God has written for you.
