Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated from some of the scholars of the first book: that Adam ordered his son Cain to marry his twin sister, Abel, and ordered Abel to marry Cain’s twin sister, so Abel submitted to that and was satisfied, but Cain refused and hated it out of generosity towards Abel’s sister, and he desired his sister over Abel and said: We are from the birth of Paradise, and they are from the birth of the Earth, and I am more deserving of my sister. Some of the scholars of the first book say: Cain’s sister was one of the best people, so he was stingy with her towards his brother and wanted her for himself, and God knows best which of them it was, so his father said to him: O my son, she is not lawful for you, but Cain refused to accept that from his father’s words, his father said to him: O my son, offer a sacrifice and your brother Abel will offer a sacrifice, so whichever of you accepts his sacrifice is more deserving of it, and Cain was in charge of sowing the land, and Abel was in charge of tending the livestock, so Cain offered wheat and Abel offered firstborns from the firstborns of his sheep, and some of them said: He said: He offered a cow, so God sent a white fire that ate Abel’s offering and left Cain’s offering. Thus, he accepted the offering if he accepted it. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It was their nature that no poor person was to be given charity, but rather the offering was offered by a man. While the two sons of Adam were sitting, they said, If we offered an offering. When a man offered an offering and God was pleased with him, He would send a fire to him and consume him. If God was not pleased with him, the fire would go out. So they offered an offering, and one of them was a shepherd and the other was a farmer. The owner of the sheep offered the best and fattest of his sheep, and the other offered some of his crops. Then the fire came and descended between them and consumed the sheep and left the crops. The son of Adam said to his brother, Do you walk among the people and they know that you offered an offering and it was accepted from you and returned to me? No, by God, the people will not look at me, and you are better than me. He said, I will kill you. His brother said to him, What is my sin? God only accepts from the righteous. Narrated by Ibn Jarir, so this trace indicates that the offering was not for a reason or to avoid a woman, as was previously mentioned by a group of those mentioned, and it is apparent in the Qur’an: When they both offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them but not from the other, he said, ‘I will surely kill you.’ He said, ‘God only accepts from the righteous.’ So the context indicates that he was angry with him and envied him because his offering was accepted but not his. Then it is well-known among the majority that the one who offered the sheep was Abel and the one who offered the food was Qabil, and that the sheep was accepted from Abel, until Ibn Abbas and others said that it was the ram that was used to ransom the slaughtered animal, which is appropriate, and God knows best, and it was not accepted from Qabil. This is also what was stated by more than one of the early and later generations, and it is also well-known from Mujahid, but Ibn Jarir narrated from him that he said the one who offered the crops was Qabil, and it was accepted from him. This is contrary to the well-known view, and perhaps it was not well-recorded from him, and God knows best. The meaning of his saying, God only accepts from the righteous is from those who fear God in their actions. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibrahim bin Al-Ala bin Zaid told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us, Safwan bin Amr told me on the authority of Tamim, meaning Ibn Malik Al-Muqri, who said: I heard Abu Al-Darda’ say: For me to be certain that God has accepted a single prayer from me is dearer to me than the world and what is in it, for God says, God only accepts from the righteous. My father told us, Abdullah bin Imran told us, Ishaq bin Sulaiman, meaning Al-Razi, told us on the authority of Al-Mughira bin Muslim, on the authority of Maymun bin Abi Hamza, who said: I was sitting with Abu Wa’il when a man called Abu Afif, one of the companions of Muadh, entered upon us. Shuqaiq bin Salamah said to him: O Abu Afif, will you not tell us about Muadh bin Jabal? He said: Yes, I heard him say: The people will be detained in a single place in Baqi’, then a caller will call out: Where are the righteous? So they will stand in the protection of the Most Merciful, God will not hide from them nor conceal Himself. I said: Who are the righteous? He said, People avoid polytheism and idol worship and are sincere in their worship, so they will pass to Paradise. And his saying: “If you should stretch your hand against me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear God, the Lord of the worlds.” His brother, the righteous man whose sacrifice God accepted because of his piety, said to him when his brother threatened to kill him for no sin on his part: If you should stretch your hand against me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand against you to kill you. That is, I will not respond to your corrupt action with the same, so that you and I will be equal in sin. Indeed, I fear God, the Lord of the worlds. That is, I will not do as you want me to do, but I will be patient and seek reward. Abdullah bin Amr said: By God, he was the stronger of the two men, but his scruples prevented him, meaning his piety. That is why it was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: If two Muslims confront each other with their swords, then the killer and the killed will be in Hellfire. They said: O Messenger of God, this is the killer, but what about the killed? He said: He was eager to kill his companion. Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah ibn Sa`id told us, Layth ibn Sa`d told us, on the authority of `Ayyash ibn `Abbas, on the authority of Bakir ibn `Abdullah, on the authority of Bishr ibn Sa`id, that Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas said during the tribulation of `Uthman: I bear witness that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “There will be a tribulation in which the one who sits is better than the one who stands, and the one who stands is better than the one who walks, and the one who walks is better than the one who runs.” He said: What if someone enters my house and stretches out his hand to kill me and says, Be like the son of Adam. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it likewise on the authority of Qutaybah ibn Sa`id, and he said: This is a good hadith. There are narrations on this topic on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, Khabbab ibn al-Arat, Abu Bakr, Ibn Mas`ud, Abu Waqid, Abu Musa, and Kharsha. Some of them narrated it on the authority of al-Layth ibn Sa`d, and he added a man to the chain of transmission. Al-Hafiz Ibn `Asakir said: The man is Husayn al-Ashja`i. I said: Abu Dawud narrated it from his path, and he said: Yazid ibn Khalid al-Ramli told us, al-Fadl told us on the authority of `Ayyash ibn `Abbas, on the authority of Bakir, on the authority of Bishr ibn Sa`id, on the authority of Husayn ibn `Abd al-Rahman al-Ashja`i, that he heard Sa`d ibn Abi Waqas narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this hadith. He said: I said: O Messenger of God, what if he enters my house and stretches out his hand to kill me? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Be like the son of Adam and recited: “If you should stretch out your hand against me to kill me, I will not stretch out my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds.” Ayyub Al-Sakhtiyani said: The first person from this nation to take this verse “If you should stretch your hand against me to kill me, I will not stretch my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds” was Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Hazm told us, Abu Imran Al-Jawni told me, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Al-Samit, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, rode a donkey with me riding behind him and said: O Abu Dharr, tell me if the people are afflicted with severe hunger such that you cannot get up from your bed to go to your mosque, what would you do? He said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Be chaste. He said: O Abu Dharr, tell me if a severe death afflicts the people and the house is occupied by the slave, meaning the grave, what would you do? I said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Be patient. He said: O Abu Dharr, tell me if the people kill one another, meaning until the stones of oil are drowned in blood, what would you do? He said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Sit in your house and close your door. He said: If I do not leave you alone? He said: Then go to whoever you are from and be one of them. He said: Then I will take my weapon. He said: Then you will share in what they are doing, but if you fear that the radiance of the sword will deter you, then throw the edge of your cloak over your face so that he may bear his sin and your sin. Muslim and the people of Sunan, except for al-Nasa’i, narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Abu Imran al-Jawni on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Samit, and Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it through the chain of transmission of Hammad ibn Zayd on the authority of Abu Imran, on the authority of al-Mush’ath ibn Tarif, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Samit, on the authority of Abu Dharr, similarly. Abu Dawud said: Al-Mush’ath did not mention anyone in this hadith except Hammad ibn Zayd. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Duhaim narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, Qubaysah ibn Uqbah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Rub’i, who said: We were at the funeral of Hudhayfah and I heard a man say: I heard this man saying about some people, from what I heard. From the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “If you fight, I will look to the furthest part of my house and I will go to Paradise. If so-and-so enters upon me, I will say, ‘Here, bear my sin and your sin,’ and I will be like the best of the sons of Adam.” And his saying: “Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin and be among the companions of the Fire. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.” Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah and As-Suddi said regarding his saying: Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin meaning the sin of killing me and the sin that was upon you before that, as Ibn Jarir said. Others said: What he means by that is that I want you to bear my sin and bear its burden and your sin in killing me. This is a statement that I found from Mujahid and I fear that it is a mistake because the correct narration from him is the opposite, meaning what Sufyan Ath-Thawri narrated from Mansur from Mujahid: Indeed, I want you to bear my sin he said: by killing me and your sin he said: for what was upon you before that, and Isa bin Abi Nujayh narrated it similarly, from Mujahid, and Shibl narrated from Ibn Abi Nujayh from Mujahid: Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin he said: I want my sin and my blood to be upon you so that you bear both of them. I said Many people may imagine this statement, and they mention a hadith that has no basis in it, The killer does not leave any sin for the one killed. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated a hadith similar to this, but it is not the same. He said: Amr ibn Ali told us, Aamer ibn Ibrahim al-Isfahani told us, Yaqub ibn Abdullah told us, Utbah ibn Saeed told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Killing with patience does not pass by a sin except that it erases it. This is not correct in this sense, and if it is correct, then its meaning is that God expiates the sins of the one killed by the pain of killing, but as for it being borne by the killer, then no. However, this may happen in some people, and it is the most common, for the one killed demands the killer in the open spaces, and his good deeds are taken from him according to the extent of his injustice. If they are exhausted and his right is not fulfilled, then some of the bad deeds of the one killed are taken and placed on the killer, so perhaps no sin remains for the one killed except that it is placed on the killer. The hadith about this has been authenticated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding all injustices, and killing is one of the greatest of them. And the most severe, and God knows best. As for Ibn Jarir, he said: The correct statement in this regard is to say that its interpretation is that I want you to turn away with your sin in killing me, and this is the meaning of his saying: I want you to bear my sin. As for the meaning of and your sin, it is his sin, meaning killing him, and that is disobeying God Almighty in the actions of someone other than Him. We only said that this is correct because of the consensus of the people of interpretation on it, and that God Almighty informed us that every worker has the recompense for his actions for him or against him. If this is His ruling in His creation, then it is not permissible for the sins of the one killed to be taken by the killer. Rather, the killer is taken by his sin for the forbidden killing and the rest of the sins of his disobedience that he committed himself without what his victim committed. This is his wording. Then he raised a question about this, the gist of which is: How did Abel want his brother Cain to bear the sin of killing him and his own sin, even though killing him was forbidden? He answered with the gist of which is that Abel informed about himself that he would not fight his brother if he fought him, but rather he would refrain from him, seeking that if he killed someone, he would be… From his brother, not from him. I said: This speech includes a sermon to him if he takes heed, and a warning to him if he is deterred. That is why he said, Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin, meaning, bear my sin and your sin, “and be among the companions of the Fire. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.” Ibn Abbas said: He frightened him with the Fire, but he did not stop or deter. And the Almighty said: Then his soul encouraged him to kill his brother, so he killed him and became among the losers. That is, his soul tempted him and encouraged him to kill his brother, so he killed him, that is, after this admonition and this warning. It was mentioned previously in the narration on the authority of Abu Ja`far al-Baqir, who is Muhammad ibn `Ali ibn al-Husayn, that he killed him with an iron rod in his hand. Al-Suddi said, on the authority of Abu Malik, and on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, and on the authority of Murrah ibn `Abdullah, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that his soul encouraged him to kill his brother, so he sought him out to kill him. The boy finished with him on the mountaintops, and one day he came to him while he was tending his sheep while he was asleep, so he lifted a rock and smashed his head with it, so he died, so he left him in the open. This was narrated by Ibn Jarir. And on the authority of some of the People of the Book, he killed him by strangulation and biting him as wild beasts kill. Ibn Jarir said: When he wanted to kill him, he started twisting his neck, so Satan took a beast and put its head on a rock, then he took another rock and hit its head with it until he killed it while the son of Adam was watching, so he did the same to his brother. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Abdullah bin Wahb said, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of his father, who said: He took him by the head to kill him, so he lay down for him and started poking his head and bones, not knowing how to kill him. Satan came to him and said: Do you want to kill him? He said: Yes. He said: Take this rock and throw it on his head. He said: So he took it and threw it at him and smashed his head. Then Satan came to Eve quickly and said: O Eve, Cain killed Abel. She said to him: Woe to you! What kind of killing is that? He said: He neither eats nor drinks nor moves. She said: That is death. He said: So it is death. She started screaming until Adam entered upon her while she was screaming, so he said: What is the matter with you? She did not speak to him, so he returned to her twice, but God did not speak to him. So he said: The shout is upon you and your daughters, and I and my sons are innocent of her. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. And his saying, So he became among the losers, meaning in this world and the Hereafter. What loss is greater than this? Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu’awiyah and Waki’ told us: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No soul is killed unjustly except that the first son of Adam will bear a share of its blood, because he was the first to institute killing. And the group, except for Abu Dawud, transmitted it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Al-A’mash. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, who said: Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: One of the killer’s legs was suspended by its shin to its thigh from that day on, and his face was in the sun wherever he turned. In the summer, there was a fence of fire over him, and in the winter, there was a fence of snow over him. He said: Abdullah bin Amr said: We find that the son of Adam, the murderer, shares the people of Hell in a correct division of punishment, with half of their punishment upon him. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Hakim bin Hakim, that he told on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr that he used to say: The most wretched of people is the son of Adam who killed his brother. No blood has been shed on earth since he killed his brother until the Day of Resurrection except that evil has befallen him from it, and that is because he was the first to institute killing. Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said: There is no one who is killed unjustly except that it is upon the first son of Adam and the devil as a share of it. Ibn Jarir also narrated it. And the Almighty said: “So God sent a raven, scratching the ground, to show him how to cover the shame of his brother. He said, ‘Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven and cover the shame of my brother?’ So he became one of the regretful.” Al-Suddi said, with his chain of transmission that goes back to the Companions, may God be pleased with them: When the boy died, he left him in the open, not knowing how to bury him. So God sent two brothers, ravens, and they fought. One of them killed the other, so he dug a grave for him and threw dirt on him. When he saw him, he said, Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven and cover the shame of my brother? Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A raven came to a dead raven and threw dirt on him until he covered him. Then the one who killed his brother said, Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven and cover the shame of my brother? Ad-Dahhak said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He continued carrying his brother in a bag on his shoulder for a year until God sent the two crows. He saw them searching, so he said, Am I unable to be like this crow? So he buried his brother. Laith bin Abi Salim said, on the authority of Mujahid: He carried him on his shoulder for a hundred years, dead, not knowing what to do with him. He carried him and put him on the ground until he saw the crow burying the crow. He said, Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow and cover my brother’s nakedness? I have become one of the regretful ones. Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. Atiyah Al-Awfi said: When he killed him, he regretted it and held him close to him until he died, and the birds and beasts swarmed around him, waiting for him to throw him away so they could eat him. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated on the authority of some of the scholars of the first book: When he killed him, he was disappointed, meaning he did not know how to bury him, because he was, as they claim, the first of the sons of Adam to be killed, and the first to die. “So God sent a raven to scratch the ground to show him how to bury his brother’s body. He said, ‘Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven and bury my brother’s body?’ So he became one of the regretful ones.” He said: The people of the Torah claimed that when Cain killed his brother Abel, God the Almighty said to him: O Cain, where is your brother Abel? He said: I do not know, I was not watching over him. So God said: The sound of your brother’s blood is calling me from the ground now. You are cursed in the ground that opened its mouth and received your brother’s blood from your hand. If you work the ground, it will no longer yield its crops to you until you become a wandering, frightened person in the earth. And his saying, So he became among the regretful, Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: May God exalt him with regret after loss. These are the sayings of the commentators on this story, and they all agree that these two sons of Adam were from his loins, as is apparent in the Qur’an, and as stated in the hadith in His saying, Except that the first son of Adam would bear a share of her blood because he was the first to establish killing. This is apparent and clear, but Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Sahl bin Yusuf told us on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he is Al-Basri, he said: The two men in the Qur’an about whom God said, And recite to them the report of the two sons of Adam in truth, were from the Children of Israel, and they were not the sons of Adam from his loins, but rather the sacrifice was from the Children of Israel, and Adam was the first to die. This is very strange, and there is a problem with its chain of transmission. Abd Al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The two sons of Adam, peace be upon him, are an example for this nation, so take the better of them.” And Ibn Al-Mubarak narrated it on the authority of Asim Al-Ahwal, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And peace be upon him: God has given you an example of the two sons of Adam, so take from their good and leave their evil. This hadith was also transmitted by Bakir bin Abdullah Al-Muzani. All of this was narrated by Ibn Jarir. Salim bin Abi Al-Ja’d said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, Adam remained sad for a hundred years, not laughing. Then he came and it was said to him: May God give you life and make you laugh. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Then he said: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ghiyath bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Hamadani, who said: Ali bin Abi Talib said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, Adam cried for him, so he said: The country and its people have changed, the color of the earth is dusty and ugly Everything changed in color and taste, and the pretty face became less cheerful. So Adam, peace be upon him, was answered: Abel's father and father were both killed, and the living became the dead slaughtered. And Bashir came, for he was afraid of him, so he brought her, shouting: It appears that Cain was punished quickly, as Mujahid and Ibn Jubayr mentioned, that his leg was attached to his thigh until the Day of Resurrection, and God turned his face to the sun as a punishment and torment for him. It was mentioned in the hadith that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, There is no sin more deserving of God hastening its punishment in this world, along with what He has stored up for its perpetrator in the Hereafter, than oppression and severing family ties. Cain’s actions combined this and that, so to God we belong and to Him we shall return.
5:25: God Almighty says, explaining the dire consequences of transgression, envy and injustice in the story of the two sons of Adam, according to the majority, who are Cain and Abel, how one of them transgressed against the other and killed him, transgressing against him and envying him, in what God had given him of blessings and accepting the sacrifice in which he had been sincere to God Almighty, so the one killed won by putting away sins and entering Paradise, and the killer was disappointed and returned with the losing deal in both worlds, so God Almighty said: And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth, meaning, tell these transgressors and envious ones, brothers of the pigs and monkeys from the Jews and their likes and their likes, the story of the two sons of Adam, who are Cain and Abel, according to what was mentioned by more than one of the predecessors and successors. And His saying, in truth, meaning in a clear and unambiguous manner, without ambiguity, falsehood, illusion, change, addition, or subtraction, like the saying of God Almighty: Indeed, this is the true story. And His saying, We relate to you their story in truth. And He said, That is Jesus, son of Mary, the word of truth. And from their story, as mentioned by more than one of the predecessors and successors, was that God Almighty: He prescribed for Adam, peace be upon him, to marry his daughters to his sons due to the necessity of the situation, but they said: A male and a female were born to him in every womb, so he would marry the female of this womb to the male of the other womb, and Abel’s sister was ugly and Cain’s sister was beautiful, so he wanted to keep her for himself over his brother, but Adam refused that, unless they offer a sacrifice, and whoever it is accepted from, it is his, so it is accepted from Abel and not from Cain, so what happened to them is what God narrated in His Book. Mention the sayings of the commentators here Al-Suddi said, according to what was mentioned on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: That no child was born to Adam except that a girl was born with him, so he would marry the boy of this womb to the girl of this other womb, and he would marry the girl of this womb to the boy of this other womb, until he had two sons called Abel and Qabil. Qabil was a farmer, and Abel was a milker, and Qabil was the older of them, and he had a sister more beautiful than Abel’s sister, and that Abel asked to marry Qabil’s sister, but he refused, and said, She is my sister, she was born with me, and she is more beautiful than your sister, and I am more deserving of marrying her. So his father ordered him to marry her to Abel, but he refused, and they offered a sacrifice to God Almighty, which of them was more deserving of the girl, and Adam, peace be upon him, had been absent from them, and he came to Mecca to look at it, and God Almighty said: Do you know that I have a house on earth? He said: O God, no. He said: I have a house in Mecca, so go to it. Adam said to the sky: Keep my son in trust, but it refused. He said to the earth, but it refused. He said to the mountains, but they refused. He said to Cain, and it said: Yes, you go and come back and find your family as you please. When Adam set out, he offered a sacrifice, and Cain was proud of him, so he said: I have more right to it than you, she is my sister and I am older than you and I am my father’s successor. When they offered it, Abel offered a fat young tree and Cain offered a bundle of ears of corn, and he found a large ear of corn in it, so he rubbed it and ate it, so the fire came down and ate Abel’s sacrifice and left Cain’s sacrifice. He became angry and said: I will kill you so that you will not marry my sister. Abel said: God only accepts from the righteous. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who told me: Ibn Khaitham told me: I came with Saeed bin Jubair, and he told me on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It was forbidden for a woman to marry her twin brother, and he was ordered to marry her to someone other than her brothers. He used to have a man and a woman born to him in every pregnancy. While they were like that, a beautiful woman was born to him, and another ugly, hideous woman was born to him. The brother of the ugly woman said: Marry me to your sister and I will marry you to my sister. He said: No, I have more right to my sister. So they offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from the owner of the ram, but it was not accepted from the owner of the crops, so he killed him. A good chain of transmission. My father told us, Abu Salamah told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Othman bin Khaitham, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and his saying: When they offered a sacrifice so they offered their sacrifice, and the owner of the sheep brought a ram with two white horns, and the owner of the crops brought a heap of… His food, so God accepted the ram and stored it in Paradise for forty autumns. It is the ram that Abraham, peace be upon him, slaughtered. Good chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Awf told us on the authority of Abu al-Mughira on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Amr, who said: The two sons of Adam who offered a sacrifice and it was accepted from one of them and not accepted from the other, one of them was a farmer and the other was a sheep owner. They were both commanded to offer a sacrifice, and the sheep owner offered the most honorable, fattest, and best of his sheep, and he was pleased with it. The farmer offered the worst of his farms, the colocynth and tares, and he was not pleased with it. God, the Almighty, accepted the sacrifice of the sheep owner, and He did not accept the sacrifice of the farmer. And from their story is what God has narrated in His Book. He said: By God, the one who was killed was the stronger of the two men, but his shyness prevented him from extending his hand to his brother. Ismail ibn Rafi` al-Madani, the storyteller, said: It has reached me that when the two sons of Adam were commanded to offer a sacrifice, one of them was a sheep owner and he had a lamb among his sheep, and he loved it so much that he would give it preference at night, and he would carry it on his back out of love for it, until he had no one to give it to him. Money was dearer to him than it. When he was ordered to offer the sacrifice, he offered it to God Almighty, and God accepted it from him. He continued to enjoy it in Paradise until he ransomed the son of Abraham, peace be upon him, with it. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Al-Ansari told us, Al-Qasim bin Abdul Rahman told us, Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Adam, peace be upon him, said to Abel and Cain: My Lord has promised me that there will be from my offspring someone who will offer a sacrifice, so offer a sacrifice so that my eyes may be comforted. If your sacrifice is accepted, then offer it. Abel was a sheep owner, so he offered the best of his wealth from his sheep. Cain was a farmer, so he offered a tow from his crops. Adam set out with them, and with them were their sacrifices. They climbed the mountain, and they placed their sacrifices. Then the three of them sat, Adam and they were looking at the sacrifice. Then God sent a fire, and when it was above them, a neck approached it, and it carried Abel’s sacrifice, and left Cain’s sacrifice. They turned away, and Adam knew that Cain was angry with him, so he said: Woe to you, Cain, your sacrifice was returned to you. Cain said: I loved him, so I prayed over his sacrifice and supplicated for him, so his sacrifice was accepted and my sacrifice was returned to me. Cain said to Abel: To kill you and be rid of you, your father prayed for you and prayed over your sacrifice and it was accepted from you, and he threatened to kill him until one evening Abel was detained with his sheep, so Adam said: O Cain, where is your brother? He said: And you sent me to him as a shepherd, I do not know, so Adam said: Woe to you, Cain, go and look for your brother, so Cain said to himself: Tonight I will kill him, and he took with him an iron rod and met him as he was turning over, and said: O Abel, accept your sacrifice and return mine to me so that I may kill you, so Abel said: I offered the best of my wealth, and you offered the worst of your wealth, and God does not accept except the good, God only accepts from the righteous, so when he said that, Cain became angry, so he picked up the iron rod and struck him with it, and he said: Woe to you, Cain, where are you in front of God, how will He reward you for your work? So he killed him, and threw him in a pit of the ground, and threw some dirt on him. Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated from some of the scholars of the first book: that Adam ordered his son Cain to marry his twin sister, Abel, and ordered Abel to marry Cain’s twin sister, so Abel submitted to that and was satisfied, but Cain refused and hated it out of generosity towards Abel’s sister, and he desired his sister over Abel and said: We are from the birth of Paradise, and they are from the birth of the Earth, and I am more deserving of my sister. Some of the scholars of the first book say: Cain’s sister was one of the best people, so he was stingy with her towards his brother and wanted her for himself, and God knows best which of them it was, so his father said to him: O my son, she is not lawful for you, but Cain refused to accept that from his father’s words, his father said to him: O my son, offer a sacrifice and your brother Abel will offer a sacrifice, so whichever of you accepts his sacrifice is more deserving of it, and Cain was in charge of sowing the land, and Abel was in charge of tending the livestock, so Cain offered wheat and Abel offered firstborns from the firstborns of his sheep, and some of them said: He said: He offered a cow, so God sent a white fire that ate Abel’s offering and left Cain’s offering. Thus, he accepted the offering if he accepted it. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It was their nature that no poor person was to be given charity, but rather the offering was offered by a man. While the two sons of Adam were sitting, they said, If we offered an offering. When a man offered an offering and God was pleased with him, He would send a fire to him and consume him. If God was not pleased with him, the fire would go out. So they offered an offering, and one of them was a shepherd and the other was a farmer. The owner of the sheep offered the best and fattest of his sheep, and the other offered some of his crops. Then the fire came and descended between them and consumed the sheep and left the crops. The son of Adam said to his brother, Do you walk among the people and they know that you offered an offering and it was accepted from you and returned to me? No, by God, the people will not look at me, and you are better than me. He said, I will kill you. His brother said to him, What is my sin? God only accepts from the righteous. Narrated by Ibn Jarir, so this trace indicates that the offering was not for a reason or to avoid a woman, as was previously mentioned by a group of those mentioned, and it is apparent in the Qur’an: When they both offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them but not from the other, he said, ‘I will surely kill you.’ He said, ‘God only accepts from the righteous.’ So the context indicates that he was angry with him and envied him because his offering was accepted but not his. Then it is well-known among the majority that the one who offered the sheep was Abel and the one who offered the food was Qabil, and that the sheep was accepted from Abel, until Ibn Abbas and others said that it was the ram that was used to ransom the slaughtered animal, which is appropriate, and God knows best, and it was not accepted from Qabil. This is also what was stated by more than one of the early and later generations, and it is also well-known from Mujahid, but Ibn Jarir narrated from him that he said the one who offered the crops was Qabil, and it was accepted from him. This is contrary to the well-known view, and perhaps it was not well-recorded from him, and God knows best. The meaning of his saying, God only accepts from the righteous is from those who fear God in their actions. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibrahim bin Al-Ala bin Zaid told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us, Safwan bin Amr told me on the authority of Tamim, meaning Ibn Malik Al-Muqri, who said: I heard Abu Al-Darda’ say: For me to be certain that God has accepted a single prayer from me is dearer to me than the world and what is in it, for God says, God only accepts from the righteous. My father told us, Abdullah bin Imran told us, Ishaq bin Sulaiman, meaning Al-Razi, told us on the authority of Al-Mughira bin Muslim, on the authority of Maymun bin Abi Hamza, who said: I was sitting with Abu Wa’il when a man called Abu Afif, one of the companions of Muadh, entered upon us. Shuqaiq bin Salamah said to him: O Abu Afif, will you not tell us about Muadh bin Jabal? He said: Yes, I heard him say: The people will be detained in a single place in Baqi’, then a caller will call out: Where are the righteous? So they will stand in the protection of the Most Merciful, God will not hide from them nor conceal Himself. I said: Who are the righteous? He said, People avoid polytheism and idol worship and are sincere in their worship, so they will pass to Paradise. And his saying: “If you should stretch your hand against me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear God, the Lord of the worlds.” His brother, the righteous man whose sacrifice God accepted because of his piety, said to him when his brother threatened to kill him for no sin on his part: If you should stretch your hand against me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand against you to kill you. That is, I will not respond to your corrupt action with the same, so that you and I will be equal in sin. Indeed, I fear God, the Lord of the worlds. That is, I will not do as you want me to do, but I will be patient and seek reward. Abdullah bin Amr said: By God, he was the stronger of the two men, but his scruples prevented him, meaning his piety. That is why it was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: If two Muslims confront each other with their swords, then the killer and the killed will be in Hellfire. They said: O Messenger of God, this is the killer, but what about the killed? He said: He was eager to kill his companion. Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah ibn Sa`id told us, Layth ibn Sa`d told us, on the authority of `Ayyash ibn `Abbas, on the authority of Bakir ibn `Abdullah, on the authority of Bishr ibn Sa`id, that Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas said during the tribulation of `Uthman: I bear witness that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “There will be a tribulation in which the one who sits is better than the one who stands, and the one who stands is better than the one who walks, and the one who walks is better than the one who runs.” He said: What if someone enters my house and stretches out his hand to kill me and says, Be like the son of Adam. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it likewise on the authority of Qutaybah ibn Sa`id, and he said: This is a good hadith. There are narrations on this topic on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, Khabbab ibn al-Arat, Abu Bakr, Ibn Mas`ud, Abu Waqid, Abu Musa, and Kharsha. Some of them narrated it on the authority of al-Layth ibn Sa`d, and he added a man to the chain of transmission. Al-Hafiz Ibn `Asakir said: The man is Husayn al-Ashja`i. I said: Abu Dawud narrated it from his path, and he said: Yazid ibn Khalid al-Ramli told us, al-Fadl told us on the authority of `Ayyash ibn `Abbas, on the authority of Bakir, on the authority of Bishr ibn Sa`id, on the authority of Husayn ibn `Abd al-Rahman al-Ashja`i, that he heard Sa`d ibn Abi Waqas narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this hadith. He said: I said: O Messenger of God, what if he enters my house and stretches out his hand to kill me? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Be like the son of Adam and recited: “If you should stretch out your hand against me to kill me, I will not stretch out my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds.” Ayyub Al-Sakhtiyani said: The first person from this nation to take this verse “If you should stretch your hand against me to kill me, I will not stretch my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds” was Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Hazm told us, Abu Imran Al-Jawni told me, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Al-Samit, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, rode a donkey with me riding behind him and said: O Abu Dharr, tell me if the people are afflicted with severe hunger such that you cannot get up from your bed to go to your mosque, what would you do? He said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Be chaste. He said: O Abu Dharr, tell me if a severe death afflicts the people and the house is occupied by the slave, meaning the grave, what would you do? I said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Be patient. He said: O Abu Dharr, tell me if the people kill one another, meaning until the stones of oil are drowned in blood, what would you do? He said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Sit in your house and close your door. He said: If I do not leave you alone? He said: Then go to whoever you are from and be one of them. He said: Then I will take my weapon. He said: Then you will share in what they are doing, but if you fear that the radiance of the sword will deter you, then throw the edge of your cloak over your face so that he may bear his sin and your sin. Muslim and the people of Sunan, except for al-Nasa’i, narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Abu Imran al-Jawni on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Samit, and Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it through the chain of transmission of Hammad ibn Zayd on the authority of Abu Imran, on the authority of al-Mush’ath ibn Tarif, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Samit, on the authority of Abu Dharr, similarly. Abu Dawud said: Al-Mush’ath did not mention anyone in this hadith except Hammad ibn Zayd. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Duhaim narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, Qubaysah ibn Uqbah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Rub’i, who said: We were at the funeral of Hudhayfah and I heard a man say: I heard this man saying about some people, from what I heard. From the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “If you fight, I will look to the furthest part of my house and I will go to Paradise. If so-and-so enters upon me, I will say, ‘Here, bear my sin and your sin,’ and I will be like the best of the sons of Adam.” And his saying: “Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin and be among the companions of the Fire. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.” Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah and As-Suddi said regarding his saying: Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin meaning the sin of killing me and the sin that was upon you before that, as Ibn Jarir said. Others said: What he means by that is that I want you to bear my sin and bear its burden and your sin in killing me. This is a statement that I found from Mujahid and I fear that it is a mistake because the correct narration from him is the opposite, meaning what Sufyan Ath-Thawri narrated from Mansur from Mujahid: Indeed, I want you to bear my sin he said: by killing me and your sin he said: for what was upon you before that, and Isa bin Abi Nujayh narrated it similarly, from Mujahid, and Shibl narrated from Ibn Abi Nujayh from Mujahid: Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin he said: I want my sin and my blood to be upon you so that you bear both of them. I said Many people may imagine this statement, and they mention a hadith that has no basis in it, The killer does not leave any sin for the one killed. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated a hadith similar to this, but it is not the same. He said: Amr ibn Ali told us, Aamer ibn Ibrahim al-Isfahani told us, Yaqub ibn Abdullah told us, Utbah ibn Saeed told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Killing with patience does not pass by a sin except that it erases it. This is not correct in this sense, and if it is correct, then its meaning is that God expiates the sins of the one killed by the pain of killing, but as for it being borne by the killer, then no. However, this may happen in some people, and it is the most common, for the one killed demands the killer in the open spaces, and his good deeds are taken from him according to the extent of his injustice. If they are exhausted and his right is not fulfilled, then some of the bad deeds of the one killed are taken and placed on the killer, so perhaps no sin remains for the one killed except that it is placed on the killer. The hadith about this has been authenticated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding all injustices, and killing is one of the greatest of them. And the most severe, and God knows best. As for Ibn Jarir, he said: The correct statement in this regard is to say that its interpretation is that I want you to turn away with your sin in killing me, and this is the meaning of his saying: I want you to bear my sin. As for the meaning of and your sin, it is his sin, meaning killing him, and that is disobeying God Almighty in the actions of someone other than Him. We only said that this is correct because of the consensus of the people of interpretation on it, and that God Almighty informed us that every worker has the recompense for his actions for him or against him. If this is His ruling in His creation, then it is not permissible for the sins of the one killed to be taken by the killer. Rather, the killer is taken by his sin for the forbidden killing and the rest of the sins of his disobedience that he committed himself without what his victim committed. This is his wording. Then he raised a question about this, the gist of which is: How did Abel want his brother Cain to bear the sin of killing him and his own sin, even though killing him was forbidden? He answered with the gist of which is that Abel informed about himself that he would not fight his brother if he fought him, but rather he would refrain from him, seeking that if he killed someone, he would be… From his brother, not from him. I said: This speech includes a sermon to him if he takes heed, and a warning to him if he is deterred. That is why he said, Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin, meaning, bear my sin and your sin, “and be among the companions of the Fire. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.” Ibn Abbas said: He frightened him with the Fire, but he did not stop or deter. And the Almighty said: Then his soul encouraged him to kill his brother, so he killed him and became among the losers. That is, his soul tempted him and encouraged him to kill his brother, so he killed him, that is, after this admonition and this warning. It was mentioned previously in the narration on the authority of Abu Ja`far al-Baqir, who is Muhammad ibn `Ali ibn al-Husayn, that he killed him with an iron rod in his hand. Al-Suddi said, on the authority of Abu Malik, and on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, and on the authority of Murrah ibn `Abdullah, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that his soul encouraged him to kill his brother, so he sought him out to kill him. The boy finished with him on the mountaintops, and one day he came to him while he was tending his sheep while he was asleep, so he lifted a rock and smashed his head with it, so he died, so he left him in the open. This was narrated by Ibn Jarir. And on the authority of some of the People of the Book, he killed him by strangulation and biting him as wild beasts kill. Ibn Jarir said: When he wanted to kill him, he started twisting his neck, so Satan took a beast and put its head on a rock, then he took another rock and hit its head with it until he killed it while the son of Adam was watching, so he did the same to his brother. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Abdullah bin Wahb said, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of his father, who said: He took him by the head to kill him, so he lay down for him and started poking his head and bones, not knowing how to kill him. Satan came to him and said: Do you want to kill him? He said: Yes. He said: Take this rock and throw it on his head. He said: So he took it and threw it at him and smashed his head. Then Satan came to Eve quickly and said: O Eve, Cain killed Abel. She said to him: Woe to you! What kind of killing is that? He said: He neither eats nor drinks nor moves. She said: That is death. He said: So it is death. She started screaming until Adam entered upon her while she was screaming, so he said: What is the matter with you? She did not speak to him, so he returned to her twice, but God did not speak to him. So he said: The shout is upon you and your daughters, and I and my sons are innocent of her. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. And his saying, So he became among the losers, meaning in this world and the Hereafter. What loss is greater than this? Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu’awiyah and Waki’ told us: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No soul is killed unjustly except that the first son of Adam will bear a share of its blood, because he was the first to institute killing. And the group, except for Abu Dawud, transmitted it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Al-A’mash. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, who said: Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: One of the killer’s legs was suspended by its shin to its thigh from that day on, and his face was in the sun wherever he turned. In the summer, there was a fence of fire over him, and in the winter, there was a fence of snow over him. He said: Abdullah bin Amr said: We find that the son of Adam, the murderer, shares the people of Hell in a correct division of punishment, with half of their punishment upon him. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Hakim bin Hakim, that he told on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr that he used to say: The most wretched of people is the son of Adam who killed his brother. No blood has been shed on earth since he killed his brother until the Day of Resurrection except that evil has befallen him from it, and that is because he was the first to institute killing. Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said: There is no one who is killed unjustly except that it is upon the first son of Adam and the devil as a share of it. Ibn Jarir also narrated it. And the Almighty said: “So God sent a raven, scratching the ground, to show him how to cover the shame of his brother. He said, ‘Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven and cover the shame of my brother?’ So he became one of the regretful.” Al-Suddi said, with his chain of transmission that goes back to the Companions, may God be pleased with them: When the boy died, he left him in the open, not knowing how to bury him. So God sent two brothers, ravens, and they fought. One of them killed the other, so he dug a grave for him and threw dirt on him. When he saw him, he said, Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven and cover the shame of my brother? Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A raven came to a dead raven and threw dirt on him until he covered him. Then the one who killed his brother said, Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven and cover the shame of my brother? Ad-Dahhak said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He continued carrying his brother in a bag on his shoulder for a year until God sent the two crows. He saw them searching, so he said, Am I unable to be like this crow? So he buried his brother. Laith bin Abi Salim said, on the authority of Mujahid: He carried him on his shoulder for a hundred years, dead, not knowing what to do with him. He carried him and put him on the ground until he saw the crow burying the crow. He said, Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow and cover my brother’s nakedness? I have become one of the regretful ones. Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. Atiyah Al-Awfi said: When he killed him, he regretted it and held him close to him until he died, and the birds and beasts swarmed around him, waiting for him to throw him away so they could eat him. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated on the authority of some of the scholars of the first book: When he killed him, he was disappointed, meaning he did not know how to bury him, because he was, as they claim, the first of the sons of Adam to be killed, and the first to die. “So God sent a raven to scratch the ground to show him how to bury his brother’s body. He said, ‘Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven and bury my brother’s body?’ So he became one of the regretful ones.” He said: The people of the Torah claimed that when Cain killed his brother Abel, God the Almighty said to him: O Cain, where is your brother Abel? He said: I do not know, I was not watching over him. So God said: The sound of your brother’s blood is calling me from the ground now. You are cursed in the ground that opened its mouth and received your brother’s blood from your hand. If you work the ground, it will no longer yield its crops to you until you become a wandering, frightened person in the earth. And his saying, So he became among the regretful, Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: May God exalt him with regret after loss. These are the sayings of the commentators on this story, and they all agree that these two sons of Adam were from his loins, as is apparent in the Qur’an, and as stated in the hadith in His saying, Except that the first son of Adam would bear a share of her blood because he was the first to establish killing. This is apparent and clear, but Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Sahl bin Yusuf told us on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he is Al-Basri, he said: The two men in the Qur’an about whom God said, And recite to them the report of the two sons of Adam in truth, were from the Children of Israel, and they were not the sons of Adam from his loins, but rather the sacrifice was from the Children of Israel, and Adam was the first to die. This is very strange, and there is a problem with its chain of transmission. Abd Al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The two sons of Adam, peace be upon him, are an example for this nation, so take the better of them.” And Ibn Al-Mubarak narrated it on the authority of Asim Al-Ahwal, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And peace be upon him: God has given you an example of the two sons of Adam, so take from their good and leave their evil. This hadith was also transmitted by Bakir bin Abdullah Al-Muzani. All of this was narrated by Ibn Jarir. Salim bin Abi Al-Ja’d said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, Adam remained sad for a hundred years, not laughing. Then he came and it was said to him: May God give you life and make you laugh. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Then he said: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ghiyath bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Hamadani, who said: Ali bin Abi Talib said: When the son of Adam killed his brother, Adam cried for him, so he said: The country and its people have changed, the color of the earth is dusty and ugly Everything changed in color and taste, and the pretty face became less cheerful. So Adam, peace be upon him, was answered: Abel's father and father were both killed, and the living became the dead slaughtered. And Bashir came, for he was afraid of him, so he brought her, shouting: It appears that Cain was punished quickly, as Mujahid and Ibn Jubayr mentioned, that his leg was attached to his thigh until the Day of Resurrection, and God turned his face to the sun as a punishment and torment for him. It was mentioned in the hadith that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, There is no sin more deserving of God hastening its punishment in this world, along with what He has stored up for its perpetrator in the Hereafter, than oppression and severing family ties. Cain’s actions combined this and that, so to God we belong and to Him we shall return.
5:26: God Almighty says, explaining the dire consequences of transgression, envy and injustice in the story of the two sons of Adam, according to the majority, who are Cain and Abel, how one of them transgressed against the other and killed him, transgressing against him and envying him, in what God had given him of blessings and accepting the sacrifice in which he had been sincere to God Almighty, so the one killed won by putting away sins and entering Paradise, and the killer was disappointed and returned with the losing deal in both worlds, so God Almighty said: And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth, meaning, tell these transgressors and envious ones, brothers of the pigs and monkeys from the Jews and their likes and their likes, the story of the two sons of Adam, who are Cain and Abel, according to what was mentioned by more than one of the predecessors and successors. And His saying, in truth, meaning in a clear and unambiguous manner, without ambiguity, falsehood, illusion, change, addition, or subtraction, like the saying of God Almighty: Indeed, this is the true story. And His saying, We relate to you their story in truth. And He said, That is Jesus, son of Mary, the word of truth. And from their story, as mentioned by more than one of the predecessors and successors, was that God Almighty: He prescribed for Adam, peace be upon him, to marry his daughters to his sons due to the necessity of the situation, but they said: A male and a female were born to him in every womb, so he would marry the female of this womb to the male of the other womb, and Abel’s sister was ugly and Cain’s sister was beautiful, so he wanted to keep her for himself over his brother, but Adam refused that, unless they offer a sacrifice, and whoever it is accepted from, it is his, so it is accepted from Abel and not from Cain, so what happened to them is what God narrated in His Book. Mention the sayings of the commentators here Al-Suddi said, according to what was mentioned on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: That no child was born to Adam except that a girl was born with him, so he would marry the boy of this womb to the girl of this other womb, and he would marry the girl of this womb to the boy of this other womb, until he had two sons called Abel and Qabil. Qabil was a farmer, and Abel was a milker, and Qabil was the older of them, and he had a sister more beautiful than Abel’s sister, and that Abel asked to marry Qabil’s sister, but he refused, and said, She is my sister, she was born with me, and she is more beautiful than your sister, and I am more deserving of marrying her. So his father ordered him to marry her to Abel, but he refused, and they offered a sacrifice to God Almighty, which of them was more deserving of the girl, and Adam, peace be upon him, had been absent from them, and he came to Mecca to look at it, and God Almighty said: Do you know that I have a house on earth? He said: O God, no. He said: I have a house in Mecca, so go to it. Adam said to the sky: Keep my son in trust, but it refused. He said to the earth, but it refused. He said to the mountains, but they refused. He said to Cain, and it said: Yes, you go and come back and find your family as you please. When Adam set out, he offered a sacrifice, and Cain was proud of him, so he said: I have more right to it than you, she is my sister and I am older than you and I am my father’s successor. When they offered it, Abel offered a fat young tree and Cain offered a bundle of ears of corn, and he found a large ear of corn in it, so he rubbed it and ate it, so the fire came down and ate Abel’s sacrifice and left Cain’s sacrifice. He became angry and said: I will kill you so that you will not marry my sister. Abel said: God only accepts from the righteous. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who told me: Ibn Khaitham told me: I came with Saeed bin Jubair, and he told me on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It was forbidden for a woman to marry her twin brother, and he was ordered to marry her to someone other than her brothers. He used to have a man and a woman born to him in every pregnancy. While they were like that, a beautiful woman was born to him, and another ugly, hideous woman was born to him. The brother of the ugly woman said: Marry me to your sister and I will marry you to my sister. He said: No, I have more right to my sister. So they offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from the owner of the ram, but it was not accepted from the owner of the crops, so he killed him. A good chain of transmission. My father told us, Abu Salamah told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Othman bin Khaitham, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and his saying: When they offered a sacrifice so they offered their sacrifice, and the owner of the sheep brought a ram with two white horns, and the owner of the crops brought a heap of… His food, so God accepted the ram and stored it in Paradise for forty autumns. It is the ram that Abraham, peace be upon him, slaughtered. Good chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Awf told us on the authority of Abu al-Mughira on the authority of `Abdullah ibn `Amr, who said: The two sons of Adam who offered a sacrifice and it was accepted from one of them and not accepted from the other, one of them was a farmer and the other was a sheep owner. They were both commanded to offer a sacrifice, and the sheep owner offered the most honorable, fattest, and best of his sheep, and he was pleased with it. The farmer offered the worst of his farms, the colocynth and tares, and he was not pleased with it. God, the Almighty, accepted the sacrifice of the sheep owner, and He did not accept the sacrifice of the farmer. And from their story is what God has narrated in His Book. He said: By God, the one who was killed was the stronger of the two men, but his shyness prevented him from extending his hand to his brother. Ismail ibn Rafi` al-Madani, the storyteller, said: It has reached me that when the two sons of Adam were commanded to offer a sacrifice, one of them was a sheep owner and he had a lamb among his sheep, and he loved it so much that he would give it preference at night, and he would carry it on his back out of love for it, until he had no one to give it to him. Money was dearer to him than it. When he was ordered to offer the sacrifice, he offered it to God Almighty, and God accepted it from him. He continued to enjoy it in Paradise until he ransomed the son of Abraham, peace be upon him, with it. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Al-Ansari told us, Al-Qasim bin Abdul Rahman told us, Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Adam, peace be upon him, said to Abel and Cain: My Lord has promised me that there will be from my offspring someone who will offer a sacrifice, so offer a sacrifice so that my eyes may be comforted. If your sacrifice is accepted, then offer it. Abel was a sheep owner, so he offered the best of his wealth from his sheep. Cain was a farmer, so he offered a tow from his crops. Adam set out with them, and with them were their sacrifices. They climbed the mountain, and they placed their sacrifices. Then the three of them sat, Adam and they were looking at the sacrifice. Then God sent a fire, and when it was above them, a neck approached it, and it carried Abel’s sacrifice, and left Cain’s sacrifice. They turned away, and Adam knew that Cain was angry with him, so he said: Woe to you, Cain, your sacrifice was returned to you. Cain said: I loved him, so I prayed over his sacrifice and supplicated for him, so his sacrifice was accepted and my sacrifice was returned to me. Cain said to Abel: To kill you and be rid of you, your father prayed for you and prayed over your sacrifice and it was accepted from you, and he threatened to kill him until one evening Abel was detained with his sheep, so Adam said: O Cain, where is your brother? He said: And you sent me to him as a shepherd, I do not know, so Adam said: Woe to you, Cain, go and look for your brother, so Cain said to himself: Tonight I will kill him, and he took with him an iron rod and met him as he was turning over, and said: O Abel, accept your sacrifice and return mine to me so that I may kill you, so Abel said: I offered the best of my wealth, and you offered the worst of your wealth, and God does not accept except the good, God only accepts from the righteous, so when he said that, Cain became angry, so he picked up the iron rod and struck him with it, and he said: Woe to you, Cain, where are you in front of God, how will He reward you for your work? So he killed him, and threw him in a pit of the ground, and threw some dirt on him. Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated from some of the scholars of the first book: that Adam ordered his son Cain to marry his twin sister, Abel, and ordered Abel to marry Cain’s twin sister, so Abel submitted to that and was satisfied, but Cain refused and hated it out of generosity towards Abel’s sister, and he desired his sister over Abel and said: We are from the birth of Paradise, and they are from the birth of the Earth, and I am more deserving of my sister. Some of the scholars of the first book say: Cain’s sister was one of the best people, so he was stingy with her towards his brother and wanted her for himself, and God knows best which of them it was, so his father said to him: O my son, she is not lawful for you, but Cain refused to accept that from his father’s words, his father said to him: O my son, offer a sacrifice and your brother Abel will offer a sacrifice, so whichever of you accepts his sacrifice is more deserving of it, and Cain was in charge of sowing the land, and Abel was in charge of tending the livestock, so Cain offered wheat and Abel offered firstborns from the firstborns of his sheep, and some of them said: He said: He offered a cow, so God sent a white fire that ate Abel’s offering and left Cain’s offering. Thus, he accepted the offering if he accepted it. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It was their nature that no poor person was to be given charity, but rather the offering was offered by a man. While the two sons of Adam were sitting, they said, If we offered an offering. When a man offered an offering and God was pleased with him, He would send a fire to him and consume him. If God was not pleased with him, the fire would go out. So they offered an offering, and one of them was a shepherd and the other was a farmer. The owner of the sheep offered the best and fattest of his sheep, and the other offered some of his crops. Then the fire came and descended between them and consumed the sheep and left the crops. The son of Adam said to his brother, Do you walk among the people and they know that you offered an offering and it was accepted from you and returned to me? No, by God, the people will not look at me, and you are better than me. He said, I will kill you. His brother said to him, What is my sin? God only accepts from the righteous. Narrated by Ibn Jarir, so this trace indicates that the offering was not for a reason or to avoid a woman, as was previously mentioned by a group of those mentioned, and it is apparent in the Qur’an: When they both offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them but not from the other, he said, ‘I will surely kill you.’ He said, ‘God only accepts from the righteous.’ So the context indicates that he was angry with him and envied him because his offering was accepted but not his. Then it is well-known among the majority that the one who offered the sheep was Abel and the one who offered the food was Qabil, and that the sheep was accepted from Abel, until Ibn Abbas and others said that it was the ram that was used to ransom the slaughtered animal, which is appropriate, and God knows best, and it was not accepted from Qabil. This is also what was stated by more than one of the early and later generations, and it is also well-known from Mujahid, but Ibn Jarir narrated from him that he said the one who offered the crops was Qabil, and it was accepted from him. This is contrary to the well-known view, and perhaps it was not well-recorded from him, and God knows best. The meaning of his saying, God only accepts from the righteous is from those who fear God in their actions. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibrahim bin Al-Ala bin Zaid told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us, Safwan bin Amr told me on the authority of Tamim, meaning Ibn Malik Al-Muqri, who said: I heard Abu Al-Darda’ say: For me to be certain that God has accepted a single prayer from me is dearer to me than the world and what is in it, for God says, God only accepts from the righteous. My father told us, Abdullah bin Imran told us, Ishaq bin Sulaiman, meaning Al-Razi, told us on the authority of Al-Mughira bin Muslim, on the authority of Maymun bin Abi Hamza, who said: I was sitting with Abu Wa’il when a man called Abu Afif, one of the companions of Muadh, entered upon us. Shuqaiq bin Salamah said to him: O Abu Afif, will you not tell us about Muadh bin Jabal? He said: Yes, I heard him say: The people will be detained in a single place in Baqi’, then a caller will call out: Where are the righteous? So they will stand in the protection of the Most Merciful, God will not hide from them nor conceal Himself. I said: Who are the righteous? He said, People avoid polytheism and idol worship and are sincere in their worship, so they will pass to Paradise. And his saying: “If you should stretch your hand against me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear God, the Lord of the worlds.” His brother, the righteous man whose sacrifice God accepted because of his piety, said to him when his brother threatened to kill him for no sin on his part: If you should stretch your hand against me to kill me, I shall not stretch my hand against you to kill you. That is, I will not respond to your corrupt action with the same, so that you and I will be equal in sin. Indeed, I fear God, the Lord of the worlds. That is, I will not do as you want me to do, but I will be patient and seek reward. Abdullah bin Amr said: By God, he was the stronger of the two men, but his scruples prevented him, meaning his piety. That is why it was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: If two Muslims confront each other with their swords, then the killer and the killed will be in Hellfire. They said: O Messenger of God, this is the killer, but what about the killed? He said: He was eager to kill his companion. Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah ibn Sa`id told us, Layth ibn Sa`d told us, on the authority of `Ayyash ibn `Abbas, on the authority of Bakir ibn `Abdullah, on the authority of Bishr ibn Sa`id, that Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas said during the tribulation of `Uthman: I bear witness that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “There will be a tribulation in which the one who sits is better than the one who stands, and the one who stands is better than the one who walks, and the one who walks is better than the one who runs.” He said: What if someone enters my house and stretches out his hand to kill me and says, Be like the son of Adam. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it likewise on the authority of Qutaybah ibn Sa`id, and he said: This is a good hadith. There are narrations on this topic on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, Khabbab ibn al-Arat, Abu Bakr, Ibn Mas`ud, Abu Waqid, Abu Musa, and Kharsha. Some of them narrated it on the authority of al-Layth ibn Sa`d, and he added a man to the chain of transmission. Al-Hafiz Ibn `Asakir said: The man is Husayn al-Ashja`i. I said: Abu Dawud narrated it from his path, and he said: Yazid ibn Khalid al-Ramli told us, al-Fadl told us on the authority of `Ayyash ibn `Abbas, on the authority of Bakir, on the authority of Bishr ibn Sa`id, on the authority of Husayn ibn `Abd al-Rahman al-Ashja`i, that he heard Sa`d ibn Abi Waqas narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this hadith. He said: I said: O Messenger of God, what if he enters my house and stretches out his hand to kill me? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Be like the son of Adam and recited: “If you should stretch out your hand against me to kill me, I will not stretch out my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds.” Ayyub Al-Sakhtiyani said: The first person from this nation to take this verse “If you should stretch your hand against me to kill me, I will not stretch my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds” was Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Hazm told us, Abu Imran Al-Jawni told me, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Al-Samit, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, rode a donkey with me riding behind him and said: O Abu Dharr, tell me if the people are afflicted with severe hunger such that you cannot get up from your bed to go to your mosque, what would you do? He said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Be chaste. He said: O Abu Dharr, tell me if a severe death afflicts the people and the house is occupied by the slave, meaning the grave, what would you do? I said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Be patient. He said: O Abu Dharr, tell me if the people kill one another, meaning until the stones of oil are drowned in blood, what would you do? He said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Sit in your house and close your door. He said: If I do not leave you alone? He said: Then go to whoever you are from and be one of them. He said: Then I will take my weapon. He said: Then you will share in what they are doing, but if you fear that the radiance of the sword will deter you, then throw the edge of your cloak over your face so that he may bear his sin and your sin. Muslim and the people of Sunan, except for al-Nasa’i, narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Abu Imran al-Jawni on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Samit, and Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it through the chain of transmission of Hammad ibn Zayd on the authority of Abu Imran, on the authority of al-Mush’ath ibn Tarif, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Samit, on the authority of Abu Dharr, similarly. Abu Dawud said: Al-Mush’ath did not mention anyone in this hadith except Hammad ibn Zayd. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Duhaim narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, Qubaysah ibn Uqbah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Rub’i, who said: We were at the funeral of Hudhayfah and I heard a man say: I heard this man saying about some people, from what I heard. From the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “If you fight, I will look to the furthest part of my house and I will go to Paradise. If so-and-so enters upon me, I will say, ‘Here, bear my sin and your sin,’ and I will be like the best of the sons of Adam.” And his saying: “Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin and be among the companions of the Fire. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.” Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah and As-Suddi said regarding his saying: Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin meaning the sin of killing me and the sin that was upon you before that, as Ibn Jarir said. Others said: What he means by that is that I want you to bear my sin and bear its burden and your sin in killing me. This is a statement that I found from Mujahid and I fear that it is a mistake because the correct narration from him is the opposite, meaning what Sufyan Ath-Thawri narrated from Mansur from Mujahid: Indeed, I want you to bear my sin he said: by killing me and your sin he said: for what was upon you before that, and Isa bin Abi Nujayh narrated it similarly, from Mujahid, and Shibl narrated from Ibn Abi Nujayh from Mujahid: Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin he said: I want my sin and my blood to be upon you so that you bear both of them. I said Many people may imagine this statement, and they mention a hadith that has no basis in it, The killer does not leave any sin for the one killed. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated a hadith similar to this, but it is not the same. He said: Amr ibn Ali told us, Aamer ibn Ibrahim al-Isfahani told us, Yaqub ibn Abdullah told us, Utbah ibn Saeed told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Killing with patience does not pass by a sin except that it erases it.
