He said: God Almighty disliked the gouging out of eyes, so God revealed this verse: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger to the end of the verse. This is a strange hadith, and in its chain of transmission is Al-Rabdhi, who is weak. In its chain of transmission is a benefit, which is the mention of the leader of this The secret, which is Jarir bin Abdullah Al-Bajali, and it was mentioned in Sahih Muslim that this secret was twenty horsemen from the Ansar. As for his saying: God disliked the gouging out of the eyes, so God revealed this verse, then it is strange, and it was mentioned in Sahih Muslim that they gouged out the eyes of the shepherds, so what was done to them was retaliation, and God knows best. Abdul-Zarraq said on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhammad Al-Aslami, on the authority of Salih, the freed slave of Al-Taw’amah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: Some men from Banu Fazarah who had died of emaciation came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to go to his camels, so they drank from them until they recovered, then they went to his camels and stole them, so they were sought and brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he cut off their hands and feet and gouged out their eyes. Abu Hurairah said: This verse was revealed about them: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped gouging out their eyes after that. It was narrated from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Hurairah. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Al-Husayn bin Ishaq Al-Tastari told us, Abu Al-Qasim Muhammad bin Al-Waleed told us, on the authority of Amr bin Muhammad Al-Madini, Muhammad bin Talha told us, on the authority of Musa bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Taimi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Salamah bin Al-Akwa’, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a boy called Yasar. He saw that he prayed well, so he freed him and sent him with his camels in Al-Harrah, and he was there. He said: Then the people of Uraynah declared Islam, and they came while they were sick and ill, and their bellies had become large. He said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent them to Yasar, and they drank camel milk until their bellies collapsed. Then they ran after Yasar and slaughtered him, and put thorns in his eyes, then they chased the camels. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a cavalry of Muslims after them, their leader being Karz bin Jaber Al-Fihri, and he caught up with them and brought them to him, and he cut off their hands and feet and blinded them. Their eyes, very strange, and he narrated the story of the two Arabs from the hadith of a group of companions, including Jabir, Aisha, and more than one, and the great hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh took care to trace this hadith from many aspects, so may God have mercy on him and reward him. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq told us, I heard my father say: I heard Abu Hamza from Abdul Karim, and he was asked about camel urine, so he said: Saeed bin Jubair told me from the warriors, so he said: There were people who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: We pledge allegiance to you on Islam, so they pledged allegiance to him while they were lying, and they did not want Islam, then they said: We are going to Medina, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: These camels come to you in the morning and in the evening, so drink from their urine and milk, he said: While they were like that, the scream came to them, so they screamed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: They killed the shepherd and drove away the camels, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that it be announced to the al-Nas 114:O horses of God, ride, he said: So they rode, not waiting for a horseman, he said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rode after them, and they did not stop pursuing them until they brought them to their place of safety, so the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned and they had taken some of them captive, so they brought them to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God revealed: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger the verse. He said: So their exile was that they were exiled until they entered their place of safety and their land, and they were exiled from the land of the Muslims, and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed some of them and crucified them, and cut off and gouged out their eyes. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not mutilate anything before or after. He said: And he forbade mutilation, and said: And do not mutilate anything. He said: Anas used to say that, except that he said: He burned them with fire after he killed them. He said: And some of them say: They are people from Banu Salim, and some from Uraynah, and some from Bajila. The imams differed regarding the ruling on these Arabs: Is it abrogated or decisive? Some of them said: It is abrogated by this verse, and they claimed that it contains a rebuke to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, as in his saying, May God forgive you, why did you give them permission? Some of them said: It is abrogated by the Prophet’s prohibition of mutilation, and this statement is questionable, and the one who says it is required to explain the delay of the abrogating verse that he claimed after the abrogated verse. Some of them said: This was before the punishments were revealed, as Muhammad ibn Sirin said, and this is questionable, because his story is later, and in Jarir ibn Abdullah’s narration of their story there is evidence that it was later, because he converted to Islam after the revelation of the Table. Some of them said that the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, did not blind them, but rather decided to do so until the Qur’an was revealed and explained the ruling on those who fight. This statement is also questionable, because it was mentioned in the agreed upon hadith that he blinded them, and in another narration that he gouged out their eyes. Ibn Jarir said: Ali bin Sahl told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us: Al-Layth bin Saad mentioned what happened when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) blinded their eyes and left them until they died, so he said: I heard Muhammad bin Ajlan say: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) as a reprimand for that, and he taught him the punishment for their likes of killing, cutting off, and banishment, and no one else was blinded after them. He said: This statement was mentioned to Abu Amr, meaning Al-Awza’i, so he denied that it was revealed as a reprimand, and he said: Rather, the punishment for those people was their own people, then this verse was revealed regarding the punishment for others who fought after them, and the blinding was lifted from them. Then the majority of scholars used the generality of this verse as evidence in their view that the ruling on fighting in cities and on the roads is the same, based on His saying: And they strive to cause corruption in the land. This is the school of Malik, Al-Awza’i, Al-Layth bin Saad, Al-Shafi’i, and Ahmad bin Hanbal, until Malik said about the one who assassinates a man and deceives him until he enters a house and kills him, And he takes what he has with him: This is fighting, and his blood is for the Sultan, not for the guardian of the murdered person, and his pardon is not taken into account in dropping the killing. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: Fighting only takes place on the roads, but not in the cities, because help will reach him if he calls for help, unlike the road because of its distance from those who can help and support him. And the Almighty’s saying: That they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off from opposite sides or that they be exiled from the land. Ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: Whoever draws arms in the army of Islam, and frightens the wayfarer, then he is captured and overpowered, then the leader of the Muslims has the choice regarding him. If he wishes, he may kill him, or if he wishes, he may crucify him, or if he wishes, he may cut off his hand and foot. And this is what Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Mujahid, Ata’, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, and Ad-Dahhak said. Abu Ja’far bin Jarir narrated all of this, and he narrated something similar on the authority of Malik bin Anas, may God have mercy on him. The basis for this statement is that the apparent meaning of or is for choice, as in similar verses in the Qur’an, such as His saying regarding the penalty for hunting: “Then the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from livestock, as judged by two just men among you, as an offering delivered to the Ka’bah, or an expiation of feeding poor people, or its equivalent in fasting.” And His saying regarding the expiation of ransom: But if any of you is ill or has an ailment in his head, [he must] offer a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice. And His saying regarding the expiation of an oath: Then its expiation is feeding ten. Poor people, from the average of what you feed your families, or clothing them, or freeing a slave. All of these are optional, so let this verse be the same. The majority said: This verse was revealed in terms of circumstances, as Abu Abdullah Al-Shafi’i said: Ibrahim bin Abi Yahya informed us on the authority of Salih, the client of Al-Taw’amah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding highway robbers: If they kill and take money, they are killed and crucified. If they kill but do not take money, they are killed but not crucified. If they take money but do not kill, their hands and feet are cut off from opposite sides. If they frighten people on the road but do not take money, they are banished from the land. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it on the authority of Abd Al-Rahim bin Sulayman, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, in a similar manner, and on the authority of Abu Mukhallad, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, and Ata Al-Khurasani, in a similar manner. More than one of the early Muslims and imams said the same, and they differed: Should he be crucified alive and left until he dies by preventing him from food and drink, or by killing him with a spear or something similar, or should he be killed first and then crucified as a punishment and punishment for other corruptors? Should he be crucified for three days and then disembarked, or should he be left until his pus flows? There is a difference of opinion on all of this, which will be discussed in its proper place. We trust in God and rely on Him. This detail is supported by the hadith narrated by Ibn Jarir in his Tafsir, if its chain of transmission is sound. He said: Ali ibn Sahl told us, Al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, that Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan wrote to Anas ibn Malik asking him about this verse. He wrote to him informing him that it was revealed about those Arab men from Bajila. Anas said: They apostatized from Islam, killed the shepherd, drove away the camels, frightened the wayfarers, and violated the forbidden vagina. Anas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel, peace be upon him, about the ruling on those who wage war, and he said: Whoever steals money and frightens the wayfarers, cut off his hand for stealing and his foot for frightening him. Whoever kills, kill him. Whoever kills and frightens the wayfarers and violates the forbidden vagina, crucify him. As for the Almighty’s saying: or be banished from the land, some of them said: It means that he is sought until he is caught and the prescribed punishment is carried out on him or he flees from the land of Islam. This was narrated by Ibn Jarir on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Anas bin Malik, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, Az-Zuhri, Al-Layth bin Sa’d, and Malik bin Anas. Others said: It means that he is banished from his country to another country or that the sultan or his deputy removes him from his dealings completely. Ash-Sha’bi said: He is banished - as Ibn Hubayrah said - from all his work. Ata’ Al-Khurasani said that he is banished from one army to another for years, but he is not expelled from the land of Islam. This is also what Saeed bin Jubayr, Abu Al-Sha’tha’, Al-Hasan, Az-Zuhri, Ad-Dahhak, and Muqatil bin Hayyan said, that he is banished but not expelled from the land of Islam. Others said: What is meant by banishment here is imprisonment, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifa and his companions. Ibn Jarir chose that what is meant by banishment here is that he is expelled from his country to another country and imprisoned there. And the Almighty said: That is for them a disgrace in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment. That is, what I mentioned of killing them, crucifying them, cutting off their hands and feet from opposite sides, and banishing them, is a disgrace for them among the people in this worldly life, along with what God has stored up for them of great punishment on the Day of Resurrection. This supports the statement of those who said: It was revealed about the polytheists. As for the people of Islam, in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took from us as he took from women, that we would not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill our children, nor bite each other. So whoever among you fulfills his obligation, his reward is with God Almighty. And whoever commits any of that and is punished, it is an expiation for him. And whoever God conceals, his matter is up to God: If He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will pardon him. And on the authority of Ali, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever commits a sin in this world and is punished for it, God is more just than to double His punishment for His servant. And whoever commits a sin in this world, God conceals it for him and pardons him.” On his authority, God is too generous to return to him in something that He has pardoned.” Narrated by Imam Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and strange. Al-Hafiz Al-Daraqutni was asked about this hadith, and he said: It was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet and with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. He said: Its chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet is authentic. Ibn Jarir said about His statement: That is for them a disgrace in this world, meaning evil, shame, humiliation, degradation and punishment in this world before the Hereafter. And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment, meaning if they do not repent from their action until they perish in the Hereafter along with the recompense with which You punished them in this world, and the punishment with which You punished them therein, a great punishment, meaning the punishment of Hell. And the statement of the Most High: “Except for those who repent before you have them in your power. So know that God is Forgiving and Merciful,” as for the statement of those who said that it is for the people of polytheism, then it is clear. As for the Muslim combatants, if they repent before they are in your power, then the inevitable killing, crucifixion and amputation of the leg is dropped from them. Is the amputation of the hand dropped or not? There are two opinions of the scholars, and the apparent meaning of the verse requires that all of them be dropped, and this is what the Companions acted upon, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashja’ told us, Abu Usama told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: Haritha bin Badr Al-Tamimi was from the people of Basra, and he had caused corruption in the land and fought, so he spoke to men from Quraysh, including Al-Hasan bin Ali, Ibn Abbas, and Abdullah bin Ja’far, and they spoke to Ali about him, but he did not grant him security, so he came to Saeed bin Qais Al-Hamdani and left him in his house, then he came to Ali and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what do you think of someone who fought God and His Messenger, and sought to spread corruption in the land, so he recited until he reached except those who repent before you have them in your power He said: So he wrote him a security, Saeed bin Qais said: He is Haritha bin Badr, and Ibn Jarir narrated it in the same way from other sources on the authority of Mujalid on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, and he added, so Haritha bin Badr said: Have you not reached Hamdan? Have you not met her far away? No enemy can escape her fault. By the life of her father, Hamdan fears God and her fiancé rules according to the Book. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri on the authority of al-Suddi, and on the authority of Ash’ath, both on the authority of Amir al-Sha’bi, who said: A man from Murad came to Abu Musa while he was in Kufa during the emirate of Uthman, may God be pleased with him, after he had prayed the obligatory prayer. He said: O Abu Musa, this is the place of the one seeking refuge with you. I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so al-Muradi. I fought against God and His Messenger and sought to spread corruption on earth. I repented before you could overpower me. Abu Musa said: This is so-and-so, son of so-and-so. He fought against God and His Messenger and sought to spread corruption on earth. He repented before we could overpower him. Whoever meets him should not treat him except with good. If he is truthful, then it is the way of the truthful. If he is a liar, his sins will overtake him. The man stayed as long as God willed. Then he went out, and God Almighty overtook him with his sins and killed him. Then Ibn Jarir said: Ali told me, al-Walid ibn Muslim told us. Al-Layth said: And Musa ibn Ishaq al-Madani, who is the emir according to us, told me likewise that Ali al-Asadi fought and frightened. The way and he took blood and money, so the imams and the common people sought him, but he refused and they could not find him until he came repentant, and that is because he heard a man reciting this verse: “O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.” So he stopped at him and said: O servant of God, recite it again. So he repeated it to him, so he sheathed his sword, then he came repentant until he arrived in Medina at dawn, so he washed himself and then came to the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and prayed the dawn prayer, then he sat with Abu Hurairah in the midst of his companions. When dawn broke, the people recognized him and stood up to him, so he said: You have no way against me, I came repentant before you could find me. Abu Hurairah said: He is truthful, and he took him by the hand until he came to Marwan bin Al-Hakam, who was the governor of Medina during the time of Muawiyah, and said: This is Ali, he came repentant and you have no way against him or killing, so he left all of that. He said: Ali went out repentant, fighting in the way of God at sea, so they met the Romans, so they brought his ship close to one of their ships, so he stormed the Romans in Their ship sank, so they fled from it to the other side, but it tilted with them and they all drowned.
5:34: God Almighty says: Because of the son of Adam killing his brother unjustly and aggressively, We decreed for the Children of Israel meaning We legislated for them and informed them “that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had killed all mankind. And whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved all mankind” meaning whoever kills a soul without a reason such as retaliation or corruption in the land, and considers killing it permissible without a reason or crime, it is as if he had killed all mankind, because he does not differentiate between one soul and another. And whoever saves a life, meaning he forbade killing it and believed in that, then all people were safe from him on this basis. That is why he said it is as if he had saved all mankind. Al-A’mash and others said, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: I entered upon Uthman on the day of the house and said: I have come to support you, and the beating has become pleasant, O Commander of the Faithful. So he said: O Abu Hurairah, would you like to kill all the people and me with them? I said: No. He said: If you kill one man, it is as if you killed all of humanity, so leave with permission and reward, not sin. He said: So I left and did not fight. Ali bin Abi Talha said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is as God Almighty said: “Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had slain mankind entirely. And whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely.” And saving a life means that he does not kill a soul that God has forbidden. So that is what saves the life of all of humanity, meaning that whoever has forbidden killing it except for a right, saves the people from it. And thus Mujahid said: And whoever saves a life, that is, he refrains from killing it. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: It is as if he had killed all of mankind, meaning: Whoever kills a single soul that God has forbidden, is like someone who has killed all of mankind. Saeed bin Jubair said: Whoever considers the blood of a Muslim permissible, it is as if he has considered the blood of all of mankind permissible, and whoever considers the blood of a Muslim forbidden, it is as if he has considered the blood of all of mankind forbidden. This is one statement and it is the most apparent. Ikrimah and Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Whoever kills a prophet or a just leader, it is as if he has killed all of mankind, and whoever supports a prophet or a just leader, it is as if he has saved the lives of all of mankind. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Mujahid said in another narration on his authority: Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul, it is as if he had killed all of mankind, because whoever kills a soul will be in Hellfire, so it is as if he had killed all of mankind. Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Al-A’raj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: It is as if he had killed all of mankind, whoever intentionally kills a believing soul, God will make Hell his punishment, and He will be angry with him and curse him, and prepare for him a great punishment. He says: If he had killed all of mankind, it would not have been more than that punishment. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: And whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved all of mankind, he said: Whoever does not kill anyone has saved all of mankind from him. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: Whoever kills a soul, it is as if he has killed all mankind, meaning that retaliation is obligatory upon him, so there is no difference between one person and a group. And whoever saves a soul, i.e., pardons the killer of his guardian, it is as if he has saved all mankind. And he narrated that from his father, narrated by Ibn Jarir. And Mujahid said in a narration: And whoever saves a soul, i.e., saves it from drowning, burning, or destruction. And al-Hasan and Qatadah said regarding his statement: Whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land, it is as if he had killed all mankind, this is an exaggeration of committing murder. Qatadah said: Great, by God, is its sin, and great, by God, is its reward. And Ibn al-Mubarak said, on the authority of Salam ibn Miski, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Ali al-Rab’i, he said: I said to al-Hasan: This verse is for us, O Abu Sa’id, as it was for the Children of Israel. So he said: Yes, by the One besides Whom there is no god, as it was for the Children of Israel, and He did not make the blood of the Children of Israel more precious to God than our blood. And al-Hasan al-Basri said: It is as if he had killed all mankind, he said: A sin, and Whoever saves a soul, it is as if he had killed all mankind. It is as if he had saved all of mankind,” he said: A reward. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Huyayy ibn Abdullah told us, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, give me something to live on. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Hamza, is a soul that you save more beloved to you than a soul that you kill? He said: Rather, a soul that I save. He said: Take care of yourself. The Almighty says: And indeed Our messengers came to them with clear proofs, meaning with arguments, evidence, and clear proofs. Then many of them, after that, were transgressors in the land. This is a rebuke and rebuke to them for committing forbidden acts after they knew about them, just as the Banu Qurayzah, the Nadir, and others from Banu Qaynuqa’ who were around Medina from the Jews who used to fight with the Aws and the Khazraj, when wars broke out between them in the pre-Islamic era, then when the wars ended. They ransomed those they captured and loved those they killed. God has denied this to them in Surat Al-Baqarah, where He says: “And when We took a covenant from you, ‘You shall not shed one another’s blood, nor expel one another from your homes,’ then you acknowledged it, while you were witnesses. Then it is you who kill yourselves and expel a party of you from their homes, supporting one another against them in sin and aggression. And if they come to you as captives, you ransom them, although their expulsion was forbidden to you. Then what is the reward of those who do that among you except disgrace in the life of this world? And on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned to the severest of the punishment. And God is not unaware of what you do.” And His saying, “The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive upon earth to cause corruption is that they will be killed or crucified or have their hands and feet on alternate sides cut off or be exiled from the land,” the verse. Warfare is opposition and opposition, and it is true of disbelief, highway robbery, and frightening the wayfarer. Likewise, corruption on earth is applied to types of evil, to the extent that many of the Salaf, including Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, said: Seizing dirhams and dinars is corruption on earth. God the Almighty said: “And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and animals. And God does not love corruption.” Then some of them said: This noble verse was revealed about the polytheists, as Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us on the authority of Yazid on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, they said: “The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive to cause corruption upon earth is that they will be killed or crucified or have their hands and feet on alternate sides cut off or be exiled from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world, and in the Hereafter they will have a great punishment. Except for those who repent before you are able to overpower them. So know that God is Forgiving and Merciful.” This verse was revealed about the polytheists, so whoever among them repents before you are able to overpower him, there is no way against him, and this verse does not protect a Muslim man from the punishment if he kills, or causes corruption on the land, or wages war against God and His Messenger, then joins the infidels before they are able to overpower him, that does not prevent him from having the punishment he committed carried out on him. Abu Dawud and An-Nasa'i, through Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive to cause corruption on earth was revealed regarding the polytheists who repented before he was overpowered. That did not prevent him from having the prescribed punishment carried out on him. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive to cause corruption on earth the verse, he said: There were a group of people from the People of the Book between whom and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a covenant and a pact, so they broke the covenant and spread corruption on earth, so God gave His Messenger the choice: if He wished, he could kill them or if He wished, he could cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Shu`bah narrated on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hilal ibn Yassaf, on the authority of Mus`ab ibn Sa`d, on the authority of his father, who said: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive to cause corruption in the land was revealed concerning the Kharijites. Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. The correct view is that this verse is general in its application to the polytheists and others who committed these characteristics, as narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim from the hadith of Abu Qilabah, whose name was `Abdullah ibn Zayd al-Jarmi al-Basri, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that eight men from `Ukl came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and pledged allegiance to him on Islam. They felt ill in Medina and their bodies became sick, so they complained about that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Why don’t you go out with our shepherd with his camels and drink from their urine and milk? They said: Yes. So they went out and drank from their urine and milk and recovered, so they killed the shepherd and drove away the camels. report of that reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he sent after them and they caught up with them and brought them, so he ordered…” Their hands and feet were cut off, their eyes were gouged out, and they were thrown out into the sun until they died. This is the wording of Muslim. In another wording of theirs: from Ukul or Uraynah. In another wording: and they were thrown into the lava field and began to pray for rain, but they were not given rain. In a wording of Muslim: And he did not cut them off. And in Bukhari, Abu Qilabah said: These people stole, killed, and disbelieved after their belief, and fought against God and His Messenger. And Muslim narrated it through the chain of transmission of Hisham from Abdul Aziz bin Suhaib, and Hamid from Anas, so he mentioned something similar to it, and with him they apostatized. And they included it through the narration of Qatada from Anas in a similar manner. And Saeed said from Qatada: From Ukl and Uraynah. And Muslim narrated it through the chain of transmission of Sulayman al-Taymi, from Anas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, only gouged out the eyes of those people because they gouged out the eyes of the shepherds. And Muslim narrated it through the hadith of Muawiyah bin Qurrah from Anas, who said: A group of people from Uraynah came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they converted to Islam and pledged allegiance to him, and blood had been shed in Medina, which is leprosy. Then he mentioned something similar to their hadith and added: With him were young men from the Ansar, about twenty, horsemen, so he sent them out and sent with them a tracker to follow their tracks. And all of these are the words of Muslim, may God have mercy on him. Hammad bin Salamah said: Qatada, Thabit al-Banani and Hamid al-Tawil narrated to us on the authority of Anas bin Malik that some people from Uraynah came to Madinah and were thirsty. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent them with the camels of charity and ordered them to drink from their urine and milk. They did so and recovered. They apostatized from Islam, killed the shepherd and drove the camels away. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent after them and they were brought back. He cut off their hands and feet on opposite sides, gouged out their eyes and threw them into the lava field. Anas said: I saw one of them striking the ground with his mouth out of thirst until they died. Then the verse was revealed: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger al-Baqarah 2:177. It was narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i and Ibn Mardawayh, and this is its wording. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan sahih. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through many chains of narration on the authority of Anas bin Malik, including what he narrated through two chains of narration on the authority of Salam bin Abi Al-Sahbaa, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: I have never regretted a hadith, as I have regretted a hadith that Al-Hajjaj asked me about, he said: Tell me about the most severe punishment with which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, punished. He said: I said: A group of people from Uraynah in Bahrain came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and complained to the Messenger of God about what they had suffered from their stomachs, their colors had turned yellow and their stomachs had shriveled up, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to go to the camels of charity and drink from their urine and milk, until their colors had returned to them and their stomachs had shriveled up, then they went to the shepherd and killed him, and drove away the camels, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent after them and cut off their hands and feet and gouged out their eyes, then threw them into the hot sand until they died. Whenever Al-Hajjaj ascended the pulpit, he would say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cut off the hands and feet of some people, then threw them into the hot sand until they died, just like a herd of camels. Al-Hajjaj would use this hadith as evidence for the people. Ibn Jarir said: Ali bin Sahl told us, Al-Walid - meaning Ibn Muslim - told us, Saeed told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, who said: There were four men from Uraynah and three men from Ukl. When they were brought to him, he cut off their hands and feet, gouged out their eyes, did not cauterize them and left them to pick up stones in Al-Harrah. So God revealed about that: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger Al-Ma’idah 1:17. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Harb Al-Mawsili told us, Abu Masoud, meaning Abdul Rahman bin Al-Hasan Al-Zajjaj told us, Abu Saeed, meaning the grocer, told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: There were a group of people from Uraynah who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were exhausted, their colors were yellow, and their bellies were large. So he ordered them to catch up with the camels and drink from their urine and milk, so they did, and their colors became yellow, their bellies became empty, and they grew fat. So they killed the shepherd and drove away the camels. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent someone to pursue them, and they were brought, and some of them were killed, and the eyes of some of them were gouged out, and the hands and feet of some of them were cut off, and the verse was revealed: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger until the end of the verse. Abu Ja`far bin Jarir said: Abu Ali bin Sahl told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Yazid bin Lahi`ah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Habib that Abdul Malik bin Marwan wrote to Anas asking him about this verse, so Anas wrote to him informing him that this verse was revealed about those people. The Arniyyin, who were from Bajila. Anas said: They apostatized from Islam, killed the shepherd, drove away the camels, frightened the wayfarers, and committed unlawful sexual intercourse. Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ubayd God, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar or Amr - Yunus was uncertain - on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with that, meaning the story of the Arniyyin, and the verse of fighting was revealed about them. Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, and in it on the authority of Ibn Umar without a doubt. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Khalaf told us, Al-Hasan ibn Hammad told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Hashim, on the authority of Musa ibn Ubaydah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Jarir, who said: A group of people from Uraynah came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, barefoot and harmed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to be killed. When they recovered and became strong, they killed the shepherds of the camels, then they went out with the camels, intending to go to the land of their people. Jarir said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me with a group of Muslims until we caught up with them after they had reached the land of their people. We brought them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he cut off their hands and feet from opposite sides, and gouged out their eyes. They kept saying: Water, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Fire, until they perished. He said: God Almighty disliked the gouging out of eyes, so God revealed this verse: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger to the end of the verse. This is a strange hadith, and in its chain of transmission is Al-Rabdhi, who is weak. In its chain of transmission is a benefit, which is the mention of the leader of this The secret, which is Jarir bin Abdullah Al-Bajali, and it was mentioned in Sahih Muslim that this secret was twenty horsemen from the Ansar. As for his saying: God disliked the gouging out of the eyes, so God revealed this verse, then it is strange, and it was mentioned in Sahih Muslim that they gouged out the eyes of the shepherds, so what was done to them was retaliation, and God knows best. Abdul-Zarraq said on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhammad Al-Aslami, on the authority of Salih, the freed slave of Al-Taw’amah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: Some men from Banu Fazarah who had died of emaciation came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to go to his camels, so they drank from them until they recovered, then they went to his camels and stole them, so they were sought and brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he cut off their hands and feet and gouged out their eyes. Abu Hurairah said: This verse was revealed about them: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped gouging out their eyes after that. It was narrated from another chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Hurairah. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Al-Husayn bin Ishaq Al-Tastari told us, Abu Al-Qasim Muhammad bin Al-Waleed told us, on the authority of Amr bin Muhammad Al-Madini, Muhammad bin Talha told us, on the authority of Musa bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Taimi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Salamah bin Al-Akwa’, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a boy called Yasar. He saw that he prayed well, so he freed him and sent him with his camels in Al-Harrah, and he was there. He said: Then the people of Uraynah declared Islam, and they came while they were sick and ill, and their bellies had become large. He said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent them to Yasar, and they drank camel milk until their bellies collapsed. Then they ran after Yasar and slaughtered him, and put thorns in his eyes, then they chased the camels. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a cavalry of Muslims after them, their leader being Karz bin Jaber Al-Fihri, and he caught up with them and brought them to him, and he cut off their hands and feet and blinded them. Their eyes, very strange, and he narrated the story of the two Arabs from the hadith of a group of companions, including Jabir, Aisha, and more than one, and the great hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh took care to trace this hadith from many aspects, so may God have mercy on him and reward him. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq told us, I heard my father say: I heard Abu Hamza from Abdul Karim, and he was asked about camel urine, so he said: Saeed bin Jubair told me from the warriors, so he said: There were people who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: We pledge allegiance to you on Islam, so they pledged allegiance to him while they were lying, and they did not want Islam, then they said: We are going to Medina, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: These camels come to you in the morning and in the evening, so drink from their urine and milk, he said: While they were like that, the scream came to them, so they screamed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: They killed the shepherd and drove away the camels, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that it be announced to the al-Nas 114:O horses of God, ride, he said: So they rode, not waiting for a horseman, he said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rode after them, and they did not stop pursuing them until they brought them to their place of safety, so the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned and they had taken some of them captive, so they brought them to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God revealed: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger the verse. He said: So their exile was that they were exiled until they entered their place of safety and their land, and they were exiled from the land of the Muslims, and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed some of them and crucified them, and cut off and gouged out their eyes. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not mutilate anything before or after. He said: And he forbade mutilation, and said: And do not mutilate anything. He said: Anas used to say that, except that he said: He burned them with fire after he killed them. He said: And some of them say: They are people from Banu Salim, and some from Uraynah, and some from Bajila. The imams differed regarding the ruling on these Arabs: Is it abrogated or decisive? Some of them said: It is abrogated by this verse, and they claimed that it contains a rebuke to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, as in his saying, May God forgive you, why did you give them permission? Some of them said: It is abrogated by the Prophet’s prohibition of mutilation, and this statement is questionable, and the one who says it is required to explain the delay of the abrogating verse that he claimed after the abrogated verse. Some of them said: This was before the punishments were revealed, as Muhammad ibn Sirin said, and this is questionable, because his story is later, and in Jarir ibn Abdullah’s narration of their story there is evidence that it was later, because he converted to Islam after the revelation of the Table. Some of them said that the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, did not blind them, but rather decided to do so until the Qur’an was revealed and explained the ruling on those who fight. This statement is also questionable, because it was mentioned in the agreed upon hadith that he blinded them, and in another narration that he gouged out their eyes. Ibn Jarir said: Ali bin Sahl told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us: Al-Layth bin Saad mentioned what happened when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) blinded their eyes and left them until they died, so he said: I heard Muhammad bin Ajlan say: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) as a reprimand for that, and he taught him the punishment for their likes of killing, cutting off, and banishment, and no one else was blinded after them. He said: This statement was mentioned to Abu Amr, meaning Al-Awza’i, so he denied that it was revealed as a reprimand, and he said: Rather, the punishment for those people was their own people, then this verse was revealed regarding the punishment for others who fought after them, and the blinding was lifted from them. Then the majority of scholars used the generality of this verse as evidence in their view that the ruling on fighting in cities and on the roads is the same, based on His saying: And they strive to cause corruption in the land. This is the school of Malik, Al-Awza’i, Al-Layth bin Saad, Al-Shafi’i, and Ahmad bin Hanbal, until Malik said about the one who assassinates a man and deceives him until he enters a house and kills him, And he takes what he has with him: This is fighting, and his blood is for the Sultan, not for the guardian of the murdered person, and his pardon is not taken into account in dropping the killing. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: Fighting only takes place on the roads, but not in the cities, because help will reach him if he calls for help, unlike the road because of its distance from those who can help and support him. And the Almighty’s saying: That they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off from opposite sides or that they be exiled from the land. Ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: Whoever draws arms in the army of Islam, and frightens the wayfarer, then he is captured and overpowered, then the leader of the Muslims has the choice regarding him. If he wishes, he may kill him, or if he wishes, he may crucify him, or if he wishes, he may cut off his hand and foot. And this is what Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Mujahid, Ata’, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, and Ad-Dahhak said. Abu Ja’far bin Jarir narrated all of this, and he narrated something similar on the authority of Malik bin Anas, may God have mercy on him. The basis for this statement is that the apparent meaning of or is for choice, as in similar verses in the Qur’an, such as His saying regarding the penalty for hunting: “Then the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from livestock, as judged by two just men among you, as an offering delivered to the Ka’bah, or an expiation of feeding poor people, or its equivalent in fasting.” And His saying regarding the expiation of ransom: But if any of you is ill or has an ailment in his head, [he must] offer a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice. And His saying regarding the expiation of an oath: Then its expiation is feeding ten. Poor people, from the average of what you feed your families, or clothing them, or freeing a slave. All of these are optional, so let this verse be the same. The majority said: This verse was revealed in terms of circumstances, as Abu Abdullah Al-Shafi’i said: Ibrahim bin Abi Yahya informed us on the authority of Salih, the client of Al-Taw’amah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding highway robbers: If they kill and take money, they are killed and crucified. If they kill but do not take money, they are killed but not crucified. If they take money but do not kill, their hands and feet are cut off from opposite sides. If they frighten people on the road but do not take money, they are banished from the land. Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it on the authority of Abd Al-Rahim bin Sulayman, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, in a similar manner, and on the authority of Abu Mukhallad, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, and Ata Al-Khurasani, in a similar manner. More than one of the early Muslims and imams said the same, and they differed: Should he be crucified alive and left until he dies by preventing him from food and drink, or by killing him with a spear or something similar, or should he be killed first and then crucified as a punishment and punishment for other corruptors? Should he be crucified for three days and then disembarked, or should he be left until his pus flows? There is a difference of opinion on all of this, which will be discussed in its proper place. We trust in God and rely on Him. This detail is supported by the hadith narrated by Ibn Jarir in his Tafsir, if its chain of transmission is sound. He said: Ali ibn Sahl told us, Al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, that Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan wrote to Anas ibn Malik asking him about this verse. He wrote to him informing him that it was revealed about those Arab men from Bajila. Anas said: They apostatized from Islam, killed the shepherd, drove away the camels, frightened the wayfarers, and violated the forbidden vagina. Anas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel, peace be upon him, about the ruling on those who wage war, and he said: Whoever steals money and frightens the wayfarers, cut off his hand for stealing and his foot for frightening him. Whoever kills, kill him. Whoever kills and frightens the wayfarers and violates the forbidden vagina, crucify him. As for the Almighty’s saying: or be banished from the land, some of them said: It means that he is sought until he is caught and the prescribed punishment is carried out on him or he flees from the land of Islam. This was narrated by Ibn Jarir on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Anas bin Malik, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, Az-Zuhri, Al-Layth bin Sa’d, and Malik bin Anas. Others said: It means that he is banished from his country to another country or that the sultan or his deputy removes him from his dealings completely. Ash-Sha’bi said: He is banished - as Ibn Hubayrah said - from all his work. Ata’ Al-Khurasani said that he is banished from one army to another for years, but he is not expelled from the land of Islam. This is also what Saeed bin Jubayr, Abu Al-Sha’tha’, Al-Hasan, Az-Zuhri, Ad-Dahhak, and Muqatil bin Hayyan said, that he is banished but not expelled from the land of Islam. Others said: What is meant by banishment here is imprisonment, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifa and his companions. Ibn Jarir chose that what is meant by banishment here is that he is expelled from his country to another country and imprisoned there. And the Almighty said: That is for them a disgrace in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment. That is, what I mentioned of killing them, crucifying them, cutting off their hands and feet from opposite sides, and banishing them, is a disgrace for them among the people in this worldly life, along with what God has stored up for them of great punishment on the Day of Resurrection. This supports the statement of those who said: It was revealed about the polytheists. As for the people of Islam, in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took from us as he took from women, that we would not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill our children, nor bite each other. So whoever among you fulfills his obligation, his reward is with God Almighty. And whoever commits any of that and is punished, it is an expiation for him. And whoever God conceals, his matter is up to God: If He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will pardon him. And on the authority of Ali, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever commits a sin in this world and is punished for it, God is more just than to double His punishment for His servant. And whoever commits a sin in this world, God conceals it for him and pardons him.” On his authority, God is too generous to return to him in something that He has pardoned.” Narrated by Imam Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and strange. Al-Hafiz Al-Daraqutni was asked about this hadith, and he said: It was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet and with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. He said: Its chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet is authentic. Ibn Jarir said about His statement: That is for them a disgrace in this world, meaning evil, shame, humiliation, degradation and punishment in this world before the Hereafter. And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment, meaning if they do not repent from their action until they perish in the Hereafter along with the recompense with which You punished them in this world, and the punishment with which You punished them therein, a great punishment, meaning the punishment of Hell. And the statement of the Most High: “Except for those who repent before you have them in your power. So know that God is Forgiving and Merciful,” as for the statement of those who said that it is for the people of polytheism, then it is clear. As for the Muslim combatants, if they repent before they are in your power, then the inevitable killing, crucifixion and amputation of the leg is dropped from them. Is the amputation of the hand dropped or not? There are two opinions of the scholars, and the apparent meaning of the verse requires that all of them be dropped, and this is what the Companions acted upon, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashja’ told us, Abu Usama told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: Haritha bin Badr Al-Tamimi was from the people of Basra, and he had caused corruption in the land and fought, so he spoke to men from Quraysh, including Al-Hasan bin Ali, Ibn Abbas, and Abdullah bin Ja’far, and they spoke to Ali about him, but he did not grant him security, so he came to Saeed bin Qais Al-Hamdani and left him in his house, then he came to Ali and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what do you think of someone who fought God and His Messenger, and sought to spread corruption in the land, so he recited until he reached except those who repent before you have them in your power He said: So he wrote him a security, Saeed bin Qais said: He is Haritha bin Badr, and Ibn Jarir narrated it in the same way from other sources on the authority of Mujalid on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, and he added, so Haritha bin Badr said: Have you not reached Hamdan? Have you not met her far away? No enemy can escape her fault. By the life of her father, Hamdan fears God and her fiancé rules according to the Book. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri on the authority of al-Suddi, and on the authority of Ash’ath, both on the authority of Amir al-Sha’bi, who said: A man from Murad came to Abu Musa while he was in Kufa during the emirate of Uthman, may God be pleased with him, after he had prayed the obligatory prayer. He said: O Abu Musa, this is the place of the one seeking refuge with you. I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so al-Muradi. I fought against God and His Messenger and sought to spread corruption on earth. I repented before you could overpower me. Abu Musa said: This is so-and-so, son of so-and-so. He fought against God and His Messenger and sought to spread corruption on earth. He repented before we could overpower him. Whoever meets him should not treat him except with good. If he is truthful, then it is the way of the truthful. If he is a liar, his sins will overtake him. The man stayed as long as God willed. Then he went out, and God Almighty overtook him with his sins and killed him. Then Ibn Jarir said: Ali told me, al-Walid ibn Muslim told us. Al-Layth said: And Musa ibn Ishaq al-Madani, who is the emir according to us, told me likewise that Ali al-Asadi fought and frightened. The way and he took blood and money, so the imams and the common people sought him, but he refused and they could not find him until he came repentant, and that is because he heard a man reciting this verse: “O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.” So he stopped at him and said: O servant of God, recite it again. So he repeated it to him, so he sheathed his sword, then he came repentant until he arrived in Medina at dawn, so he washed himself and then came to the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and prayed the dawn prayer, then he sat with Abu Hurairah in the midst of his companions. When dawn broke, the people recognized him and stood up to him, so he said: You have no way against me, I came repentant before you could find me. Abu Hurairah said: He is truthful, and he took him by the hand until he came to Marwan bin Al-Hakam, who was the governor of Medina during the time of Muawiyah, and said: This is Ali, he came repentant and you have no way against him or killing, so he left all of that. He said: Ali went out repentant, fighting in the way of God at sea, so they met the Romans, so they brought his ship close to one of their ships, so he stormed the Romans in Their ship sank, so they fled from it to the other side, but it tilted with them and they all drowned.
5:35: The Almighty says, commanding His believing servants to fear Him, and if it is coupled with His obedience, it means refraining from what is forbidden and abandoning what is prohibited. And after that He said, And seek the means of approach to Him. Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of Talhah, on the authority of Ata', on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning closeness. And this is what Mujahid, Abu Wa'il, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abdullah ibn Kathir, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd, and more than one said. Qatadah said: meaning, draw near to Him by obeying Him and doing what pleases Him. And Ibn Zayd read, Those are the ones they call upon, seeking the means of approach to their Lord. And what these imams said is not disputed among the commentators. And Ibn Jarir recited the following poet's saying: If the informers are absent-minded, we will return to our connection and the reconciliation between us and the means will return The means is that by which one reaches the desired goal. The means is also a sign of the highest station in Paradise, which is the station of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his home in Paradise. It is the closest place in Paradise to the Throne. It has been proven in Sahih al-Bukhari on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever says when he hears the call: ‘O God, Lord of this perfect call and the established prayer, grant Muhammad the means and excellence, and raise him to the praised station that You promised him,’ then intercession will be permitted for him on the Day of Resurrection.” [Another hadith] - In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ka`b ibn Alqamah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-`As, that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, “When you hear the muezzin, say what he says, then pray for me, for whoever prays for me, God will pray for him ten times. Then ask for intercession for me, for it is a station in Paradise that is not appropriate for anyone but one of God’s servants, and I hope that I am that one. Whoever asks for intercession for me, intercession will be granted to him.” [Another Hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Ka’b, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When you send blessings upon me, then ask for al-Wasilah for me. It was said: O Messenger of God, what is al-Wasilah? He said: The highest degree in Paradise, which none will attain except one man, and I hope that I am he. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Abu Asim, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Laith ibn Abi Sulaym, on the authority of Ka’b, who said: Abu Hurayrah told me, then he said: It is strange, and Ka’b is not well-known, we do not know anyone who narrated from him except Laith ibn Abi Sulaym. [Another hadith] - On the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Abdul-Baqi bin Qani’ told us, Muhammad bin Nasr al-Tirmidhi told us, Abdul-Hamid bin Salih told us, Ibn Shihab told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of al-Mu’alla, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: Pray for me as you pray and ask God to grant me al-Wasilah. So they asked Him, or He told them that al-Wasilah is a degree in Paradise that only one man will attain, and I hope that I will be that. [Another Hadith] - Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad bin Ali Al-Abbar told us, Al-Walid bin Abdul Malik Al-Harrani told us, Musa bin A’yan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr bin Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Ask God for me the means, for no servant asks for it from me in this world except that I will be a witness or intercessor for him on the Day of Resurrection. Then Al-Tabarani said: No one narrated it from Ibn Abi Dhi’b except Musa bin A’yan, that’s what he said. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it: Muhammad bin Ali bin Duhaim told us, Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, Musa bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr bin Ata’, and he mentioned something similar with his chain of transmission. [Another hadith] - Ibn Mardawayh narrated with his chain of transmission on the authority of Amara bin Ghaziya, on the authority of Musa bin Wardan, that he heard Abu Saeed Al-Khudri say that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, intercession is a degree with God, and there is no degree above it, so ask God to grant me intercession over His creation. [Another hadith] - Ibn Mardawayh also narrated through two chains of transmission on the authority of Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahr, who told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: In Paradise there is a level called al-Wasilah, so if you ask God for al-Wasilah for me. They said: O Messenger of God, who will live with you? He said: Ali, Fatima, Al-Hasan and Al-Hussain. This is a strange and rejected hadith from this aspect. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussain told us, Al-Hasan Al-Dashtaki told us, Abu Zuhair told us, Saeed bin Tarif told us on the authority of Ali bin Al-Hussain Al-Azdi, the client of Salim bin Thauban, who said: I heard Ali bin Abi Talib calling out from the pulpit of Kufa: O people, in Paradise there are two pearls: one of them is white, and the other is yellow. As for the white pearl, it is to the depths of the Throne, and the praised station of the white pearl is seventy thousand rooms, each room of which is three miles away, and its rooms, doors, beds and inhabitants are from one race, and its name is Al-Wasilah, it is for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his family, and the yellow one is like that, it is for Abraham, peace be upon him, and his family. This is also a strange trace. And His saying, And strive in His cause that you may succeed, when He commanded them to abandon the forbidden things and perform acts of obedience, He commanded them to fight the enemies from among the infidels and polytheists who have deviated from the straight path and abandoned the upright religion, and He encouraged them to do so by means of what He has prepared for those who strive in His cause on the Day of Resurrection of success and great, everlasting, continuous happiness that will not perish, change, or disappear in the high, lofty rooms, safe, with beautiful views, pleasant dwellings, in which whoever dwells in them will enjoy himself and not be miserable, and will live and not die, his clothes will not wear out, and his youth will not fade away. Then the Almighty informed us of what He has prepared for His disbelieving enemies of torment and punishment on the Day of Resurrection, saying: “Indeed, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth and as much more with it to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and they will have a painful punishment.” That is, if one of them came on the Day of Resurrection with the earth full of gold and as much as it to ransom himself thereby from the punishment of God that has encompassed him, and he was certain that it would reach him, it would not be accepted from him. Rather, there is no escape from it, no way out, and no escape. For this reason, He said: And for them is a painful punishment. That is, painful. “They want to get out of the Fire, but they will not get out of it. And for them is an enduring punishment.” As the Almighty said: Every time they want to get out of it, out of distress, they are returned to it. The verse, so they will not stop wanting to get out of what they are in of its severity and painful touch, and they have no way to do so. And every time the flames raise them up and they are at the top of Hell, the guards strike them with iron clubs and throw them back to its bottom. And for them is an enduring punishment. That is, permanent and continuous, there is no way out for them from it, and there is no escape for them from it. And He said: Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A man from the people of Hell will be brought and it will be said to him: O son of Adam, how did you find your bed? He will say: The worst bed. It will be said: Will you ransom yourself with an earth full of gold? He will say: Yes, O Lord. God will say: You have lied. I asked You for less than that and you did not do it. So he will be ordered to Hell.” Narrated by Muslim and al-Nasa’i on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah in a similar manner. Al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Mu’adh ibn Hisham al-Dastawai on the authority of his father on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Anas on his authority. They also narrated it on the authority of Abu Imran al-Jawni, whose name is Abd al-Malik ibn Habib, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik on his authority. Matar al-Warraq narrated it on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on his authority on his authority. Then Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Mas’udi on the authority of Yazid bin Suhaib Al-Faqir on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, A people will come out of the Fire and enter Paradise. He said: So I said to Jabir bin Abdullah: God says, They want to come out of the Fire, but they will not come out of it. He said: Recite the beginning of the verse, Indeed, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth and as much more with it, would offer it as ransom themselves. The verse, beware, they are the ones who disbelieved. Imam Ahmad and Muslim narrated this hadith from another source on the authority of Yazid al-Faqir, on the authority of Jabir, and this is a simpler context. So he recited: Indeed, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth and the like thereof with it, they would ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection until he reached and for them is a lasting punishment. Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise.” So that is the station, for God Almighty detains people because of their sins in the Fire for as long as He wills. 5:36: The Almighty says, commanding His believing servants to fear Him, and if it is coupled with His obedience, it means refraining from what is forbidden and abandoning what is prohibited. And after that He said, And seek the means of approach to Him. Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of Talhah, on the authority of Ata', on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning closeness. And this is what Mujahid, Abu Wa'il, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abdullah ibn Kathir, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd, and more than one said. Qatadah said: meaning, draw near to Him by obeying Him and doing what pleases Him. And Ibn Zayd read, Those are the ones they call upon, seeking the means of approach to their Lord. And what these imams said is not disputed among the commentators. And Ibn Jarir recited the following poet's saying: If the informers are absent-minded, we will return to our connection and the reconciliation between us and the means will return The means is that by which one reaches the desired goal. The means is also a sign of the highest station in Paradise, which is the station of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his home in Paradise. It is the closest place in Paradise to the Throne. It has been proven in Sahih al-Bukhari on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever says when he hears the call: ‘O God, Lord of this perfect call and the established prayer, grant Muhammad the means and excellence, and raise him to the praised station that You promised him,’ then intercession will be permitted for him on the Day of Resurrection.” [Another hadith] - In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ka`b ibn Alqamah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-`As, that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, “When you hear the muezzin, say what he says, then pray for me, for whoever prays for me, God will pray for him ten times. Then ask for intercession for me, for it is a station in Paradise that is not appropriate for anyone but one of God’s servants, and I hope that I am that one. Whoever asks for intercession for me, intercession will be granted to him.” [Another Hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Ka’b, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When you send blessings upon me, then ask for al-Wasilah for me. It was said: O Messenger of God, what is al-Wasilah? He said: The highest degree in Paradise, which none will attain except one man, and I hope that I am he. Then Al-Tabarani said: No one narrated it from Ibn Abi Dhi’b except Musa bin A’yan, that’s what he said. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it: Muhammad bin Ali bin Duhaim told us, Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, Musa bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr bin Ata’, and he mentioned something similar with his chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussain told us, Al-Hasan Al-Dashtaki told us, Abu Zuhair told us, Saeed bin Tarif told us on the authority of Ali bin Al-Hussain Al-Azdi, the client of Salim bin Thauban, who said: I heard Ali bin Abi Talib calling out from the pulpit of Kufa: O people, in Paradise there are two pearls: one of them is white, and the other is yellow. And His saying, And strive in His cause that you may succeed, when He commanded them to abandon the forbidden things and perform acts of obedience, He commanded them to fight the enemies from among the infidels and polytheists who have deviated from the straight path and abandoned the upright religion, and He encouraged them to do so by means of what He has prepared for those who strive in His cause on the Day of Resurrection of success and great, everlasting, continuous happiness that will not perish, change, or disappear in the high, lofty rooms, safe, with beautiful views, pleasant dwellings, in which whoever dwells in them will enjoy himself and not be miserable, and will live and not die, his clothes will not wear out, and his youth will not fade away. 5:38: The Almighty says, as a judge and an orderer to cut off the hand of the male and female thief. Al-Thawri narrated on the authority of Jabir bin Yazid Al-Ja'fi, on the authority of Aamer bin Shurahil Al-Sha'bi that Ibn Mas'ud used to read it: And the male thief, male and female, cut off their hands. This is an anomalous reading, even though the ruling according to all scholars is in agreement with it, rather it is derived from another proof. Cutting off the hand was practiced in the pre-Islamic era, so it was decided in Islam, and other conditions were added as we will mention, God willing, as were the blood money, the qirad, and other things that the Shari'ah came to confirm as they were, and the additions are from the completion of interests. It is said that the first to cut off hands in the pre-Islamic era were the Quraysh. They cut off a man called Duwaik, a client of Banu Malih bin Amr from Khuza'ah, who had stolen the treasure of the Kaaba. It is said that some people stole it and placed it with him. Some of the jurists from the people of the apparent have said that whenever a thief steals something, his hand is cut off for it, whether it was Little or much, according to the generality of this verse: And the male thief, male thief, cut off their hands. They did not consider it a minimum amount or a safe haven, but rather they were taken merely for theft. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abdul-Mumin on the authority of Najdah al-Hanafi, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about his statement, And as for the male thief, male thief, cut off their hands. Is it specific or general? He said: Rather, it is general. This may be that Ibn Abbas agreed with what these people said, and it may be otherwise, and God knows best. They held fast to what was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God curse the thief who steals an egg and his hand is cut off, and who steals a rope and his hand is cut off. They said, "Who would dare to do so except Usamah ibn Zayd, the beloved of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace?" Usamah said to him: Ask forgiveness for me, O Messenger of God. When it was evening, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and delivered a sermon in which he praised God as He deserved, then he said: “As for what follows, those who came before you were destroyed because if a noble person among them stole, they would leave him alone, but if a weak person among them stole, they would carry out the prescribed punishment on him. This is the wording of Muslim. On the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: There was a Makhzumi woman who used to borrow things on the tongues of her neighbors and she denied it, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that her hand be cut off. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Get up, Bilal, take her hand and cut it off. Then God the Almighty said: Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? That is, He is the owner of all that, the judge in it, whose judgment cannot be reversed, and He is the doer of whatever He wills. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and God is over all things competent.
