So she was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Usamah ibn Zayd spoke to him about her, and the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, changed color, so he said, Are you interceding regarding one of the limits of God, the Almighty and Majestic? Usamah said to him: Ask forgiveness for me, O Messenger of God. When it was evening, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and delivered a sermon in which he praised God as He deserved, then he said: “As for what follows, those who came before you were destroyed because if a noble person among them stole, they would leave him alone, but if a weak person among them stole, they would carry out the prescribed punishment on him. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if Fatimah, the daughter of Muhammad, were to steal, I would cut off her hand.” Then he ordered that the hand of the woman who had stolen be cut off. Aisha said: Her repentance was good after that, and she got married. She used to come after that and I would present her needs to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is the wording of Muslim. In a wording of his on the authority of Aisha, she said: There was a Makhzumi woman who used to borrow goods and deny it, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered her hand to be cut off. On the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: There was a Makhzumi woman who used to borrow things on the tongues of her neighbors and she denied it, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that her hand be cut off. Narrated by Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i, and this is his wording. In another version of his, it is said that a woman used to borrow jewelry from people and then keep it, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let this woman repent to God and His Messenger, and return what she took from the people. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Get up, Bilal, take her hand and cut it off. There are many hadiths mentioned in the Book of Rulings on theft, and praise and thanks be to God. Then God the Almighty said: Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? That is, He is the owner of all that, the judge in it, whose judgment cannot be reversed, and He is the doer of whatever He wills. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and God is over all things competent.
5:40: The Almighty says, as a judge and an orderer to cut off the hand of the male and female thief. Al-Thawri narrated on the authority of Jabir bin Yazid Al-Ja'fi, on the authority of Aamer bin Shurahil Al-Sha'bi that Ibn Mas'ud used to read it: And the male thief, male and female, cut off their hands. This is an anomalous reading, even though the ruling according to all scholars is in agreement with it, rather it is derived from another proof. Cutting off the hand was practiced in the pre-Islamic era, so it was decided in Islam, and other conditions were added as we will mention, God willing, as were the blood money, the qirad, and other things that the Shari'ah came to confirm as they were, and the additions are from the completion of interests. It is said that the first to cut off hands in the pre-Islamic era were the Quraysh. They cut off a man called Duwaik, a client of Banu Malih bin Amr from Khuza'ah, who had stolen the treasure of the Kaaba. It is said that some people stole it and placed it with him. Some of the jurists from the people of the apparent have said that whenever a thief steals something, his hand is cut off for it, whether it was Little or much, according to the generality of this verse: And the male thief, male thief, cut off their hands. They did not consider it a minimum amount or a safe haven, but rather they were taken merely for theft. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Abdul-Mumin on the authority of Najdah al-Hanafi, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about his statement, And as for the male thief, male thief, cut off their hands. Is it specific or general? He said: Rather, it is general. This may be that Ibn Abbas agreed with what these people said, and it may be otherwise, and God knows best. They held fast to what was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God curse the thief who steals an egg and his hand is cut off, and who steals a rope and his hand is cut off. As for the majority, they considered the nisab in the theft, even though there was disagreement among them about its amount, and each of the four imams went to a separate opinion. According to Imam Malik bin Anas, may God have mercy on him, the nisab is three pure minted dirhams, so when he steals it or what is equal to its price or more, the cutting off is obligatory. He provided evidence for that with what he narrated on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cut off the hand for a shield whose price was three dirhams. They included it in the two Sahihs. Malik, may God have mercy on him, said: And Uthman, may God be pleased with him, cut off the hand for a citron that was valued at three dirhams, and this is the most beloved thing I have heard about that. This trace from Uthman, may God be pleased with him, was narrated by Malik on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Bakr on the authority of his father, on the authority of Umrah bint Abd al-Rahman that a thief stole a citron during the time of Uthman, so Uthman ordered it to be valued and it was valued at three dirhams out of the twelve dirhams, so Uthman cut off his hand. The companions of Malik said: Such an action is well-known and has not been denied. From such a thing, tacit consensus is reported. It indicates that the fruits should be cut off, contrary to the Hanafis, and that three dirhams should be considered, contrary to them that ten dirhams are necessary, and to the Shafi’is that a quarter of a dinar should be considered, and God knows best. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said that the consideration in cutting off the hand of a thief is a quarter of a dinar or its equivalent in prices or goods or more. The evidence for that is what was narrated by the two sheikhs, Al-Bukhari and Muslim, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Umrah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The hand of a thief is cut off for a quarter of a dinar or more. And Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm, on the authority of Umrah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The hand of a thief is not cut off except for a quarter of a dinar or more. Our companions said: This hadith is decisive in the issue, and it is a text in considering a quarter of a dinar, not what is equal to it. They said: The hadith about the price of the shield, and that it was three dirhams, does not contradict this because at that time the dinar was worth twelve dirhams, which was the price of a quarter of a dinar, so it was possible to combine them by this method. This doctrine is narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, Uthman ibn Affan, and Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with them, and it is what Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, al-Layth ibn Sa`d, al-Awza`i, al-Shafi`i and his companions say, and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh in a narration on his authority, and Abu Thawr and Dawud ibn Ali al-Dhahiri, may God have mercy on them. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh in a narration from him, said that each of the quarter of a dinar and three dirhams is a legal return, so whoever steals one of them or what is equal to it, his hand will be cut off, in accordance with the hadith of Ibn Umar and the hadith of Aisha, may God be pleased with her. It was reported in a wording of Imam Ahmad on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Cut off for a quarter of a dinar, and do not cut off for anything less than that. At that time, a quarter of a dinar was three dirhams, and a dinar was twelve dirhams. In a wording of al-Nasa’i, The hand of a thief is not cut off for anything less than the price of a shield. It was said to Aisha: What is the price of a shield? She said: A quarter of a dinar. All of these are texts indicating that ten dirhams are not a condition, and God knows best. As for Imam Abu Hanifa and his companions Abu Yusuf, Muhammad and Zufar, as well as Sufyan al-Thawri, may God have mercy on them, they went to the view that the nisab is ten minted dirhams, not adulterated, and they argued that the price of a shield for which a thief was cut off during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was ten dirhams. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated: Ibn Numayr and Abd al-A’la told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Ayoub ibn Musa, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The price of a shield during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was ten dirhams. Then he said: Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu’ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The hand of a thief is not cut off for less than the price of a shield. The price of a shield was ten dirhams. They said: So Ibn Abbas and Abd God ibn Amr disagreed with Ibn Umar regarding the price of a shield, so it is more cautious to take the greater amount, because the prescribed punishments are prevented by doubts. Some of the Salaf said that the hand of a thief is cut off for ten dirhams or a dinar or the equivalent value of one of them. This is narrated from Ali, Ibn Masoud, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i and Abu Ja’far al-Baqir, may God Almighty have mercy on them. Some of the Salaf said: The fifth is not cut off except for five, meaning five dinars or fifty dirhams. This is narrated from Sa’id ibn Jubayr, may God have mercy on him. The majority responded to what the Zahiris held on to from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, He steals an egg and his hand is cut off, and he steals a rope and his hand is cut off, with answers. [One of them] is that it was abrogated by the hadith of Aisha, and there is a view on this, because the date must be stated. [The second] is that it is interpreted as an iron egg and a ship’s rope, as al-A’mash said in what al-Bukhari and others narrated from him. [The third] is that this is a means of gradual progression in theft from a small amount to a large amount for which the hand is cut off. It is possible that this was taken as a way of reporting what the situation was like in the pre-Islamic era, when they used to cut off the hand for a small amount and a large amount. So the thief who spends his valuable hand on insignificant things was cursed. They mentioned that when Abu al-Ala al-Ma’arri came to Baghdad, it became famous that he raised a problem with the jurists regarding their setting the minimum amount for theft at a quarter of a dinar, and he composed poetry about that which indicated his ignorance and lack of intelligence, so he said: A hand worth five hundred amber, why was it cut off for a quarter of a dinar? We have no choice but to remain silent and seek refuge in our Lord from the Fire. When he said that and became famous about him, the jurists sought him out, but he fled from them. The people responded to him about that, and the response of Judge Abdul Wahhab Al-Maliki, may God have mercy on him, was that he said: When she was trustworthy, she was valuable, and when she betrayed, she became worthless. Some of them said: This is from the perfection of wisdom, interest, and the great secrets of the Shari’ah, because in the chapter on crimes, it is appropriate to increase the value of the hand by five hundred dinars, so that it will not be wronged. And in the chapter on theft, it is appropriate that the amount for which it should be cut off be a quarter of a dinar, so that people will not rush to steal money. This is the essence of wisdom according to those with understanding. That is why he said: “The recompense for what they have earned is a punishment from God. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise.” That is, a recompense for their evil deeds in taking people’s money with their hands, so it is appropriate to cut off what they used in that as a punishment from God, that is, a punishment from God to them for committing that. And God is Exalted in Might that is, in His vengeance, Wise that is, in His commands, prohibitions, laws, and decree. Then God the Almighty said, “But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and amends, then indeed, God will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.” That is, whoever repents after stealing and returns to God, then God will turn to him in forgiveness, so whatever is between him and Him, as for the money of the people, it must be returned to them or its replacement according to the majority. Abu Hanifa said: When the hand is cut off and it is lost in his hand, then its replacement is not returned. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Hasan al-Daraqutni narrated from the hadith of… on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought a thief who had stolen a cloak, so he said: I do not think he stole, so the thief said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Go with him and cut his hand off, then brand him, then bring him to me. So he cut his hand off and he was brought to him and he said: Repent to God. So he said: I repent to God. He said: May God accept your repentance. It was narrated from another source as a mursal, and Ali ibn al-Madini and Ibn Khuzaymah, may God have mercy on them, preferred its mursal. Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of Ibn Lahi’ah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Tha’labah al-Ansari, on the authority of his father that Umar ibn Samurah ibn Habib ibn Abd Shams came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I have stolen a camel belonging to Banu so-and-so, so purify me. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for them and they said: We have lost our camel, so he ordered that its hand be cut off while he was saying: Praise be to God who purified me from you. You wanted to send my body to Hell. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Musa ibn Dawud told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us on the authority of Yahya ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: A woman stole jewelry and those she had stolen from came and said: O Messenger of God, this woman has stolen from us. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Cut off her right hand. So the woman said: Is there repentance? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Today you are free from your sin as on the day your mother bore you. He said, “Then God Almighty revealed, ‘But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms - then indeed, God will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.’” Imam Ahmad narrated it in a simpler way than this, saying: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Yahya ibn Abdullah told me, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, that a woman stole during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He brought her to those from whom she had stolen, and they said: O Messenger of God, this woman stole from us. Her people said: We will ransom her. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Cut off her hand. They said: We will ransom her for five hundred dinars. He said: Cut off her hand. So her right hand was cut off, and the woman said: Is there any repentance for me, O Messenger of God? He said, Yes, you are today as free from your sin as the day your mother bore you. So God revealed in Surat Al-Ma'idah, "But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and amends - then indeed, God will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful." This woman is the Makhzumi woman who stole, and her hadith is confirmed in the two Sahihs on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aishah that the Quraysh were concerned about the matter of the woman who had stolen, during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, during the conquest of Mecca. They said, "Who will speak to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about her?" They said, "Who would dare to do so except Usamah ibn Zayd, the beloved of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace?" So she was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Usamah ibn Zayd spoke to him about her, and the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, changed color, so he said, Are you interceding regarding one of the limits of God, the Almighty and Majestic? Usamah said to him: Ask forgiveness for me, O Messenger of God. When it was evening, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and delivered a sermon in which he praised God as He deserved, then he said: “As for what follows, those who came before you were destroyed because if a noble person among them stole, they would leave him alone, but if a weak person among them stole, they would carry out the prescribed punishment on him. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if Fatimah, the daughter of Muhammad, were to steal, I would cut off her hand.” Then he ordered that the hand of the woman who had stolen be cut off. Aisha said: Her repentance was good after that, and she got married. She used to come after that and I would present her needs to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is the wording of Muslim. In a wording of his on the authority of Aisha, she said: There was a Makhzumi woman who used to borrow goods and deny it, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered her hand to be cut off. On the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: There was a Makhzumi woman who used to borrow things on the tongues of her neighbors and she denied it, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that her hand be cut off. Narrated by Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i, and this is his wording. In another version of his, it is said that a woman used to borrow jewelry from people and then keep it, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let this woman repent to God and His Messenger, and return what she took from the people. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Get up, Bilal, take her hand and cut it off. There are many hadiths mentioned in the Book of Rulings on theft, and praise and thanks be to God. Then God the Almighty said: Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? That is, He is the owner of all that, the judge in it, whose judgment cannot be reversed, and He is the doer of whatever He wills. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and God is over all things competent.
5:41: These noble verses were revealed about those who hastened to disbelief, who disobeyed God and His Messenger, who put their opinions and desires before the laws of God the Almighty, Of those who said, ‘We believe,’ with their mouths, while their hearts did not believe, meaning they showed faith with their tongues, but their hearts were ruined and empty of it. These are the hypocrites, Of those who are Jews, the enemies of Islam and its people. All of these are listeners to falsehood, meaning they respond to it and are affected by it. Listeners to other people who have not come to you, meaning they respond to other people who do not come to your gathering, O Muhammad. It was said that what is meant is that they listen to speech and pass it on to other people who are not present with you, from your enemies. They distort words from their [proper] places, meaning they interpret them in a way other than their interpretation, and they change them after they have understood them, and they know. They say, ‘If you are given this, then take it, and if you are not given it, then beware.’ It was said that it was revealed about a group of Jews. They killed a man and said: Come, let us go to Muhammad for judgment. If he rules with blood money, then accept it. If he rules with retaliation, then do not listen to him. The correct view is that it was revealed about the two Jews who committed adultery and had changed the Book of God that was in their hands from the command to stone those who were married among them. They distorted it and agreed among themselves to flog one hundred lashes, to be blackened and to be ridden on two donkeys upside down. When that event occurred after the migration, they said among themselves: Come, let us go to him for judgment. If he rules with flogging and blackening, then take it from him and make it an argument between you and God. It will be a prophet of God who has ruled between you with that. If he rules with stoning, then do not follow him in that. The hadiths have been narrated on this subject. Malik said, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both: The Jews came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned to him that a man and a woman among them had committed adultery. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them, What do you find in the Torah regarding stoning? They said, We will disgrace them and flog them. Abdullah ibn Salam said, “You have lied. It contains stoning.” So they brought the Torah. They brought the Torah and spread it out. One of them put his hand on the verse of stoning and read what came before it and what came after it. Abdullah ibn Salam said to him, Raise your hand. So he raised his hand and there was the verse of stoning. They said, “He has spoken the truth, O Muhammad. It contains the verse of stoning.” So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to be stoned. I saw the man bending over the woman to protect her from the stones. They both narrated it. This is the wording of Bukhari. In another wording of his: He said to the Jews, What will you do with them? They said: We will disfigure their faces and disgrace them. He said: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful. So they came and said to a man among them who was one-eyed and whom they were pleased with: Read. So he read until he reached a place in it, and he put his hand on it and said: Raise your hand. So he raised it, and behold, the verse of stoning appeared. He said: O Muhammad, in it is the verse of stoning, but we conceal it among ourselves. So he ordered them to be stoned. Muslim narrated that a Jewish man and a Jewish woman who had committed adultery were brought to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) set out until he came to the Jews and said, What do you find in the Torah about those who commit adultery? They said, We will blacken their faces and make them red, and we will carry them and make their faces different and they will be paraded around. He said, Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful. They brought it and recited it. When they came to the verse of stoning, the young man who was reciting put his hand on the verse of stoning and recited what was in front of it and behind it. Abdullah ibn Salam, who was with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), said to him, Tell him to raise his hand. So he raised his hand, and there was beneath it the verse of stoning. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded that they be stoned. Abdullah ibn Umar said, I was among those who stoned them, and I saw him protecting her from the stones with his own hand. Abu Dawud said: Ahmad ibn Sa`id al-Hamdani told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Hisham ibn Sa`d told us that Zayd ibn Aslam told him on the authority of Ibn `Umar who said: A group of Jews came and invited the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the Qaf. He came to them in the school house and said: O Abu al-Qasim, a man among us has committed adultery with a woman, so pass judgment. He said: They placed a cushion for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he sat on it. Then he said: Bring me the Torah. So it was brought to him. He removed the cushion from under him and placed the Torah on it and said: I believe in you and in the One who sent you down. Then he said: Bring me the most knowledgeable among you. So a young man was brought. Then he mentioned the story of stoning similar to the hadith of Malik on the authority of Nafi`. Al-Zuhri said: I heard a man from Muzaynah who follows knowledge and understands it, and we were with Ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: A Jewish man committed adultery with a woman. Some of them said to each other: Go to this prophet, for he was sent to alleviate the punishment. If he issues a fatwa to us other than stoning, we will accept it and use it as evidence before God. We said: The fatwa of one of your prophets. He said: So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sitting in the mosque with his companions, and they said: O Abu al-Qasim, what do you say about a man and a woman among them who commit adultery? He did not say a word to them until he reached the house of their schools. He stood at the door and said: I ask you by God who sent down the Torah to Moses, what do you find in the Torah regarding one who commits adultery if he is married? They said: He should be washed, flogged and flogged. Flogging is when the two adulterers are carried on a donkey and their backs are opposite each other and they are paraded around. He said: A young man among them was silent, but when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him, he was silent. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, insisted on asking him, so he said: O God, since you ask us, we find stoning in the Torah. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What was the first thing that you made permissible for God’s command? He said: A relative of one of our kings committed adultery, so stoning was delayed for him. Then a man among the people committed adultery after him, so he wanted to stone him, but his people prevented him and said: We will not stone our companion until you bring your companion and stone him. So they agreed on this punishment among themselves. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will judge by what is in the Torah. So he ordered them to be stoned. Al-Zuhri said: It reached us that this verse was revealed about them: “Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted to God judged by it.” So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was one of them. Narrated by Ahmad and Abu Dawood, and this is his wording, and Ibn Jarir. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: A Jewish man who had been flogged and had been bathed passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He called them and said, Is this how you find the punishment for adultery in your book? They said, Yes. So he called one of their scholars and said, I ask you by the One who sent down the Torah to Moses, is this how you find the punishment for adultery in your book? He said: No, by God, and if you had not asked me about this, I would not have told you. We find stoning as the punishment for adultery in our book, but it is common among our nobles. If we took the noble, we would leave him, and if we took the weak, we would carry out the punishment on him. So we said: Come, let us make something that we can carry out on the noble and the lowly. So we agreed on the stoning and flogging. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, I am the first to revive your command when they killed him. He said: So he ordered him to be stoned. He said: Then God Almighty revealed: O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you. They say: If you are given this, take it. That is, they say: Go to Muhammad, and if he gives you a fatwa regarding stoning and flogging, then take it. If he gives you a fatwa regarding stoning, then beware. He said: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, then those are the disbelievers. He said about the Jews, to His saying: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, then those are the wrongdoers. He said about the Jews: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, then those are the wicked. He said: Regarding all the disbelievers. It was narrated by Muslim alone, not by Al-Bukhari, Abu Dawood, Al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah, through more than one chain of transmission on the authority of Al-A’mash. Imam Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr Al-Humaidi said in his Musnad: Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, Mujalid bin Saeed Al-Hamadani told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: A man from the people of Fadak committed adultery, so the people of Fadak wrote to some Jews in Medina, asking Muhammad about that, so if he orders you to flog, then take it from him, and if he orders you to stone, then do not take it from him. So they asked him about that, and he said, Send to me the two most knowledgeable men among you. So they brought a one-eyed man called Ibn Suriya, and another, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them, You are more knowledgeable than those before you. They said, Our people have called us to that. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them, Do you not have the Torah in which is the judgment of God? They said, Yes. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Then I ask you by He who split the sea for the Children of Israel, and shaded you with clouds, and saved you from the people of Pharaoh, and sent down manna and quails upon the Children of Israel, what do you find in the Torah regarding stoning?” One of them said, To the other: I have never heard anything like it. Then they said: We find that looking repeatedly is adultery, embracing is adultery, and kissing is adultery. So if four testify that they saw him appear and repeat, as a pen enters a kohl container, then stoning is obligatory. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is it. So he ordered him to be stoned, and then the verse was revealed: “So if they come to you, either judge between them or turn away from them. But if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all. But if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, God loves those who act justly.” Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Mujalid, with a similar wording. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Jews brought a man and a woman from among them who had committed adultery, so he said: Bring me the two most knowledgeable men among you. So they brought him the two sons of Suriya, and he asked them: How do you find the matter of these two in the Torah? They said: We find that if four testify that they saw his penis in her vagina like a kohl stick in a container, they are to be stoned. He said: What prevents you from stoning them? They said: Our authority has gone and we dislike killing. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for witnesses, and four came and testified that they saw his penis like a kohl stick in a container. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that they be stoned. Then Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Al-Sha’bi and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i as a mursal, and he did not mention in it: So he called for witnesses and they testified. These hadiths indicate that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled in accordance with the ruling of the Torah. This is not out of respect for them for what they believe to be correct, because they are commanded to follow the Muhammadan law without fail. Rather, this is by special revelation from God Almighty to him regarding this, and His asking them about it, to confirm what they have in their hands, which they conspired to conceal, deny, and not act upon for those long ages. So when they acknowledged it, knowing that it was contrary to it, their deviation, stubbornness, and denial of what they believe to be correct from the book in their hands, and their turning to the arbitration of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was only due to their own whims and desires to agree with their opinions, not because they believe that what he rules is correct. For this reason, they said, If you are given this, meaning flogging and burning, then take it, meaning accept it, and if you are not given it, then beware, meaning from accepting and following it. God the Almighty said: “And whomsoever God intends to test, you will not possess for him anything against God. Those are the ones whose hearts God does not intend to purify. For them is disgrace in this world, and for them is a great punishment in the Hereafter. They are listeners to falsehood, devourers of unlawful gain, as Ibn Mas`ud and others have said. How can God purify the heart of one who has this characteristic and how can He respond to him? Then He said to His Prophet: “If they come to you” meaning seeking judgment from you, “then judge between them or turn away from them. But if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all” meaning, you do not have to judge between them, because they do not intend by their judgment to you to follow the truth, but rather what agrees with their desires. Ibn `Abbas, Mujahid, `Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, Zayd ibn Aslam, `Ata’ Al-Khurasani, Al-Hasan and others have said: It was abrogated by His statement: And judge between them by what God has revealed, and And if you judge, judge between them with justice, meaning with truth and justice, even if they are oppressors who have deviated from the path of justice. Indeed, God loves those who act justly. Then the Almighty said, denouncing them for their corrupt opinions and their deviant intentions in abandoning what they believe to be correct from the Book in their hands, which they claim they are commanded to adhere to forever, then they went beyond its ruling and turned to something else which they believe in the matter to be false and not binding on them, so He said, “And how can they make you judge while they have the Torah, in which is the ruling of God? Then they turn away after that. And those are not believers.” Then He praised the Torah that He sent down to His servant and Messenger Moses, son of Imran, so He said, “Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to God] judged by it for those who were Jews,” meaning they do not go beyond its ruling, nor do they change it, nor do they distort it, and the rabbis and the scholars, meaning likewise the rabbis among them, who are the learned worshippers, and the rabbis, who are the scholars, for what they were entrusted with of the Book of God, meaning what they were entrusted with of the Book of God which they were commanded to make manifest and act upon, “and they were witnesses over it. So do not fear the people but fear Me,” meaning do not fear them and fear. From me, “And do not exchange My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers.” There are two sayings about it, the explanation of which will come. Another reason for the revelation of these noble verses Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim bin Abbas told us, Abdul Rahman bin Abi Al-Zinad told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God revealed: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers “And it is those who are the wrongdoers” And it is those who are the defiantly disobedient Ibn Abbas said: God revealed it regarding the two groups of Jews, one of which had subjugated the other in the pre-Islamic era until they were satisfied and agreed that for every slain person killed by the powerful woman from the humiliated, his ransom would be fifty wasqs, and for every slain person killed by the humiliated woman from the powerful woman, his ransom would be one hundred wasqs. They remained like that until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, and the humiliated woman from the powerful woman killed someone, so the powerful woman sent to the humiliated woman to send us one hundred wasqs. The humiliated woman said: Was there ever a group of two groups whose religion was the same, whose lineage was the same, and whose country was the same, and the blood money of one of them was half the blood money of the other? We only gave you this out of your oppression of us and fear from you. But when Muhammad came, we will not give you anything. So war almost broke out between them. Then they agreed to make the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among them. Then the Aziza mentioned and said: By God, Muhammad will not give you from them twice what he gives them from you, and they have told the truth. They did not give us this except out of injustice from us and to subjugate them. So they sent to Muhammad someone to tell you his opinion. If he gives you what you want, you will rule according to him, and if he does not give you, you will be wary and do not rule according to him. So they sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, some hypocrites to tell them the opinion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So when they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God informed His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, of their entire affair and what they wanted. So God Almighty revealed: O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you until His saying the wicked. By God, it was revealed about them, and God Almighty meant them. Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Abi al-Zinad from his father in a similar manner. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Hannad ibn al-Sarri and Abu Kurayb told us: Yunus ibn Bakir told us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Dawud ibn al-Husayn told me on the authority of `Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas: The verses in al-Ma`idah, “Then judge between them or turn away from them. But if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, God loves those who act justly,” were revealed regarding the blood money of Banu al-Nadir and Banu Qurayzah. That is because the slain of Banu al-Nadir had honor, and the full blood money was paid to them, while the Qurayzah were paid half the blood money. So they brought their case to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) regarding that, and God revealed that regarding them. So the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) held them to the truth regarding that, and made the blood money equal in that. And God knows best which of them it was. Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa’i narrated it in a similar manner from the hadith of Ibn Ishaq. Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ubaydullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Ali bin Salih, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There were Qurayzah and Nadir, and Nadir were more noble than Qurayzah, so if a Qurayzi killed a man from Nadir, he was killed for him, and if a Nadir killed a man from Qurayzah, blood money was paid with one hundred wasqs of dates. So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, a man from Nadir killed a man from Qurayzah, and they said: Give him over to him. They said: Between us and you is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the verse was revealed: And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Hibban, and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak narrated it in a similar manner from the hadith of Ubaydullah bin Musa. Qatadah, Muqatil bin Hibban, Ibn Zayd, and more than one other said the same. Al-Awfi and Ali bin Abi Talha Al-Walibi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that these verses were revealed about the two Jews who committed adultery, as the hadiths mentioned earlier. It is possible that these two reasons came together at the same time, so these verses were revealed about all of that, and God knows best. That is why he said after that, And We prescribed for them therein that a life for a life and an eye for an eye, to the end of it. This strengthens the fact that the reason for the revelation was the issue of retaliation, and God Almighty knows best. And the Almighty’s saying, And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, Al-Bara’ bin Azib, Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman, Ibn Abbas, Abu Majlaz, Abu Raja’ Al-Attardi, Ikrimah, Ubayd God bin Abdullah, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others said: They were revealed about the People of the Book. Al-Hasan Al-Basri added: They are obligatory upon us. Abd Al-Razzaq said on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, that these verses were revealed about the Children of Israel, and God was pleased with them for this nation. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Ibn Jarir also said: Yaqub told us, Hisham told us, Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulayman told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Alqamah and Masruq, that they asked Ibn Masoud about bribery. He said: It is from ill-gotten gains. They said: And in the ruling. He said: That is disbelief. Then he recited, And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. Al-Suddi said: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He said: Whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, abandoning it intentionally or acting unjustly while he knows, is one of the disbelievers. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He said: Whoever denies what God has revealed has disbelieved, and whoever acknowledges it but does not rule by it is a wrongdoer and a sinner. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Then he chose that the verse refers to the People of the Book, or whoever denies the ruling of God revealed in the Book. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of al-Sha’bi: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, he said to the Muslims. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Abd Al-Samad told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Al-Safar, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then those are the disbelievers. He said: This is about the Muslims. And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then those are the wrongdoers. He said: This is about the Jews. And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then those are the wicked. He said: This is about the Christians. Hisham and Al-Thawri narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Zakariya Ibn Abi Za’idah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi. Abd Al-Razzaq also said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked about his statement, And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, the verse. He said: It is disbelief. Ibn Tawus said: It is not like the one who disbelieves in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers. Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, that he said: Disbelief less than disbelief, oppression less than oppression, and immorality less than immorality. Ibn Jarir narrated it. Waki’ said, on the authority of Sa’id Al-Makki, on the authority of Tawus, And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then those are the wicked. They are the disbelievers.” He said: It is not disbelief that removes one from the religion. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Maqri told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hujayr, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He said: It is not the disbelief that you are going to. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, and he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, but they did not include it.
5:42: These noble verses were revealed about those who hastened to disbelief, who disobeyed God and His Messenger, who put their opinions and desires before the laws of God the Almighty, Of those who said, ‘We believe,’ with their mouths, while their hearts did not believe, meaning they showed faith with their tongues, but their hearts were ruined and empty of it. These are the hypocrites, Of those who are Jews, the enemies of Islam and its people. All of these are listeners to falsehood, meaning they respond to it and are affected by it. Listeners to other people who have not come to you, meaning they respond to other people who do not come to your gathering, O Muhammad. It was said that what is meant is that they listen to speech and pass it on to other people who are not present with you, from your enemies. They distort words from their [proper] places, meaning they interpret them in a way other than their interpretation, and they change them after they have understood them, and they know. They say, ‘If you are given this, then take it, and if you are not given it, then beware.’ It was said that it was revealed about a group of Jews. They killed a man and said: Come, let us go to Muhammad for judgment. If he rules with blood money, then accept it. If he rules with retaliation, then do not listen to him. The correct view is that it was revealed about the two Jews who committed adultery and had changed the Book of God that was in their hands from the command to stone those who were married among them. They distorted it and agreed among themselves to flog one hundred lashes, to be blackened and to be ridden on two donkeys upside down. When that event occurred after the migration, they said among themselves: Come, let us go to him for judgment. If he rules with flogging and blackening, then take it from him and make it an argument between you and God. It will be a prophet of God who has ruled between you with that. If he rules with stoning, then do not follow him in that. The hadiths have been narrated on this subject. Malik said, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both: The Jews came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned to him that a man and a woman among them had committed adultery. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them, What do you find in the Torah regarding stoning? They said, We will disgrace them and flog them. Abdullah ibn Salam said, “You have lied. It contains stoning.” So they brought the Torah. They brought the Torah and spread it out. One of them put his hand on the verse of stoning and read what came before it and what came after it. Abdullah ibn Salam said to him, Raise your hand. So he raised his hand and there was the verse of stoning. They said, “He has spoken the truth, O Muhammad. It contains the verse of stoning.” So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to be stoned. I saw the man bending over the woman to protect her from the stones. They both narrated it. This is the wording of Bukhari. In another wording of his: He said to the Jews, What will you do with them? They said: We will disfigure their faces and disgrace them. He said: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful. So they came and said to a man among them who was one-eyed and whom they were pleased with: Read. So he read until he reached a place in it, and he put his hand on it and said: Raise your hand. So he raised it, and behold, the verse of stoning appeared. He said: O Muhammad, in it is the verse of stoning, but we conceal it among ourselves. So he ordered them to be stoned. Muslim narrated that a Jewish man and a Jewish woman who had committed adultery were brought to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) set out until he came to the Jews and said, What do you find in the Torah about those who commit adultery? They said, We will blacken their faces and make them red, and we will carry them and make their faces different and they will be paraded around. He said, Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful. They brought it and recited it. When they came to the verse of stoning, the young man who was reciting put his hand on the verse of stoning and recited what was in front of it and behind it. Abdullah ibn Salam, who was with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), said to him, Tell him to raise his hand. So he raised his hand, and there was beneath it the verse of stoning. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded that they be stoned. Abdullah ibn Umar said, I was among those who stoned them, and I saw him protecting her from the stones with his own hand. Abu Dawud said: Ahmad ibn Sa`id al-Hamdani told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Hisham ibn Sa`d told us that Zayd ibn Aslam told him on the authority of Ibn `Umar who said: A group of Jews came and invited the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the Qaf. He came to them in the school house and said: O Abu al-Qasim, a man among us has committed adultery with a woman, so pass judgment. He said: They placed a cushion for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he sat on it. Then he said: Bring me the Torah. So it was brought to him. He removed the cushion from under him and placed the Torah on it and said: I believe in you and in the One who sent you down. Then he said: Bring me the most knowledgeable among you. So a young man was brought. Then he mentioned the story of stoning similar to the hadith of Malik on the authority of Nafi`. Al-Zuhri said: I heard a man from Muzaynah who follows knowledge and understands it, and we were with Ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: A Jewish man committed adultery with a woman. Some of them said to each other: Go to this prophet, for he was sent to alleviate the punishment. If he issues a fatwa to us other than stoning, we will accept it and use it as evidence before God. We said: The fatwa of one of your prophets. He said: So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sitting in the mosque with his companions, and they said: O Abu al-Qasim, what do you say about a man and a woman among them who commit adultery? He did not say a word to them until he reached the house of their schools. He stood at the door and said: I ask you by God who sent down the Torah to Moses, what do you find in the Torah regarding one who commits adultery if he is married? They said: He should be washed, flogged and flogged. Flogging is when the two adulterers are carried on a donkey and their backs are opposite each other and they are paraded around. He said: A young man among them was silent, but when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him, he was silent. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, insisted on asking him, so he said: O God, since you ask us, we find stoning in the Torah. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What was the first thing that you made permissible for God’s command? He said: A relative of one of our kings committed adultery, so stoning was delayed for him. Then a man among the people committed adultery after him, so he wanted to stone him, but his people prevented him and said: We will not stone our companion until you bring your companion and stone him. So they agreed on this punishment among themselves. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will judge by what is in the Torah. So he ordered them to be stoned. Al-Zuhri said: It reached us that this verse was revealed about them: “Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted to God judged by it.” So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was one of them. Narrated by Ahmad and Abu Dawood, and this is his wording, and Ibn Jarir. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: A Jewish man who had been flogged and had been bathed passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He called them and said, Is this how you find the punishment for adultery in your book? They said, Yes. So he called one of their scholars and said, I ask you by the One who sent down the Torah to Moses, is this how you find the punishment for adultery in your book? He said: No, by God, and if you had not asked me about this, I would not have told you. We find stoning as the punishment for adultery in our book, but it is common among our nobles. If we took the noble, we would leave him, and if we took the weak, we would carry out the punishment on him. So we said: Come, let us make something that we can carry out on the noble and the lowly. So we agreed on the stoning and flogging. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, I am the first to revive your command when they killed him. He said: So he ordered him to be stoned. He said: Then God Almighty revealed: O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you. They say: If you are given this, take it. That is, they say: Go to Muhammad, and if he gives you a fatwa regarding stoning and flogging, then take it. If he gives you a fatwa regarding stoning, then beware. He said: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, then those are the disbelievers. He said about the Jews, to His saying: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, then those are the wrongdoers. He said about the Jews: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, then those are the wicked. He said: Regarding all the disbelievers. It was narrated by Muslim alone, not by Al-Bukhari, Abu Dawood, Al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah, through more than one chain of transmission on the authority of Al-A’mash. Imam Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr Al-Humaidi said in his Musnad: Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, Mujalid bin Saeed Al-Hamadani told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: A man from the people of Fadak committed adultery, so the people of Fadak wrote to some Jews in Medina, asking Muhammad about that, so if he orders you to flog, then take it from him, and if he orders you to stone, then do not take it from him. So they asked him about that, and he said, Send to me the two most knowledgeable men among you. So they brought a one-eyed man called Ibn Suriya, and another, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them, You are more knowledgeable than those before you. They said, Our people have called us to that. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them, Do you not have the Torah in which is the judgment of God? They said, Yes. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Then I ask you by He who split the sea for the Children of Israel, and shaded you with clouds, and saved you from the people of Pharaoh, and sent down manna and quails upon the Children of Israel, what do you find in the Torah regarding stoning?” One of them said, To the other: I have never heard anything like it. Then they said: We find that looking repeatedly is adultery, embracing is adultery, and kissing is adultery. So if four testify that they saw him appear and repeat, as a pen enters a kohl container, then stoning is obligatory. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is it. So he ordered him to be stoned, and then the verse was revealed: “So if they come to you, either judge between them or turn away from them. But if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all. But if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, God loves those who act justly.” Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Mujalid, with a similar wording. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Jews brought a man and a woman from among them who had committed adultery, so he said: Bring me the two most knowledgeable men among you. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for witnesses, and four came and testified that they saw his penis like a kohl stick in a container. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that they be stoned. Then Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Al-Sha’bi and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i as a mursal, and he did not mention in it: So he called for witnesses and they testified. And those are not believers.” Then He praised the Torah that He sent down to His servant and Messenger Moses, son of Imran, so He said, “Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to God] judged by it for those who were Jews,” meaning they do not go beyond its ruling, nor do they change it, nor do they distort it, and the rabbis and the scholars, meaning likewise the rabbis among them, who are the learned worshippers, and the rabbis, who are the scholars, for what they were entrusted with of the Book of God, meaning what they were entrusted with of the Book of God which they were commanded to make manifest and act upon, “and they were witnesses over it. So do not fear the people but fear Me,” meaning do not fear them and fear. From me, “And do not exchange My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers.” There are two sayings about it, the explanation of which will come. Another reason for the revelation of these noble verses Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim bin Abbas told us, Abdul Rahman bin Abi Al-Zinad told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God revealed: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers “And it is those who are the wrongdoers” And it is those who are the defiantly disobedient Ibn Abbas said: God revealed it regarding the two groups of Jews, one of which had subjugated the other in the pre-Islamic era until they were satisfied and agreed that for every slain person killed by the powerful woman from the humiliated, his ransom would be fifty wasqs, and for every slain person killed by the humiliated woman from the powerful woman, his ransom would be one hundred wasqs. They remained like that until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, and the humiliated woman from the powerful woman killed someone, so the powerful woman sent to the humiliated woman to send us one hundred wasqs. The humiliated woman said: Was there ever a group of two groups whose religion was the same, whose lineage was the same, and whose country was the same, and the blood money of one of them was half the blood money of the other? We only gave you this out of your oppression of us and fear from you. But when Muhammad came, we will not give you anything. So war almost broke out between them. Then they agreed to make the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among them. Then the Aziza mentioned and said: By God, Muhammad will not give you from them twice what he gives them from you, and they have told the truth. They did not give us this except out of injustice from us and to subjugate them. So they sent to Muhammad someone to tell you his opinion. If he gives you what you want, you will rule according to him, and if he does not give you, you will be wary and do not rule according to him. So they sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, some hypocrites to tell them the opinion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So when they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God informed His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, of their entire affair and what they wanted. So God Almighty revealed: O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you until His saying the wicked. By God, it was revealed about them, and God Almighty meant them. Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Abi al-Zinad from his father in a similar manner. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Hannad ibn al-Sarri and Abu Kurayb told us: Yunus ibn Bakir told us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Dawud ibn al-Husayn told me on the authority of `Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas: The verses in al-Ma`idah, “Then judge between them or turn away from them. But if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, God loves those who act justly,” were revealed regarding the blood money of Banu al-Nadir and Banu Qurayzah. That is because the slain of Banu al-Nadir had honor, and the full blood money was paid to them, while the Qurayzah were paid half the blood money. So they brought their case to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) regarding that, and God revealed that regarding them. So the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) held them to the truth regarding that, and made the blood money equal in that. And God knows best which of them it was. Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa’i narrated it in a similar manner from the hadith of Ibn Ishaq. Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ubaydullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Ali bin Salih, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There were Qurayzah and Nadir, and Nadir were more noble than Qurayzah, so if a Qurayzi killed a man from Nadir, he was killed for him, and if a Nadir killed a man from Qurayzah, blood money was paid with one hundred wasqs of dates. So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, a man from Nadir killed a man from Qurayzah, and they said: Give him over to him. They said: Between us and you is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the verse was revealed: And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Hibban, and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak narrated it in a similar manner from the hadith of Ubaydullah bin Musa. Qatadah, Muqatil bin Hibban, Ibn Zayd, and more than one other said the same. Al-Awfi and Ali bin Abi Talha Al-Walibi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that these verses were revealed about the two Jews who committed adultery, as the hadiths mentioned earlier. It is possible that these two reasons came together at the same time, so these verses were revealed about all of that, and God knows best. That is why he said after that, And We prescribed for them therein that a life for a life and an eye for an eye, to the end of it. This strengthens the fact that the reason for the revelation was the issue of retaliation, and God Almighty knows best. And the Almighty’s saying, And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, Al-Bara’ bin Azib, Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman, Ibn Abbas, Abu Majlaz, Abu Raja’ Al-Attardi, Ikrimah, Ubayd God bin Abdullah, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others said: They were revealed about the People of the Book. Al-Hasan Al-Basri added: They are obligatory upon us. Abd Al-Razzaq said on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, that these verses were revealed about the Children of Israel, and God was pleased with them for this nation. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Ibn Jarir also said: Yaqub told us, Hisham told us, Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulayman told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Alqamah and Masruq, that they asked Ibn Masoud about bribery. He said: It is from ill-gotten gains. They said: And in the ruling. He said: That is disbelief. Then he recited, And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. Al-Suddi said: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He said: Whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, abandoning it intentionally or acting unjustly while he knows, is one of the disbelievers. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He said: Whoever denies what God has revealed has disbelieved, and whoever acknowledges it but does not rule by it is a wrongdoer and a sinner. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Then he chose that the verse refers to the People of the Book, or whoever denies the ruling of God revealed in the Book. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of al-Sha’bi: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, he said to the Muslims. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Abd Al-Samad told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Al-Safar, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then those are the disbelievers. He said: This is about the Muslims. And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then those are the wrongdoers. He said: This is about the Jews. And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then those are the wicked. He said: This is about the Christians. Hisham and Al-Thawri narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Zakariya Ibn Abi Za’idah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi. Abd Al-Razzaq also said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked about his statement, And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, the verse. He said: It is disbelief. Ibn Tawus said: It is not like the one who disbelieves in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers. Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, that he said: Disbelief less than disbelief, oppression less than oppression, and immorality less than immorality. Ibn Jarir narrated it. Waki’ said, on the authority of Sa’id Al-Makki, on the authority of Tawus, And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then those are the wicked. They are the disbelievers.” He said: It is not disbelief that removes one from the religion. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Maqri told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hujayr, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He said: It is not the disbelief that you are going to. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, and he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, but they did not include it.
5:43: These noble verses were revealed about those who hastened to disbelief, who disobeyed God and His Messenger, who put their opinions and desires before the laws of God the Almighty, Of those who said, ‘We believe,’ with their mouths, while their hearts did not believe, meaning they showed faith with their tongues, but their hearts were ruined and empty of it. These are the hypocrites, Of those who are Jews, the enemies of Islam and its people. All of these are listeners to falsehood, meaning they respond to it and are affected by it. Listeners to other people who have not come to you, meaning they respond to other people who do not come to your gathering, O Muhammad. It was said that what is meant is that they listen to speech and pass it on to other people who are not present with you, from your enemies. They distort words from their [proper] places, meaning they interpret them in a way other than their interpretation, and they change them after they have understood them, and they know. They say, ‘If you are given this, then take it, and if you are not given it, then beware.’ It was said that it was revealed about a group of Jews. They killed a man and said: Come, let us go to Muhammad for judgment. If he rules with blood money, then accept it. If he rules with retaliation, then do not listen to him. The correct view is that it was revealed about the two Jews who committed adultery and had changed the Book of God that was in their hands from the command to stone those who were married among them. They distorted it and agreed among themselves to flog one hundred lashes, to be blackened and to be ridden on two donkeys upside down. When that event occurred after the migration, they said among themselves: Come, let us go to him for judgment. If he rules with flogging and blackening, then take it from him and make it an argument between you and God. It will be a prophet of God who has ruled between you with that. If he rules with stoning, then do not follow him in that. The hadiths have been narrated on this subject. Malik said, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both: The Jews came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned to him that a man and a woman among them had committed adultery. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them, What do you find in the Torah regarding stoning? They said, We will disgrace them and flog them. Abdullah ibn Salam said, “You have lied. It contains stoning.” So they brought the Torah. They brought the Torah and spread it out. One of them put his hand on the verse of stoning and read what came before it and what came after it. Abdullah ibn Salam said to him, Raise your hand. So he raised his hand and there was the verse of stoning. They said, “He has spoken the truth, O Muhammad. It contains the verse of stoning.” So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to be stoned. I saw the man bending over the woman to protect her from the stones. They both narrated it. This is the wording of Bukhari. In another wording of his: He said to the Jews, What will you do with them? They said: We will disfigure their faces and disgrace them. He said: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful. So they came and said to a man among them who was one-eyed and whom they were pleased with: Read. So he read until he reached a place in it, and he put his hand on it and said: Raise your hand. So he raised it, and behold, the verse of stoning appeared. He said: O Muhammad, in it is the verse of stoning, but we conceal it among ourselves. So he ordered them to be stoned. Muslim narrated that a Jewish man and a Jewish woman who had committed adultery were brought to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) set out until he came to the Jews and said, What do you find in the Torah about those who commit adultery? They said, We will blacken their faces and make them red, and we will carry them and make their faces different and they will be paraded around. He said, Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful. They brought it and recited it. When they came to the verse of stoning, the young man who was reciting put his hand on the verse of stoning and recited what was in front of it and behind it. Abdullah ibn Salam, who was with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), said to him, Tell him to raise his hand. So he raised his hand, and there was beneath it the verse of stoning. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded that they be stoned. Abdullah ibn Umar said, I was among those who stoned them, and I saw him protecting her from the stones with his own hand. Abu Dawud said: Ahmad ibn Sa`id al-Hamdani told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Hisham ibn Sa`d told us that Zayd ibn Aslam told him on the authority of Ibn `Umar who said: A group of Jews came and invited the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the Qaf. He came to them in the school house and said: O Abu al-Qasim, a man among us has committed adultery with a woman, so pass judgment. He said: They placed a cushion for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he sat on it. Then he said: Bring me the Torah. So it was brought to him. He removed the cushion from under him and placed the Torah on it and said: I believe in you and in the One who sent you down. Then he said: Bring me the most knowledgeable among you. So a young man was brought. Then he mentioned the story of stoning similar to the hadith of Malik on the authority of Nafi`. Al-Zuhri said: I heard a man from Muzaynah who follows knowledge and understands it, and we were with Ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: A Jewish man committed adultery with a woman. Some of them said to each other: Go to this prophet, for he was sent to alleviate the punishment. If he issues a fatwa to us other than stoning, we will accept it and use it as evidence before God. We said: The fatwa of one of your prophets. He said: So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sitting in the mosque with his companions, and they said: O Abu al-Qasim, what do you say about a man and a woman among them who commit adultery? He did not say a word to them until he reached the house of their schools. He stood at the door and said: I ask you by God who sent down the Torah to Moses, what do you find in the Torah regarding one who commits adultery if he is married? They said: He should be washed, flogged and flogged. Flogging is when the two adulterers are carried on a donkey and their backs are opposite each other and they are paraded around. He said: A young man among them was silent, but when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him, he was silent. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, insisted on asking him, so he said: O God, since you ask us, we find stoning in the Torah. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What was the first thing that you made permissible for God’s command? He said: A relative of one of our kings committed adultery, so stoning was delayed for him. Then a man among the people committed adultery after him, so he wanted to stone him, but his people prevented him and said: We will not stone our companion until you bring your companion and stone him. So they agreed on this punishment among themselves. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will judge by what is in the Torah. So he ordered them to be stoned. Al-Zuhri said: It reached us that this verse was revealed about them: “Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted to God judged by it.” So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was one of them. Narrated by Ahmad and Abu Dawood, and this is his wording, and Ibn Jarir. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: A Jewish man who had been flogged and had been bathed passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He called them and said, Is this how you find the punishment for adultery in your book? They said, Yes. So he called one of their scholars and said, I ask you by the One who sent down the Torah to Moses, is this how you find the punishment for adultery in your book? He said: No, by God, and if you had not asked me about this, I would not have told you. We find stoning as the punishment for adultery in our book, but it is common among our nobles. If we took the noble, we would leave him, and if we took the weak, we would carry out the punishment on him. So we said: Come, let us make something that we can carry out on the noble and the lowly. So we agreed on the stoning and flogging. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, I am the first to revive your command when they killed him. He said: So he ordered him to be stoned. He said: Then God Almighty revealed: O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you. They say: If you are given this, take it. That is, they say: Go to Muhammad, and if he gives you a fatwa regarding stoning and flogging, then take it. If he gives you a fatwa regarding stoning, then beware. He said: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, then those are the disbelievers. He said about the Jews, to His saying: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, then those are the wrongdoers. He said about the Jews: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, then those are the wicked. He said: Regarding all the disbelievers. It was narrated by Muslim alone, not by Al-Bukhari, Abu Dawood, Al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah, through more than one chain of transmission on the authority of Al-A’mash. Imam Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr Al-Humaidi said in his Musnad: Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, Mujalid bin Saeed Al-Hamadani told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: A man from the people of Fadak committed adultery, so the people of Fadak wrote to some Jews in Medina, asking Muhammad about that, so if he orders you to flog, then take it from him, and if he orders you to stone, then do not take it from him. So they asked him about that, and he said, Send to me the two most knowledgeable men among you. So they brought a one-eyed man called Ibn Suriya, and another, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them, You are more knowledgeable than those before you. They said, Our people have called us to that. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them, Do you not have the Torah in which is the judgment of God? They said, Yes.
