The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Then I ask you by He who split the sea for the Children of Israel, and shaded you with clouds, and saved you from the people of Pharaoh, and sent down manna and quails upon the Children of Israel, what do you find in the Torah regarding stoning?” One of them said, To the other: I have never heard anything like it. Then they said: We find that looking repeatedly is adultery, embracing is adultery, and kissing is adultery. So if four testify that they saw him appear and repeat, as a pen enters a kohl container, then stoning is obligatory. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is it. So he ordered him to be stoned, and then the verse was revealed: “So if they come to you, either judge between them or turn away from them. But if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all. But if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, God loves those who act justly.” Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Mujalid, with a similar wording. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Jews brought a man and a woman from among them who had committed adultery, so he said: Bring me the two most knowledgeable men among you. So they brought him the two sons of Suriya, and he asked them: How do you find the matter of these two in the Torah? They said: We find that if four testify that they saw his penis in her vagina like a kohl stick in a container, they are to be stoned. He said: What prevents you from stoning them? They said: Our authority has gone and we dislike killing. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for witnesses, and four came and testified that they saw his penis like a kohl stick in a container. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that they be stoned. Then Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Al-Sha’bi and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i as a mursal, and he did not mention in it: So he called for witnesses and they testified. These hadiths indicate that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled in accordance with the ruling of the Torah. This is not out of respect for them for what they believe to be correct, because they are commanded to follow the Muhammadan law without fail. Rather, this is by special revelation from God Almighty to him regarding this, and His asking them about it, to confirm what they have in their hands, which they conspired to conceal, deny, and not act upon for those long ages. So when they acknowledged it, knowing that it was contrary to it, their deviation, stubbornness, and denial of what they believe to be correct from the book in their hands, and their turning to the arbitration of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was only due to their own whims and desires to agree with their opinions, not because they believe that what he rules is correct. For this reason, they said, If you are given this, meaning flogging and burning, then take it, meaning accept it, and if you are not given it, then beware, meaning from accepting and following it. God the Almighty said: “And whomsoever God intends to test, you will not possess for him anything against God. Those are the ones whose hearts God does not intend to purify. For them is disgrace in this world, and for them is a great punishment in the Hereafter. They are listeners to falsehood, devourers of unlawful gain, as Ibn Mas`ud and others have said. How can God purify the heart of one who has this characteristic and how can He respond to him? Then He said to His Prophet: “If they come to you” meaning seeking judgment from you, “then judge between them or turn away from them. But if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all” meaning, you do not have to judge between them, because they do not intend by their judgment to you to follow the truth, but rather what agrees with their desires. Ibn `Abbas, Mujahid, `Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, Zayd ibn Aslam, `Ata’ Al-Khurasani, Al-Hasan and others have said: It was abrogated by His statement: And judge between them by what God has revealed, and And if you judge, judge between them with justice, meaning with truth and justice, even if they are oppressors who have deviated from the path of justice. Indeed, God loves those who act justly. Then the Almighty said, denouncing them for their corrupt opinions and their deviant intentions in abandoning what they believe to be correct from the Book in their hands, which they claim they are commanded to adhere to forever, then they went beyond its ruling and turned to something else which they believe in the matter to be false and not binding on them, so He said, “And how can they make you judge while they have the Torah, in which is the ruling of God? Then they turn away after that. And those are not believers.” Then He praised the Torah that He sent down to His servant and Messenger Moses, son of Imran, so He said, “Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to God] judged by it for those who were Jews,” meaning they do not go beyond its ruling, nor do they change it, nor do they distort it, and the rabbis and the scholars, meaning likewise the rabbis among them, who are the learned worshippers, and the rabbis, who are the scholars, for what they were entrusted with of the Book of God, meaning what they were entrusted with of the Book of God which they were commanded to make manifest and act upon, “and they were witnesses over it. So do not fear the people but fear Me,” meaning do not fear them and fear. From me, “And do not exchange My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers.” There are two sayings about it, the explanation of which will come. Another reason for the revelation of these noble verses Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim bin Abbas told us, Abdul Rahman bin Abi Al-Zinad told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God revealed: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers “And it is those who are the wrongdoers” And it is those who are the defiantly disobedient Ibn Abbas said: God revealed it regarding the two groups of Jews, one of which had subjugated the other in the pre-Islamic era until they were satisfied and agreed that for every slain person killed by the powerful woman from the humiliated, his ransom would be fifty wasqs, and for every slain person killed by the humiliated woman from the powerful woman, his ransom would be one hundred wasqs. They remained like that until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, and the humiliated woman from the powerful woman killed someone, so the powerful woman sent to the humiliated woman to send us one hundred wasqs. The humiliated woman said: Was there ever a group of two groups whose religion was the same, whose lineage was the same, and whose country was the same, and the blood money of one of them was half the blood money of the other? We only gave you this out of your oppression of us and fear from you. But when Muhammad came, we will not give you anything. So war almost broke out between them. Then they agreed to make the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among them. Then the Aziza mentioned and said: By God, Muhammad will not give you from them twice what he gives them from you, and they have told the truth. They did not give us this except out of injustice from us and to subjugate them. So they sent to Muhammad someone to tell you his opinion. If he gives you what you want, you will rule according to him, and if he does not give you, you will be wary and do not rule according to him. So they sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, some hypocrites to tell them the opinion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So when they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God informed His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, of their entire affair and what they wanted. So God Almighty revealed: O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you until His saying the wicked. By God, it was revealed about them, and God Almighty meant them. Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Abi al-Zinad from his father in a similar manner. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Hannad ibn al-Sarri and Abu Kurayb told us: Yunus ibn Bakir told us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Dawud ibn al-Husayn told me on the authority of `Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas: The verses in al-Ma`idah, “Then judge between them or turn away from them. But if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, God loves those who act justly,” were revealed regarding the blood money of Banu al-Nadir and Banu Qurayzah. That is because the slain of Banu al-Nadir had honor, and the full blood money was paid to them, while the Qurayzah were paid half the blood money. So they brought their case to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) regarding that, and God revealed that regarding them. So the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) held them to the truth regarding that, and made the blood money equal in that. And God knows best which of them it was. Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa’i narrated it in a similar manner from the hadith of Ibn Ishaq. Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ubaydullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Ali bin Salih, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There were Qurayzah and Nadir, and Nadir were more noble than Qurayzah, so if a Qurayzi killed a man from Nadir, he was killed for him, and if a Nadir killed a man from Qurayzah, blood money was paid with one hundred wasqs of dates. So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, a man from Nadir killed a man from Qurayzah, and they said: Give him over to him. They said: Between us and you is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the verse was revealed: And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Hibban, and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak narrated it in a similar manner from the hadith of Ubaydullah bin Musa. Qatadah, Muqatil bin Hibban, Ibn Zayd, and more than one other said the same. Al-Awfi and Ali bin Abi Talha Al-Walibi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that these verses were revealed about the two Jews who committed adultery, as the hadiths mentioned earlier. It is possible that these two reasons came together at the same time, so these verses were revealed about all of that, and God knows best. That is why he said after that, And We prescribed for them therein that a life for a life and an eye for an eye, to the end of it. This strengthens the fact that the reason for the revelation was the issue of retaliation, and God Almighty knows best. And the Almighty’s saying, And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, Al-Bara’ bin Azib, Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman, Ibn Abbas, Abu Majlaz, Abu Raja’ Al-Attardi, Ikrimah, Ubayd God bin Abdullah, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others said: They were revealed about the People of the Book. Al-Hasan Al-Basri added: They are obligatory upon us. Abd Al-Razzaq said on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, that these verses were revealed about the Children of Israel, and God was pleased with them for this nation. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Ibn Jarir also said: Yaqub told us, Hisham told us, Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulayman told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Alqamah and Masruq, that they asked Ibn Masoud about bribery. He said: It is from ill-gotten gains. They said: And in the ruling. He said: That is disbelief. Then he recited, And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. Al-Suddi said: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He said: Whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, abandoning it intentionally or acting unjustly while he knows, is one of the disbelievers. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He said: Whoever denies what God has revealed has disbelieved, and whoever acknowledges it but does not rule by it is a wrongdoer and a sinner. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Then he chose that the verse refers to the People of the Book, or whoever denies the ruling of God revealed in the Book. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of al-Sha’bi: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, he said to the Muslims. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Abd Al-Samad told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Al-Safar, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then those are the disbelievers. He said: This is about the Muslims. And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then those are the wrongdoers. He said: This is about the Jews. And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then those are the wicked. He said: This is about the Christians. Hisham and Al-Thawri narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Zakariya Ibn Abi Za’idah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi. Abd Al-Razzaq also said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked about his statement, And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, the verse. He said: It is disbelief. Ibn Tawus said: It is not like the one who disbelieves in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers. Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, that he said: Disbelief less than disbelief, oppression less than oppression, and immorality less than immorality. Ibn Jarir narrated it. Waki’ said, on the authority of Sa’id Al-Makki, on the authority of Tawus, And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then those are the wicked. They are the disbelievers.” He said: It is not disbelief that removes one from the religion. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Maqri told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hujayr, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He said: It is not the disbelief that you are going to. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, and he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, but they did not include it.
5:44: These noble verses were revealed about those who hastened to disbelief, who disobeyed God and His Messenger, who put their opinions and desires before the laws of God the Almighty, Of those who said, ‘We believe,’ with their mouths, while their hearts did not believe, meaning they showed faith with their tongues, but their hearts were ruined and empty of it. These are the hypocrites, Of those who are Jews, the enemies of Islam and its people. All of these are listeners to falsehood, meaning they respond to it and are affected by it. Listeners to other people who have not come to you, meaning they respond to other people who do not come to your gathering, O Muhammad. It was said that what is meant is that they listen to speech and pass it on to other people who are not present with you, from your enemies. They distort words from their [proper] places, meaning they interpret them in a way other than their interpretation, and they change them after they have understood them, and they know. They say, ‘If you are given this, then take it, and if you are not given it, then beware.’ It was said that it was revealed about a group of Jews. They killed a man and said: Come, let us go to Muhammad for judgment. If he rules with blood money, then accept it. If he rules with retaliation, then do not listen to him. The correct view is that it was revealed about the two Jews who committed adultery and had changed the Book of God that was in their hands from the command to stone those who were married among them. They distorted it and agreed among themselves to flog one hundred lashes, to be blackened and to be ridden on two donkeys upside down. When that event occurred after the migration, they said among themselves: Come, let us go to him for judgment. If he rules with flogging and blackening, then take it from him and make it an argument between you and God. It will be a prophet of God who has ruled between you with that. If he rules with stoning, then do not follow him in that. The hadiths have been narrated on this subject. Malik said, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both: The Jews came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned to him that a man and a woman among them had committed adultery. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them, What do you find in the Torah regarding stoning? They said, We will disgrace them and flog them. Abdullah ibn Salam said, “You have lied. It contains stoning.” So they brought the Torah. They brought the Torah and spread it out. One of them put his hand on the verse of stoning and read what came before it and what came after it. Abdullah ibn Salam said to him, Raise your hand. So he raised his hand and there was the verse of stoning. They said, “He has spoken the truth, O Muhammad. It contains the verse of stoning.” So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to be stoned. I saw the man bending over the woman to protect her from the stones. They both narrated it. This is the wording of Bukhari. In another wording of his: He said to the Jews, What will you do with them? They said: We will disfigure their faces and disgrace them. He said: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful. So they came and said to a man among them who was one-eyed and whom they were pleased with: Read. So he read until he reached a place in it, and he put his hand on it and said: Raise your hand. So he raised it, and behold, the verse of stoning appeared. He said: O Muhammad, in it is the verse of stoning, but we conceal it among ourselves. So he ordered them to be stoned. Muslim narrated that a Jewish man and a Jewish woman who had committed adultery were brought to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) set out until he came to the Jews and said, What do you find in the Torah about those who commit adultery? They said, We will blacken their faces and make them red, and we will carry them and make their faces different and they will be paraded around. He said, Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful. They brought it and recited it. When they came to the verse of stoning, the young man who was reciting put his hand on the verse of stoning and recited what was in front of it and behind it. Abdullah ibn Salam, who was with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), said to him, Tell him to raise his hand. So he raised his hand, and there was beneath it the verse of stoning. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded that they be stoned. Abdullah ibn Umar said, I was among those who stoned them, and I saw him protecting her from the stones with his own hand. Abu Dawud said: Ahmad ibn Sa`id al-Hamdani told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Hisham ibn Sa`d told us that Zayd ibn Aslam told him on the authority of Ibn `Umar who said: A group of Jews came and invited the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the Qaf. He came to them in the school house and said: O Abu al-Qasim, a man among us has committed adultery with a woman, so pass judgment. He said: They placed a cushion for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he sat on it. Then he said: Bring me the Torah. So it was brought to him. He removed the cushion from under him and placed the Torah on it and said: I believe in you and in the One who sent you down. Then he said: Bring me the most knowledgeable among you. So a young man was brought. Then he mentioned the story of stoning similar to the hadith of Malik on the authority of Nafi`. Al-Zuhri said: I heard a man from Muzaynah who follows knowledge and understands it, and we were with Ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: A Jewish man committed adultery with a woman. Some of them said to each other: Go to this prophet, for he was sent to alleviate the punishment. If he issues a fatwa to us other than stoning, we will accept it and use it as evidence before God. We said: The fatwa of one of your prophets. He said: So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sitting in the mosque with his companions, and they said: O Abu al-Qasim, what do you say about a man and a woman among them who commit adultery? He did not say a word to them until he reached the house of their schools. He stood at the door and said: I ask you by God who sent down the Torah to Moses, what do you find in the Torah regarding one who commits adultery if he is married? They said: He should be washed, flogged and flogged. Flogging is when the two adulterers are carried on a donkey and their backs are opposite each other and they are paraded around. He said: A young man among them was silent, but when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him, he was silent. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, insisted on asking him, so he said: O God, since you ask us, we find stoning in the Torah. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What was the first thing that you made permissible for God’s command? He said: A relative of one of our kings committed adultery, so stoning was delayed for him. Then a man among the people committed adultery after him, so he wanted to stone him, but his people prevented him and said: We will not stone our companion until you bring your companion and stone him. So they agreed on this punishment among themselves. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will judge by what is in the Torah. So he ordered them to be stoned. Al-Zuhri said: It reached us that this verse was revealed about them: “Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted to God judged by it.” So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was one of them. Narrated by Ahmad and Abu Dawood, and this is his wording, and Ibn Jarir. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: A Jewish man who had been flogged and had been bathed passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He called them and said, Is this how you find the punishment for adultery in your book? They said, Yes. So he called one of their scholars and said, I ask you by the One who sent down the Torah to Moses, is this how you find the punishment for adultery in your book? He said: No, by God, and if you had not asked me about this, I would not have told you. We find stoning as the punishment for adultery in our book, but it is common among our nobles. If we took the noble, we would leave him, and if we took the weak, we would carry out the punishment on him. So we said: Come, let us make something that we can carry out on the noble and the lowly. So we agreed on the stoning and flogging. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, I am the first to revive your command when they killed him. He said: So he ordered him to be stoned. He said: Then God Almighty revealed: O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you. They say: If you are given this, take it. That is, they say: Go to Muhammad, and if he gives you a fatwa regarding stoning and flogging, then take it. If he gives you a fatwa regarding stoning, then beware. He said: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, then those are the disbelievers. He said about the Jews, to His saying: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, then those are the wrongdoers. He said about the Jews: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, then those are the wicked. He said: Regarding all the disbelievers. It was narrated by Muslim alone, not by Al-Bukhari, Abu Dawood, Al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah, through more than one chain of transmission on the authority of Al-A’mash. Imam Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr Al-Humaidi said in his Musnad: Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, Mujalid bin Saeed Al-Hamadani told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: A man from the people of Fadak committed adultery, so the people of Fadak wrote to some Jews in Medina, asking Muhammad about that, so if he orders you to flog, then take it from him, and if he orders you to stone, then do not take it from him. So they asked him about that, and he said, Send to me the two most knowledgeable men among you. So they brought a one-eyed man called Ibn Suriya, and another, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them, You are more knowledgeable than those before you. They said, Our people have called us to that. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them, Do you not have the Torah in which is the judgment of God? They said, Yes. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Then I ask you by He who split the sea for the Children of Israel, and shaded you with clouds, and saved you from the people of Pharaoh, and sent down manna and quails upon the Children of Israel, what do you find in the Torah regarding stoning?” One of them said, To the other: I have never heard anything like it. Then they said: We find that looking repeatedly is adultery, embracing is adultery, and kissing is adultery. So if four testify that they saw him appear and repeat, as a pen enters a kohl container, then stoning is obligatory. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is it. So he ordered him to be stoned, and then the verse was revealed: “So if they come to you, either judge between them or turn away from them. But if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all. But if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, God loves those who act justly.” Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Mujalid, with a similar wording. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Jews brought a man and a woman from among them who had committed adultery, so he said: Bring me the two most knowledgeable men among you. So they brought him the two sons of Suriya, and he asked them: How do you find the matter of these two in the Torah? They said: We find that if four testify that they saw his penis in her vagina like a kohl stick in a container, they are to be stoned. He said: What prevents you from stoning them? They said: Our authority has gone and we dislike killing. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for witnesses, and four came and testified that they saw his penis like a kohl stick in a container. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that they be stoned. Then Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Al-Sha’bi and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i as a mursal, and he did not mention in it: So he called for witnesses and they testified. These hadiths indicate that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled in accordance with the ruling of the Torah. This is not out of respect for them for what they believe to be correct, because they are commanded to follow the Muhammadan law without fail. Rather, this is by special revelation from God Almighty to him regarding this, and His asking them about it, to confirm what they have in their hands, which they conspired to conceal, deny, and not act upon for those long ages. So when they acknowledged it, knowing that it was contrary to it, their deviation, stubbornness, and denial of what they believe to be correct from the book in their hands, and their turning to the arbitration of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was only due to their own whims and desires to agree with their opinions, not because they believe that what he rules is correct. For this reason, they said, If you are given this, meaning flogging and burning, then take it, meaning accept it, and if you are not given it, then beware, meaning from accepting and following it. God the Almighty said: “And whomsoever God intends to test, you will not possess for him anything against God. Those are the ones whose hearts God does not intend to purify. For them is disgrace in this world, and for them is a great punishment in the Hereafter. They are listeners to falsehood, devourers of unlawful gain, as Ibn Mas`ud and others have said. How can God purify the heart of one who has this characteristic and how can He respond to him? Then He said to His Prophet: “If they come to you” meaning seeking judgment from you, “then judge between them or turn away from them. But if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all” meaning, you do not have to judge between them, because they do not intend by their judgment to you to follow the truth, but rather what agrees with their desires. Ibn `Abbas, Mujahid, `Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Suddi, Zayd ibn Aslam, `Ata’ Al-Khurasani, Al-Hasan and others have said: It was abrogated by His statement: And judge between them by what God has revealed, and And if you judge, judge between them with justice, meaning with truth and justice, even if they are oppressors who have deviated from the path of justice. Indeed, God loves those who act justly. Then the Almighty said, denouncing them for their corrupt opinions and their deviant intentions in abandoning what they believe to be correct from the Book in their hands, which they claim they are commanded to adhere to forever, then they went beyond its ruling and turned to something else which they believe in the matter to be false and not binding on them, so He said, “And how can they make you judge while they have the Torah, in which is the ruling of God? Then they turn away after that. And those are not believers.” Then He praised the Torah that He sent down to His servant and Messenger Moses, son of Imran, so He said, “Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to God] judged by it for those who were Jews,” meaning they do not go beyond its ruling, nor do they change it, nor do they distort it, and the rabbis and the scholars, meaning likewise the rabbis among them, who are the learned worshippers, and the rabbis, who are the scholars, for what they were entrusted with of the Book of God, meaning what they were entrusted with of the Book of God which they were commanded to make manifest and act upon, “and they were witnesses over it. So do not fear the people but fear Me,” meaning do not fear them and fear. From me, “And do not exchange My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers.” There are two sayings about it, the explanation of which will come. Another reason for the revelation of these noble verses Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim bin Abbas told us, Abdul Rahman bin Abi Al-Zinad told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God revealed: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers “And it is those who are the wrongdoers” And it is those who are the defiantly disobedient Ibn Abbas said: God revealed it regarding the two groups of Jews, one of which had subjugated the other in the pre-Islamic era until they were satisfied and agreed that for every slain person killed by the powerful woman from the humiliated, his ransom would be fifty wasqs, and for every slain person killed by the humiliated woman from the powerful woman, his ransom would be one hundred wasqs. They remained like that until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, and the humiliated woman from the powerful woman killed someone, so the powerful woman sent to the humiliated woman to send us one hundred wasqs. The humiliated woman said: Was there ever a group of two groups whose religion was the same, whose lineage was the same, and whose country was the same, and the blood money of one of them was half the blood money of the other? We only gave you this out of your oppression of us and fear from you. But when Muhammad came, we will not give you anything. So war almost broke out between them. Then they agreed to make the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among them. Then the Aziza mentioned and said: By God, Muhammad will not give you from them twice what he gives them from you, and they have told the truth. They did not give us this except out of injustice from us and to subjugate them. So they sent to Muhammad someone to tell you his opinion. If he gives you what you want, you will rule according to him, and if he does not give you, you will be wary and do not rule according to him. So they sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, some hypocrites to tell them the opinion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So when they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God informed His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, of their entire affair and what they wanted. So God Almighty revealed: O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you until His saying the wicked. By God, it was revealed about them, and God Almighty meant them. Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Abi al-Zinad from his father in a similar manner. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Hannad ibn al-Sarri and Abu Kurayb told us: Yunus ibn Bakir told us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Dawud ibn al-Husayn told me on the authority of `Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas: The verses in al-Ma`idah, “Then judge between them or turn away from them. But if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, God loves those who act justly,” were revealed regarding the blood money of Banu al-Nadir and Banu Qurayzah. That is because the slain of Banu al-Nadir had honor, and the full blood money was paid to them, while the Qurayzah were paid half the blood money. So they brought their case to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) regarding that, and God revealed that regarding them. So the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) held them to the truth regarding that, and made the blood money equal in that. And God knows best which of them it was. Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa’i narrated it in a similar manner from the hadith of Ibn Ishaq. Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ubaydullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Ali bin Salih, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There were Qurayzah and Nadir, and Nadir were more noble than Qurayzah, so if a Qurayzi killed a man from Nadir, he was killed for him, and if a Nadir killed a man from Qurayzah, blood money was paid with one hundred wasqs of dates. So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, a man from Nadir killed a man from Qurayzah, and they said: Give him over to him. They said: Between us and you is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the verse was revealed: And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Hibban, and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak narrated it in a similar manner from the hadith of Ubaydullah bin Musa. Qatadah, Muqatil bin Hibban, Ibn Zayd, and more than one other said the same. Al-Awfi and Ali bin Abi Talha Al-Walibi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that these verses were revealed about the two Jews who committed adultery, as the hadiths mentioned earlier. It is possible that these two reasons came together at the same time, so these verses were revealed about all of that, and God knows best. That is why he said after that, And We prescribed for them therein that a life for a life and an eye for an eye, to the end of it. This strengthens the fact that the reason for the revelation was the issue of retaliation, and God Almighty knows best. And the Almighty’s saying, And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, Al-Bara’ bin Azib, Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman, Ibn Abbas, Abu Majlaz, Abu Raja’ Al-Attardi, Ikrimah, Ubayd God bin Abdullah, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others said: They were revealed about the People of the Book. Al-Hasan Al-Basri added: They are obligatory upon us. Abd Al-Razzaq said on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, that these verses were revealed about the Children of Israel, and God was pleased with them for this nation. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Ibn Jarir also said: Yaqub told us, Hisham told us, Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulayman told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Alqamah and Masruq, that they asked Ibn Masoud about bribery. He said: It is from ill-gotten gains. They said: And in the ruling. He said: That is disbelief. Then he recited, And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. Al-Suddi said: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He said: Whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, abandoning it intentionally or acting unjustly while he knows, is one of the disbelievers. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He said: Whoever denies what God has revealed has disbelieved, and whoever acknowledges it but does not rule by it is a wrongdoer and a sinner. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Then he chose that the verse refers to the People of the Book, or whoever denies the ruling of God revealed in the Book. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of al-Sha’bi: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, he said to the Muslims. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Abd Al-Samad told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Al-Safar, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then those are the disbelievers. He said: This is about the Muslims. And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then those are the wrongdoers. He said: This is about the Jews. And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then those are the wicked. He said: This is about the Christians. Hisham and Al-Thawri narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Zakariya Ibn Abi Za’idah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi. Abd Al-Razzaq also said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked about his statement, And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, the verse. He said: It is disbelief. Ibn Tawus said: It is not like the one who disbelieves in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers. Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, that he said: Disbelief less than disbelief, oppression less than oppression, and immorality less than immorality. Ibn Jarir narrated it. Waki’ said, on the authority of Sa’id Al-Makki, on the authority of Tawus, And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed, then those are the wicked. They are the disbelievers.” He said: It is not disbelief that removes one from the religion. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Maqri told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Hujayr, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. He said: It is not the disbelief that you are going to. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, and he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, but they did not include it.
5:45: This is also something that the Jews were rebuked for and criticized, because they have in the text of the Torah that a life for a life, and they deliberately and stubbornly contradict the ruling on that, and they restrict the Nadhri from the Qurashi, and they do not restrict the Qurashi from the Nadhri, but rather they turn to blood money as they contradicted the ruling of the Torah that is stipulated for them in stoning the married adulterer, and they turned to what they agreed upon of flogging, blackening, and publicizing. For this reason, He said there, And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers, because they denied the ruling of God intentionally, stubbornly, and deliberately. And He said here, Then it is those who are the wrongdoers, because they did not treat the wronged fairly from the wrongdoer in the matter in which God commanded justice and equality between everyone, so they contradicted, were unjust, and transgressed against one another. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Adam told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Yunus bin Yazid, on the authority of Ali bin Yazid, the brother of Yunus bin Yazid, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Anas bin Malik that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it: And We ordained for them therein that a life for a life and an eye for an eye, placing the life in the accusative case and raising the eye. This is how Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Abdullah bin al-Mubarak. Al-Tirmidhi said it is good and strange. Al-Bukhari said that Ibn al-Mubarak was the only one to narrate this hadith. Many of those who went from the scholars of the principles of jurisprudence and jurists have used as evidence that the law of those before us is a law for us if it is narrated as established and not abrogated, as is well-known from the majority, and as Sheikh Abu Ishaq al-Isfarayini narrated from the text of al-Shafi’i, and most of the companions with this verse, since the ruling with us was in accordance with it in crimes according to all the imams. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: It applies to them and to all people in general. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Sheikh Abu Zakariya al-Nawawi narrated three aspects regarding this issue, the third of which is that the law of Abraham is an argument and not others. He confirmed that it is not an argument, and Sheikh Abu Ishaq al-Isfarayini transmitted statements from al-Shafi’i and most of the companions, and he preferred that it is an argument according to the majority of our companions. And God knows best. Imam Abu Nasr ibn al-Sabbagh, may God have mercy on him, narrated in his book al-Shamel the consensus of scholars on using this verse as evidence for what it indicates. All the imams have used this verse as evidence that a man is killed for a woman based on the generality of this noble verse. Likewise, it was mentioned in the hadith narrated by al-Nasa’i and others that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote in the book of Amr ibn Hazm that a man is killed for a woman, and in another hadith the blood of Muslims is equal, and this is the opinion of the majority of scholars. And from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, that if a man kills a woman, he is not killed for her unless her guardian pays half of the blood money to his guardians, because her blood money is half of the blood money of a man. Ahmad went to this in a narration, and it was narrated from al-Hasan, Ata’, and Uthman al-Basti, and a narration from Ahmad, that if a man kills a woman, he is not killed for her, but her blood money is obligatory. And thus Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, used this verse as evidence that a Muslim is killed for a non-Muslim dhimmi, and that a free man is killed for a slave. The majority disagreed with him on both of them. In the two Sahihs, from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A Muslim is not killed for a disbeliever. As for the slave, there are many reports from the predecessors that they did not restrict the slave from the free man, nor did they kill a free man for a slave. There are hadiths about this that are not authentic, and Al-Shafi’i reported the consensus contrary to the Hanafi view on this, but this does not necessarily invalidate their view except with evidence that specifies the noble verse. What Ibn al-Sabbagh said about using this noble verse as evidence is supported by the authentic hadith on this matter, as Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi Uday told us, Hamid told us on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that al-Rabi’, the paternal aunt of Anas, broke the front tooth of a slave girl, so they asked the people for forgiveness but they refused, so they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said, Retaliation. Her brother Anas ibn al-Nadr said, O Messenger of God, will so-and-so’s front tooth be broken? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, O Anas, the Book of God is retaliation. He said, No, by Him who sent you with the truth, do not break so-and-so’s front tooth. The people agreed and forgave and left the retaliation, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, There are some servants of God who, if they swear by God, He will fulfill their oath. They included it in the two Sahihs. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Muthanna al-Ansari narrated it in the famous part of his hadith, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that al-Rabi’, the daughter of al-Nadr, his paternal aunt, slapped a slave girl and broke her front tooth, so they compensated them with compensation but they refused. They asked for compensation and forgiveness, but they refused. So they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he ordered them to retaliate. Then her brother Anas ibn al-Nadr came and said: O Messenger of God, will you break al-Rabi’s front tooth? By Him Who sent you with the truth, her front tooth will not be broken. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Anas, God’s decree is retaliation. So the people pardoned him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There are among God’s servants those who, if they swear by God, He will fulfill their oath. Narrated by al-Bukhari on the authority of al-Ansari in a similar manner. Abu Dawud narrated: Ahmad ibn Hanbal told us, Muadh ibn Hisham told us, my father told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn, that a slave of poor people cut off the ear of a slave of rich people. His family came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, we are poor people. So he did not impose anything on him. And al-Nasa’i narrated it likewise on the authority of Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, on the authority of Muadh ibn Hisham al-Dastawai, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatadah, with the same chain of transmission. This is a strong chain of transmission, all of whose men are trustworthy. It is a problematic hadith, unless it is said that the perpetrator was before puberty, so there is no retaliation against him. Perhaps he bore the blood money for what was lost from the slave of the rich for the poor, or he excused them from it. And the Almighty’s saying: And wounds are retaliation. Ali bin Abi Talha said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A life is killed for a life, an eye is gouged out for an eye, a nose is cut off for a nose, a tooth is pulled out for a tooth, and wounds are retaliated for wounds. In this, the free Muslims are equal among themselves, their men and women, if it was deliberate in a life or less than a life, and the slaves are equal among themselves, their men and women, if it was deliberate in a life or less than a life. Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. Important rule Sometimes wounds are in a joint, in which case retaliation is required by consensus, such as amputating the hand, foot, palm, foot, and the like. However, if the wound is not in a joint but in a bone, Malik, may God have mercy on him, said: Retaliation is required for it, except in the thigh and the like, because it is a dangerous matter. Abu Hanifa and his two companions said: Retaliation is not required for any bone except the tooth. Al-Shafi’i said: Retaliation is not obligatory for any bone at all. This was narrated from ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab and Ibn ‘Abbas. ‘Ata’, al-Sha’bi, al-Hasan al-Basri, al-Zuhri, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, and ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz said the same. Sufyan al-Thawri and al-Layth ibn Sa’d also held this view. This is the well-known view of Imam Ahmad. Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, cited the hadith of al-Rabi’ bint al-Nadr as evidence for his view that there is no retaliation for a bone except for a tooth. The hadith of al-Rabi’ is not an argument because it was narrated in the words Jari’ah’s incisor was broken. It is possible that it fell without being broken, so retaliation is obligatory in this case by consensus. They completed the evidence from what Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn ‘Ayyash, on the authority of Dahsham ibn Qaran, on the authority of Nimran ibn Jariyah, on the authority of his father Jariyah ibn Thafar al-Hanafi: “A man struck a man on his forearm with a sword, not at the joint, and cut it off. He sought the help of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who ordered blood money for him. He said: “O Messenger of God, I want retaliation.” He said: Take the blood money, may God bless you in it. He did not rule. He has retaliation, and Sheikh Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said: This hadith has no chain of transmission other than this, and Dahsham bin Qaran Al-Akli is weak, a Bedouin whose hadith is not reliable, and Nimran bin Jariyah is weak, a Bedouin as well, and his father Jariyah bin Thafar is mentioned among the Companions, then they said: It is not permissible to take retaliation for a wound until the wound of the victim heals, so if retaliation is taken from him before it heals and then his wound worsens, then he does not get anything, and the evidence for that is what Imam Ahmad narrated on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather that a man stabbed a man with a horn in his knee, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Give me retaliation, so he said: Until you recover, then he came to him and said: Give me retaliation, so he gave him retaliation and he said: O Messenger of God, you have limped, so he said: I forbade you and you disobeyed me, so may God distance you and make your limping null. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade taking retaliation for a wound until its owner recovers, and Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. [Question] If the victim takes revenge on the offender and he dies as a result of the retaliation, then nothing is due from him according to Malik, Al-Shafi’i, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and it is the opinion of the majority of the Companions, Followers, and others. Abu Hanifa said: The blood money must be paid from the money of the one taking revenge. Aamer Al-Sha’bi, Ata’, Tawus, Umar ibn Dinar, Al-Harith Al-‘Uqli, Ibn Abi Laila, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, Al-Zuhri, and Al-Thawri said: The blood money must be paid by the family of the one taking revenge. Ibn Mas’ud, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Hakam ibn ‘Uyaynah, and ‘Uthman Al-Basti said: The amount of the injury is dropped from the one taking revenge, and the remainder must be paid from his money. And the Almighty said: So whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So whoever gives it in charity means: So whoever pardons and gives it in charity, it is an expiation for the one who was wronged and a reward for the one who sought it. Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of Ata bin al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for the one who wounded him and the reward for the one who was wounded is from God, the Almighty. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, then he said: And it was narrated on the authority of Khaithamah bin Abd al-Rahman, Mujahid, Ibrahim in one of his two opinions, Amer al-Sha’bi, and Jabir bin Zaid something similar to that. [The second aspect] Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Hammad bin Zadhan told us, Harmi told us, meaning Ibn Amara, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Amara, meaning Ibn Abi Hafsa, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, regarding the statement of God Almighty, But whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him, he said: for the wounded. And it was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i in one of his two opinions and Abu Ishaq Al-Hamadani something similar to that, and Ibn Jarir narrated something similar on the authority of Amer Al-Sha’bi and Qatadah. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus bin Habib told us, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi told us, Shu`bah told us on the authority of Qays, meaning Ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Tariq bin Shihab narrating on the authority of al-Haytham bin al-`Aryan al-Nakha`i, who said: I saw `Abdullah bin `Amr with Mu`awiyah, red, resembling a slave, so I asked him about the statement of God, But whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him. He said: It removes from him some of his sins in proportion to the amount he gave in charity. This is how Sufyan al-Thawri narrated it on the authority of Qays bin Muslim, and this is how Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Sufyan and Shu`bah. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ali told me, Abd al-Rahim ibn Muhammad al-Majashi’i told us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hajjaj al-Mahri told us, Yahya ibn Sulayman al-Ja’fi told us, Mu’alla, meaning ibn Hilal, told us that he heard Abaan ibn Tha’lab from al-Aryan ibn al-Haytham ibn al-Aswad, from Abdullah ibn Amr, from Abaan ibn Tha’lab, from al-Sha’bi, from a man from the Ansar, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement, So whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him, he said: It is the one whose tooth is broken, or whose hand is cut off, or something is cut off from him, or who is wounded in his body, and he forgives that, he said, “so the amount of his sins is reduced from him. If it is a quarter of the blood money, then a quarter of his sins, and if it is a third, then a third of his sins, and if it is the blood money, then his sins are reduced from him in the same way.” Then Ibn Jarir said: Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told us, Ibn Fadil told us on the authority of Yunus bin Abi Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Safar, who said: A man from Quraysh pushed a man from the Ansar, and his front tooth broke. The Ansari took him to Muawiyah. When the man insisted, he said: It is up to you and your friend. He said: Abu al-Darda was with Muawiyah, so Abu al-Darda said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There is no Muslim who is afflicted with something in his body and gives it away, except that God raises him a degree because of it and removes a sin from him because of it. The Ansari said: Did you hear that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: My ears heard it and my heart retained it. So he let the Quraysh man go. Muawiyah said: Give him some money. This is how Ibn Jarir narrated it. Imam Ahmad narrated it and said: We were told by Wakee’, we were told by Yunus bin Abi Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Safar, who said: A man from Quraysh broke the tooth of a man from the Ansar, so he sought redress from Mu’awiyah against him. Mu’awiyah said: We will satisfy him, but the Ansari insisted, so Mu’awiyah said: You deal with your friend, and Abu al-Darda’ was sitting, so Abu al-Darda’ said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There is no Muslim who is afflicted with something in his body and gives it in charity, except that God will raise him a degree thereby and remove a sin from him thereby. The Ansari said: Then I have forgiven him. And thus it was narrated by al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Ibn al-Mubarak, and by Ibn Majah from the hadith of Wakee’, both from Yunus bin Abi Ishaq with it. Then al-Tirmidhi said: It is strange from this aspect, and I do not know of Abu al-Safar hearing it from Abu al-Darda’. Ibn Mardawayh said: Dalaj bin Ahmad told us, Muhammad bin Ali bin Zaid told us, Saeed bin Mansour told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Imran bin Dhibyan, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, that a man’s mouth was infected during the time of Muawiyah, may God be pleased with him, and he was offered blood money, but he refused except to take retaliation. He was offered two blood moneys, but he refused, then he was offered three, but he refused. Then a man from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever gives in charity the blood of a person or less, it is an expiation for him from the day he was born until the day he dies. Imam Ahmad said: Shuraih bin An-Nu’man told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, that Ubadah bin As-Samit said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There is no man who is wounded in his body and gives in charity, except that God expiates for him the equivalent of what he gave in charity. An-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Ali bin Hajar, on the authority of Jarir bin Abdul Hamid, and Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Mahmoud bin Khidash, on the authority of Hisham, both of them on the authority of Al-Mughira with it. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Al-Muharrir bin Abi Hurairah, on the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever is afflicted with something in his body and abandons it for the sake of God, it will be an expiation for him. And his statement, And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers, has already been mentioned previously from Tawus and Ata’ that they said: Disbelief less than disbelief, oppression less than oppression, and immorality less than immorality.
5:46: God the Almighty says: And We sent meaning We followed in their footsteps, meaning the prophets of the Children of Israel with Jesus, son of Mary, confirming what was before him of the Torah meaning believing in it and ruling by what is in it, And We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light meaning guidance to the truth and light by which to be enlightened in removing doubts and solving problems, and confirming what was before him of the Torah meaning following it and not contradicting what is in it except in a little of what was explained to the Children of Israel about some of what they differed about, as God the Almighty said, informing us about the Messiah that he said to the Children of Israel And to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you and for this reason it is well-known from the scholars' saying that the Gospel abrogated some of the rulings of the Torah. God the Almighty says: And guidance and instruction for the righteous meaning And We made the Gospel a guidance to be followed, and an instruction, meaning a deterrent from committing forbidden acts and sins, for the righteous, meaning for those who fear God and fear His threat and punishment. And the Almighty’s saying: And let the People of the Gospel judge by what God has revealed therein is read and let the People of the Gospel judge by what God has revealed therein in the accusative case, on the basis that the lam is the lam of ki, meaning, We gave him the Gospel so that the people of his religion might judge by it in their time. And it is read and let him judge in the jussive case, on the basis that the lam is the lam of command, meaning that they should believe in all that is in it, and that they should establish what they were commanded to do therein, and among what is in it is the good report of the mission of Muhammad and the command to follow him and believe in him if he finds him, as God the Almighty said: Say, ‘O People of the Scripture, you are upon nothing until you establish the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord’ 10:13. And God the Almighty said: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah 10:13 until His saying the successful ones. That is why He said here: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wicked, meaning those who have disobeyed their Lord, who incline toward falsehood, and who abandon the truth. It was previously mentioned that this verse was revealed about the Christians, and this is apparent from the context.
5:47: God the Almighty says: And We sent meaning We followed in their footsteps, meaning the prophets of the Children of Israel with Jesus, son of Mary, confirming what was before him of the Torah meaning believing in it and ruling by what is in it, And We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light meaning guidance to the truth and light by which to be enlightened in removing doubts and solving problems, and confirming what was before him of the Torah meaning following it and not contradicting what is in it except in a little of what was explained to the Children of Israel about some of what they differed about, as God the Almighty said, informing us about the Messiah that he said to the Children of Israel And to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you and for this reason it is well-known from the scholars' saying that the Gospel abrogated some of the rulings of the Torah. 5:48: When God Almighty mentioned the Torah that He sent down to His interlocutor Moses, and praised it and commended it and commanded its followers to follow it where it was permissible to follow, and mentioned the Gospel and praised it and commanded its people to establish it and follow what is in it, as was explained above, He began to mention the great Qur’an that He sent down to His servant and noble Messenger, so God Almighty said: And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, meaning with the truth in which there is no doubt that it is from God, confirming what was before it of the Scripture, meaning of the previous books that included mentioning and praising it, and that it would be sent down from God to His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So its sending down was as I informed, which increased its truthfulness for its bearers from those with insight who submitted to God’s command, followed God’s laws, and believed in God’s Messengers, as God Almighty said: “Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall upon their faces in prostration * And say, ‘Glory be to our Lord. Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled.’” That is, if what God promised us through the tongues of His previous messengers regarding the coming of Muhammad, peace be upon him, is to be done, that is, it will inevitably and necessarily happen. God the Almighty said: And a guardian over it. Sufyan al-Thawri and others said, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning a trustee over it. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The guardian is the trustworthy. He said: The Qur’an is a trustee over every book before it. And it was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Atiyyah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ata’ al-Khurasani, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd, something similar to that. Ibn Jarir said: The Qur’an is a trustee over the books that came before it, so whatever is in agreement with it is true, and whatever is contrary to it is false. And on the authority of al-Walibi on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And a guardian means a witness, and this is what Mujahid, Qatadah, and al-Suddi said. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And a guardian over it, meaning a ruler over the books that came before it. All of these statements are close in meaning, for the name the guardian over it includes all of this. He is trustworthy, a witness, and a ruler over every book that came before it. God made this great book that He revealed as the last and final of the books the most comprehensive, greatest, and most perfect of them, as He gathered in it the merits of what came before it, and added to it perfections that are not in any other. For this reason, He made it a witness, a guardian, and a ruler over all of them, and He undertook to preserve it with His noble Self, as He, the Most High, said: Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur’an and indeed, We will be its guardian. As for what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ata’ al-Khurasani, and Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid, that they said regarding His statement, And a guardian over it, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is trustworthy over the Qur’an, then it is correct in meaning, but there is a problem with interpreting this in this way, and there is also a problem with its revelation to him in terms of Arabic. In short, the first is correct. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said after narrating it from Mujahid: This interpretation is far from what is understood in the speech of the Arabs, rather it is a mistake, because al-Muhaymin is in apposition to al-Musaddiq, so it can only be an attribute of what al-Musaddiq is an attribute of. He said: If the matter were as Mujahid said, he would have said: And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what came before it of the Scripture, as a guardian over it, meaning without apposition. And the Almighty’s saying: Then judge between them by what God has revealed means, O Muhammad, judge between the people, Arabs and non-Arabs, illiterate and People of the Book, by what God has revealed to you in this great book, and by what He has decreed for you as the ruling of the prophets who came before you and did not abrogate it in your law. This is how Ibn Jarir interpreted it in its meaning. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ammar told us, Saeed ibn Sulayman told us, Ibad ibn al-Awwam told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Husayn, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had the choice of whether he wanted to judge between them or whether he wanted to turn away from them, and he returned them to their rulings. Then the verse was revealed: And judge between them by what God has revealed and do not follow their inclinations. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to judge between them by what is in our book. And His statement, And do not follow their inclinations, meaning their opinions that they agreed upon, and because of them they abandoned what God revealed to His Messengers. For this reason, God the Almighty said, And do not follow their inclinations away from the truth that has come to you, meaning do not turn away from the truth that God has commanded you to the inclinations of these ignorant, wretched people. So they went to him and said: O Muhammad, you know that we are the rabbis of the Jews, their nobles, and their leaders, and if we follow you, we will follow the Jews and they will not oppose us.
