Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said after narrating it from Mujahid: This interpretation is far from what is understood in the speech of the Arabs, rather it is a mistake, because al-Muhaymin is in apposition to al-Musaddiq, so it can only be an attribute of what al-Musaddiq is an attribute of. He said: If the matter were as Mujahid said, he would have said: And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what came before it of the Scripture, as a guardian over it, meaning without apposition. And the Almighty’s saying: Then judge between them by what God has revealed means, O Muhammad, judge between the people, Arabs and non-Arabs, illiterate and People of the Book, by what God has revealed to you in this great book, and by what He has decreed for you as the ruling of the prophets who came before you and did not abrogate it in your law. This is how Ibn Jarir interpreted it in its meaning. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ammar told us, Saeed ibn Sulayman told us, Ibad ibn al-Awwam told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Husayn, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had the choice of whether he wanted to judge between them or whether he wanted to turn away from them, and he returned them to their rulings. Then the verse was revealed: And judge between them by what God has revealed and do not follow their inclinations. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to judge between them by what is in our book. And His statement, And do not follow their inclinations, meaning their opinions that they agreed upon, and because of them they abandoned what God revealed to His Messengers. For this reason, God the Almighty said, And do not follow their inclinations away from the truth that has come to you, meaning do not turn away from the truth that God has commanded you to the inclinations of these ignorant, wretched people. And His statement, the Almighty, For each among you We prescribed a law and a method, Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Yusuf bin Abi Ishaq, on the authority of Abi Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, For each among you We prescribed a law, he said: a way. Abu Saeed told us, Waki` told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, A way he said: and a Sunnah, thus Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, A law and a way means a path and a Sunnah, and thus it was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Qatadah, Al-Dahhak, As-Suddi, and Abu Ishaq Al-Sabi`i, that they said regarding his statement, A law and a way meaning a path and a Sunnah, and on the authority of Ibn Abbas also, and Mujahid, that is, Ata Al-Khurasani, the opposite of it, A law and a way meaning a Sunnah and a path, and the first is more appropriate, because the law, which is also the Shari`ah, is that which one begins with towards something, and from it it is said: he began with such-and-such, meaning he began with it, thus the Shari`ah is that which one begins with towards water. As for the way, it is the clear and easy path, and the Sunnahs are the methods. The interpretation of his statement: A law and a way as a path and a Sunnah is more apparent in the appropriateness than the opposite, and God knows best. Then this is a report about nations of different religions, considering what God sent His noble messengers with of different laws in the rulings that agree on monotheism, as it was proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We, the prophets, are brothers in religion, our religion is one, meaning by that the monotheism with which God sent every messenger He sent and included in every book He revealed, as God the Almighty said: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him, ‘There is no god except Me, so worship Me,’ and God the Almighty said: And We have certainly sent to every nation a messenger, [saying], ‘Worship God and avoid false deities,’ and the verse. As for the laws, they differ in their commands and prohibitions. Something may be forbidden in one law, then permitted in another law, and vice versa, and something light may be increased in severity in one without the other, and that is because of the perfect wisdom and conclusive proof that God the Almighty has in that. Saeed bin Abi Aruba said on the authority of Qatada: His statement, For each of you We have prescribed a law and a method, means: a path and a sunnah. And the sunnahs are different. In the Torah there is a law, in the Gospel there is a law, and in the Criterion there is a law. In them God makes lawful what He wills and forbids what He wills, to know who obeys Him from who disobeys Him. And the religion that God does not accept other than it is monotheism and sincerity to God that all the messengers, peace and blessings be upon them, came with. And it was said: The one addressed in this verse is this nation, and its meaning is that for each of you, O nation, We have prescribed the Qur’an as a law and a method, meaning it is for all of you to follow. And the accusative pronoun was omitted in His statement, For each of you, We have prescribed, meaning We have prescribed it, meaning the Qur’an, as a law and a method, meaning a path to the correct objectives, and a sunnah means a clear and evident path and course. This is the meaning of what Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Mujahid, may God have mercy on him. And the correct statement is the first, and this is indicated by His statement after it, And if God had willed, He would have made you one nation. So if This was addressed to this nation, because it is correct to say, And if God had willed, He would have made you one nation, and they are one nation, but this is addressed to all nations and informing of His great power, which if He had willed, He would have gathered all people on one religion and one law, none of which would be abrogated, but He, the Most High, prescribed a law for each messenger separately, then abrogated it or some of it with the message of the next one after him, until He abrogated all of it with what He sent His servant and messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, whom He sent to all the people of the earth, and made him the seal of all the prophets, and for this reason the Most High said, And if God had willed, He would have made you one nation, but to test you in what He has given you, meaning that the Most High prescribed different laws to test His servants in what He has prescribed for them and to reward or punish them for their obedience and disobedience to Him by what they did or resolved to do from all of that. Abdullah bin Kathir said, in what He has given you means from the Book. Then, the Almighty urged them to hasten to do good deeds and take the initiative in them, saying: So race to do good deeds, which is obeying God and following His law, which He made abrogate what came before it, and believing in His Book, the Qur’an, which is the last book He revealed. Then the Almighty said: To God is your return, meaning your return, O people, and your final destination to Him on the Day of Resurrection. Then He will inform you about that over which you used to differ, meaning He will inform you about the truth over which you differed. He will reward the truthful for their truthfulness, and punish the disbelievers who deny the truth and turn away from it to something else without evidence or proof. Rather, they are stubborn against the conclusive proofs, the comprehensive arguments, and the overwhelming evidence. Ad-Dahhak said: So race to do good deeds, meaning the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the first is more apparent. And His statement, And judge between them by what God has revealed and do not follow their inclinations, is an emphasis on what preceded from the command to do so and the prohibition against going against it. Then He said, And beware of them, lest they tempt you away from some of what God has revealed to you, meaning, beware of your Jewish enemies, lest they deceive you about the truth in what they convey to you of matters, so do not be deceived by them, for they are liars, infidels, and traitors. But if they turn away, meaning, from what you judge between them of the truth and go against the law of God, then know that God only intends to afflict them for some of their sins, meaning, know that this is due to God’s decree and wisdom in them, to divert them from guidance because of their previous sins that necessitated their misguidance and punishment. And indeed, many of the people are wicked, meaning, most of the people are disobedient to their Lord, disobeying the truth and deviating from it, as God the Almighty said, And most of the people are not believers, even if you strive to do so. And God the Almighty said, And if you obey most of those on the earth, they will mislead you from the way of God, the verse. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client of Zayd ibn Thabit, told me: Saeed ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Ka`b ibn Asad, Ibn Saluba, Abdullah ibn Suriya, and Shas ibn Qays said to each other: Let us go to Muhammad, so that we may tempt him away from his religion. So they went to him and said: O Muhammad, you know that we are the rabbis of the Jews, their nobles, and their leaders, and if we follow you, we will follow the Jews and they will not oppose us. There is a dispute between us and our people, so we will bring them to you for judgment, so you can judge for them, and we will believe you and confirm you. But the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, refused that, so God, the Almighty, revealed about them: And judge between them by what God has revealed and do not follow their inclinations and beware of them, lest they tempt you away from some of what God has revealed to you until His saying: for a people who are certain. Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. And the Almighty’s saying: Do they then seek the judgment of [the time of] ignorance? And who is better than God in judgment for a people who are certain? The Almighty denounces those who depart from the decisive judgment of God, which includes all good, forbids all evil and justice, to other opinions, whims, and conventions that men have established without any basis in the law of God, just as the people of ignorance used to rule by it from the misguidance and ignorance that they established by their opinions and whims, and just as the Tatars used to rule by the royal policies taken from their king Genghis Khan, who established for them Al-Yasaq, which is a book compiled from rulings that he had taken from various laws: from Judaism, Christianity, the Islamic religion, and others, and in it are many rulings that he took from his own opinion and whims, so it became a law that his people followed and preferred over ruling by the Book of God and the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So whoever among them does that is a disbeliever who must be fought until he returns to the judgment of God and His Messenger, so he does not rule other than it in little or much. The Almighty said: Do they then seek the judgment of [the time of] ignorance? That is, they seek. They want, and they deviate from the judgment of God, And who is better than God in judgment for a people who are certain? That is, who is more just than God in His judgment for those who understand God’s law, believe in it, are certain, and know that God is the most just of judges, and more merciful to His creation than a mother to her child, for He, the Most High, is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful, the Just in all things. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hilal bin Fayyad told us, Abu Ubaidah Al-Naji told us: I heard Al-Hasan say: Whoever rules other than by the rule of God, he rules according to the pre-Islamic era. Yunus bin Abdul A’la told us, reciting, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, who said: When a man asked Tawus: Should I give preference to my sons in beekeeping? He would recite: Do they then seek the rule of the time of ignorance? Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad bin Abdul Wahhab bin Najdah Al-Hawti told us, Abu Al-Yaman Al-Hakam bin Nafi’ told us, Shu’aib bin Abi Hamza told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Abi Hussain, on the authority of Nafi’ bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The most hated of people to God, the Almighty, is he who seeks the ways of the pre-Islamic era in Islam, and demands the blood of a person unjustly in order to shed his blood. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Yaman with a similar chain of transmission, with an addition.
5:51: The Blessed and Exalted forbids His believing servants from befriending the Jews and Christians, who are the enemies of Islam and its people - may God kill them - then He informed that some of them are allies of others, then He threatened and warned whoever does that, saying, And whoever among you befriends them - then indeed, he is one of them the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Kathir bin Shihab told us, Muhammad - meaning Ibn Saeed bin Sabeq - told us, Amr bin Abi Qais told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Iyadh that Omar ordered Abu Musa al-Ash'ari to present to him what he had taken and given in one leather, and he had a Christian scribe, so he presented that to him, and Omar was amazed and said: This is a memorizer, will you read us a letter in the mosque that came from Syria? He said: He cannot, so Omar said: Is he ritually impure? He said: No, he is a Christian. He said: He rebuked me and struck my thigh, then said: Get him out, then he recited: O you who believe! Take not the Jews and the Christians as allies 1:130, then he said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabah told us, Uthman ibn Umar told us, Ibn Awn told us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: Abdullah ibn Utbah said: Let one of you beware of being a Jew or a Christian without realizing it. He said: We thought he meant this verse: O you who believe! Take not the Jews and the Christians as allies 1:130, and Abu Saeed al-Ashj told us, Ibn Fadil told us on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he was asked about the sacrifices of the Arab Christians, so he said: Eat, for God the Most High said: And whoever among you takes them as allies - then indeed, he is one of them 1:130, and something similar was narrated on the authority of Abu al-Zinad. God the Almighty says: Then you will see those in whose hearts is disease meaning doubt, suspicion, and hypocrisy, hastening to befriend and love them inwardly and outwardly, saying, ‘We fear that a misfortune may befall us’ meaning they interpret their friendship and support as meaning that they fear that something will happen such as the disbelievers gaining control over the Muslims, and that they will have power over the Jews and Christians, which will benefit them. At that point God the Almighty says: Perhaps God will bring about victory Al-Suddi said: meaning the conquest of Mecca. Another said: meaning judgment and decision, or a command from Him. Al-Suddi said: It means imposing the jizya on the Jews and Christians, and they will become meaning those hypocrites who sided with the Jews and Christians regretful of what they concealed within themselves of allegiance, regretful meaning for what they did, for which He did not find anything against them, nor did He protect them from any harm, but rather it was the very essence of corruption, for they were disgraced and God revealed their affair in this world to His believing servants after they had been hidden, and it was not known what their condition was. So when the reasons for disgracing them were established, their affair became clear to God’s believing servants, and they were amazed at them, how they had appeared to be believers, and swore to that and interpreted, but their lies and fabrications became clear. For this reason, God Almighty said: And those who believed will say, ‘Are these the ones who swore by God with their most solemn oaths that they were with you?’ Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers. The reciters differed on this letter, as the majority read it with the addition of the waw in His statement and he says, then some of them raised and said: as a beginning, and some of them lowered it in apposition to His statement perhaps God will bring about the conquest or a decision from Him, so its meaning is that he will come and that he says. The people of Medina read those who believe say without the waw, and this is how it is in their copies of the Qur’an according to what Ibn Jarir mentioned. Ibn Jarir said on the authority of Mujahid, perhaps God will bring about the conquest or a decision from Him, its meaning then is those who believe say, ‘Are these the ones who swore by God with their most solemn oaths that they were with you?’ Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers. The commentators differed on the reason for the revelation of these noble verses. Al-Suddi mentioned that they were revealed about two men, one of whom said to his companion after the Battle of UHud 11:As for me, I am going to that Jew and seek refuge with him and become a Jew with him, perhaps he will benefit me if something happens or an incident occurs. The other said: As for me, I am going to so-and-so the Christian in Ash-Sham, so I will seek refuge with him and become a Christian with him. So God revealed: O you who believe! Take not the Jews and the Christians as allies (al-Baqarah 2:170). Ikrimah said: It was revealed about Abu Lubabah ibn Abd al-Mundhir when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to Banu Qurayzah. They asked him: What are you going to do with us? He pointed with his hand to his throat, meaning that it was slaughter. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. It was said: It was revealed about Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, as Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ibn Idris told us: I heard my father on the authority of Atiyah bin Saad, who said: Ubadah bin al-Samit from Banu al-Harith bin al-Khazraj came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I have many Jewish clients, and I declare before God and His Messenger that I am innocent of the guardianship of the Jews, and I am loyal to God and His Messenger. Abdullah bin Ubayy said: I am a man who fears calamities, but I do not declare myself innocent of the guardianship of my clients. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abdullah bin Ubayy: O Abu al-Habbab, whatever you withheld from Ubadah bin al-Samit of the guardianship of the Jews, it is yours and not his. He said: I have accepted. Then God Almighty revealed: O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. Then Ibn Jarir said: Hannad told us, Yunus bin Bakir told us, Uthman bin Abdul Rahman told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri: He said: When the people of Badr were defeated, the Muslims said to their Jewish allies: Convert to Islam before God afflicts you with a day like the day of Badr. Malik bin Al-Saif said: You have been deceived by the fact that you have struck a group of Quraysh who have no knowledge of fighting. If we were to command the resolve to unite against you, you would not have the power to fight us. Ubadah bin Al-Samit said: O Messenger of God, my Jewish allies were very strong in spirit, their weapons were many, and their strength was strong. I declare before God and His Messenger that I am innocent of the guardianship of the Jews, and I have no guardian except God and His Messenger. Abdullah bin Ubayy said: But I do not declare myself innocent of the guardianship of the Jews. I am a man who cannot do without them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Al-Habbab, what do you think of the guardianship of the Jews over Ubadah bin Al-Samit? It is yours and not his. He said: Then accept. He said: Then God revealed: O you who believe! Do not take the Jews as your friends. The Christians are allies of one another. And whoever among you takes them as allies - then indeed, he is one of them. Indeed, God guides not the wrongdoing people. Then you see those in whose hearts is disease hastening into them, saying, We fear that a misfortune may strike us. But perhaps God will bring about victory or a decision from Him, and they will become, over what they concealed within themselves, regretful. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The first tribe of Jews to break their covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was Banu Qaynuqa. Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada told me: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, besieged them until they submitted to his judgment. Then Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul stood up to him when God gave him power over them and said: O Muhammad, be good to my clients. They were allies of the Khazraj. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was slow to approach him, and he said: O Muhammad, be good to my clients. He said: So he turned away from him. He said: So he put his hand in the pocket of the armour of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Leave me, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry until they saw a shadow on his face, then he said: Woe to you, send me. He said: No, by God, I will not send you until you treat my clients well, four hundred bareheaded and three hundred wearing armour. They have protected me from the red and black. You will reap me in one morning, for I am a man who fears calamities. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are yours. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Abu Ishaq ibn Yasar told me on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Walid ibn Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: When the Banu Qaynuqa’ fought the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abdullah ibn Ubayy held fast to their affair and stood up for them. Ubadah ibn al-Samit walked to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was one of the Banu Awf ibn al-Khazraj, and he had the same alliance with them as Abdullah ibn Ubayy, so he made them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he disavowed their alliance to God and His Messenger, and he said: O Messenger of God, I disavow to God and His Messenger from their alliance, and he said: O Messenger of God, I disavow to God and His Messenger from Their oath, and I take God and His Messenger and the believers as allies, and I disavow the oath of the infidels, and their allegiance, for it was about him and Abdullah bin Ubay that the verses were revealed in al-Ma’idah 5:“O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever takes them as allies among you - then indeed, he is one of them. Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people. * Then you will see those in whose hearts is disease hastening into them, saying, “We fear that a misfortune may strike us.” But perhaps God will bring victory or a decision from Him, and they will become, over what they concealed within themselves, regretful. * And those who believed will say, Are these the ones who swore by God with their most solemn oaths that they were with you? Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers. * O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert from his religion - God will bring forth [in place of them] a people He will love and who will love Him [who are] humble toward the believers, powerful against the disbelievers; they strive in the cause of God and do not fear the blame of a critic. That is the bounty of God which He bestows upon whom He wills, and God is all-Encompassing and Knowing. * Your ally is only God and His Messenger and those who believe - those who establish prayer and give zakah, while they bow [in prayer]. * And whoever disbelieves, God will bring forth [in place of them] a people who will love Him [who are] humble toward the believers, powerful against the disbelievers; they strive in the cause of God and do not fear the blame of a critic. That is the bounty of God, which He bestows upon whom He wills, and God is All-Encompassing and Knowing. * Your ally is only God and His Messenger and those who believe - those who establish prayer and give zakah, while they bow [in prayer]. * And whoever disbelieves, God will bring forth [in place of them] a God, His Messenger, and those who believe are allies of God. Indeed, the party of God will be the victorious.” Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Yahya bin Zakariya bin Abi Ziyadah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid, who said: I entered with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, upon Abdullah bin Abi Na’ud, to visit him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: I used to forbid you from loving the Jews. Abdullah said: As’ad bin Zuraat hated them and died. Abu Dawud narrated it in this way from the hadith of Muhammad bin Ishaq.

Abdullah bin Ubayy said: I am a man who fears calamities, but I do not declare myself innocent of the guardianship of my clients. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abdullah bin Ubayy: O Abu al-Habbab, whatever you withheld from Ubadah bin al-Samit of the guardianship of the Jews, it is yours and not his. He said: I have accepted. Then God Almighty revealed: O you who believe, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. Then Ibn Jarir said: Hannad told us, Yunus bin Bakir told us, Uthman bin Abdul Rahman told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri: He said: When the people of Badr were defeated, the Muslims said to their Jewish allies: Convert to Islam before God afflicts you with a day like the day of Badr. Malik bin Al-Saif said: You have been deceived by the fact that you have struck a group of Quraysh who have no knowledge of fighting. If we were to command the resolve to unite against you, you would not have the power to fight us. Ubadah bin Al-Samit said: O Messenger of God, my Jewish allies were very strong in spirit, their weapons were many, and their strength was strong. I declare before God and His Messenger that I am innocent of the guardianship of the Jews, and I have no guardian except God and His Messenger. Abdullah bin Ubayy said: But I do not declare myself innocent of the guardianship of the Jews. I am a man who cannot do without them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Al-Habbab, what do you think of the guardianship of the Jews over Ubadah bin Al-Samit? It is yours and not his. He said: Then accept. He said: Then God revealed: O you who believe! Do not take the Jews as your friends. The Christians are allies of one another. And whoever among you takes them as allies - then indeed, he is one of them. Indeed, God guides not the wrongdoing people. Then you see those in whose hearts is disease hastening into them, saying, We fear that a misfortune may strike us. But perhaps God will bring about victory or a decision from Him, and they will become, over what they concealed within themselves, regretful. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The first tribe of Jews to break their covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was Banu Qaynuqa. Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada told me: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, besieged them until they submitted to his judgment. Then Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul stood up to him when God gave him power over them and said: O Muhammad, be good to my clients. They were allies of the Khazraj. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was slow to approach him, and he said: O Muhammad, be good to my clients. He said: So he turned away from him. He said: So he put his hand in the pocket of the armour of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Leave me, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry until they saw a shadow on his face, then he said: Woe to you, send me. He said: No, by God, I will not send you until you treat my clients well, four hundred bareheaded and three hundred wearing armour. They have protected me from the red and black. You will reap me in one morning, for I am a man who fears calamities. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are yours. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Abu Ishaq ibn Yasar told me on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Walid ibn Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: When the Banu Qaynuqa’ fought the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abdullah ibn Ubayy held fast to their affair and stood up for them. Ubadah ibn al-Samit walked to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was one of the Banu Awf ibn al-Khazraj, and he had the same alliance with them as Abdullah ibn Ubayy, so he made them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he disavowed their alliance to God and His Messenger, and he said: O Messenger of God, I disavow to God and His Messenger from their alliance, and he said: O Messenger of God, I disavow to God and His Messenger from Their oath, and I take God and His Messenger and the believers as allies, and I disavow the oath of the infidels, and their allegiance, for it was about him and Abdullah bin Ubay that the verses were revealed in al-Ma’idah 5:“O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever takes them as allies among you - then indeed, he is one of them. Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people. * Then you will see those in whose hearts is disease hastening into them, saying, “We fear that a misfortune may strike us.” But perhaps God will bring victory or a decision from Him, and they will become, over what they concealed within themselves, regretful. * And those who believed will say, Are these the ones who swore by God with their most solemn oaths that they were with you? Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers. * O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert from his religion - God will bring forth [in place of them] a people He will love and who will love Him [who are] humble toward the believers, powerful against the disbelievers; they strive in the cause of God and do not fear the blame of a critic. That is the bounty of God which He bestows upon whom He wills, and God is all-Encompassing and Knowing. * Your ally is only God and His Messenger and those who believe - those who establish prayer and give zakah, while they bow [in prayer]. * And whoever disbelieves, God will bring forth [in place of them] a people who will love Him [who are] humble toward the believers, powerful against the disbelievers; they strive in the cause of God and do not fear the blame of a critic. That is the bounty of God, which He bestows upon whom He wills, and God is All-Encompassing and Knowing. * Your ally is only God and His Messenger and those who believe - those who establish prayer and give zakah, while they bow [in prayer]. * And whoever disbelieves, God will bring forth [in place of them] a God, His Messenger, and those who believe are allies of God. Indeed, the party of God will be the victorious.” Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, Yahya bin Zakariya bin Abi Ziyadah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid, who said: I entered with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, upon Abdullah bin Abi Na’ud, to visit him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: I used to forbid you from loving the Jews. Abdullah said: As’ad bin Zuraat hated them and died. Abu Dawud narrated it in this way from the hadith of Muhammad bin Ishaq.
5:53: The Blessed and Exalted forbids His believing servants from befriending the Jews and Christians, who are the enemies of Islam and its people - may God kill them - then He informed that some of them are allies of others, then He threatened and warned whoever does that, saying, And whoever among you befriends them - then indeed, he is one of them the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Kathir bin Shihab told us, Muhammad - meaning Ibn Saeed bin Sabeq - told us, Amr bin Abi Qais told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Iyadh that Omar ordered Abu Musa al-Ash'ari to present to him what he had taken and given in one leather, and he had a Christian scribe, so he presented that to him, and Omar was amazed and said: This is a memorizer, will you read us a letter in the mosque that came from Syria? He said: He cannot, so Omar said: Is he ritually impure? He said: No, he is a Christian. He said: He rebuked me and struck my thigh, then said: Get him out, then he recited: O you who believe! Take not the Jews and the Christians as allies 1:130, then he said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabah told us, Uthman ibn Umar told us, Ibn Awn told us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: Abdullah ibn Utbah said: Let one of you beware of being a Jew or a Christian without realizing it. He said: We thought he meant this verse: O you who believe! Take not the Jews and the Christians as allies 1:130, and Abu Saeed al-Ashj told us, Ibn Fadil told us on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he was asked about the sacrifices of the Arab Christians, so he said: Eat, for God the Most High said: And whoever among you takes them as allies - then indeed, he is one of them 1:130, and something similar was narrated on the authority of Abu al-Zinad. God the Almighty says: Then you will see those in whose hearts is disease meaning doubt, suspicion, and hypocrisy, hastening to befriend and love them inwardly and outwardly, saying, ‘We fear that a misfortune may befall us’ meaning they interpret their friendship and support as meaning that they fear that something will happen such as the disbelievers gaining control over the Muslims, and that they will have power over the Jews and Christians, which will benefit them. At that point God the Almighty says: Perhaps God will bring about victory Al-Suddi said: meaning the conquest of Mecca. Another said: meaning judgment and decision, or a command from Him. Al-Suddi said: It means imposing the jizya on the Jews and Christians, and they will become meaning those hypocrites who sided with the Jews and Christians regretful of what they concealed within themselves of allegiance, regretful meaning for what they did, for which He did not find anything against them, nor did He protect them from any harm, but rather it was the very essence of corruption, for they were disgraced and God revealed their affair in this world to His believing servants after they had been hidden, and it was not known what their condition was. So when the reasons for disgracing them were established, their affair became clear to God’s believing servants, and they were amazed at them, how they had appeared to be believers, and swore to that and interpreted, but their lies and fabrications became clear. For this reason, God Almighty said: And those who believed will say, ‘Are these the ones who swore by God with their most solemn oaths that they were with you?’ Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers. The reciters differed on this letter, as the majority read it with the addition of the waw in His statement and he says, then some of them raised and said: as a beginning, and some of them lowered it in apposition to His statement perhaps God will bring about the conquest or a decision from Him, so its meaning is that he will come and that he says. The people of Medina read those who believe say without the waw, and this is how it is in their copies of the Qur’an according to what Ibn Jarir mentioned. Ibn Jarir said on the authority of Mujahid, perhaps God will bring about the conquest or a decision from Him, its meaning then is those who believe say, ‘Are these the ones who swore by God with their most solemn oaths that they were with you?’ Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers. The commentators differed on the reason for the revelation of these noble verses. Al-Suddi mentioned that they were revealed about two men, one of whom said to his companion after the Battle of UHud 11:As for me, I am going to that Jew and seek refuge with him and become a Jew with him, perhaps he will benefit me if something happens or an incident occurs. The other said: As for me, I am going to so-and-so the Christian in Ash-Sham, so I will seek refuge with him and become a Christian with him. So God revealed: O you who believe! Take not the Jews and the Christians as allies (al-Baqarah 2:170). 5:54: God the Almighty says, informing about His great power, that whoever turns away from supporting His religion and establishing His law, God will replace him with someone who is better for it than him, stronger in strength, and on a more upright path, as God the Almighty said: And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be the likes of you. And God the Almighty said: "If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation. And that is not difficult for God." That is, impossible or difficult. And God the Almighty said here: O you who have believed, whoever among you should revert from his religion that is, turn away from the truth to falsehood. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: It was revealed about the governors of Quraysh. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: It was revealed about the apostates during the time of Abu Bakr: Then God will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him. Al-Hasan said: By God, it is Abu Bakr and his companions. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: I heard Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash say: In His statement: Then God will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him, they are the people of al-Qadisiyyah. Laith bin Abi Salim said, on the authority of Mujahid: They are a people from Saba. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashja told us, Abdullah bin Al-Ajlah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Then God will bring forth a people whom He will love and who will love Him, he said: People from the people of Yemen, then from Kinda, from Sakun. My father told us, Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa told us, Muawiyah told us, meaning ibn Hafs, on the authority of Abu Ziyad al-Halfani, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about his statement, God will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him. He said, These are people from Yemen, then from Kinda, then from Sukun, then from Tajib. This is a very strange hadith. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Omar bin Shabah told us, Abdul Samad told us, meaning Ibn Abdul Warith, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Samak, I heard Ayyad narrating on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, he said: When the verse, God will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, They are this people. Ibn Jarir narrated it in a similar manner from the hadith of Shu’bah. And the Almighty’s statement, Humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers, these are the attributes of the perfect believers, that one of them should be humble toward his brother and friend, and mighty toward his opponent and enemy, as God the Almighty said, Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. And in the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he is the one who laughs and fights, so he laughs toward his friends and fights his enemies. And the Almighty’s saying, They strive in the cause of God and do not fear the blame of a critic, meaning that they are not deterred from what they are doing of obeying God, establishing the limits, fighting His enemies, enjoining what is right, and forbidding what is wrong. No one deters them from that, no one turns them away from it, no one blames them, and no one reproaches them. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Salam Abu al-Mundhir told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Was’, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Samit, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: My friend, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, commanded me with seven things: He commanded me to love the poor and to be close to them, and he commanded me to look at those who are below me and not to look at those who are above me, and he commanded me to maintain family ties even if they turn away, and he commanded me not to ask anyone for anything, and he commanded me to speak the truth even if it is bitter, and he commanded me not to fear the blame of a critic in God’s cause, and he commanded me to say often, There is no power and no strength except with God, for they are from the treasure beneath the Throne. Al-Bukhari said: Ibn al-Mubarak is the only one to narrate this hadith. Many of the scholars of the principles of jurisprudence and jurists who have gone to the view that the law of those before us is our law if it is narrated as established and not abrogated have used as evidence, as is well-known from the majority, and as Sheikh Abu Ishaq al-Isfarayini narrated from the text of al-Shafi’i and most of the companions with this verse, since the ruling according to us was in accordance with it in crimes according to all the imams. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: It applies to them and to all people in general. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Sheikh Abu Zakariya al-Nawawi narrated three aspects regarding this issue, the third of which is that the law of Ibrahim is a proof and not others. He confirmed that it is not a proof, and Sheikh Abu Ishaq al-Isfarayini transmitted statements from al-Shafi’i and most of the companions, and he preferred that it is a proof according to the majority of our companions, and God knows best. Imam Abu Nasr bin Al-Sabbagh, may God have mercy on him, narrated in his book Al-Shamel the consensus of scholars on using this verse as evidence for what it indicates. All the imams have used this verse as evidence that a man is killed for a woman based on the generality of this noble verse. Likewise, it was mentioned in the hadith narrated by Al-Nasa’i and others that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote in the book of Amr bin Hazm that a man is killed for a woman, and in another hadith the blood of Muslims is equal, and this is the opinion of the majority of scholars. And from the Commander of the Faithful, Ali bin Abi Talib, that if a man kills a woman, he is not to be killed for her unless her guardian pays half of the blood money to his guardians, because her blood money is half of the blood money of a man. Ahmad went with this in a narration, and it was narrated from Al-Hasan, Ata’, and Uthman Al-Basti, And God is Vast and Knowing, meaning He is Vast in His bounty, and He knows who deserves it from whom He deprives him of it. God the Almighty says: Your guardian is only God, His Messenger, and those who believe. That is, the Jews are not your guardians, rather your guardianship is with God, His Messenger, and the believers. And His statement: Those who establish prayer and give zakat means the believers who are characterized by these qualities of establishing prayer, which is the greatest pillar of Islam, which is the worship of God alone with no partner, and giving zakat, which is the right of creation and helping the needy and poor. As for His statement: and they are bowing, some people have imagined that this sentence is in the place of the state of His statement: and they give zakat, that is, while they are bowing. If this were the case, then paying zakat while bowing would be better than otherwise, because it is praiseworthy. This is not the case according to any of the scholars that we know of among the imams of fatwas. Some of them even mentioned a trace on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib that this verse was revealed about him, and that was because a beggar passed by him while he was bowing, so he gave him his ring. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman Al-Muradi told us, Ayoub bin Suwaid told us on the authority of Utbah bin Abi Hakim regarding his statement, Your ally is only God and His Messenger and those who believe, he said: They are the believers and Ali bin Abi Talib. Abu Saeed Al-Ashja told us, Al-Fadl bin Dukayn Abu Na’im Al-Ahwal told us, Musa bin Qais Al-Hadrami told us on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, he said: He gave me his ring as charity while he was bowing, so the verse was revealed, Your ally is only God and His Messenger and those who believe, who establish prayer and give zakat, while they bow down. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Harith told me, Abdul Aziz told us, Ghalib bin Ubaidullah told us, I heard Mujahid say regarding his statement, Your ally is only God and His Messenger, the verse. It was revealed about Ali bin Abi Talib, he gave charity while he was bowing, and Abdul Razzaq said: Abdul Wahhab bin Mujahid told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Your guardian is only God and His Messenger, the verse, it was revealed about Ali bin Abi Talib, Abdul Wahhab bin Mujahid is not to be relied upon. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Ali ibn Abi Talib was standing and praying, and a beggar passed by while he was bowing, so he gave him his ring, and then the verse, Your guardian is only God and His Messenger was revealed. Ad-Dahhak did not meet Ibn Abbas. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Sa’ib al-Kalbi, who is rejected, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to the mosque and the people were praying, some bowing, some prostrating, some standing, and some sitting, and there was a poor man begging, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered and said: Did someone give you something? He said: Yes. He said: Who? He said: That standing man. He said: In what condition did he give it to you? He said: While he was bowing. He said: And that was Ali ibn Abi Talib. He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, And whoever takes God and His Messenger and those who believe as allies - then indeed, the party of God - it is they who will be victorious. This is an isnad that is not to be rejoiced at. Then Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him, Ammar ibn Yasir and Abu Rafi`, and none of it is authentic at all due to the weakness of its chains of transmission and the ignorance of its men. Then he narrated with his chain of transmission from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Your ally is only God and His Messenger, it was revealed about the believers and Ali ibn Abi Talib was the first of them. Ibn Jarir said: Hannad told us, Abdah told us, from Abdul Malik, from Abu Ja`far, who said: I asked him about this verse, Your ally is only God and His Messenger and those who believe, who establish prayer and give zakat, while they bow in prayer. We said: Who are those who believe? He said: Those who believe. We said: We were informed that it was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib. He said: Ali is one of those who believe. Laith bin Abi Salim said, on the authority of Mujahid: They are a people from Saba. My father told us, Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa told us, Muawiyah told us, meaning ibn Hafs, on the authority of Abu Ziyad al-Halfani, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about his statement, God will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him. He confirmed that it is not a proof, and Sheikh Abu Ishaq al-Isfarayini transmitted statements from al-Shafi’i and most of the companions, and he preferred that it is a proof according to the majority of our companions, and God knows best. All the imams have used this verse as evidence that a man is killed for a woman based on the generality of this noble verse. 5:57: This is a warning against befriending the enemies of Islam and its people from the People of the Book and the polytheists, who take the best of what the workers do: which are the pure and perfect laws of Islam, which include every worldly and otherworldly good, and take them as a mockery that they ridicule, and a game that they believe is a kind of game in their corrupt view and cold thinking, as the poet said: How many people criticize a correct statement when their fault is a faulty understanding? And the Almighty’s saying: “Of those who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers” from here is to clarify the type like His saying: So avoid the uncleanness of idols. Some of them read: and the disbelievers in the accusative case as an appositive, and others read it in the accusative case as an object, Do not take those who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement from among those who were given the Scripture before you its meaning is nor the disbelievers meaning do not take these or those as allies, and what is meant by the disbelievers here are the polytheists, and this is also what occurred in the reading of Ibn Mas’ud in what Ibn Jarir narrated: Do not take those who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement from among those who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers. And His saying, And fear God, if you are believers, meaning, fear God lest you take these enemies of yourselves and your religion as allies if you are believers in God’s law, which these people have taken as a joke and a game, as God Almighty said: “Let not believers take disbelievers as allies rather than believers. And whoever does that has nothing to do with God, unless you fear them out of fear. And God warns you of Himself, and to God is the final destination.” And His saying: And when you call to prayer, they take it in ridicule and play. That is, likewise when you call to prayer, which is the best of deeds for those who are rational and know among the wise, they take it also “in ridicule and play. That is because they are a people who do not reason.” The meanings of worshipping God and His laws, and these are the characteristics of the followers of Satan who “when he hears the call to prayer, he turns away farting, so that he does not hear the call to prayer. Then when the call to prayer is finished, he comes back. Then when the call to prayer is finished, he turns away. Then when the call to prayer is finished, he comes back until he comes between a person and his heart, and says: Remember such and such, remember such and such, because he did not remember until a man does not know how much he prayed. So if one of you finds that, then let him prostrate twice before the salutation.” Agreed upon. Al-Zuhri said: God mentioned the call to prayer in His Book, saying: “And when you call to prayer, they take it in ridicule and play. That is because they are a people who do not reason.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Asbat said on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement, And when you call to prayer, they take it in ridicule and amusement, he said: There was a Christian man in Medina who, when he heard the caller calling, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, said, Burn the liar. One night, a servant girl entered with a fire while he was asleep and his family was asleep, and a spark fell and burned the house, so he and his family were burned. Narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar mentioned in the biography that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered the Kaaba in the year of the conquest with Bilal, so he ordered him to call to prayer, and Abu Sufyan bin Harb, Atab bin Asid, and Al-Harith bin Hisham were sitting in the courtyard of the Kaaba. Atab bin Asid said, God has honored Asid so that he would not have heard this and heard from him what would anger him. Al-Harith bin Hisham said, By God, if I knew that he was right, I would have followed him. Abu Sufyan said, “I will not say anything. If I spoke, these pebbles would have spoken about me.” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to them and said, I know what you are saying. You said, “Then he mentioned that to them, and Al-Harith and Atab said: We bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. No one who was with us knew about this, so we would say: He told you.” Imam Ahmad said: Ruh bin Ubadah told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, Abdul Aziz bin Abdul Malik bin Abi Mahdhurah told us that Abdullah bin Muhairiz told him, and he was an orphan in the care of Abi Mahdhurah. He said: I said to Abi Mahdhurah: O uncle, I am going to Ash-Sham, and I fear that I will be asked about your call to prayer. So he told me that Abi Mahdhurah said to him: Yes, I went out with a group of people and we were on some of the road to Hunayn, where the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was returning from Hunayn. So we met the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on some of the road, and the muezzin of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for prayer in the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So we heard the muezzin’s voice while we were standing on our sides, so we shouted, telling him stories and mocking him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard him, so he sent for us until we stood in front of him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Which of you heard his voice raised? Then all the people pointed to me and believed me, so he sent them all and detained me, and said, Get up and call to prayer. So I got up and there was nothing more hateful to me than the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor what he ordered me to do. So I stood in front of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave me the call to prayer himself. He said, “Say, ‘God is Great, God is Great. I bear witness that there is no god but God. I bear witness that there is no god but God. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Come to prayer, come to prayer. Come to success, come to success. God is Great, God is Great. There is no god but God.’” Then he called me when I had finished the call to prayer and gave me a purse containing some silver. Then he placed his hand on the forehead of Abu Mahdhurah, then passed it over his face, then between his breasts, then over his liver, until the hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reached the navel of Abu Mahdhurah. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “May God bless you and grant you peace.” So I said, O Messenger of God, command me to call to prayer in Mecca. He said, I have commanded you to do so. And everyone left. Something that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, hated, and all of that turned into love for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so I went to Atab bin Asid, the agent of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I called the prayer with him on the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I was informed of that by someone from my family who had known Abu Mahdhurah, in the same way that Abdullah bin Muhairiz informed me on the authority of Abu Mahdhurah, whose name was Samurah bin Mu’ayr bin Lawdhan, one of the four muezzins of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was the muezzin of the people of Mecca, and his days were long, may God be pleased with him and satisfy him.
5:58: This is a warning against befriending the enemies of Islam and its people from the People of the Book and the polytheists, who take the best of what the workers do: which are the pure and perfect laws of Islam, which include every worldly and otherworldly good, and take them as a mockery that they ridicule, and a game that they believe is a kind of game in their corrupt view and cold thinking, as the poet said: How many people criticize a correct statement when their fault is a faulty understanding? And the Almighty’s saying: Of those who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers from here is to clarify the type like His saying: So avoid the uncleanness of idols. Some of them read: and the disbelievers in the accusative case as an appositive, and others read it in the accusative case as an object, Do not take those who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement from among those who were given the Scripture before you its meaning is nor the disbelievers meaning do not take these or those as allies, and what is meant by the disbelievers here are the polytheists, and this is also what occurred in the reading of Ibn Mas’ud in what Ibn Jarir narrated: Do not take those who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement from among those who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers. And His saying, And fear God, if you are believers, meaning, fear God lest you take these enemies of yourselves and your religion as allies if you are believers in God’s law, which these people have taken as a joke and a game, as God Almighty said: “Let not believers take disbelievers as allies rather than believers. And whoever does that has nothing to do with God, unless you fear them out of fear. And God warns you of Himself, and to God is the final destination.” And His saying: And when you call to prayer, they take it in ridicule and play. That is, likewise when you call to prayer, which is the best of deeds for those who are rational and know among the wise, they take it also “in ridicule and play. That is because they are a people who do not reason.” The meanings of worshipping God and His laws, and these are the characteristics of the followers of Satan who “when he hears the call to prayer, he turns away farting, so that he does not hear the call to prayer. Then when the call to prayer is finished, he comes back. Then when the call to prayer is finished, he turns away. Then when the call to prayer is finished, he comes back until he comes between a person and his heart, and says: Remember such and such, remember such and such, because he did not remember until a man does not know how much he prayed. So if one of you finds that, then let him prostrate twice before the salutation.” Agreed upon. That is because they are a people who do not reason.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. 5:59: God the Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to those among the People of the Book who have taken your religion as a mockery and a game: Do you blame us for anything except that we believe in God and in what was revealed to us and what was revealed before? That is, do you have any criticism or fault with us other than this? This is not a fault or a reproach, so the exception is discontinuous, as in the Almighty’s saying: And they blamed them for nothing except that they believed in God, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy, and as He says: And they blamed them for nothing except that God and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty. And in the agreed upon hadith: Ibn Jameel blamed him for nothing except that he was poor and God enriched him, and His saying and that most of you are wicked is conjoined with that we believe in God and in what was revealed to us and what was revealed before, that is, and we believe that most of you are wicked, that is, deviating from the straight path. Then he said, Say, ‘Shall I inform you of something worse than that as a reward from God?’ That is, shall I inform you of something worse than that as a reward from God on the Day of Resurrection than what you think of us? And it is you who are described by these characteristics explained by His statement, He whom God has cursed, that is, removed from His mercy, and with whom He has become angry, that is, an anger with which He will never be pleased, and made of them apes and pigs, as was explained previously in Surat Al-Baqarah, and as will be explained in Surat Al-A’raf. Sufyan Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Alqamah bin Marthad, on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Abdullah, on the authority of Al-Ma’rur bin Suwayd, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about apes and pigs: Are they among those that God has transformed? He said, “God did not destroy a people, or transform a people, and give them offspring or descendants. Rather, there were monkeys and pigs before that.” Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri and Misa’ar, both of them on the authority of Mughirah ibn Abdullah al-Yashkari, and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Dawud ibn Abi al-Furat told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Zayd, on the authority of Abu al-A’in al-Abdi, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: We asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about monkeys and pigs: Are they from the offspring of the Jews? He said, “No, God never cursed a people and transformed them, so that they had offspring. Rather, this was a creation that existed. When God became angry with the Jews and transformed them, He made them like them.” Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of Dawud ibn Abi al-Furat, and Ibn Mardawayh said: Abd al-Baqi told us, Ahmad ibn Salih told us, al-Hasan ibn Mahbub told us, Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Snakes are the transformation of the jinn, just as monkeys and pigs were transformed. This is a very strange hadith. And the Almighty’s saying: And the worshipper of Taghut was read: And the worshipper of Taghut as a past tense verb, and Taghut is accusative with it, meaning and He made from them those who worshipped Taghut. It was read: And the worshipper of Taghut with addition that the meaning is and He made from them the servants of Taghut, meaning his servants and slaves. It was read: And the worshipper of Taghut as a plural of the plural slave and slaves, and slave is like fruits and fruits, Ibn Jarir narrated it from Al-A’mash, and he narrated from Buraidah Al-Aslami that he used to read it and the worshipper of Taghut, and from Abi and Ibn Mas’ud: and they worshipped, and Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu Ja’far Al-Qari’ that he used to read it: And the worshipper of Taghut as an object of what its agent was not named, then he excluded its meaning, and it appears that there is nothing wrong with that, because this is from the category of allusion to them, meaning and Taghut was worshipped among you and you are the ones who did it, and the meaning of all these readings goes back to you, O People of the Book, who attack our religion, which is the oneness of God and His singling out. With acts of worship and nothing else, how can this come from you, while everything mentioned has been found in you? That is why He said, Those are worse in position, meaning than what you think of us, and more astray from the right path. This is from the category of using the comparative in what the other side does not share, like the Almighty’s saying, The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be better in settlement and better in resting place. And the Almighty said: And when they come to you, they say, ‘We believe,’ but they entered with disbelief, and they have already left with it. This is the description of the hypocrites among them, that they pretend to be believers outwardly, but their hearts are filled with disbelief. For this reason, He said, and they have entered, meaning with you, O Muhammad, with disbelief, meaning they have continued to carry disbelief in their hearts, then they left while it was hidden in them. They did not benefit from what they heard from you of knowledge, and the sermons and deterrents did not work on them. For this reason, He said, and they have already left with it, so He singled them out from others. And the Almighty said: And God knows best what they were concealing, meaning God knows their secrets and what their consciences conceal, even if they show His creation otherwise, and adorn themselves with what is not in them, for God, the Knower of the unseen and the seen, knows them better than they do, and He will reward them for that with the most complete reward. And His statement, And you will see many of them hastening into sin and aggression and consuming what is unlawful, meaning they hasten to do that by engaging in sins and forbidden things, transgressing against people, and consuming their money. In vain, How evil is what they were doing, meaning how evil was their work, and how evil was their aggression. And the Almighty’s saying: Why do not the rabbis and the scholars forbid them from their sinful speech and from their consumption of what is unlawful? Evil is that which they do. That is, why do not the rabbis and the scholars forbid them from doing that? The rabbis are the working scholars who are the rulers over them, and the scholars are only the scholars. Evil is that which they do. That is, from their leaving that. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said it on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said it to these when they did not forbid it and to those when they knew. He said: And that was the matter. He said: And they work and make one thing. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ibn Atiyyah told us, Qais told us on the authority of al-Ala’ ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Khalid ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There is no verse in the Qur’an that is more severe in rebuke than this verse: Why do not the rabbis and the scholars forbid them from their sinful speech and from their consumption of what is unlawful? Evil is that which they do. He said: This is how he read it, and this is what al-Dahhak said: What is in the Qur’an A verse that I fear more than it is: We do not forbid. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Ibn Abi Hatim said, Yunus bin Habib mentioned it, Abu Dawud told us, Muhammad bin Muslim bin Abi Al-Waddah told us, Thabit Abu Saeed Al-Hamdani told us, he said: I met him in Rayy and he narrated from Yahya bin Ya`mar, he said: Ali bin Abi Talib gave a sermon, praised God and thanked Him, then he said: O people, those who came before you were destroyed because they committed sins and the rabbis and scholars did not forbid them. When they persisted in sins, punishments seized them, so enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong before what befell them befalls you, and know that enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong does not cut off provision or bring about a shortening of life. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Sharik told us from Abu Ishaq from Al-Mundhir bin Jarir, from his father, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no people among whom there are those who commit sins who are more honorable and more secure than them, and they do not change except that God will afflict them with a punishment from them. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this source, and Abu Dawud narrated it from Musaddad. On the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Mundhir bin Jarir, on the authority of Jarir, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There is no man who is among a people who commit sins and they are able to change him, but they do not change him, except that God will afflict them with a punishment before they die. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Ali bin Muhammad, on the authority of Wakee’, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Ubayd God bin Jarir, on the authority of his father, on his authority. Al-Hafiz Al-Mizzi said: And this is how Shu’bah narrated it on the authority of Abu Ishaq on his authority.

5:64: God Almighty tells us about the Jews - upon them be the continuous curses of God until the Day of Resurrection - that they described God Almighty, the Most High, far above what they say, as being stingy, just as they described Him as being poor, even though they were rich, and they expressed stinginess by saying, The hand of God is chained. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abdullah al-Tahrani told us, Hafs bin Omar al-Adani told us, al-Hakam bin Abaan told us on the authority of Ikrimah who said: Ibn Abbas said: Mughlulah means stingy. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And the Jews say, ‘The hand of God is chained,’ he said: They do not mean by that that the hand of God is tied, but they say: stingy, meaning he withheld what he has. God is exalted far above what they say. This is how it was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and al-Dahhak. He recited, And do not make your hand chained to your neck nor stretch it forth to its utmost extension, lest you sit down blamed and regretful, meaning that he forbade miserliness and extravagance, which is spending more than it should be. He expressed miserliness by saying, And do not make your hand chained to your neck, and this is what these Jews intended upon them, may God’s curses be upon them. Ikrimah said: It was revealed about Phinehas the Jew, may God’s curse be upon him, and it was mentioned earlier that he was the one who said, Indeed, God is poor, and we are rich, so Abu Bakr struck him. Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, and Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad told us on the authority of Saeed or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A Jewish man called Shas bin Qais said: Your Lord is stingy and does not spend. So God revealed: “And the Jews say: The hand of God is chained. Chained are their hands, and cursed are they for what they said.
