We said: O Messenger of God, how can knowledge be lost when we recite the Qur’an, and teach it to our children, and our children teach it to their children until the Day of Resurrection? He said: “May your mother be bereaved of you, O son of Umm Labid, I used to see you as one of the most knowledgeable men in Madinah. Do not these Jews and Christians recite the Torah and the Gospel and benefit from what is in them at all?” This is how Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Waki` with a similar chain of transmission. This is a sound chain of transmission. And the Almighty’s saying: Among them is a moderate nation, but many of them are evil in what they do is like His saying: And among the people of Moses is a nation guiding with the truth and doing justice thereby and like His saying about the followers of Jesus: So We gave those among them who believed their reward verse. So He made the highest of their stations moderation, which is the middle station of this nation, and above that is the rank of the foremost, as in His Almighty’s saying: “Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants. And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by permission of God. That is the great bounty. * Gardens of Eden, which they will enter” verse. And the correct view is that all three groups of this nation will enter Paradise. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Abdullah ibn Ja’far told us, Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Dhabi told us, Asim ibn ‘Adi told us, Abu Ma’shar told us, on the authority of Ya’qub ibn Yazid ibn Talhah, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “The nation of Moses was divided into seventy-one sects: Seventy of them will be in Hell, and one will be in Paradise. The nation of Jesus will be divided into seventy-two sects: one will be in Paradise, and seventy-one of them will be in Hell. My nation will be superior to both sects: one will be in Paradise, and seventy-two will be in Hell.” They said: Who are they, O Messenger of God? He said: The groups, the groups. Yaqub ibn Zayd said: When Ali ibn Abi Talib narrated this hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would recite the Qur’an in which he said: And if the People of the Scripture had believed and feared God, We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to Gardens of Pleasure. to the words of God the Almighty: Among them is a moderate nation, but many of them - evil is what they do. He also recited the words of God the Almighty: And among those We created is a nation who guide with the truth and do justice thereby. He meant the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This hadith is very strange from this aspect and in this context. The hadith of the nations being divided into seventy-something is narrated through many chains of narration, and we have mentioned it in another place, and praise and thanks be to God.
5:67: God Almighty says, addressing His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, by the name of the message, and commanding him to convey all that God sent him with, and he complied with the best of prayers and peace, and carried it out perfectly. Al-Bukhari said when interpreting this verse: Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: Whoever tells you that Muhammad concealed something of what God revealed to him has lied. God says, O Messenger, announce what has been revealed to you from your Lord the verse, thus he narrated it here in abbreviated form, and he included it in several places in his Sahih in full, and Muslim narrated it in the Books of Faith, and Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i in the Book of Interpretation from their Sunan through chains of transmission on the authority of Amer Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq bin Al-Ajda’, on her authority, may God be pleased with her, and in the two Sahihs also on her authority that she said: If Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, had concealed anything of the Qur’an, he would have concealed this verse, And you conceal within yourself what God has revealed to you You show it and fear people, but God is more deserving of being feared. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Ramadi told us: Saeed bin Sulaiman told us: Ibad told us on the authority of Harun bin Antara, on the authority of his father, who said: We were with Ibn Abbas when a man came and said to him: Some people come to us and tell us that you have something that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not reveal to the people. Ibn Abbas said: Did you not know that God, the Most High, said: O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord? By God, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not inherit from us blackness in whiteness. This is a good chain of transmission, and it is also in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Abu Juhayfah Wahb bin Abdullah Al-Suwai’i, who said: I said to Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him: Do you have anything from the revelation that is not in the Qur’an? He said: No, by Him who split the seed and created the soul, except an understanding that God gives a man in the Qur’an and what is in this document. I said: What is in this document? He said: Reason, the release of prisoners, and that a Muslim should not be killed for an unbeliever. Al-Bukhari said: Al-Zuhri said: The message is from God, and the Messenger is responsible for conveying it, and we must submit. His nation testified to his conveying the message and fulfilling the trust, and he asked them to speak about that in the greatest gatherings in his sermon on the day of the Farewell Pilgrimage, and there were about forty thousand of his companions there, as was proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his sermon on that day: O people, you will be asked about me, so what will you say? They said: We testify that you have conveyed, fulfilled your duty, and given sincere advice. So he raised his finger to the sky and lowered it to them, saying: O God, have I conveyed the message? Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr told us, Fadil, meaning Ibn Ghazwan, told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in the Farewell Pilgrimage: O people, what day is this? They said: A sacred day. He said: What city is this? They said: A sacred city. He said: What month is this? They said: A sacred month. He said: Your wealth, your blood, and your honor are sacred to you, as sacred as this day of yours, in this city of yours, in this month of yours. Then he repeated it several times. Then he raised his finger to the sky and said: O God, have I conveyed the message? several times. Ibn Abbas said: By God, it is a testament to his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. Then he said: “Let the witness convey to the absent one: Do not return after me as disbelievers, striking the necks of one another.” Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ali ibn al-Madini, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa`id, on the authority of Fadil ibn Ghazwan, something similar. And the Almighty’s saying: And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message, meaning if you do not convey to the people what He sent you with, then you have not conveyed His message, that is, He knows what would result from that if it happened. And Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message, meaning if you concealed a verse of what was revealed to you from your Lord, then you have not conveyed His message. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Qubaysah bin Uqbah told us, Sufyan told us on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: When the verse O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord, was revealed, he said: O Lord, what can I do when I am alone and they will gather against me? So the verse And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message was revealed. And Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Sufyan, and he is al-Thawri on his authority. And the Almighty’s saying: And God will protect you from the people means, convey My message and I will protect you, support you, and help you against your enemies and make you victorious over them, so do not fear or grieve, for none of them will come to you with harm that will hurt you. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was guarded before this verse was revealed, as Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Yahya told us: I heard Abdullah bin Amir bin Rabi’ah narrating that Aisha, may God be pleased with her, was narrating that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stayed up one night and she was beside him. She said: I said, What is the matter with you, O Messenger of God? He said, If only a righteous man from among my companions would guard me tonight. She said: While I was like that, I heard the sound of weapons, so he said, Who is this? He said, I am Sa’d bin Malik. He said, What brought you? He said, I came to guard you, O Messenger of God. She said: I heard the snoring of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his sleep. They included it in the two Sahihs on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed Al-Ansari, and in another version: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stayed up one night upon his arrival in Medina, meaning after his migration after entering upon Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and that was in the second year of it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ibrahim bin Marzouq Al-Basri, a resident of Egypt, told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Al-Harith bin Ubaid, meaning Abu Qudamah, told us, on the authority of Al-Jariri, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was guarded until this verse was revealed: And God will protect you from the people. She said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stuck his head out of the dome and said: O people, go back, for God Almighty has protected me. And this is how Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abd bin Hamid, and on the authority of Nasr bin Ali Al-Jahdhami, both of them on the authority of Muslim bin Ibrahim, on his authority. Then he said: This is a strange hadith, and this is how Ibn Jarir and Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Muslim bin Ibrahim, on his authority. Al-Hakim said: Its chain of transmission is sound, and they did not include it. And this is how Saeed bin Mansour narrated it on the authority of Al-Harith bin Ubaid Abu Qudamah on the authority of Al-Jariri, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, on the authority of Aisha, on his authority. Then Al-Tirmidhi said: Some of them narrated this on the authority of Al-Jariri on the authority of Ibn Shaqiq, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was guarded until this verse was revealed. The verse, and he did not mention Aisha. I said: This is how Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ismail bin Aliyah, and Ibn Mardawayh on the authority of Wahib, both of them on the authority of Al-Jariry on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, without a chain of transmission. This was narrated without a chain of transmission on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair and Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi, narrated by Ibn Jarir and Al-Rabi bin Anas, narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, then he said: Sulayman bin Ahmad told us, Ahmad bin Rushdin Al-Masri told us, Khalid bin Abdul Salam Al-Sadfi told us, Al-Fadl bin Al-Mukhtar told us on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhab, on the authority of Asmah bin Malik Al-Khazmi, who said: We used to guard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at night. Until the verse, And God will protect you from the people, was revealed, so he left the guards. Sulayman ibn Ahmad told us, Hamad ibn Muhammad ibn Hamad Abu Nasr al-Katib al-Baghdadi told us, Kurdus ibn Muhammad al-Wasiti told us, Ya’la ibn Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Fadil ibn Marzuq, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said: Al-Abbas, the uncle of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was among those who guarded him. When this verse, And God will protect you from the people, was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left the guards. Ali bin Abi Hamid Al-Madani narrated to us, Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Saeed narrated to us, Muhammad bin Mufaddal bin Ibrahim Al-Ash’ari narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Muhammad bin Mu’awiyah bin Ammar narrated to us, my father said: I heard Abu Al-Zubayr Al-Makki narrating on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: Whenever the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out, Abu Talib would send someone with him to protect him until the verse, And God will protect you from the people, was revealed. So he went to send someone with him, but he said, O uncle, God has protected me, I have no need of anyone you send. This is a strange hadith and it is objectionable, for this verse is Medinan, and this hadith indicates that it is Meccan. Then he said: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Ibrahim narrated to us, Muhammad bin Yahya narrated to us, Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abdul Hamid Al-Hammani narrated to us on the authority of Al-Nadr, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was guarded, so Abu Talib would send men from Banu Hashim to guard him every day until this verse was revealed to him, O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed. His message: And God will protect you from the people. He said: So his uncle wanted to send someone with him to guard him, so he said: God has protected me from the jinn and mankind. Al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Ya’qub bin Ghailan Al-Omani, on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on his authority. This is also a strange hadith, and the correct view is that this verse was revealed in Medina, and it is one of the last verses to be revealed, and God knows best. And from God’s protection of His Messenger, He protected him from the people of Mecca, their leaders, their envious people, their opponents, and their wealthy people, despite the intensity of the enmity and hatred, and the great causes that God creates for him by His great power and wisdom. So He protected him at the beginning of the message through his uncle Abu Talib, as he was a great and obeyed leader in Quraysh, and God created in his heart a natural love for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, not a legitimate one. If he had converted to Islam, their infidels and leaders would have dared to attack him, but because there was a common level of disbelief between him and them, they feared and respected him. So when his uncle Abu Talib died, the polytheists caused him a little harm, then God provided him with the Ansar, so they pledged allegiance to him on Islam and that he would move to their home, which is Medina. So when he reached it, they protected him from the red and the black, and whenever one of the polytheists and the People of the Book intended to harm him, God plotted against him and repelled his plot. Upon him, just as the Jews plotted against him with magic, but God protected him from them, and revealed to him the two Mu’awwidhatayn Surahs as a cure for that disease. And when the Jews poisoned him in the arm of that sheep in Khaybar, God informed him of it and protected him from it. And there are many similarities to this, too many to mention. Among them is what the commentators mentioned regarding this noble verse: Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Al-Harith told us, `Abd al-`Aziz told us, Abu Ma`shar told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi and others, they said: Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped at a place, his companions would choose a shady tree for him to take a nap under. Then a Bedouin came to him and drew his sword, then said: Who will protect you from me? He said: God Almighty. The Bedouin’s hand trembled and the sword fell from his hand, and he struck the tree with his head until his brain was scattered, so God Almighty revealed: And God will protect you from the people. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan told us, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, Musa bin Ubaidah told us, Zaid bin Aslam told me on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah Al-Ansari, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raided Banu Anmar, he camped at Dhat Al-Riqa’ at the top of a palm grove. While he was sitting at the top of a well with his feet dangling, Ghawrath bin Al-Harith of Banu Al-Najjar said: I will kill Muhammad. His companions said to him: How will you kill him? He said: I will say to him: Give me your sword. When he gives it to me, I will kill him with it. He said: So he came to him and said: O Muhammad, give me your sword, I will kill him. So he gave it to him, and his hand trembled until the sword fell from his hand. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has come between you and what you want. So God Almighty revealed: “O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And God will protect you from the people.” This is a strange hadith from this source, and the story of Ghawrath bin Al-Harith is well-known in Sahih. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Abu Amr bin Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim told us, Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab told us, Adam told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: When we accompanied the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a journey, we would leave for him the largest and most shady tree, and he would camp under it. One day he camped under a tree and hung his sword in it, and a man came and took it and said: O Muhammad, who will protect you from me? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God will protect me from you. Put down the sword.” So he put it down, and God, the Almighty, revealed: And God will protect you from the people. Abu Hatim bin Hibban narrated it in his Sahih on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad, on the authority of Ishaq bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Mu’ammil bin Ismail, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah on his authority. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, I heard Abu Isra`il, meaning Al-Jashmi, I heard Ja`dah, he is the son of Khalid ibn Al-Samma Al-Jashmi, may God be pleased with him, say: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he saw a fat man, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to point to his stomach with his hand and say: If this were not for this, it would have been better for you. He said: A man was brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was said: This man wanted to kill you, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: You did not take heed, and if you had wanted that, God would not have given you power over me. His statement, Indeed, God does not guide the disbelieving people, means you convey the message, and God is the One who guides whom He wills and misguides whom He wills, as God, the Most High, said: It is not upon you to guide them, but God guides whom He wills and He said: Upon you is only the conveyance, and upon Us is the reckoning.
5:68: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, O People of the Scripture, you are upon nothing meaning of religion until you establish the Torah and the Gospel, meaning until you believe in all that is in your hands of the books revealed by God to the prophets, and act according to what is in them, and what is in them is the command to follow Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to believe in his mission, and to follow his law, and for this reason Laith bin Abi Salim said on the authority of Mujahid: In His statement and what has been revealed to you from your Lord: meaning the Great Qur’an, and His statement and what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief its interpretation was presented, so do not grieve over the disbelieving people meaning do not grieve over them, and do not be led astray by them, then He said Indeed, those who believed and they are the Muslims, and those who were Jews and they are the bearers of the Torah, and the Sabians since the separation was long, it was good to connect with the nominative, and the Sabians are a group of Christians and Magians who have no religion, Mujahid said, and on his authority: from the Jews and Magians, and Saeed bin Jubayr: From the Jews and Christians, and on the authority of Al-Hasan and Al-Hakam: They are like the Magians, and Qatada said: They are a people who worship angels, pray in a direction other than the Qiblah, and recite the Psalms. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: They are a people who know God alone, and they do not have a law that they act upon, and they have not committed blasphemy. Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Abi al-Zinad told me on the authority of his father, who said: The Sabians are a people near Iraq, and they are in Kutha, and they believe in all the prophets, and they fast thirty days every year, and they pray five prayers every day in Yemen, and other things have been said. As for the Christians, they are well-known and they are the bearers of the Gospel, and the point is that every group believed in God and the Last Day, which is the appointed time and the reward on the Day of Judgment, and did righteous deeds, and that will not be so until it is in accordance with the Muhammadan law after the sending of its messenger to all of mankind. So whoever is characterized by that, then there is no fear for them in what they will face, nor for what they have left behind them, nor will they grieve. The discussion of its counterpart has already been presented in Surat al-Baqarah, so there is no need to repeat it here.

5:70: The Almighty mentions that He took covenants and agreements from the Children of Israel to hear and obey God and His Messenger, but they broke those covenants and agreements and followed their opinions and desires, and presented them over the laws, so they accepted whatever agreed with them and rejected whatever disagreed with them. That is why the Almighty said: “Whenever there came to them a messenger with what their souls did not desire, a party they denied and a party they killed. And they thought that there would be no trial.” That is, they thought that no evil would result from what they did, so it did, which is that they were blind to the truth and deaf, so they did not hear the truth nor were they guided to it. Then God repented of them, that is, from what they were in, then they became blind and deaf that is, after that, many of them, and God is Seeing of what they do. That is, He is aware of them and knows who among them deserves guidance and who among them deserves misguidance.
5:71: The Almighty mentions that He took covenants and agreements from the Children of Israel to hear and obey God and His Messenger, but they broke those covenants and agreements and followed their opinions and desires, and presented them over the laws, so they accepted whatever agreed with them and rejected whatever disagreed with them. That is why the Almighty said: “Whenever there came to them a messenger with what their souls did not desire, a party they denied and a party they killed. And they thought that there would be no trial.” That is, they thought that no evil would result from what they did, so it did, which is that they were blind to the truth and deaf, so they did not hear the truth nor were they guided to it. Then God repented of them, that is, from what they were in, then they became blind and deaf that is, after that, many of them, and God is Seeing of what they do. That is, He is aware of them and knows who among them deserves guidance and who among them deserves misguidance.
5:72: God Almighty says, ruling that the Christian sects of the Royalists, Jacobites, and Nestorians are infidels, among those who said: that Christ is God. God is exalted above what they say, and He is far above and sanctified. It has already been mentioned to them that Christ is the servant and messenger of God, and the first word he uttered while he was still in the cradle was: I am the servant of God. He did not say I am God or the son of God, but he said: "I am the servant of God. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet." until he said: "And God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path." And he also said to them in his adulthood and prophethood, commanding them to worship his Lord and their Lord, alone, with no partner for Him. For this reason God Almighty said: "And the Messiah said, O Children of Israel, worship God, my Lord and your Lord. Indeed, whoever associates others with God" meaning worships others with Him, God has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire meaning He has made the Fire obligatory for him and forbidden him Paradise, as God Almighty said: God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills. God the Almighty said: “And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise, ‘Pour upon us some water or whatever God has provided you.’ They will say, ‘Indeed, God has forbidden them both to the disbelievers.’” In Sahih, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a crier to call out to the al-Nas 114:No one will enter Paradise except a Muslim soul, and in another version: a believer. It was mentioned at the beginning of Surat An-Nisa’ when he said: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, in the hadith of Yazid bin Babnous on the authority of Aisha: The registers are three. He mentioned one of them that God does not forgive, which is association with God. God the Almighty said: Whoever associates others with God, God has forbidden Paradise to him, and the hadith is in Musnad Ahmad. For this reason, God the Almighty said, informing about the Messiah that he said to the Children of Israel: “Indeed, whoever associates others with God, God has forbidden Paradise to him, and his refuge is the Fire. And there are no helpers for the wrongdoers,” meaning that he has no supporter, helper, or savior from what he is in with God. And his saying, Indeed they have disbelieved who say, ‘God is the third of three,’ Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Hasanjani told us, Saeed ibn al-Hakam ibn Abi Maryam told us, al-Fadl told us, Abu Sakhr told me regarding the saying of God the Most High, Indeed they have disbelieved who say, ‘God is the third of three,’ he said: It is the saying of the Jews that Ezra is the son of God, and the saying of the Christians that the Messiah is the son of God, so they made God the third of three. 5:78: God Almighty tells us that He cursed the disbelievers among the Children of Israel a long time ago in what He revealed to His Prophet David, peace be upon him, and on the tongue of Jesus, son of Mary, because of their disobedience to God and their aggression against His creation. Al-Awfi said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They were cursed in the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the Criterion. Then He explained their condition in what they relied on in their time, and God Almighty said: “They did not forbid one another from the evil they did. Evil was that which they were doing.” That is, none of them would forbid anyone from committing sins and forbidden acts. Then He condemned them for that to warn against committing the same as they committed, and He said: Evil was that which they were doing. Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Yazid told us. Sharik ibn Abdullah narrated to us on the authority of Ali ibn Badhima, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the Children of Israel fell into sin, their scholars forbade them, but they did not desist. So they sat with them in their gatherings.” Yazid said: I think he said: “and their markets, and their eaters and drinkers. So God set the hearts of some of them against others, and cursed them on the tongues of David and Jesus, son of Mary. “That was because they disobeyed and were transgressors.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reclining, so he sat up and said: No, by the One in Whose hand is my soul, until you force them to adhere to the truth. Abu Dawud said: Abdullah bin Muhammad al-Nufaili told us, Yunus bin Rashid told us, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first thing that began to be deficient among the Children of Israel was that a man would meet another man and say: ‘O man, fear God and leave what you are doing, for it is not permissible for you. ’ Then he would meet him the next day and that would not prevent him from being his food, drink, and seat. When they did that, God struck the hearts of some of them with others. Then he said: ‘Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus, the son of Mary,’ until His saying: ‘disobedient. ’ Then he said: ‘No, by God, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and you must take the hand of the oppressor and force him to follow the truth completely, or force him to follow the truth completely. ’” And al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, and al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Gharib. Then he and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Ibn Mahdi, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, with no chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashja and Harun bin Ishaq Al-Hamadani told us: Abd Al-Rahman bin Muhammad Al-Maharibi told us on the authority of Al-Ala bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Ibn Abi Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If a man from the Children of Israel saw his brother committing a sin, he would forbid him from it as an excuse. But the next day, what he saw from him did not prevent him from being his eater, his companion, and his partner.” And in the hadith of Harun: and his drinker. Then they agreed in the text: “So when God saw that from them, He struck the hearts of some of them against others, and cursed them on the tongues of their prophets David and Jesus, son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressors.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and you must seize the hand of the wrongdoer and force him to do the truth, or God will strike the hearts of some of you against one another.” Some, or to curse you as he cursed them.” The context is from Abu Saeed, this is what he said in the narration of this hadith, and Abu Dawud also narrated it on the authority of Khalaf bin Hisham, on the authority of Abu Shihab Al-Khayyat, on the authority of Al-Ala bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Salim, who is Ibn Ajlan Al-Aftas, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah bin Abdullah bin Masoud, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. Then Abu Dawud said: This is how Khalid narrated it on the authority of Al-Ala, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, and Al-Maharibi narrated it on the authority of Al-Ala bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah. Our Sheikh, the hafiz Abu Al-Hajjaj Al-Mizzi said: Khalid bin Abdullah Al-Wasiti narrated it on the authority of Al-Ala bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Musa. There are many hadiths about enjoining good and forbidding evil, and we will mention what is appropriate for this situation. The hadith of Jabir has already been mentioned when he said, Why do the rabbis and scholars not forbid them? and it will come when he said, “O you who believe, upon you is yourselves. He who strays will not harm you if you are guided.” The hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Abu Tha’labah al-Khushani. Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman al-Hashimi told us, Ismail ibn Ja’far informed us, Amr ibn Abi Amr informed me on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ashhali, on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, By the One in Whose hand is my soul, you must enjoin good and forbid evil, or God will soon send upon you a punishment from Him, and then you will call upon Him and He will not respond to you. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Ali ibn Hajar on the authority of Ismail ibn Ja’far on his authority, and he said: This is a good hadith. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Yazid bin Majah said: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Muawiyah bin Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Saad, on the authority of Amr bin Othman, on the authority of Asim bin Omar bin Othman, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Command what is right and forbid what is wrong before you call upon God and your call is not answered. He is the only one who transmitted it, and this Asim is unknown. In Sahih, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ismail bin Raja’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Saeed, and on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand. If he is unable to do so, then with his tongue. If he is unable to do so, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith.” Narrated by Muslim. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr told us, Saif, he is Ibn Abi Sulayman, told us, I heard Adi bin Adi Al-Kindi narrating on the authority of Mujahid, he said: A freed slave of ours told me that he heard my grandfather, meaning Adi bin Umaira, may God be pleased with him, say: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “God does not punish the general public for the actions of the elite until they see evil among them and they are able to denounce it but they do not denounce it. If they do that, God will punish the elite and the general public.” Then Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Saif bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Isa bin Adi Al-Kindi, a freed slave of ours told me that he heard my grandfather say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, and he mentioned it. This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it from these two sources. Abu Dawud said: Abu Al-Ala’ told us, Abu Bakr told us, Al-Mughirah bin Ziyad Al-Mawsili told us, on the authority of Adi bin Adi, on the authority of Al-Aras, meaning Ibn Umairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When a sin is committed on earth, whoever witnesses it and dislikes it - and he said once, he disapproves of it - is like someone who was absent from it, and whoever is absent from it and approves of it is like someone who witnessed it.” Abu Dawud is the only one to narrate it, then he narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Mughirah bin Ziyad, on the authority of Adi bin Adi, as a mursal. Abu Dawud said: Sulayman bin Harb and Hafs bin Umar told us, they said: Shu’bah told us - and this is his wording - on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Al-Buhturi, who said: Someone who heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, told me, and Sulayman said: A man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, told me that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: People will not perish until they excuse themselves or excuse themselves. He said: Abu Saeed cried and said: By God, we have seen things that made us fear. In the hadith of Israel on the authority of Atiyah on the authority of Abu Saeed, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best jihad is a word of truth in the presence of an unjust ruler. It was narrated by Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan gharib from this source. Ibn Majah said: Rashid bin Saeed Al-Ramli told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us on the authority of Abu Ghalib, on the authority of Abu Umamah: He said: A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the first Jamarat and said: O Messenger of God, which jihad is best? He kept quiet about it. When he threw the second Jamarat and asked him, he kept quiet about it. When he threw the Jamarat Al-Aqaba and put his foot in the stirrup to mount, he said: Where is the questioner? He said: I will, O Messenger of God. He said: A word of truth said in the presence of an unjust ruler. It is narrated only by him. Ibn Majah said: Abu Kurayb told us, Abdullah bin Numayr and Abu Muawiyah told us on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Al-Buhturi, on the authority of Abu Saeed, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let none of you belittle himself. Imam Ahmad said: Amr ibn Asim narrated to us on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Jundub, on the authority of Hudhayfah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A Muslim should not humiliate himself. It was said: How does he humiliate himself? He said: He exposes himself to trials that he cannot bear. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah both narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bashar, on the authority of Amr ibn Asim, and Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good, authentic, rare hadith. He said: When what appeared among the nations before you appears among you. We said: O Messenger of God, and what appeared among the nations before us? He said, Kingship is among your young, immorality is among your old, and knowledge is among your wicked. Zayd said: The interpretation of the meaning of the Prophet’s statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, and knowledge is among your wicked, if knowledge is among the wicked, is unique to Ibn Majah, and it will come in the hadith of Abu Tha’labah when he said, He who goes astray will not harm you if you are guided, is evidence for this, God willing, and He is trustworthy. God the Almighty said: You will see many of them taking as allies those who disbelieve. Mujahid said: He means the hypocrites. And His statement: How evil is that which their souls have put forward for them means their friendship with the disbelievers and their abandonment of friendship with the believers, which resulted in hypocrisy in their hearts and incurred God’s wrath upon them with a wrath that will continue until the Day of Resurrection. For this reason He said: God’s wrath is upon them, and He explained with that what He condemned them with, then He informed about them that they will abide eternally in the punishment, meaning on the Day of Resurrection. As for the one in this world, it takes away beauty, causes poverty, and shortens life. As for the one in the Hereafter, it causes the wrath of the Lord, a bad reckoning, and eternity in the Fire.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “How evil is that which their souls have put forward for them: that God is angry with them, and in the punishment they will abide eternally.” This is how Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned it. He also cited it on the authority of Sa’id bin Ghafir, on the authority of Muslimah, on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Kufi, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Hudhayfah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar. This is a weak hadith in any case, and God knows best. God Almighty says: And if they had believed in God and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies. That is, if they had truly believed in God, the Messenger, and the Qur’an, they would not have committed what they committed of befriending the disbelievers in secret, and opposing the believers in God, the Prophet, and what was revealed to him. But many of them are wicked. That is, they are outside the obedience of God and His Messenger, disobeying the verses of His revelation and sending down.

For this reason He said: God’s wrath is upon them, and He explained with that what He condemned them with, then He informed about them that they will abide eternally in the punishment, meaning on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hisham bin Ammar told us, Muslim bin Ali told us on the authority of Al-A’mash with a chain of transmission that he mentioned, he said: “O group of Muslims, beware of adultery, for there are six consequences to it: three in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for the one in this world, it takes away beauty, causes poverty, and shortens life. As for the one in the Hereafter, it causes the wrath of the Lord, a bad reckoning, and eternity in the Fire.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “How evil is that which their souls have put forward for them: that God is angry with them, and in the punishment they will abide eternally.” This is how Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned it. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Hisham bin Ammar, on the authority of Muslimah, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Hudhayfah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned it. He also cited it on the authority of Sa’id bin Ghafir, on the authority of Muslimah, on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Kufi, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Hudhayfah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar. This is a weak hadith in any case, and God knows best. God Almighty says: And if they had believed in God and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies. That is, if they had truly believed in God, the Messenger, and the Qur’an, they would not have committed what they committed of befriending the disbelievers in secret, and opposing the believers in God, the Prophet, and what was revealed to him. But many of them are wicked. That is, they are outside the obedience of God and His Messenger, disobeying the verses of His revelation and sending down.
5:80: God Almighty tells us that He cursed the disbelievers among the Children of Israel a long time ago in what He revealed to His Prophet David, peace be upon him, and on the tongue of Jesus, son of Mary, because of their disobedience to God and their aggression against His creation. Al-Awfi said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They were cursed in the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the Criterion. Then He explained their condition in what they relied on in their time, and God Almighty said: “They did not forbid one another from the evil they did. Evil was that which they were doing.” That is, none of them would forbid anyone from committing sins and forbidden acts. Then He condemned them for that to warn against committing the same as they committed, and He said: Evil was that which they were doing. Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Yazid told us. Sharik ibn Abdullah narrated to us on the authority of Ali ibn Badhima, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the Children of Israel fell into sin, their scholars forbade them, but they did not desist. So they sat with them in their gatherings.” Yazid said: I think he said: “and their markets, and their eaters and drinkers. So God set the hearts of some of them against others, and cursed them on the tongues of David and Jesus, son of Mary. “That was because they disobeyed and were transgressors.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reclining, so he sat up and said: No, by the One in Whose hand is my soul, until you force them to adhere to the truth. Abu Dawud said: Abdullah bin Muhammad al-Nufaili told us, Yunus bin Rashid told us, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first thing that began to be deficient among the Children of Israel was that a man would meet another man and say: ‘O man, fear God and leave what you are doing, for it is not permissible for you. ’ Then he would meet him the next day and that would not prevent him from being his food, drink, and seat. When they did that, God struck the hearts of some of them with others. Then he said: ‘Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus, the son of Mary,’ until His saying: ‘disobedient. ’ Then he said: ‘No, by God, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and you must take the hand of the oppressor and force him to follow the truth completely, or force him to follow the truth completely. ’” And al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it in the same way, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, and al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Gharib. Then he and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Ibn Mahdi, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, with no chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashja and Harun bin Ishaq Al-Hamadani told us: Abd Al-Rahman bin Muhammad Al-Maharibi told us on the authority of Al-Ala bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Ibn Abi Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If a man from the Children of Israel saw his brother committing a sin, he would forbid him from it as an excuse. But the next day, what he saw from him did not prevent him from being his eater, his companion, and his partner.” And in the hadith of Harun: and his drinker. Then they agreed in the text: “So when God saw that from them, He struck the hearts of some of them against others, and cursed them on the tongues of their prophets David and Jesus, son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressors.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and you must seize the hand of the wrongdoer and force him to do the truth, or God will strike the hearts of some of you against one another.” Some, or to curse you as he cursed them.” The context is from Abu Saeed, this is what he said in the narration of this hadith, and Abu Dawud also narrated it on the authority of Khalaf bin Hisham, on the authority of Abu Shihab Al-Khayyat, on the authority of Al-Ala bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Salim, who is Ibn Ajlan Al-Aftas, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah bin Abdullah bin Masoud, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. Then Abu Dawud said: This is how Khalid narrated it on the authority of Al-Ala, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, and Al-Maharibi narrated it on the authority of Al-Ala bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah. Our Sheikh, the hafiz Abu Al-Hajjaj Al-Mizzi said: Khalid bin Abdullah Al-Wasiti narrated it on the authority of Al-Ala bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Musa. There are many hadiths about enjoining good and forbidding evil, and we will mention what is appropriate for this situation. The hadith of Jabir has already been mentioned when he said, Why do the rabbis and scholars not forbid them? and it will come when he said, “O you who believe, upon you is yourselves. He who strays will not harm you if you are guided.” The hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Abu Tha’labah al-Khushani. Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman al-Hashimi told us, Ismail ibn Ja’far informed us, Amr ibn Abi Amr informed me on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ashhali, on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, By the One in Whose hand is my soul, you must enjoin good and forbid evil, or God will soon send upon you a punishment from Him, and then you will call upon Him and He will not respond to you. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Ali ibn Hajar on the authority of Ismail ibn Ja’far on his authority, and he said: This is a good hadith. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Yazid bin Majah said: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Muawiyah bin Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Saad, on the authority of Amr bin Othman, on the authority of Asim bin Omar bin Othman, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Command what is right and forbid what is wrong before you call upon God and your call is not answered. He is the only one who transmitted it, and this Asim is unknown. In Sahih, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ismail bin Raja’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Saeed, and on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand. If he is unable to do so, then with his tongue. If he is unable to do so, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith.” Narrated by Muslim. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr told us, Saif, he is Ibn Abi Sulayman, told us, I heard Adi bin Adi Al-Kindi narrating on the authority of Mujahid, he said: A freed slave of ours told me that he heard my grandfather, meaning Adi bin Umaira, may God be pleased with him, say: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “God does not punish the general public for the actions of the elite until they see evil among them and they are able to denounce it but they do not denounce it. If they do that, God will punish the elite and the general public.” Then Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Saif bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Isa bin Adi Al-Kindi, a freed slave of ours told me that he heard my grandfather say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, and he mentioned it. This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it from these two sources. Abu Dawud said: Abu Al-Ala’ told us, Abu Bakr told us, Al-Mughirah bin Ziyad Al-Mawsili told us, on the authority of Adi bin Adi, on the authority of Al-Aras, meaning Ibn Umairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When a sin is committed on earth, whoever witnesses it and dislikes it - and he said once, he disapproves of it - is like someone who was absent from it, and whoever is absent from it and approves of it is like someone who witnessed it.” Abu Dawud is the only one to narrate it, then he narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Mughirah bin Ziyad, on the authority of Adi bin Adi, as a mursal. Abu Dawud said: Sulayman bin Harb and Hafs bin Umar told us, they said: Shu’bah told us - and this is his wording - on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Al-Buhturi, who said: Someone who heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, told me, and Sulayman said: A man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, told me that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: People will not perish until they excuse themselves or excuse themselves. Ibn Majah said: Imran bin Musa told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, Ali bin Zaid bin Jadaan told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to deliver a sermon, and among what he said was: Do not let fear of people prevent a man from speaking the truth if he knows it. He said: Abu Saeed cried and said: By God, we have seen things that made us fear. In the hadith of Israel on the authority of Atiyah on the authority of Abu Saeed, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best jihad is a word of truth in the presence of an unjust ruler. It was narrated by Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan gharib from this source. Ibn Majah said: Rashid bin Saeed Al-Ramli told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us on the authority of Abu Ghalib, on the authority of Abu Umamah: He said: A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the first Jamarat and said: O Messenger of God, which jihad is best? He kept quiet about it. When he threw the second Jamarat and asked him, he kept quiet about it. When he threw the Jamarat Al-Aqaba and put his foot in the stirrup to mount, he said: Where is the questioner? He said: I will, O Messenger of God. He said: A word of truth said in the presence of an unjust ruler. It is narrated only by him. Ibn Majah said: Abu Kurayb told us, Abdullah bin Numayr and Abu Muawiyah told us on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Al-Buhturi, on the authority of Abu Saeed, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let none of you belittle himself. They said: O Messenger of God, how can one of us belittle himself? He said: “He sees a matter of God that he has to say about it, but he does not say anything about it. So God will say to him on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:What prevented you from saying something about such and such and such? He will say: Fear of people. So God will say: Then I was more deserving of your fear.” He is the only one who narrated it. He also said: Ali bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Fadil told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Abu Tawala told us, Nahar Al-Abdi told us that he heard Abu Saeed Al-Khudri say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God will ask the servant on the Day of Resurrection until He says: What prevented you from denouncing it when you saw an evil? If God teaches a servant his argument, he says: O Lord, I hoped in You and You divided the people. This was also narrated by Ibn Majah alone, and its chain of transmission is acceptable. Imam Ahmad said: Amr ibn Asim narrated to us on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Jundub, on the authority of Hudhayfah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A Muslim should not humiliate himself. It was said: How does he humiliate himself? He said: He exposes himself to trials that he cannot bear. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah both narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bashar, on the authority of Amr ibn Asim, and Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good, authentic, rare hadith. Ibn Majah said: Al-Abbas ibn Al-Waleed Al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Zayd ibn Yahya ibn Ubayd Al-Khuza’i narrated to us, Al-Haitham ibn Hamid narrated to us, Abu Ma’bad Hafs ibn Ghailan Al-Ra’ini narrated to us on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: It was said: O Messenger of God, when will enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong be abandoned? He said, Kingship is among your young, immorality is among your old, and knowledge is among your wicked. Zayd said: The interpretation of the meaning of the Prophet’s statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, and knowledge is among your wicked, if knowledge is among the wicked, is unique to Ibn Majah, and it will come in the hadith of Abu Tha’labah when he said, He who goes astray will not harm you if you are guided, is evidence for this, God willing, and He is trustworthy. Ibn Majah said: Rashid bin Saeed Al-Ramli told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us on the authority of Abu Ghalib, on the authority of Abu Umamah: He said: A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the first Jamarat and said: O Messenger of God, which jihad is best? He kept quiet about it. When he threw the second Jamarat and asked him, he kept quiet about it. When he threw the Jamarat Al-Aqaba and put his foot in the stirrup to mount, he said: Where is the questioner? He said: I will, O Messenger of God. He said: A word of truth said in the presence of an unjust ruler. It is narrated only by him. Ibn Majah said: Abu Kurayb told us, Abdullah bin Numayr and Abu Muawiyah told us on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Al-Buhturi, on the authority of Abu Saeed, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let none of you belittle himself. They said: O Messenger of God, how can one of us belittle himself? He said: “He sees a matter of God that he has to say about it, but he does not say anything about it. So God will say to him on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:What prevented you from saying something about such and such and such? He will say: Fear of people. So God will say: Then I was more deserving of your fear.” He is the only one who narrated it. He also said: Ali bin Muhammad told us, Muhammad bin Fadil told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Abu Tawala told us, Nahar Al-Abdi told us that he heard Abu Saeed Al-Khudri say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God will ask the servant on the Day of Resurrection until He says: What prevented you from denouncing it when you saw an evil? If God teaches a servant his argument, he says: O Lord, I hoped in You and You divided the people. This was also narrated by Ibn Majah alone, and its chain of transmission is acceptable. Imam Ahmad said: Amr ibn Asim narrated to us on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Jundub, on the authority of Hudhayfah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A Muslim should not humiliate himself. It was said: How does he humiliate himself? He said: He exposes himself to trials that he cannot bear. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah both narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bashar, on the authority of Amr ibn Asim, and Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good, authentic, rare hadith. Ibn Majah said: Al-Abbas ibn Al-Waleed Al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Zayd ibn Yahya ibn Ubayd Al-Khuza’i narrated to us, Al-Haitham ibn Hamid narrated to us, Abu Ma’bad Hafs ibn Ghailan Al-Ra’ini narrated to us on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: It was said: O Messenger of God, when will enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong be abandoned? He said: When what appeared among the nations before you appears among you. We said: O Messenger of God, and what appeared among the nations before us? He said, Kingship is among your young, immorality is among your old, and knowledge is among your wicked. Zayd said: The interpretation of the meaning of the Prophet’s statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, and knowledge is among your wicked, if knowledge is among the wicked, is unique to Ibn Majah, and it will come in the hadith of Abu Tha’labah when he said, He who goes astray will not harm you if you are guided, is evidence for this, God willing, and He is trustworthy. God the Almighty said: You will see many of them taking as allies those who disbelieve. Mujahid said: He means the hypocrites. And His statement: How evil is that which their souls have put forward for them means their friendship with the disbelievers and their abandonment of friendship with the believers, which resulted in hypocrisy in their hearts and incurred God’s wrath upon them with a wrath that will continue until the Day of Resurrection. For this reason He said: God’s wrath is upon them, and He explained with that what He condemned them with, then He informed about them that they will abide eternally in the punishment, meaning on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hisham bin Ammar told us, Muslim bin Ali told us on the authority of Al-A’mash with a chain of transmission that he mentioned, he said: “O group of Muslims, beware of adultery, for there are six consequences to it: three in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for the one in this world, it takes away beauty, causes poverty, and shortens life. As for the one in the Hereafter, it causes the wrath of the Lord, a bad reckoning, and eternity in the Fire.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “How evil is that which their souls have put forward for them: that God is angry with them, and in the punishment they will abide eternally.” This is how Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned it. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Hisham bin Ammar, on the authority of Muslimah, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Hudhayfah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned it. He also cited it on the authority of Sa’id bin Ghafir, on the authority of Muslimah, on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Kufi, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Hudhayfah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar. This is a weak hadith in any case, and God knows best. God Almighty says: And if they had believed in God and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies. That is, if they had truly believed in God, the Messenger, and the Qur’an, they would not have committed what they committed of befriending the disbelievers in secret, and opposing the believers in God, the Prophet, and what was revealed to him. But many of them are wicked. That is, they are outside the obedience of God and His Messenger, disobeying the verses of His revelation and sending down.
5:82: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: These verses were revealed about the Negus and his companions who, when Ja'far bin Abi Talib recited the Qur'an to them in Abyssinia, cried until their beards were wet. This statement is questionable, because this verse was revealed in Medina, and the story of Ja'far with the Negus was before the migration. Sa'id bin Jubayr, Al-Suddi and others said: It was revealed about a delegation sent by the Negus to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to hear his speech and see his attributes. When they saw him and he recited the Qur'an to them, they converted to Islam, cried and were humbled, then they returned to the Negus and informed him. Al-Suddi said: The Negus emigrated and died on the way. This is one of the individuals of Al-Suddi, because the Negus died while he was the king of Abyssinia, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed over him on the day he died, and he informed his companions about it, and he said that he died in the land of Abyssinia. Then there was a difference of opinion regarding the number of this delegation, and it was said: Twelve: Seven priests and five monks. And it was said: The opposite. It was said: Fifty. It was said: Sixty-odd. It was said: Seventy men, and God knows best. Ata bin Abi Rabah said: They are a people from Abyssinia who converted to Islam when the Muslim immigrants from Abyssinia came to them. Qatada said: They are a people who followed the religion of Jesus, son of Mary, and when they saw the Muslims and heard the Qur’an, they converted to Islam and did not falter. Ibn Jarir chose that these verses were revealed describing people of this status, whether they were from Abyssinia or elsewhere. God Almighty says: You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with God. This is only because the disbelief of the Jews is a disbelief of stubbornness, denial, and boasting about the truth, belittling people, and belittling the bearers of knowledge. For this reason, they killed many of the prophets, to the point that they intended to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, more than once. They poisoned him and cast a spell on him, and they incited against him those like them from among the polytheists. Upon them be the continuous curses of God until the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said when interpreting this verse: Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Al-Sarri told us, Muhammad bin Ali bin Habib Al-Raqqi told us, Ali bin Saeed Al-Alaaf told us, Abu Al-Nadr told us, on the authority of Al-Ashja’i, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Yahya bin Abdullah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A Jew has never been alone with a Muslim except that he thought of killing him. Then he narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Ishaq Al-Askari, Ahmad bin Ayoub Al-Ahwazi told us, Faraj bin Ubaid told us, Ibad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Abdullah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A Jew has never been alone with a Muslim except that he thought of killing him. This is a very strange hadith. God the Almighty says: And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to the believers to be those who say, ‘We are Christians.’ That is, those who claimed to be Christians, followers of Christ and on the path of his Gospel, have affection for Islam and its people in general. This is only because of the tenderness and compassion in their hearts, since they were on the religion of Christ, as God the Almighty says: And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him, compassion and mercy and monasticism. And in their book: Whoever strikes you on the right cheek, turn to him the left cheek. Fighting is not permissible in their religion, and for this reason God the Almighty says: That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant. That is, among them are priests, who are their preachers and scholars. The singular form of a priest is also a priest, and it may be pluralized as qusus. Monks is the plural of rahib, which means a worshipper, derived from rahbah, which means fear, like raakib and rakban, and farsan. Ibn Jarir said: Monks may be one and the plural is rahbain, like qurban and qurban, and jardan and jaradain, and it may be pluralized as rahbanah. Evidence that it is one among the Arabs is the poet’s saying: If you saw the monks of a monastery in the valley, the monks would walk and descend Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Bishr bin Adam told us, Naseer bin Abi Al-Ash'ath told us, Al-Salt Al-Dahhan told me on the authority of Jathima bin Ri'ab, who said: I asked Salman about the statement of God the Most High: That is because among them are priests and monks. He said: Leave the priests in the markets and ruins. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught me: That is because among them are truthful and monks. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in the same way on the authority of Yahya bin Abdul Hamid Al-Khani on the authority of Nadir bin Ziyad Al-Ta'i, on the authority of Salt Al-Dahhan, on the authority of Jathima bin Ri'ab, on the authority of Salman on his authority. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father mentioned it, Yahya bin Abdul Hamid Al-Khani told us, Nadir bin Ziyad Al-Ta’i told us, Salt Al-Dahhan told us on the authority of Jathima bin Ri’ab, who said: I heard Salman being asked about His statement, That is because among them are priests and monks, so he said, They are the monks who are in the monasteries and ruins, so leave them in them. Salman said: I read to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, That is because among them are priests, so he read to me, That is because among them are truthful and monks. So His statement, That is because among them are priests and monks, and that they are not arrogant, includes a description of them as having knowledge, worship, and humility. Then he described them as being obedient to the truth, following it, and being fair, so He said, And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth, meaning what they have of the good report of the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. They say, ‘Our Lord, we have believed, so register us with the witnesses,’ meaning with those who testify to the truth of this and believe in it. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Ali al-Fallas, on the authority of Umar ibn Ali ibn Muqaddam, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: This verse was revealed about the Negus and his companions: “And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, ‘Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses.’” Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: So register us among the witnesses, meaning with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation are the witnesses, they testify to their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he has conveyed the message, and to the Messengers that they have conveyed the message. Then al-Hakim said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, and they did not include it. Al-Tabarani said: Abu Shabil Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Waqid told us, my father told us, Al-Abbas bin Al-Fadl told us, on the authority of Abdul Jabbar bin Nafi’ Al-Dhabi, on the authority of Qatada and Ja’far bin Iyas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God Almighty: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears, he said: They were farmers, meaning farmers, who had come with Ja’far bin Abi Talib from Abyssinia. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited the Qur’an to them, they believed and their eyes overflowed with tears. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Perhaps when you return to your land, you will convert to your religion. They said: We will not convert from our religion. So God revealed that from their statement: And why should we not believe in God and in what has come to us of the truth and hope that our Lord will admit us with the righteous people? This type of Christians are those mentioned in the statement of God Almighty: And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in God and in what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them, humbly submissive to God, the verse, and they are those about whom God said: “Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they believe in it. And when it is recited to them, they say, ‘We believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were, before it, Muslims.’” to His saying, We do not seek the ignorant. That is why God Almighty said here: So God rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is, He rewarded them for their faith, belief, and acknowledgment of the truth. Gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. That is, remaining there forever, never changing or disappearing. And that is the reward of the doers of good. That is, in following the truth and submitting to it wherever it was, wherever it was, and with whomever it was. Then He informed about the state of the wretched, saying, And those who disbelieved and denied Our verses. That is, they denied them and opposed them. Those are the companions of Hellfire. That is, they are its people and those who will enter it.

Sa'id bin Jubayr, Al-Suddi and others said: It was revealed about a delegation sent by the Negus to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to hear his speech and see his attributes. Al-Suddi said: The Negus emigrated and died on the way. This is one of the individuals of Al-Suddi, because the Negus died while he was the king of Abyssinia, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed over him on the day he died, and he informed his companions about it, and he said that he died in the land of Abyssinia. Then there was a difference of opinion regarding the number of this delegation, and it was said: Twelve: Seven priests and five monks. And it was said: The opposite. It was said: Fifty. It was said: Sixty-odd. It was said: Seventy men, and God knows best. Ata bin Abi Rabah said: They are a people from Abyssinia who converted to Islam when the Muslim immigrants from Abyssinia came to them. Qatada said: They are a people who followed the religion of Jesus, son of Mary, and when they saw the Muslims and heard the Qur’an, they converted to Islam and did not falter. Ibn Jarir chose that these verses were revealed describing people of this status, whether they were from Abyssinia or elsewhere. God Almighty says: You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with God. This is only because the disbelief of the Jews is a disbelief of stubbornness, denial, and boasting about the truth, belittling people, and belittling the bearers of knowledge. For this reason, they killed many of the prophets, to the point that they intended to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, more than once. They poisoned him and cast a spell on him, and they incited against him those like them from among the polytheists. Upon them be the continuous curses of God until the Day of Resurrection. 5:89: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: This verse was revealed about a group of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said: We will cut off our penises, abandon the desires of this world, and wander the earth as monks do. This reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he sent to them and mentioned that to them. They said: Yes. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “But I fast and break my fast, I pray, I sleep, and I marry women. Whoever follows my Sunnah is from me, and whoever does not follow my Sunnah is not from me.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. In the two Sahihs on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about his actions in secret. Some of them said: I do not eat meat. Some of them said: I do not marry women. Some of them said: I do not sleep on the bed. This reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he said: What is the matter with people who say such and such, but I fast and break my fast, sleep and pray, and eat meat? I marry women, and whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Issam Al-Ansari told us, Abu Asim Al-Dahhak bin Mukhallad told us, on the authority of Uthman, meaning Ibn Saeed, Ikrimah told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that a man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, when I eat this meat, I feel aversion to women, and I have forbidden myself meat, so the verse was revealed: O you who believe, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir both narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Ali Al-Fallas on the authority of Abu Asim Al-Nabil on his authority. He said: It is hasan gharib. It has been narrated from another source as a mursal, and it has been narrated as a mursal on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and God knows best. Sufyan Al-Thawri and Waki’ said on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: We used to go on a military campaign with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there were no women with us, so we said: Should we not castrate ourselves? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade us from that, and permitted us to marry a woman for a garment for a period of time. Then Abdullah recited, O you who believe, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you, the verse. They narrated it from the hadith of Ismail, and this was before the prohibition of temporary marriage, and God knows best.
