Al-A’mash said, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Hammam bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Amr bin Shurahbil, who said: Maqal bin Muqrin came to Abdullah bin Masoud and said: I have forbidden my bed, so he recited this verse: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you Al-A’mash 19:10. Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, who said: We were with Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, and an udder was brought to him, so a man moved away, and Abdullah said to him: Come closer, so he said: I have forbidden myself from eating it, so Abdullah said: Come closer, eat, and atone for your oath, and he recited this verse: O you who believe, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you Al-Bukhari and Muslim. The verse: Ibn Abi Hatim narrated them, and Al-Hakim narrated this last trace in his Mustadrak on the authority of Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, on the authority of Jarir, on the authority of Mansur, then he said: According to the condition of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it, then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn `Abd al-`A`la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Hisham ibn Sa`d informed me that Zayd ibn Aslam told him that Abdullah ibn Rawahah was hosted by a guest from his family, while he was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he returned to his family and found that they had not fed their guest, waiting for him, so he said to his wife: You have detained my guest for my sake, it is forbidden to me, so she said: His wife: It is forbidden to me. The guest said: It is forbidden to me. When he saw that, he put his hand and said: Eat in the name of God. Then he went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned what had happened to them. Then God revealed: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you. This is an interrupted report. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, in the story of the friend with his guests, there is something similar to this. In this story and in it there is evidence for those scholars, such as Al-Shafi’i and others, who said that whoever forbids food, clothing, or anything other than women, it is not forbidden to him, and he does not have to make expiation either. And because of the saying of God the Almighty: O you who believe! Do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful for you. And because the one who forbade meat to himself, as in the previous hadith, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not command him to make expiation. And others, including Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, said that whoever forbids food, drink, clothing, or anything else, then he must make expiation for an oath, just as if he committed himself to leaving it by swearing, so he is held accountable for merely forbidding it to himself, forcing him to do what he committed himself to, as Ibn Abbas issued a fatwa on this, and as in the saying of God the Almighty: O Prophet! Why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you, seeking the pleasure of your wives? And God is Forgiving and Merciful? Then He said: God has prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths. And likewise here, when he mentioned this ruling, he followed it up. In the verse explaining the expiation of an oath, it indicates that this is the same as an oath in requiring expiation, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Some men among them, Uthman ibn Mazun and Abdullah ibn Amr, wanted to be celibate, to dedicate themselves, and to wear hair-sackcloth, so this verse was revealed up to His saying: And fear God, in whom you are believers. Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Ikrimah: That Uthman ibn Maz’un, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn Mas’ud, Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad, and Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, and his companions were devoted to celibacy, so they sat in their homes, avoided women, wore hair-cloth, and forbade good food and clothing, except for what was eaten and worn by the travelers from the Children of Israel. They intended to castrate themselves, and they agreed to stand in prayer at night and fast during the day, so this verse was revealed: “O you who believe! Do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful to you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not like transgressors.” He said: Do not follow other than the way of the Muslims, meaning what they forbade of women, food, and clothing, and what they agreed to stand in prayer at night and fast during the day, and what they intended to do of castration. So when it was revealed about them, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to them and said: “Your souls have a right, and your eyes have a right. Fast and break your fast, pray and sleep, for he who abandons our way is not one of us.” They said: O God, keep us safe and follow what You have revealed. This story was mentioned by more than one of the followers as a mursal, and it has a corroborating report in the two Sahihs from the narration of Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, as mentioned above. Praise and thanks be to God. Asbat said on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement, “O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not like transgressors,” that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat one day and mentioned the people, then he stood up and did not increase their fear except by frightening them. Some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and they were ten, including Ali bin Abi Talib and Uthman bin Maz’un: What right do we have if we do not innovate an action? The Christians have forbidden themselves, so we forbid. Some of them forbade eating meat and fat, and eating during the day, and some of them forbade sleeping, and some of them forbade women. Uthman bin Maz’un was among those who forbade women, so he would not come near his family and they would not come near him. Then his wife Aisha, may God be pleased with her, came, and she was called Al-Hawla’. Aisha and the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who were with her, said to her: What is the matter with you, O Al-Hawla’, that your color has changed? You do not comb your hair or use perfume? She said: How can I comb my hair and use perfume when my husband has not fallen on me, and no garment has fallen off me since such and such. He said: They started laughing at her words, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered while they were laughing, so he said: What makes you laugh? She said: O Messenger of God, the cross-eyed woman asked her about her situation. She said: My husband has not dropped a garment from me for such and such a time. So he sent for him and called him and said: What is the matter with you, O Uthman? He said: I left it for God in order to devote myself to worship, and he told him his situation. Othman wanted to answer himself, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I swear to you to go back and have intercourse with your wife. He said: O Messenger of God, I am fasting. He said: Break your fast. So he broke his fast and went to his wife. The cross-eyed woman returned to Aisha, combing her hair, applying kohl, and perfume. Aisha laughed and said: What is the matter with you, O cross-eyed woman? She said: He came to her yesterday. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “What is the matter with people who have forbidden women, food and sleep? I sleep, I stand, I break my fast, I marry women. Whoever turns away from me is not of me.” Then the verse was revealed: O you who believe, do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful to you and do not transgress. He said to Uthman: Do not force yourself, for this is transgression. He ordered them to atone for their oaths, saying: God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for your deliberate oaths. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. God the Almighty said: And do not transgress. It is possible that what is meant by it is: Do not exaggerate in restricting yourselves by forbidding permissible things to you, as was said by those of the Salaf who said it. It is possible that what is meant is: Just as you do not forbid what is permissible, do not transgress in consuming what is permissible, but take from it as much as is sufficient for you and your need, and do not exceed the limit in it, as God the Almighty said: And eat and drink, but be not excessive. The verse, and He said: And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor niggardly, but are between those extremes. So God’s law is just between those who are excessive in it and those who are harsh in it, neither excessive nor negligent. For this reason He said: “Do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful to you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not like transgressors.” Then He said: And eat from what God has provided for you, lawful and good. That is, when it is lawful and good. And fear God. That is, in all your affairs, and follow His obedience and pleasure, and leave disobeying and disobeying Him. And fear God, in whom you are believers. We have already discussed the idle oath in Surat Al-Baqarah, so there is no need to repeat it here, praise and thanks be to God. It is a man saying in speech without intending it: No, by God, and Yes, by God. This is the view of Al-Shafi'i. It was also said that it is in jest. It was also said: in disobedience. It was also said: on the basis of a strong opinion, which is the view of Abu Hanifa and Ahmad. It was also said: an oath in anger. It was also said: in forgetfulness. It was also said: it is an oath to abstain from food, drink, clothing, and the like. They used as evidence the statement of God, Do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful for you. The correct view is that it is an oath without intent, as evidenced by His statement, But He will hold you accountable for what you have sworn to do, meaning what you intended and intended. And its expiation is to feed ten poor people, meaning needy people from the poor and those who do not have enough to eat. And his saying, of the best of what you feed your families, Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubair, and Ikrimah said: meaning, of the most just of what you feed your families. Ata’ al-Khurasani said: of the best of what you feed your families. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed al-Ashj told us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi’i, on the authority of al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, who said: Bread and milk, and bread and ghee. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told us, reading, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Sulayman, meaning Ibn Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A man would feed some of his family with less food, and some of them with more food, so God Almighty said: From the average of what you feed your families, meaning bread and oil. Abu Saeed Al-Ashja told us, Waki’ told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, From the average of what you feed your families, he said: From their hardship and ease. Abdul Rahman bin Khalaf Al-Himsi told us, Muhammad bin Shu’ayb, meaning Ibn Shabur, told us, and Shaiban bin Abdul Rahman Al-Tamimi told us, on the authority of Laith bin Abi Salim, on the authority of Asim Al-Ahwal, on the authority of a man called Abdul Rahman Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with him, that he said: From the average of what you feed your families, he said: Bread and meat, bread and ghee, bread and milk, bread and oil, bread and vinegar. And Ali bin Harb Al-Mawsili told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ibn Umar, regarding his statement, Of the best of what you feed your families, he said: Bread and ghee, bread and milk, bread and oil, bread and dates, and of the best of what you feed your families is bread and meat. And Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Hannad and Ibn Wakee’, both of them on the authority of Abu Muawiyah. Then Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ubaydah, Al-Aswad, Shureih Al-Qadi, Muhammad bin Sirin, Al-Hasan, Al-Dahhak, and Abu Razin, that they said something similar to that, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Makhul as well. Ibn Jarir chose that what is meant by his saying, from the average of what you feed your families, is in terms of little or much. Then the scholars differed about the amount of what he should feed them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed told us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Hisayn al-Harithi, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding his saying, from the average of what you feed your families, he said: He should feed them breakfast and dinner. Al-Hasan and Muhammad ibn Sirin said: It is sufficient for him to feed ten poor people one meal of bread and meat. Al-Hasan added: If he cannot find that, then bread, ghee and milk. If he cannot find that, then bread, oil and vinegar, until they are full. Others said: He should feed each one of the ten half a sa’ of wheat or dates or something similar. This is the saying of Umar, Ali, Aisha, Mujahid, al-Sha’bi, Saeed ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, Maymun ibn Mihran, Abu Malik, al-Dahhak, al-Hakam, Makhul, Abu Qilabah and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Abu Hanifa said: Half a saa of wheat and a saa of anything else. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Al-Hasan Al-Thaqafi told us, Ubaid bin Al-Hasan bin Yusuf told us, Muhammad bin Muawiyah told us, Ziyad bin Abdullah bin Al-Tufayl bin Sakhbarah bin Aisha’s maternal nephew told us, Umar bin Ya’la told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disbelieved with a Sa’ of dates and ordered the people to do the same, and whoever could not find anything, then half a Sa’ of wheat. And Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Al-Abbas bin Yazid, on the authority of Ziyad bin Abdullah Al-Bakka’, on the authority of Umar bin Abdullah bin Ya’la Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, with it. This hadith is not authentic due to the state of Umar bin Abdullah, as there is consensus on his weakness, and they mentioned that he used to drink alcohol. Al-Daraqutni said: He is rejected. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashja told us, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Dawud, meaning Ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: A mudd of wheat means for each poor person, along with his condiment. Then he said: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, Zaid Ibn Thabit, Saeed Ibn Al-Musayyab, Mujahid, Ata’, Ikrimah, Abu Al-Sha’tha’, Al-Qasim, Salim, Abu Salamah Ibn Abd Al-Rahman, Sulayman Ibn Yasar, Al-Hasan, Muhammad Ibn Sirin, and Al-Zuhri, something similar to that. Al-Shafi’i said: The obligatory expiation for an oath is a mudd of wheat according to the mudd of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for each poor person, and he did not mention the condiment. He cited as evidence the command of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to the one who had intercourse in Ramadan to feed sixty poor people from a measure that holds fifteen sa’s, each one of them a mudd. Another explicit hadeeth was narrated on this subject. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Muqri narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Siraj narrated to us, Qutaybah ibn Sa’id narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Zararah al-Kufi narrated to us on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar al-Amri on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to set the expiation for an oath as a mudd of wheat according to the first mudd. Its chain of transmission is weak due to the case of al-Nadr ibn Zararah ibn Abd al-Akram al-Dahli al-Kufi, a resident of Balkh. Abu Hatim al-Razi said about him: He is unknown, although more than one person narrated from him, and Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy. He said: Qutaybah ibn Sa’id narrated some reliable things from him, and God knows best. Then his sheikh al-Amri is also weak. Ahmad bin Hanbal said: It is obligatory to give a mudd of wheat or a mudd of other wheat, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: or their clothing. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: If he gave each one of the ten something that could be described as clothing, such as a shirt, trousers, a loincloth, a turban, or a veil, that would suffice him. His companions differed regarding the skullcap: is it sufficient or not? There are two views. Some of them held that it is permissible, citing as evidence what was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj and Ammar bin Khalid Al-Wasiti told us: Al-Qasim bin Malik told us on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of his father, who said: I asked Imran bin Al-Hussain about his saying or their clothing. He said: If a delegation came to your leader and he gave them a skullcap, you would say that they had been clothed. But this chain of transmission is weak due to the situation of Muhammad bin Al-Zubayr. And God knows best. Thus, Sheikh Abu Hamid Al-Isfarayini narrated: There are also two opinions regarding the sock, and the correct one is that it is not sufficient. Malik and Ahmad bin Hanbal said: It is necessary to give each one of them enough clothing to pray in, whether he is a man or a woman, each according to his ability, and God knows best. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: An cloak or a shawl for every poor person. Mujahid said: The lowest is a garment and the highest is whatever you wish. Laith said on the authority of Mujahid: Everything is sufficient for expiation for an oath except a pair of socks. Al-Hasan, Abu Ja`far al-Baqir, `Ata`, Tawus, Ibrahim al-Nakha`i, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman and Abu Malik said: A garment is a garment. Ibrahim al-Nakha`i also said: A garment that combines like a sheet and a rida`. A shield, shirt, veil, and the like are not considered to combine. Al-Ansari said on the authority of Ash`ath on the authority of Ibn Sirin: Al-Hasan is two garments, two garments. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab: A turban that he wraps around his head, and an cloak that he covers himself with. Ibn Jarir said: Hannad told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us on the authority of `Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Musa that he swore an oath, so he was clothed in two garments from the Muqaddah of Bahrain. Ibn Mardawayh said: Sulayman ibn Ahmad told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mu’alla told us, Hisham ibn ‘Ammar told us, Ismail ibn ‘Ayyash told us, on the authority of Muqatil ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Abu ‘Uthman, on the authority of Abu ‘Ayyadh, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement, or their clothing, he said, a cloak for every poor person, a strange hadith. And his saying or freeing a slave Abu Hanifa took it in general terms and said: A female unbeliever is sufficient just as a female believer is sufficient. Al-Shafi’i and others said: She must be a believer. He took the restriction of her to faith from the expiation for murder because the obligation is the same even if the reason is different. From the hadith of Mu’awiyah ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami which is in the Muwatta of Malik, the Musnad of al-Shafi’i and Sahih Muslim, he mentioned that he had to free a slave, and he brought with him a black slave girl, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to her: Where is God? She said: In the sky. He said: Who am I? She said: The Messenger of God. He said: Free her, for she is a believer. The hadith in its entirety. These are three things in the expiation for an oath, whichever action the perjurer does is sufficient for him by consensus. He started with the easiest, so feeding is easier and simpler than clothing, just as clothing is easier than freeing, so he progresses from the lowest to the highest, so if the person responsible is not able to do one of these three things, he expiates by fasting three days, as God the Almighty said: But whoever cannot find [anything] - then a fast of three days. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair and Al-Hasan Al-Basri that they said: Whoever finds three dirhams must feed the poor, otherwise he must fast. Ibn Jarir said, narrating on the authority of some of the later scholars of his time, that it is permissible for someone who does not have any surplus capital to spend on his livelihood, and what is left over is what he can use to atone for his oath. Then Ibn Jarir chose that what is not surplus over his food and the food of his family in a day is what he can use to atone for an oath. The scholars differed: Is it obligatory to do it consecutively or is it recommended but not obligatory, and is it sufficient to do it separately? There are two opinions: One of them is that it is not obligatory, and this is stated by Al-Shafi’i in the Book of Oaths, and it is the opinion of Malik because of the generality of his statement then fasting three days, and it is true for both the group and the separate days, as in making up Ramadan, because he said then a number of other days. Al-Shafi’i stated in another place in Al-Umm that it is obligatory to do it consecutively, as is the opinion of the Hanafis and Hanbalis, because it was narrated on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b and others that they used to recite it then fasting three days. Abu Jaafar Al-Razi said, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, that he used to recite it as a fast of three days. Mujahid, Al-Sha’bi and Abu Ishaq narrated it on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud. Ibrahim said regarding the recitation of the companions of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, a fast of three days. Al-A’mash said, the companions of Ibn Mas’ud used to recite it like this. If it is not proven that it is a continuous narration of the Qur’an, then it is at least a single report or an explanation from the companions, and it is considered a marfu’ hadith. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ali told us, Muhammad ibn Jaafar Al-Ash’ari told us, Al-Haitham ibn Khalid Al-Qurashi told us, Yazid ibn Qays told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Yahya, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the verse of expiations was revealed, Hudhayfah said: O Messenger of God, do we have a choice? He said: “You have a choice. If you wish, you can free a slave, or if you wish, you can clothe him, or if you wish, you can feed him. But whoever cannot find [anything], then he should fast for three consecutive days.” This is a very strange hadith. His statement, This is the expiation for your oaths when you swear, meaning this is the legal expiation for an oath. And guard your oaths. Ibn Jarir said: Its meaning is do not abandon them without expiation. Thus does God make clear to you His verses, meaning He clarifies and explains them, that you may be grateful.
5:88: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: This verse was revealed about a group of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said: We will cut off our penises, abandon the desires of this world, and wander the earth as monks do. This reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he sent to them and mentioned that to them. They said: Yes. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “But I fast and break my fast, I pray, I sleep, and I marry women. Whoever follows my Sunnah is from me, and whoever does not follow my Sunnah is not from me.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. In the two Sahihs on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about his actions in secret. Some of them said: I do not eat meat. Some of them said: I do not marry women. Some of them said: I do not sleep on the bed. This reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he said: What is the matter with people who say such and such, but I fast and break my fast, sleep and pray, and eat meat? I marry women, and whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Issam Al-Ansari told us, Abu Asim Al-Dahhak bin Mukhallad told us, on the authority of Uthman, meaning Ibn Saeed, Ikrimah told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that a man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, when I eat this meat, I feel aversion to women, and I have forbidden myself meat, so the verse was revealed: O you who believe, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Jarir both narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Ali Al-Fallas on the authority of Abu Asim Al-Nabil on his authority. He said: It is hasan gharib. It has been narrated from another source as a mursal, and it has been narrated as a mursal on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and God knows best. Sufyan Al-Thawri and Waki’ said on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: We used to go on a military campaign with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there were no women with us, so we said: Should we not castrate ourselves? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade us from that, and permitted us to marry a woman for a garment for a period of time. Then Abdullah recited, O you who believe, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you, the verse. They narrated it from the hadith of Ismail, and this was before the prohibition of temporary marriage, and God knows best. Al-A’mash said, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Hammam bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Amr bin Shurahbil, who said: Maqal bin Muqrin came to Abdullah bin Masoud and said: I have forbidden my bed, so he recited this verse: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you Al-A’mash 19:10. Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, who said: We were with Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, and an udder was brought to him, so a man moved away, and Abdullah said to him: Come closer, so he said: I have forbidden myself from eating it, so Abdullah said: Come closer, eat, and atone for your oath, and he recited this verse: O you who believe, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you Al-Bukhari and Muslim. The verse: Ibn Abi Hatim narrated them, and Al-Hakim narrated this last trace in his Mustadrak on the authority of Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, on the authority of Jarir, on the authority of Mansur, then he said: According to the condition of the two sheikhs, and they did not include it, then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn `Abd al-`A`la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Hisham ibn Sa`d informed me that Zayd ibn Aslam told him that Abdullah ibn Rawahah was hosted by a guest from his family, while he was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he returned to his family and found that they had not fed their guest, waiting for him, so he said to his wife: You have detained my guest for my sake, it is forbidden to me, so she said: His wife: It is forbidden to me. The guest said: It is forbidden to me. When he saw that, he put his hand and said: Eat in the name of God. Then he went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned what had happened to them. Then God revealed: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you. This is an interrupted report. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, in the story of the friend with his guests, there is something similar to this. In this story and in it there is evidence for those scholars, such as Al-Shafi’i and others, who said that whoever forbids food, clothing, or anything other than women, it is not forbidden to him, and he does not have to make expiation either. And because of the saying of God the Almighty: O you who believe! Do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful for you. And because the one who forbade meat to himself, as in the previous hadith, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not command him to make expiation. And others, including Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, said that whoever forbids food, drink, clothing, or anything else, then he must make expiation for an oath, just as if he committed himself to leaving it by swearing, so he is held accountable for merely forbidding it to himself, forcing him to do what he committed himself to, as Ibn Abbas issued a fatwa on this, and as in the saying of God the Almighty: O Prophet! Why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you, seeking the pleasure of your wives? And God is Forgiving and Merciful? Then He said: God has prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths. And likewise here, when he mentioned this ruling, he followed it up. In the verse explaining the expiation of an oath, it indicates that this is the same as an oath in requiring expiation, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Some men among them, Uthman ibn Mazun and Abdullah ibn Amr, wanted to be celibate, to dedicate themselves, and to wear hair-sackcloth, so this verse was revealed up to His saying: And fear God, in whom you are believers. Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Ikrimah: That Uthman ibn Maz’un, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn Mas’ud, Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad, and Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, and his companions were devoted to celibacy, so they sat in their homes, avoided women, wore hair-cloth, and forbade good food and clothing, except for what was eaten and worn by the travelers from the Children of Israel. They intended to castrate themselves, and they agreed to stand in prayer at night and fast during the day, so this verse was revealed: “O you who believe! Do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful to you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not like transgressors.” He said: Do not follow other than the way of the Muslims, meaning what they forbade of women, food, and clothing, and what they agreed to stand in prayer at night and fast during the day, and what they intended to do of castration. So when it was revealed about them, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to them and said: “Your souls have a right, and your eyes have a right. Fast and break your fast, pray and sleep, for he who abandons our way is not one of us.” They said: O God, keep us safe and follow what You have revealed. This story was mentioned by more than one of the followers as a mursal, and it has a corroborating report in the two Sahihs from the narration of Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, as mentioned above. Praise and thanks be to God. Asbat said on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement, “O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not like transgressors,” that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat one day and mentioned the people, then he stood up and did not increase their fear except by frightening them. Some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and they were ten, including Ali bin Abi Talib and Uthman bin Maz’un: What right do we have if we do not innovate an action? The Christians have forbidden themselves, so we forbid. Some of them forbade eating meat and fat, and eating during the day, and some of them forbade sleeping, and some of them forbade women. Uthman bin Maz’un was among those who forbade women, so he would not come near his family and they would not come near him. Then his wife Aisha, may God be pleased with her, came, and she was called Al-Hawla’. Aisha and the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who were with her, said to her: What is the matter with you, O Al-Hawla’, that your color has changed? You do not comb your hair or use perfume? She said: How can I comb my hair and use perfume when my husband has not fallen on me, and no garment has fallen off me since such and such. He said: They started laughing at her words, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered while they were laughing, so he said: What makes you laugh? She said: O Messenger of God, the cross-eyed woman asked her about her situation. She said: My husband has not dropped a garment from me for such and such a time. So he sent for him and called him and said: What is the matter with you, O Uthman? He said: I left it for God in order to devote myself to worship, and he told him his situation. Othman wanted to answer himself, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I swear to you to go back and have intercourse with your wife. He said: O Messenger of God, I am fasting. He said: Break your fast. So he broke his fast and went to his wife. The cross-eyed woman returned to Aisha, combing her hair, applying kohl, and perfume. Aisha laughed and said: What is the matter with you, O cross-eyed woman? She said: He came to her yesterday. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “What is the matter with people who have forbidden women, food and sleep? I sleep, I stand, I break my fast, I marry women. Whoever turns away from me is not of me.” Then the verse was revealed: O you who believe, do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful to you and do not transgress. He said to Uthman: Do not force yourself, for this is transgression. He ordered them to atone for their oaths, saying: God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for your deliberate oaths. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. God the Almighty said: And do not transgress. It is possible that what is meant by it is: Do not exaggerate in restricting yourselves by forbidding permissible things to you, as was said by those of the Salaf who said it. It is possible that what is meant is: Just as you do not forbid what is permissible, do not transgress in consuming what is permissible, but take from it as much as is sufficient for you and your need, and do not exceed the limit in it, as God the Almighty said: And eat and drink, but be not excessive. The verse, and He said: And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor niggardly, but are between those extremes. So God’s law is just between those who are excessive in it and those who are harsh in it, neither excessive nor negligent. For this reason He said: “Do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful to you, and do not transgress. Indeed, God does not like transgressors.” Then He said: And eat from what God has provided for you, lawful and good. That is, when it is lawful and good. And fear God. That is, in all your affairs, and follow His obedience and pleasure, and leave disobeying and disobeying Him. And fear God, in whom you are believers.
5:90: God the Almighty says: Forbidding His believing servants from consuming alcohol and gambling, which is betting. It was reported from the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Chess is from betting, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Isa ibn Marhum, from Hatim, from Jaafar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ali with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Ahmasi told us, Waki’ told us, from Sufyan, from Laith, from Ata’, Mujahid and Tawus said: Sufyan or two of them said: Everything from gambling is from betting, even children playing with nuts. It was reported from Rashid ibn Sa’d and Damrah ibn Habib something similar, and they said: Even the heels, nuts and eggs that children play with. Musa ibn Uqbah said, from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar, who said: Betting is gambling. Ad-Dahhak said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Gambling is gambling. They used to gamble in the pre-Islamic era until the advent of Islam, so God forbade them from these ugly morals. Malik said, on the authority of Dawud ibn al-Husayn, that he heard Saeed ibn al-Musayyab say: Gambling among the people of the pre-Islamic era was selling meat for one or two sheep. Al-Zuhri said, on the authority of Al-Araj, that he said: Gambling is casting lots for money and dice. Al-Qasim bin Muhammad said: Everything that distracts from the remembrance of God and from prayer is gambling. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Mansur Al-Ziyadi narrated to us, Hisham bin Ammar narrated to us, Sadaqah narrated to us, Uthman bin Abi Al-Atika narrated to us, on the authority of Ali bin Yazid, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Avoid these branded dice that are used to deter people, for they are gambling. This is a strange hadith, and it seems that what is meant by this is the dice that was mentioned in the hadith in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Buraydah bin Al-Husaib Al-Aslami, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever plays with dice, it is as if he dipped his hand in the flesh and blood of a pig. And in the Muwatta of Malik, Musnad Ahmad, Sunan Abi Dawud and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever plays with dice has disobeyed God and His Messenger. And it was narrated with a chain of transmission ending with Abu Musa from his statement, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Ali bin Ibrahim told us, Al-Juaid told us, on the authority of Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Khatmi, that he heard Muhammad bin Kaab asking Abdul Rahman saying: Tell me what you heard your father say about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abdul Rahman said: I heard my father say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The example of the one who plays with dice and then stands up and prays is like the example of the one who performs ablution with pus and pig’s blood and then stands up and prays. As for chess, Abdullah bin Omar said that it is worse than dice. It was previously reported from Ali that he said: It is gambling. Malik, Abu Hanifa, and Ahmad explicitly prohibited it, and Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on them, disliked it. As for idols, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata’, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, and more than one said: They are stones that they used to slaughter their sacrifices at. As for arrows, they also said: They are arrows that they used to draw lots with. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. God the Almighty said: An abomination from the work of Satan. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning anger from the work of Satan. Saeed bin Jubair said: sin. Zaid bin Aslam said: meaning evil from the work of Satan. So avoid it. The pronoun refers to the abomination, meaning leave it. That you may be successful. This is an encouragement. Then God the Almighty said: “Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of God and from prayer. So will you not desist?” This is a threat and intimidation. Mentioning the hadiths that explain the prohibition of alcohol Imam Ahmad said: Shureih told us, Abu Ma`shar told us, on the authority of Abu Wahb, the freed slave of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: Alcohol was forbidden three times. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina while they were drinking alcohol and gambling. So they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about them, and God revealed: “They ask you about alcohol and gambling. Say, ‘In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people.’” to the end of the verse. The people said: It was not forbidden to us, but He said: In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people. They used to drink alcohol until one day, a man from the Muhajireen prayed, leading his companions in the Maghrib prayer, and he mixed up his recitation, so God revealed a verse that was more severe than it: O you who believe! Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying. So the people used to drink until one of them came to the prayer while he was asleep. Then a verse that was more severe than it was revealed: “O you who believe! Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.” They said: We have finished, our Lord. The people said: O Messenger of God, people were killed in the way of God and died in their beds; they used to drink alcohol and eat gambling, and God has made it an defilement from the work of Satan. So God revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten to the end of the verse. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If it had been forbidden to them, they would have left it as you left it. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf bin Al-Waleed told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, that when the prohibition of alcohol was revealed, he said: O God, give us a clear explanation about alcohol. Then the verse in Al-Baqarah was revealed: “They ask you about alcohol and gambling. Say, ‘In them is great sin.’” So Umar was called and it was recited to him. He said: O God, give us a clear explanation about alcohol. Then the verse in Surat An-Nisa was revealed: O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated. When the caller of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Come to prayer, he would call: Do not approach prayer while drunk. So Umar was called and it was recited to him. He said: O God, give us a clear explanation about alcohol. Then the verse in Al-Ma’idah was revealed. Umar was called and it was recited to him. When he reached the words of God the Most High: Will you then desist? Umar said: We have desisted, we have desisted. And thus Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa'i narrated it through various chains of transmission, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Umar ibn Abdullah Al-Sabi'i, and on the authority of Abu Maysarah, whose name is Amr ibn Shurahbil Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Umar, and he has no other chain of transmission on his authority. Abu Zur'ah said: He did not hear from him. This hadith was authenticated by Ali ibn Al-Madini and Al-Tirmidhi. It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab that he said in his sermon on the pulpit of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him): O people, the prohibition of alcohol has been revealed, and it is from five things: grapes, dates, honey, wheat and barley. Alcohol is that which intoxicates the mind. Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, Abdul Aziz ibn Umar ibn Abdul Aziz told us, Nafi' told me on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The prohibition of alcohol was revealed, and in Madinah at that time there were five drinks, none of which included grape juice. [Another hadith] Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hamid told us, on the authority of al-Masri, meaning Abu Ta’mah, the reciter of Egypt, who said: I heard Ibn Umar say: Three verses were revealed regarding wine. The first to be revealed was: They ask you about wine and gambling, the verse. It was said: Wine has been forbidden. They said: O Messenger of God, let us benefit from it as God Almighty said. He said: So he remained silent about them. Then this verse was revealed: Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated, and it was said: Wine has been forbidden. They said: O Messenger of God, we do not drink it near prayer. He remained silent about them. Then this verse was revealed: O you who have believed, indeed, wine, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it, the two verses. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Wine has been forbidden. [Another Hadith] Imam Ahmad said: Ya`la told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Qa`qa` ibn Hakim, that Abd al-Rahman ibn Wa`lah said: I asked Ibn Abbas about selling wine, and he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a friend from Thaqeef or Daws, and he met him on the day of the conquest with a skin of wine to give him as a gift. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O so-and-so, did you not know that God has forbidden it? The man turned to his servant and said: Go and sell it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O so-and-so, what did you order him to do? He said: I ordered him to sell it. He said: He who has forbidden its drinking has forbidden its sale. So he ordered it to be emptied into the valley. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, and on the authority of Ibn Wahb also, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Bilal, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa`id, both on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Wa`lah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on his authority. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah, on the authority of Malik, on his authority. [Another hadith] Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la al-Mawsili said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami told us, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, `Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja`far told us, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Tamim al-Dari, that he used to give the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a jug of wine every year. When God revealed the prohibition of wine, he brought it. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw it, he laughed and said, It has been prohibited after you. He said, O Messenger of God, so I sell it and benefit from its price. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “May God curse the Jews. The fat of cows and sheep was prohibited to them, so they melted it and sold it. God prohibited wine and its price.” Imam Ahmad also narrated it, saying: Ruh told us, `Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram told us, he heard Shahr ibn Hawshab say, `Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanim told me that al-Dari used to give the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a jug of wine every year. When it was the year it was prohibited, he brought a jug. When he looked at it, he laughed and said, Do you know that it has been prohibited? After you,” he said: O Messenger of God, should I not sell it and benefit from its price? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God curse the Jews. They went to what was forbidden to them of the fat of cows and sheep, melted it, and sold with it what they eat. Wine is forbidden and its price is forbidden. Wine is forbidden and its price is forbidden. Wine is forbidden and its price is forbidden.” [Another Hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah ibn Sa`id narrated to us, Ibn Lahi`ah narrated to us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Sulayman ibn `Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Nafi` ibn Kaysan, that his father informed him that he was trading in wine during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that he had come from the Levant with wine in a wineskin, intending to trade with it. He brought it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I have come to you with a good drink. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Kaysan, it has been forbidden after you left. He said: Should I sell it, O Messenger of God? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It has been forbidden and so has its price. So Kaysan went to the wineskin, took hold of its legs, and poured it out. [Another hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told us on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Anas, who said: I was giving water to Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah, Ubayy bin Kaab, Saeed bin Bayda, and a group of his companions at Abu Talha’s until the drink almost took its toll on them. Then a Muslim man came and said: Did you not realize that wine has been forbidden? They said: Let us look and ask. They said: O Anas, pour out what is left in your vessel, for by God they did not return to it, and it was nothing but dates and unripe dates, and it was their wine that day. They included it in the two Sahihs from different sources on the authority of Anas, and in the narration of Hammad bin Zaid on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas, he said: I was serving the people on the day wine was forbidden in the house of Abu Talha, and their drink was nothing but unripe dates and unripe dates. Then a crier called out and said: Go out and look. Then a crier called out: Behold, wine has been forbidden, and it has flowed in the streets of Madinah. He said: Abu Talha said to me: Go out and pour it out. So I poured it out, and they said, or some of them said: So-and-so and so-and-so were killed while it was in their stomachs. He said: Then God revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten Al-Bukhari and Muslim. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Kabir ibn Abd al-Majid told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: While I was passing the cup around to Abu Talha, Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah, Abu Dujana, Muadh ibn Jabal and Suhayl ibn Bayda until their heads were tilted from the mixture of unripe dates, I heard a caller calling out: Beware, wine has been forbidden. He said: No one entered or left until we had poured out the drink, broken the jugs, some of us performed ablution, some of us washed, and we obtained some of Umm Sulaym’s perfume. Then we went out to the mosque and there the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reciting: O you who have believed, indeed, wine, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it until His saying: Will you then desist? A man said: O Messenger of God, what do you think about someone who dies while drinking it? Then God Almighty revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten Al-Baqarah 2:17. A man said to Qatada: Did you hear it from Anas bin Malik? He said: Yes. A man said to Anas bin Malik: Did you hear it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Yes, or did someone who did not lie tell me? We would not lie, and we do not know what lying is. [Another hadith] Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Ishaq told us, Yahya bin Ayoub told me, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Zahar, on the authority of Bakr bin Sawada, on the authority of Qais bin Saeed bin Ubadah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My Lord, blessed and exalted be He, has forbidden wine, the goblet, and the bottle. Beware of the ghabira’, for it is a third of the world’s wine.” [Another Hadith] Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Faraj bin Fadala told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Abdul Rahman bin Rafi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has forbidden my nation wine, gambling, azr, kubba, and qinn, and He has increased me in the witr prayer. Yazid said: The qinn is the barabat. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. Ahmad also said: Abu Asim, who is al-Nabeel, told us, Abdul Hamid bin Jaafar told us, Yazid bin Abi Habib told us, on the authority of Amr bin al-Walid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever attributes to me something that I did not say, let him take his seat in Hell. He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God has forbidden wine, gambling, kubba, ghabira, and every intoxicant is forbidden. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. [Another Hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Waki` narrated to us, `Abd al-`Aziz ibn `Umar ibn `Abd al-`Aziz narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ta`mah, their freed slave, on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn `Abdullah al-Ghafiqi, that they heard Ibn `Umar say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Wine is cursed in ten ways: wine is cursed in itself, and the one who drinks it, and the one who pours it, and the one who sells it, and the one who buys it, and the one who presses it, and the one who has it pressed, and the one who carries it, and the one to whom it is carried, and the one who consumes its price.” Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Waki` with it. Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi`ah narrated to us, Abu Ta`mah narrated to us, I heard Ibn `Umar say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to al-Marbad, so I went out with him, and I was with him, and I was on his right. Abu Bakr approached, so I delayed from him, and he was on his right and I was on his left. Then `Umar approached, so I moved aside for him, and he was on his left. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to al-Marbad, and there was a wineskin on al-Marbad in which there was wine. Ibn `Umar said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called me. God’s Messenger (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him) said: “The knife was not known until that day, so he ordered the wineskins to be torn, then he said: ‘I curse wine, its drinker, its server, its seller, its buyer, its carrier, the one to whom it is carried, its presser and the one for whom it is pressed, and the one who eats its price. ’” Ahmad said: Al-Hakam bin Nafi’ told us, Abu Bakr bin Abi Maryam told us, on the authority of Damrah bin Habib, who said: Abdullah bin Omar said: The Messenger of God (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him) ordered me to bring him a knife, which is a blade, so I brought it to him, so he sent it, and I sharpened it, then he gave it to me, and said: ‘Bring it to me tomorrow,’ so I did. Then he went out with his companions to the markets of Medina, and in it were wineskins that had been brought from Ash-Sham, so he took the knife from me and tore up what was in those wineskins in his presence, then gave it to me, and he ordered his companions who were with him to go with me and help me, and he ordered me to go to all the markets and I would not find a wineskin in them except that I would tear it up, so I did, and I did not leave a wineskin in its markets except that I would tear it up.. [Another Hadith] - Abdullah bin Wahb said: Abdul Rahman bin Shuraih, Ibn Lahi’ah and Al-Layth bin Sa’d told me, on the authority of Khalid bin Zaid, on the authority of Thabit, that Yazid Al-Khawlani told him that he had an uncle who sold wine, and he used to give charity. He said: So I forbade him from it, but he did not stop. So I went to Madinah and met Ibn Abbas and asked him about wine and its price. He said: It is forbidden, and its price is forbidden. Then Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: O people of the nation of Muhammad, if there were a book after your book, and a prophet after your prophet, it would have been revealed to you as it was revealed before you, but that has been delayed from your affair until the Day of Resurrection, and by my life it is more difficult for you. Thabit said: So I met Abdullah bin Umar and asked him about the price of wine. He said: I will tell you about wine. I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the mosque, and while he was sitting on his camel, he said: Whoever has any of this wine, let him bring it to us. So they began to come to him, and one of them would say: I have a water skin, and the other would say: I have a wineskin, or something like that. God willed that he should be with him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Gather him at such-and-such a place, then inform me. So they did, then they informed him, so he stood up and I stood up with him and walked to his right while he leaned on me. Then Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, caught up with us, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pushed me back, so he made me on his left and put Abu Bakr in my place. Then Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, caught up with us, so he pushed me back and made him on his left, so he walked between them until he stopped at the wine and said to the people, Do you recognize this? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God, this is wine. He said: You have spoken the truth. Then he said: God has cursed wine, the one who presses it, the one for whom it is pressed, the one who drinks it, the one who pours it, the one who carries it, the one to whom it is carried, the one who sells it, the one who buys it, and the one who eats its price. Then he called for a knife and said: Sharpen it. So they did. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it and cut open the wineskin with it. The people said: There is benefit in this wineskin. He said: Yes, but I only do that out of anger for God, the Almighty, because of what is in it of His wrath. So Umar said: I will suffice you, O Messenger of God. He said: No. Ibn Wahb said: Some of them add to the story of the hadith. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it. [Another Hadith] Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Al-Hussein bin Bishr informed us, Ismail bin Muhammad Al-Saffar informed us, Muhammad bin Ubaid God Al-Munadi informed us, Wahb bin Jarir informed us, Shu’bah informed us on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Mus’ab bin Sa’d, on the authority of Sa’d, who said: Four verses were revealed regarding wine, and he mentioned the hadith. He said: A man from the Ansar made food and invited us, so we drank wine before it was forbidden until we became intoxicated and then we boasted. The Ansar said: We are better, and the Quraysh said: We are better. So a man from the Ansar took a young camel’s tail and struck Sa’d’s nose with it, causing it to split, and Sa’d’s nose was split, so the verse was revealed: Indeed, wine and gambling until the Almighty’s saying: Will you then desist? Narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Shu’bah. [Another Hadith] - Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Nasr bin Qatada informed us, Abu Ali Al-Rafa’ informed us, Ali bin Abdul Aziz informed us, Hajjaj bin Munhal informed us, Rabia bin Kalthoum informed us, my father informed me on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He said: The prohibition of alcohol was revealed regarding two tribes of the Ansar. They drank, and when the people became drunk, some of them played with each other. When they sobered up, a man would see the marks on his face, head, and beard, and he would say, My brother so-and-so did this to me. They were brothers with no grudge in their hearts. He would say, By God, if He had been kind and merciful to me, He would not have done this to me. Until grudges entered their hearts, then God Almighty revealed this verse: O you who have believed, indeed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan. to His saying: Will you then desist? Some of the pretenders said: It is defilement and it is in the stomach of so-and-so, who was killed on the Day of Uhud. Then God Almighty revealed: It is not… For those who believe and do righteous deeds there is a sin for what they have eaten” to the end of the verse. Al-Nasa’i narrated it in the interpretation on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdul Rahim Sa’iqa, on the authority of Hajjaj bin Munhal. [Another hadith] - Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Khalaf told me, Saeed bin Muhammad al-Harami told us on the authority of Abu Numailah, on the authority of Salam, the freed slave of Hafs Abu al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Buraidah, on the authority of his father, who said: While we were sitting on a drink of ours, and we were on a sandy patch, and we were three or four, and we had a bowl of ours and we were drinking alcohol as it was lawful, then I got up to go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and greeted him, then the prohibition of alcohol was revealed: O you who believe, indeed, wine and gambling are but for the sake of God to the end of the two verses, So will you not desist? So I came to my companions and recited it to them until His saying: So will you not desist? He said: And some of the people had his drink in his hand, and he had drunk some of it and some remained in the vessel, so he said: With the vessel under his upper lip as a cupper does, then they poured out what was in their bowls, and they said: We have desisted, our Lord. [Another Hadith] - Al-Bukhari said: Sadaqah bin Al-Fadl told us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: Some people drank wine in the morning of the Battle of Uhud, and they were all killed as martyrs that day, and that was before it was forbidden. This is how Al-Bukhari narrated it in his interpretation of his Sahih. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad: Ahmad bin Abdah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, he heard Jabir bin Abdullah say: Some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, drank wine in the morning, and they were all killed as martyrs on the day of Uhud. The Jews said: Some of those who were killed died with it in their stomachs. So God revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten. Then he said: This is a sound chain of transmission, and it is as he said, but there is something strange in its context. [Another hadith] - Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu`bah told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Bara` ibn `Azib, who said: When the prohibition of alcohol was revealed, they said: What about those who used to drink it before it was prohibited? Then the verse was revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten al-Baqarah 2:17. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Bandar Ghandar on the authority of Shu`bah, with a similar wording, and he said: It is good and authentic. [Another Hadith] - Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la Al-Mawsili said: Ja`far bin Hamid Al-Kufi told us, Ya`qub Al-Qummi told us, on the authority of `Isa bin Jariyah, on the authority of Jabir bin `Abdullah, who said: There was a man who used to carry wine from Khaybar to Madinah and sell it to the Muslims. He carried some of it with money and brought it to Madinah. A Muslim man met him and said: O so-and-so, wine has been forbidden. So he put it down on a hill where it ended, and covered it with cloaks. Then he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, have I heard that wine has been forbidden? He said: Yes. He told me to return it to the one from whom I bought it. He said: It is not permissible to return it. He said: May I give it as a gift to someone who will reward me for it? He said: No. He said: There is money in it for orphans in my care. He said: When the money of Bahrain comes to us, come to us so that we may compensate your orphans from their money. Then he called out in Medina, and a man said: O Messenger of God, can we benefit from the vessels? He said: Then untie their ties. So it was erected until it settled in the valley. This is a strange hadith. [Another hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Waki` told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Hubayrah, who is Yahya ibn Abbad al-Ansari, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that Abu Talhah asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about orphans in his care who inherited wine, so he said, Pour it out. He said, Shall we not make it into vinegar? He said, No. Muslim, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri, with a similar wording. [Another hadith] Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abdullah bin Raja’ told us, Abdul Aziz bin Salamah told us, Hilal bin Abi Hilal told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Yasar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: This verse in the Qur’an, “O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful,” he said: It is in the Torah. God revealed the truth to remove falsehood, and to invalidate games, flutes, zithers, and kabarat, meaning the tambourine and flutes, meaning the tambourine and tambourines, poetry, and intoxicants are bitter to whoever tastes them. God swears by His right hand and His glory that whoever drinks it after I have forbidden it, I will make him thirsty on the Day of Resurrection, and whoever abandons it after I have forbidden it, I will make him drink it in the enclosure of Jerusalem. This is a sound chain of transmission. [Another hadith] - Abdullah bin Wahb said: Amr bin Al-Harith told me that Amr bin Shuaib told them on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whoever abandons prayer once out of intoxication, it is as if the world and everything in it were his and it was taken away from him. Whoever abandons prayer four times out of intoxication, it is a right upon God to make him drink from the mud of Khabal.” It was said: What is the mud of Khabal? He said: The juice of the people of Hell. Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib. [Another hadith] - Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Rafi` told us, Ibrahim ibn `Umar al-San`ani told us: I heard al-Nu`man, who is Ibn Abi Shaybah al-Jundi, say on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Everything that is intoxicating is alcohol, and every intoxicant is forbidden. Whoever drinks an intoxicant, his prayers will be diminished for forty mornings. If he repents, God will accept his repentance. If he does it a fourth time, God will have a right to make him drink from the mud of Khabal.” It was said: What is the mud of Khabal, O Messenger of God? He said: “The pus of the people of Hell. Whoever gives it to him when he is young, not knowing what is lawful from what is unlawful, God will have a right to make him drink from the mud of Khabal.” Abu Dawud alone transmitted it. [Another hadith] - Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: Malik informed us on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever drinks alcohol in this world and does not repent from it, will be forbidden from it in the Hereafter. Al-Bukhari and Muslim included it on the authority of Malik. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu al-Rabi’, on the authority of Hammad ibn Zayd, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Every intoxicant is alcohol, and every intoxicant is forbidden. Whoever drinks alcohol and dies while addicted to it and does not repent from it, will not drink it in the Hereafter.” [Another Hadith] - Ibn Wahb said: Umar ibn Muhammad informed me on the authority of Abdullah ibn Yasar that he heard Salim ibn Abdullah say: Abdullah ibn Umar said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three whom God will not look at on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:the one who disobeys his parents, the one who is addicted to alcohol, and the one who boasts about what he has given.” Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Amr ibn Ali, on the authority of Yazid ibn Zurai’, on the authority of Umar ibn Muhammad al-Amri, on his authority. Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Ghundar, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The one who boasts about what he has given will not enter Paradise, nor the one who is disobedient to his parents, nor the one who is addicted to alcohol. Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Samad, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, on his authority. Marwan ibn Shuja’, on the authority of Hasif, on the authority of Mujahid, on his authority. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Zakariya, on the authority of Husayn al-Ja’fi, on the authority of Za’idah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyadah, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d and Mujahid, both of them on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on his authority. [Another Hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of Jaban, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No one who is disobedient to his parents, nor one who is addicted to alcohol, nor one who boasts, nor the child of fornication will enter Paradise. And he narrated it in the same way on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Jaban, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on his authority. And he also narrated it on the authority of Ghundar and others, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Nabit ibn Sharit, on the authority of Jaban, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No one who boasts, nor one who is disobedient to his parents, nor one who is addicted to alcohol will enter Paradise. And al-Nasa’i narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Shu`bah, then he said: We do not know of anyone who followed Shu`bah on the authority of Nabit ibn Sharit. Al-Bukhari said: Jabban is not known to have heard from Abdullah, nor is Salim from Jabban or Nabit. This hadith was narrated by way of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and also by way of his on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and God knows best. Al-Zuhri said: Abu Bakr bin Abdul Rahman bin Al-Harith bin Hisham told me that his father said: I heard Uthman bin Affan say: Avoid alcohol, for it is the mother of all evils. There was a man among those who came before you who used to worship and isolate himself from people, but a prodigal woman caught him. She sent her slave girl to him and said: We call you for a testimony. So he entered with her, and she began to close every door behind him until he came to a beautiful woman who had a boy and a bowl of wine. She said: By God, I did not call you for a testimony, but I called you to have intercourse with me or kill this boy or drink this wine. So she gave him a cup and he said: Increase it. But he did not throw anything until he had intercourse with her and killed a soul. So avoid alcohol, for it and faith can never come together except that one of them will soon drive the other out. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it with a sound chain of transmission. Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in his book Dhamm al-Musker on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Buzay’ on the authority of al-Fudayl ibn Sulayman al-Numayri on the authority of Umar ibn Sa’id on the authority of al-Zuhri with it as a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is more sound, and God knows best. It has a corroborating report in the two Saheehs on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer, nor does he steal while he is a believer, nor does he drink alcohol while he is a believer. Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Aswad ibn Amir told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When alcohol was forbidden, some people said: O Messenger of God, our companions who died while drinking it. So God revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten to the end of the verse. And when the qiblah was changed, some people said: O Messenger of God, our brothers who died while praying towards Jerusalem. So God revealed: And God would never let your faith go to waste. Imam Ahmad said: Dawud ibn Mihran al-Dabbagh told us, Dawud, meaning al-Attar, told us, on the authority of Abu Khathim, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Asma’ bint Yazid, that she heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever drinks alcohol, God will not be pleased with him for forty nights. If he dies, he dies as an unbeliever, and if he repents, God will accept his repentance, and if he returns, it is God’s right to make him drink from the mud of Khabal.” She said: I said: O Messenger of God, and what is the mud of Khabal? He said, The pus of the people of Hell. Al-A’mash said, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when the verse, There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten as long as they fear God and believe, was revealed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, It was said to me, ‘You are one of them.’ Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, and Al-Nasa’i narrated it in this way. Abdullah bin Al-Imam Ahmad said: I read on the authority of my father, Ali bin Asim told us, Ibrahim Al-Hijri told us on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Beware of these two branded Ka’bahs that are used to play, for they are the gambling of the Persians.
5:91: God the Almighty says: Forbidding His believing servants from consuming alcohol and gambling, which is betting. It was reported from the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Chess is from betting, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Isa ibn Marhum, from Hatim, from Jaafar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ali with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Ahmasi told us, Waki’ told us, from Sufyan, from Laith, from Ata’, Mujahid and Tawus said: Sufyan or two of them said: Everything from gambling is from betting, even children playing with nuts. It was reported from Rashid ibn Sa’d and Damrah ibn Habib something similar, and they said: Even the heels, nuts and eggs that children play with. Musa ibn Uqbah said, from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar, who said: Betting is gambling. Ad-Dahhak said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Gambling is gambling. They used to gamble in the pre-Islamic era until the advent of Islam, so God forbade them from these ugly morals. Malik said, on the authority of Dawud ibn al-Husayn, that he heard Saeed ibn al-Musayyab say: Gambling among the people of the pre-Islamic era was selling meat for one or two sheep. Al-Zuhri said, on the authority of Al-Araj, that he said: Gambling is casting lots for money and dice. Al-Qasim bin Muhammad said: Everything that distracts from the remembrance of God and from prayer is gambling. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Mansur Al-Ziyadi narrated to us, Hisham bin Ammar narrated to us, Sadaqah narrated to us, Uthman bin Abi Al-Atika narrated to us, on the authority of Ali bin Yazid, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Avoid these branded dice that are used to deter people, for they are gambling. This is a strange hadith, and it seems that what is meant by this is the dice that was mentioned in the hadith in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Buraydah bin Al-Husaib Al-Aslami, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever plays with dice, it is as if he dipped his hand in the flesh and blood of a pig. And in the Muwatta of Malik, Musnad Ahmad, Sunan Abi Dawud and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever plays with dice has disobeyed God and His Messenger. And it was narrated with a chain of transmission ending with Abu Musa from his statement, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Ali bin Ibrahim told us, Al-Juaid told us, on the authority of Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Khatmi, that he heard Muhammad bin Kaab asking Abdul Rahman saying: Tell me what you heard your father say about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abdul Rahman said: I heard my father say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The example of the one who plays with dice and then stands up and prays is like the example of the one who performs ablution with pus and pig’s blood and then stands up and prays. As for chess, Abdullah bin Omar said that it is worse than dice. It was previously reported from Ali that he said: It is gambling. Malik, Abu Hanifa, and Ahmad explicitly prohibited it, and Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on them, disliked it. As for idols, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata’, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, and more than one said: They are stones that they used to slaughter their sacrifices at.
