As for arrows, they also said: They are arrows that they used to draw lots with. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. God the Almighty said: An abomination from the work of Satan. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning anger from the work of Satan. Saeed bin Jubair said: sin. Zaid bin Aslam said: meaning evil from the work of Satan. So avoid it. The pronoun refers to the abomination, meaning leave it. That you may be successful. This is an encouragement. Then God the Almighty said: “Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of God and from prayer. So will you not desist?” This is a threat and intimidation. Mentioning the hadiths that explain the prohibition of alcohol Imam Ahmad said: Shureih told us, Abu Ma`shar told us, on the authority of Abu Wahb, the freed slave of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: Alcohol was forbidden three times. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina while they were drinking alcohol and gambling. So they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about them, and God revealed: “They ask you about alcohol and gambling. Say, ‘In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people.’” to the end of the verse. The people said: It was not forbidden to us, but He said: In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people. They used to drink alcohol until one day, a man from the Muhajireen prayed, leading his companions in the Maghrib prayer, and he mixed up his recitation, so God revealed a verse that was more severe than it: O you who believe! Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying. So the people used to drink until one of them came to the prayer while he was asleep. Then a verse that was more severe than it was revealed: “O you who believe! Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.” They said: We have finished, our Lord. The people said: O Messenger of God, people were killed in the way of God and died in their beds; they used to drink alcohol and eat gambling, and God has made it an defilement from the work of Satan. So God revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten to the end of the verse. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If it had been forbidden to them, they would have left it as you left it. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf bin Al-Waleed told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, that when the prohibition of alcohol was revealed, he said: O God, give us a clear explanation about alcohol. Then the verse in Al-Baqarah was revealed: “They ask you about alcohol and gambling. Say, ‘In them is great sin.’” So Umar was called and it was recited to him. He said: O God, give us a clear explanation about alcohol. Then the verse in Surat An-Nisa was revealed: O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated. When the caller of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Come to prayer, he would call: Do not approach prayer while drunk. So Umar was called and it was recited to him. He said: O God, give us a clear explanation about alcohol. Then the verse in Al-Ma’idah was revealed. Umar was called and it was recited to him. When he reached the words of God the Most High: Will you then desist? Umar said: We have desisted, we have desisted. And thus Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa'i narrated it through various chains of transmission, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Umar ibn Abdullah Al-Sabi'i, and on the authority of Abu Maysarah, whose name is Amr ibn Shurahbil Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Umar, and he has no other chain of transmission on his authority. Abu Zur'ah said: He did not hear from him. This hadith was authenticated by Ali ibn Al-Madini and Al-Tirmidhi. It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab that he said in his sermon on the pulpit of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him): O people, the prohibition of alcohol has been revealed, and it is from five things: grapes, dates, honey, wheat and barley. Alcohol is that which intoxicates the mind. Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, Abdul Aziz ibn Umar ibn Abdul Aziz told us, Nafi' told me on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The prohibition of alcohol was revealed, and in Madinah at that time there were five drinks, none of which included grape juice. [Another hadith] Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hamid told us, on the authority of al-Masri, meaning Abu Ta’mah, the reciter of Egypt, who said: I heard Ibn Umar say: Three verses were revealed regarding wine. The first to be revealed was: They ask you about wine and gambling, the verse. It was said: Wine has been forbidden. They said: O Messenger of God, let us benefit from it as God Almighty said. He said: So he remained silent about them. Then this verse was revealed: Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated, and it was said: Wine has been forbidden. They said: O Messenger of God, we do not drink it near prayer. He remained silent about them. Then this verse was revealed: O you who have believed, indeed, wine, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it, the two verses. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Wine has been forbidden. [Another Hadith] Imam Ahmad said: Ya`la told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Qa`qa` ibn Hakim, that Abd al-Rahman ibn Wa`lah said: I asked Ibn Abbas about selling wine, and he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a friend from Thaqeef or Daws, and he met him on the day of the conquest with a skin of wine to give him as a gift. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O so-and-so, did you not know that God has forbidden it? The man turned to his servant and said: Go and sell it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O so-and-so, what did you order him to do? He said: I ordered him to sell it. He said: He who has forbidden its drinking has forbidden its sale. So he ordered it to be emptied into the valley. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, and on the authority of Ibn Wahb also, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Bilal, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa`id, both on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Wa`lah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on his authority. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah, on the authority of Malik, on his authority. [Another hadith] Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la al-Mawsili said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami told us, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, `Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja`far told us, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Tamim al-Dari, that he used to give the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a jug of wine every year. When God revealed the prohibition of wine, he brought it. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw it, he laughed and said, It has been prohibited after you. He said, O Messenger of God, so I sell it and benefit from its price. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “May God curse the Jews. The fat of cows and sheep was prohibited to them, so they melted it and sold it. God prohibited wine and its price.” Imam Ahmad also narrated it, saying: Ruh told us, `Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram told us, he heard Shahr ibn Hawshab say, `Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanim told me that al-Dari used to give the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a jug of wine every year. When it was the year it was prohibited, he brought a jug. When he looked at it, he laughed and said, Do you know that it has been prohibited? After you,” he said: O Messenger of God, should I not sell it and benefit from its price? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God curse the Jews. They went to what was forbidden to them of the fat of cows and sheep, melted it, and sold with it what they eat. Wine is forbidden and its price is forbidden. Wine is forbidden and its price is forbidden. Wine is forbidden and its price is forbidden.” [Another Hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah ibn Sa`id narrated to us, Ibn Lahi`ah narrated to us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Sulayman ibn `Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Nafi` ibn Kaysan, that his father informed him that he was trading in wine during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that he had come from the Levant with wine in a wineskin, intending to trade with it. He brought it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I have come to you with a good drink. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Kaysan, it has been forbidden after you left. He said: Should I sell it, O Messenger of God? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It has been forbidden and so has its price. So Kaysan went to the wineskin, took hold of its legs, and poured it out. [Another hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told us on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Anas, who said: I was giving water to Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah, Ubayy bin Kaab, Saeed bin Bayda, and a group of his companions at Abu Talha’s until the drink almost took its toll on them. Then a Muslim man came and said: Did you not realize that wine has been forbidden? They said: Let us look and ask. They said: O Anas, pour out what is left in your vessel, for by God they did not return to it, and it was nothing but dates and unripe dates, and it was their wine that day. They included it in the two Sahihs from different sources on the authority of Anas, and in the narration of Hammad bin Zaid on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas, he said: I was serving the people on the day wine was forbidden in the house of Abu Talha, and their drink was nothing but unripe dates and unripe dates. Then a crier called out and said: Go out and look. Then a crier called out: Behold, wine has been forbidden, and it has flowed in the streets of Madinah. He said: Abu Talha said to me: Go out and pour it out. So I poured it out, and they said, or some of them said: So-and-so and so-and-so were killed while it was in their stomachs. He said: Then God revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten Al-Bukhari and Muslim. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Kabir ibn Abd al-Majid told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: While I was passing the cup around to Abu Talha, Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah, Abu Dujana, Muadh ibn Jabal and Suhayl ibn Bayda until their heads were tilted from the mixture of unripe dates, I heard a caller calling out: Beware, wine has been forbidden. He said: No one entered or left until we had poured out the drink, broken the jugs, some of us performed ablution, some of us washed, and we obtained some of Umm Sulaym’s perfume. Then we went out to the mosque and there the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reciting: O you who have believed, indeed, wine, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it until His saying: Will you then desist? A man said: O Messenger of God, what do you think about someone who dies while drinking it? Then God Almighty revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten Al-Baqarah 2:17. A man said to Qatada: Did you hear it from Anas bin Malik? He said: Yes. A man said to Anas bin Malik: Did you hear it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Yes, or did someone who did not lie tell me? We would not lie, and we do not know what lying is. [Another hadith] Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Ishaq told us, Yahya bin Ayoub told me, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Zahar, on the authority of Bakr bin Sawada, on the authority of Qais bin Saeed bin Ubadah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My Lord, blessed and exalted be He, has forbidden wine, the goblet, and the bottle. Beware of the ghabira’, for it is a third of the world’s wine.” [Another Hadith] Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Faraj bin Fadala told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Abdul Rahman bin Rafi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has forbidden my nation wine, gambling, azr, kubba, and qinn, and He has increased me in the witr prayer. Yazid said: The qinn is the barabat. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. Ahmad also said: Abu Asim, who is al-Nabeel, told us, Abdul Hamid bin Jaafar told us, Yazid bin Abi Habib told us, on the authority of Amr bin al-Walid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever attributes to me something that I did not say, let him take his seat in Hell. He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God has forbidden wine, gambling, kubba, ghabira, and every intoxicant is forbidden. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. [Another Hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Waki` narrated to us, `Abd al-`Aziz ibn `Umar ibn `Abd al-`Aziz narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ta`mah, their freed slave, on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn `Abdullah al-Ghafiqi, that they heard Ibn `Umar say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Wine is cursed in ten ways: wine is cursed in itself, and the one who drinks it, and the one who pours it, and the one who sells it, and the one who buys it, and the one who presses it, and the one who has it pressed, and the one who carries it, and the one to whom it is carried, and the one who consumes its price.” Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Waki` with it. Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi`ah narrated to us, Abu Ta`mah narrated to us, I heard Ibn `Umar say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to al-Marbad, so I went out with him, and I was with him, and I was on his right. Abu Bakr approached, so I delayed from him, and he was on his right and I was on his left. Then `Umar approached, so I moved aside for him, and he was on his left. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to al-Marbad, and there was a wineskin on al-Marbad in which there was wine. Ibn `Umar said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called me. God’s Messenger (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him) said: “The knife was not known until that day, so he ordered the wineskins to be torn, then he said: ‘I curse wine, its drinker, its server, its seller, its buyer, its carrier, the one to whom it is carried, its presser and the one for whom it is pressed, and the one who eats its price. ’” Ahmad said: Al-Hakam bin Nafi’ told us, Abu Bakr bin Abi Maryam told us, on the authority of Damrah bin Habib, who said: Abdullah bin Omar said: The Messenger of God (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him) ordered me to bring him a knife, which is a blade, so I brought it to him, so he sent it, and I sharpened it, then he gave it to me, and said: ‘Bring it to me tomorrow,’ so I did. Then he went out with his companions to the markets of Medina, and in it were wineskins that had been brought from Ash-Sham, so he took the knife from me and tore up what was in those wineskins in his presence, then gave it to me, and he ordered his companions who were with him to go with me and help me, and he ordered me to go to all the markets and I would not find a wineskin in them except that I would tear it up, so I did, and I did not leave a wineskin in its markets except that I would tear it up.. [Another Hadith] - Abdullah bin Wahb said: Abdul Rahman bin Shuraih, Ibn Lahi’ah and Al-Layth bin Sa’d told me, on the authority of Khalid bin Zaid, on the authority of Thabit, that Yazid Al-Khawlani told him that he had an uncle who sold wine, and he used to give charity. He said: So I forbade him from it, but he did not stop. So I went to Madinah and met Ibn Abbas and asked him about wine and its price. He said: It is forbidden, and its price is forbidden. Then Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: O people of the nation of Muhammad, if there were a book after your book, and a prophet after your prophet, it would have been revealed to you as it was revealed before you, but that has been delayed from your affair until the Day of Resurrection, and by my life it is more difficult for you. Thabit said: So I met Abdullah bin Umar and asked him about the price of wine. He said: I will tell you about wine. I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the mosque, and while he was sitting on his camel, he said: Whoever has any of this wine, let him bring it to us. So they began to come to him, and one of them would say: I have a water skin, and the other would say: I have a wineskin, or something like that. God willed that he should be with him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Gather him at such-and-such a place, then inform me. So they did, then they informed him, so he stood up and I stood up with him and walked to his right while he leaned on me. Then Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, caught up with us, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pushed me back, so he made me on his left and put Abu Bakr in my place. Then Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, caught up with us, so he pushed me back and made him on his left, so he walked between them until he stopped at the wine and said to the people, Do you recognize this? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God, this is wine. He said: You have spoken the truth. Then he said: God has cursed wine, the one who presses it, the one for whom it is pressed, the one who drinks it, the one who pours it, the one who carries it, the one to whom it is carried, the one who sells it, the one who buys it, and the one who eats its price. Then he called for a knife and said: Sharpen it. So they did. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it and cut open the wineskin with it. The people said: There is benefit in this wineskin. He said: Yes, but I only do that out of anger for God, the Almighty, because of what is in it of His wrath. So Umar said: I will suffice you, O Messenger of God. He said: No. Ibn Wahb said: Some of them add to the story of the hadith. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it. [Another Hadith] Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Al-Hussein bin Bishr informed us, Ismail bin Muhammad Al-Saffar informed us, Muhammad bin Ubaid God Al-Munadi informed us, Wahb bin Jarir informed us, Shu’bah informed us on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Mus’ab bin Sa’d, on the authority of Sa’d, who said: Four verses were revealed regarding wine, and he mentioned the hadith. He said: A man from the Ansar made food and invited us, so we drank wine before it was forbidden until we became intoxicated and then we boasted. The Ansar said: We are better, and the Quraysh said: We are better. So a man from the Ansar took a young camel’s tail and struck Sa’d’s nose with it, causing it to split, and Sa’d’s nose was split, so the verse was revealed: Indeed, wine and gambling until the Almighty’s saying: Will you then desist? Narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Shu’bah. [Another Hadith] - Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Nasr bin Qatada informed us, Abu Ali Al-Rafa’ informed us, Ali bin Abdul Aziz informed us, Hajjaj bin Munhal informed us, Rabia bin Kalthoum informed us, my father informed me on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He said: The prohibition of alcohol was revealed regarding two tribes of the Ansar. They drank, and when the people became drunk, some of them played with each other. When they sobered up, a man would see the marks on his face, head, and beard, and he would say, My brother so-and-so did this to me. They were brothers with no grudge in their hearts. He would say, By God, if He had been kind and merciful to me, He would not have done this to me. Until grudges entered their hearts, then God Almighty revealed this verse: O you who have believed, indeed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan. to His saying: Will you then desist? Some of the pretenders said: It is defilement and it is in the stomach of so-and-so, who was killed on the Day of Uhud. Then God Almighty revealed: It is not… For those who believe and do righteous deeds there is a sin for what they have eaten” to the end of the verse. Al-Nasa’i narrated it in the interpretation on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdul Rahim Sa’iqa, on the authority of Hajjaj bin Munhal. [Another hadith] - Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Khalaf told me, Saeed bin Muhammad al-Harami told us on the authority of Abu Numailah, on the authority of Salam, the freed slave of Hafs Abu al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Buraidah, on the authority of his father, who said: While we were sitting on a drink of ours, and we were on a sandy patch, and we were three or four, and we had a bowl of ours and we were drinking alcohol as it was lawful, then I got up to go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and greeted him, then the prohibition of alcohol was revealed: O you who believe, indeed, wine and gambling are but for the sake of God to the end of the two verses, So will you not desist? So I came to my companions and recited it to them until His saying: So will you not desist? He said: And some of the people had his drink in his hand, and he had drunk some of it and some remained in the vessel, so he said: With the vessel under his upper lip as a cupper does, then they poured out what was in their bowls, and they said: We have desisted, our Lord. [Another Hadith] - Al-Bukhari said: Sadaqah bin Al-Fadl told us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: Some people drank wine in the morning of the Battle of Uhud, and they were all killed as martyrs that day, and that was before it was forbidden. This is how Al-Bukhari narrated it in his interpretation of his Sahih. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad: Ahmad bin Abdah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, he heard Jabir bin Abdullah say: Some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, drank wine in the morning, and they were all killed as martyrs on the day of Uhud. The Jews said: Some of those who were killed died with it in their stomachs. So God revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten. Then he said: This is a sound chain of transmission, and it is as he said, but there is something strange in its context. [Another hadith] - Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu`bah told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Bara` ibn `Azib, who said: When the prohibition of alcohol was revealed, they said: What about those who used to drink it before it was prohibited? Then the verse was revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten al-Baqarah 2:17. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Bandar Ghandar on the authority of Shu`bah, with a similar wording, and he said: It is good and authentic. [Another Hadith] - Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la Al-Mawsili said: Ja`far bin Hamid Al-Kufi told us, Ya`qub Al-Qummi told us, on the authority of `Isa bin Jariyah, on the authority of Jabir bin `Abdullah, who said: There was a man who used to carry wine from Khaybar to Madinah and sell it to the Muslims. He carried some of it with money and brought it to Madinah. A Muslim man met him and said: O so-and-so, wine has been forbidden. So he put it down on a hill where it ended, and covered it with cloaks. Then he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, have I heard that wine has been forbidden? He said: Yes. He told me to return it to the one from whom I bought it. He said: It is not permissible to return it. He said: May I give it as a gift to someone who will reward me for it? He said: No. He said: There is money in it for orphans in my care. He said: When the money of Bahrain comes to us, come to us so that we may compensate your orphans from their money. Then he called out in Medina, and a man said: O Messenger of God, can we benefit from the vessels? He said: Then untie their ties. So it was erected until it settled in the valley. This is a strange hadith. [Another hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Waki` told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Hubayrah, who is Yahya ibn Abbad al-Ansari, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that Abu Talhah asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about orphans in his care who inherited wine, so he said, Pour it out. He said, Shall we not make it into vinegar? He said, No. Muslim, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri, with a similar wording. [Another hadith] Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abdullah bin Raja’ told us, Abdul Aziz bin Salamah told us, Hilal bin Abi Hilal told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Yasar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: This verse in the Qur’an, “O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful,” he said: It is in the Torah. God revealed the truth to remove falsehood, and to invalidate games, flutes, zithers, and kabarat, meaning the tambourine and flutes, meaning the tambourine and tambourines, poetry, and intoxicants are bitter to whoever tastes them. God swears by His right hand and His glory that whoever drinks it after I have forbidden it, I will make him thirsty on the Day of Resurrection, and whoever abandons it after I have forbidden it, I will make him drink it in the enclosure of Jerusalem. This is a sound chain of transmission. [Another hadith] - Abdullah bin Wahb said: Amr bin Al-Harith told me that Amr bin Shuaib told them on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whoever abandons prayer once out of intoxication, it is as if the world and everything in it were his and it was taken away from him. Whoever abandons prayer four times out of intoxication, it is a right upon God to make him drink from the mud of Khabal.” It was said: What is the mud of Khabal? He said: The juice of the people of Hell. Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib. [Another hadith] - Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Rafi` told us, Ibrahim ibn `Umar al-San`ani told us: I heard al-Nu`man, who is Ibn Abi Shaybah al-Jundi, say on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Everything that is intoxicating is alcohol, and every intoxicant is forbidden. Whoever drinks an intoxicant, his prayers will be diminished for forty mornings. If he repents, God will accept his repentance. If he does it a fourth time, God will have a right to make him drink from the mud of Khabal.” It was said: What is the mud of Khabal, O Messenger of God? He said: “The pus of the people of Hell. Whoever gives it to him when he is young, not knowing what is lawful from what is unlawful, God will have a right to make him drink from the mud of Khabal.” Abu Dawud alone transmitted it. [Another hadith] - Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: Malik informed us on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever drinks alcohol in this world and does not repent from it, will be forbidden from it in the Hereafter. Al-Bukhari and Muslim included it on the authority of Malik. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu al-Rabi’, on the authority of Hammad ibn Zayd, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Every intoxicant is alcohol, and every intoxicant is forbidden. Whoever drinks alcohol and dies while addicted to it and does not repent from it, will not drink it in the Hereafter.” [Another Hadith] - Ibn Wahb said: Umar ibn Muhammad informed me on the authority of Abdullah ibn Yasar that he heard Salim ibn Abdullah say: Abdullah ibn Umar said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three whom God will not look at on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:the one who disobeys his parents, the one who is addicted to alcohol, and the one who boasts about what he has given.” Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Amr ibn Ali, on the authority of Yazid ibn Zurai’, on the authority of Umar ibn Muhammad al-Amri, on his authority. Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Ghundar, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The one who boasts about what he has given will not enter Paradise, nor the one who is disobedient to his parents, nor the one who is addicted to alcohol. Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Samad, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, on his authority. Marwan ibn Shuja’, on the authority of Hasif, on the authority of Mujahid, on his authority. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Zakariya, on the authority of Husayn al-Ja’fi, on the authority of Za’idah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyadah, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d and Mujahid, both of them on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on his authority. [Another Hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of Jaban, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No one who is disobedient to his parents, nor one who is addicted to alcohol, nor one who boasts, nor the child of fornication will enter Paradise. And he narrated it in the same way on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Jaban, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on his authority. And he also narrated it on the authority of Ghundar and others, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Nabit ibn Sharit, on the authority of Jaban, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No one who boasts, nor one who is disobedient to his parents, nor one who is addicted to alcohol will enter Paradise. And al-Nasa’i narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Shu`bah, then he said: We do not know of anyone who followed Shu`bah on the authority of Nabit ibn Sharit. Al-Bukhari said: Jabban is not known to have heard from Abdullah, nor is Salim from Jabban or Nabit. This hadith was narrated by way of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and also by way of his on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and God knows best. Al-Zuhri said: Abu Bakr bin Abdul Rahman bin Al-Harith bin Hisham told me that his father said: I heard Uthman bin Affan say: Avoid alcohol, for it is the mother of all evils. There was a man among those who came before you who used to worship and isolate himself from people, but a prodigal woman caught him. She sent her slave girl to him and said: We call you for a testimony. So he entered with her, and she began to close every door behind him until he came to a beautiful woman who had a boy and a bowl of wine. She said: By God, I did not call you for a testimony, but I called you to have intercourse with me or kill this boy or drink this wine. So she gave him a cup and he said: Increase it. But he did not throw anything until he had intercourse with her and killed a soul. So avoid alcohol, for it and faith can never come together except that one of them will soon drive the other out. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it with a sound chain of transmission. Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in his book Dhamm al-Musker on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Buzay’ on the authority of al-Fudayl ibn Sulayman al-Numayri on the authority of Umar ibn Sa’id on the authority of al-Zuhri with it as a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is more sound, and God knows best. It has a corroborating report in the two Saheehs on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer, nor does he steal while he is a believer, nor does he drink alcohol while he is a believer. Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Aswad ibn Amir told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When alcohol was forbidden, some people said: O Messenger of God, our companions who died while drinking it. So God revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten to the end of the verse. And when the qiblah was changed, some people said: O Messenger of God, our brothers who died while praying towards Jerusalem. So God revealed: And God would never let your faith go to waste. Imam Ahmad said: Dawud ibn Mihran al-Dabbagh told us, Dawud, meaning al-Attar, told us, on the authority of Abu Khathim, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Asma’ bint Yazid, that she heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever drinks alcohol, God will not be pleased with him for forty nights. If he dies, he dies as an unbeliever, and if he repents, God will accept his repentance, and if he returns, it is God’s right to make him drink from the mud of Khabal.” She said: I said: O Messenger of God, and what is the mud of Khabal? He said, The pus of the people of Hell. Al-A’mash said, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when the verse, There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten as long as they fear God and believe, was revealed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, It was said to me, ‘You are one of them.’ Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, and Al-Nasa’i narrated it in this way. Abdullah bin Al-Imam Ahmad said: I read on the authority of my father, Ali bin Asim told us, Ibrahim Al-Hijri told us on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Beware of these two branded Ka’bahs that are used to play, for they are the gambling of the Persians.
5:92: God the Almighty says: Forbidding His believing servants from consuming alcohol and gambling, which is betting. It was reported from the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Chess is from betting, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from Isa ibn Marhum, from Hatim, from Jaafar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ali with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Ahmasi told us, Waki’ told us, from Sufyan, from Laith, from Ata’, Mujahid and Tawus said: Sufyan or two of them said: Everything from gambling is from betting, even children playing with nuts. It was reported from Rashid ibn Sa’d and Damrah ibn Habib something similar, and they said: Even the heels, nuts and eggs that children play with. Musa ibn Uqbah said, from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar, who said: Betting is gambling. Ad-Dahhak said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Gambling is gambling. They used to gamble in the pre-Islamic era until the advent of Islam, so God forbade them from these ugly morals. Malik said, on the authority of Dawud ibn al-Husayn, that he heard Saeed ibn al-Musayyab say: Gambling among the people of the pre-Islamic era was selling meat for one or two sheep. Al-Zuhri said, on the authority of Al-Araj, that he said: Gambling is casting lots for money and dice. Al-Qasim bin Muhammad said: Everything that distracts from the remembrance of God and from prayer is gambling. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Mansur Al-Ziyadi narrated to us, Hisham bin Ammar narrated to us, Sadaqah narrated to us, Uthman bin Abi Al-Atika narrated to us, on the authority of Ali bin Yazid, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Avoid these branded dice that are used to deter people, for they are gambling. This is a strange hadith, and it seems that what is meant by this is the dice that was mentioned in the hadith in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Buraydah bin Al-Husaib Al-Aslami, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever plays with dice, it is as if he dipped his hand in the flesh and blood of a pig. And in the Muwatta of Malik, Musnad Ahmad, Sunan Abi Dawud and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever plays with dice has disobeyed God and His Messenger. And it was narrated with a chain of transmission ending with Abu Musa from his statement, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Ali bin Ibrahim told us, Al-Juaid told us, on the authority of Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Khatmi, that he heard Muhammad bin Kaab asking Abdul Rahman saying: Tell me what you heard your father say about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abdul Rahman said: I heard my father say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The example of the one who plays with dice and then stands up and prays is like the example of the one who performs ablution with pus and pig’s blood and then stands up and prays. As for chess, Abdullah bin Omar said that it is worse than dice. It was previously reported from Ali that he said: It is gambling. Malik, Abu Hanifa, and Ahmad explicitly prohibited it, and Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on them, disliked it. As for idols, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata’, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, and more than one said: They are stones that they used to slaughter their sacrifices at. As for arrows, they also said: They are arrows that they used to draw lots with. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. God the Almighty said: An abomination from the work of Satan. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning anger from the work of Satan. Saeed bin Jubair said: sin. Zaid bin Aslam said: meaning evil from the work of Satan. So avoid it. The pronoun refers to the abomination, meaning leave it. That you may be successful. This is an encouragement. Then God the Almighty said: “Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of God and from prayer. So will you not desist?” This is a threat and intimidation. Mentioning the hadiths that explain the prohibition of alcohol Imam Ahmad said: Shureih told us, Abu Ma`shar told us, on the authority of Abu Wahb, the freed slave of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: Alcohol was forbidden three times. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina while they were drinking alcohol and gambling. So they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about them, and God revealed: “They ask you about alcohol and gambling. Say, ‘In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people.’” to the end of the verse. The people said: It was not forbidden to us, but He said: In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people. They used to drink alcohol until one day, a man from the Muhajireen prayed, leading his companions in the Maghrib prayer, and he mixed up his recitation, so God revealed a verse that was more severe than it: O you who believe! Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying. So the people used to drink until one of them came to the prayer while he was asleep. Then a verse that was more severe than it was revealed: “O you who believe! Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.” They said: We have finished, our Lord. The people said: O Messenger of God, people were killed in the way of God and died in their beds; they used to drink alcohol and eat gambling, and God has made it an defilement from the work of Satan. So God revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten to the end of the verse. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If it had been forbidden to them, they would have left it as you left it. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf bin Al-Waleed told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, that when the prohibition of alcohol was revealed, he said: O God, give us a clear explanation about alcohol. Then the verse in Al-Baqarah was revealed: “They ask you about alcohol and gambling. Say, ‘In them is great sin.’” So Umar was called and it was recited to him. He said: O God, give us a clear explanation about alcohol. Then the verse in Surat An-Nisa was revealed: O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated. When the caller of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Come to prayer, he would call: Do not approach prayer while drunk. So Umar was called and it was recited to him. He said: O God, give us a clear explanation about alcohol. Then the verse in Al-Ma’idah was revealed. Umar was called and it was recited to him. When he reached the words of God the Most High: Will you then desist? Umar said: We have desisted, we have desisted. And thus Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa'i narrated it through various chains of transmission, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Umar ibn Abdullah Al-Sabi'i, and on the authority of Abu Maysarah, whose name is Amr ibn Shurahbil Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Umar, and he has no other chain of transmission on his authority. Abu Zur'ah said: He did not hear from him. This hadith was authenticated by Ali ibn Al-Madini and Al-Tirmidhi. It has been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab that he said in his sermon on the pulpit of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him): O people, the prohibition of alcohol has been revealed, and it is from five things: grapes, dates, honey, wheat and barley. Alcohol is that which intoxicates the mind. Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim told us, Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, Abdul Aziz ibn Umar ibn Abdul Aziz told us, Nafi' told me on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The prohibition of alcohol was revealed, and in Madinah at that time there were five drinks, none of which included grape juice. [Another hadith] Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hamid told us, on the authority of al-Masri, meaning Abu Ta’mah, the reciter of Egypt, who said: I heard Ibn Umar say: Three verses were revealed regarding wine. The first to be revealed was: They ask you about wine and gambling, the verse. It was said: Wine has been forbidden. They said: O Messenger of God, let us benefit from it as God Almighty said. He said: So he remained silent about them. Then this verse was revealed: Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated, and it was said: Wine has been forbidden. They said: O Messenger of God, we do not drink it near prayer. He remained silent about them. Then this verse was revealed: O you who have believed, indeed, wine, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it, the two verses. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Wine has been forbidden. [Another Hadith] Imam Ahmad said: Ya`la told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Qa`qa` ibn Hakim, that Abd al-Rahman ibn Wa`lah said: I asked Ibn Abbas about selling wine, and he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a friend from Thaqeef or Daws, and he met him on the day of the conquest with a skin of wine to give him as a gift. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O so-and-so, did you not know that God has forbidden it? The man turned to his servant and said: Go and sell it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O so-and-so, what did you order him to do? He said: I ordered him to sell it. He said: He who has forbidden its drinking has forbidden its sale. So he ordered it to be emptied into the valley. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, and on the authority of Ibn Wahb also, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Bilal, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa`id, both on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Wa`lah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on his authority. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah, on the authority of Malik, on his authority. [Another hadith] Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la al-Mawsili said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami told us, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, `Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja`far told us, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Tamim al-Dari, that he used to give the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a jug of wine every year. When God revealed the prohibition of wine, he brought it. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw it, he laughed and said, It has been prohibited after you. He said, O Messenger of God, so I sell it and benefit from its price. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “May God curse the Jews. The fat of cows and sheep was prohibited to them, so they melted it and sold it. God prohibited wine and its price.” Imam Ahmad also narrated it, saying: Ruh told us, `Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram told us, he heard Shahr ibn Hawshab say, `Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanim told me that al-Dari used to give the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a jug of wine every year. When it was the year it was prohibited, he brought a jug. When he looked at it, he laughed and said, Do you know that it has been prohibited? After you,” he said: O Messenger of God, should I not sell it and benefit from its price? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God curse the Jews. They went to what was forbidden to them of the fat of cows and sheep, melted it, and sold with it what they eat. Wine is forbidden and its price is forbidden. Wine is forbidden and its price is forbidden. Wine is forbidden and its price is forbidden.” [Another Hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah ibn Sa`id narrated to us, Ibn Lahi`ah narrated to us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Sulayman ibn `Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Nafi` ibn Kaysan, that his father informed him that he was trading in wine during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that he had come from the Levant with wine in a wineskin, intending to trade with it. He brought it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I have come to you with a good drink. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Kaysan, it has been forbidden after you left. He said: Should I sell it, O Messenger of God? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It has been forbidden and so has its price. So Kaysan went to the wineskin, took hold of its legs, and poured it out. [Another hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed told us on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Anas, who said: I was giving water to Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah, Ubayy bin Kaab, Saeed bin Bayda, and a group of his companions at Abu Talha’s until the drink almost took its toll on them. Then a Muslim man came and said: Did you not realize that wine has been forbidden? They said: Let us look and ask. They said: O Anas, pour out what is left in your vessel, for by God they did not return to it, and it was nothing but dates and unripe dates, and it was their wine that day. They included it in the two Sahihs from different sources on the authority of Anas, and in the narration of Hammad bin Zaid on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas, he said: I was serving the people on the day wine was forbidden in the house of Abu Talha, and their drink was nothing but unripe dates and unripe dates. Then a crier called out and said: Go out and look. Then a crier called out: Behold, wine has been forbidden, and it has flowed in the streets of Madinah. He said: Abu Talha said to me: Go out and pour it out. So I poured it out, and they said, or some of them said: So-and-so and so-and-so were killed while it was in their stomachs. He said: Then God revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten Al-Bukhari and Muslim. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Kabir ibn Abd al-Majid told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: While I was passing the cup around to Abu Talha, Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah, Abu Dujana, Muadh ibn Jabal and Suhayl ibn Bayda until their heads were tilted from the mixture of unripe dates, I heard a caller calling out: Beware, wine has been forbidden. He said: No one entered or left until we had poured out the drink, broken the jugs, some of us performed ablution, some of us washed, and we obtained some of Umm Sulaym’s perfume. Then we went out to the mosque and there the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reciting: O you who have believed, indeed, wine, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it until His saying: Will you then desist? A man said: O Messenger of God, what do you think about someone who dies while drinking it? Then God Almighty revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten Al-Baqarah 2:17. A man said to Qatada: Did you hear it from Anas bin Malik? He said: Yes. A man said to Anas bin Malik: Did you hear it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Yes, or did someone who did not lie tell me? We would not lie, and we do not know what lying is. [Another hadith] Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Ishaq told us, Yahya bin Ayoub told me, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Zahar, on the authority of Bakr bin Sawada, on the authority of Qais bin Saeed bin Ubadah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My Lord, blessed and exalted be He, has forbidden wine, the goblet, and the bottle. Beware of the ghabira’, for it is a third of the world’s wine.” [Another Hadith] Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Faraj bin Fadala told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Abdul Rahman bin Rafi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has forbidden my nation wine, gambling, azr, kubba, and qinn, and He has increased me in the witr prayer. Yazid said: The qinn is the barabat. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. Ahmad also said: Abu Asim, who is al-Nabeel, told us, Abdul Hamid bin Jaafar told us, Yazid bin Abi Habib told us, on the authority of Amr bin al-Walid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever attributes to me something that I did not say, let him take his seat in Hell. He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God has forbidden wine, gambling, kubba, ghabira, and every intoxicant is forbidden. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it. [Another Hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Waki` narrated to us, `Abd al-`Aziz ibn `Umar ibn `Abd al-`Aziz narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ta`mah, their freed slave, on the authority of `Abd al-Rahman ibn `Abdullah al-Ghafiqi, that they heard Ibn `Umar say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Wine is cursed in ten ways: wine is cursed in itself, and the one who drinks it, and the one who pours it, and the one who sells it, and the one who buys it, and the one who presses it, and the one who has it pressed, and the one who carries it, and the one to whom it is carried, and the one who consumes its price.” Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Waki` with it. Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi`ah narrated to us, Abu Ta`mah narrated to us, I heard Ibn `Umar say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to al-Marbad, so I went out with him, and I was with him, and I was on his right. Abu Bakr approached, so I delayed from him, and he was on his right and I was on his left. Then `Umar approached, so I moved aside for him, and he was on his left. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to al-Marbad, and there was a wineskin on al-Marbad in which there was wine. Ibn `Umar said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called me. God’s Messenger (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him) said: “The knife was not known until that day, so he ordered the wineskins to be torn, then he said: ‘I curse wine, its drinker, its server, its seller, its buyer, its carrier, the one to whom it is carried, its presser and the one for whom it is pressed, and the one who eats its price. ’” Ahmad said: Al-Hakam bin Nafi’ told us, Abu Bakr bin Abi Maryam told us, on the authority of Damrah bin Habib, who said: Abdullah bin Omar said: The Messenger of God (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him) ordered me to bring him a knife, which is a blade, so I brought it to him, so he sent it, and I sharpened it, then he gave it to me, and said: ‘Bring it to me tomorrow,’ so I did. Then he went out with his companions to the markets of Medina, and in it were wineskins that had been brought from Ash-Sham, so he took the knife from me and tore up what was in those wineskins in his presence, then gave it to me, and he ordered his companions who were with him to go with me and help me, and he ordered me to go to all the markets and I would not find a wineskin in them except that I would tear it up, so I did, and I did not leave a wineskin in its markets except that I would tear it up.. [Another Hadith] - Abdullah bin Wahb said: Abdul Rahman bin Shuraih, Ibn Lahi’ah and Al-Layth bin Sa’d told me, on the authority of Khalid bin Zaid, on the authority of Thabit, that Yazid Al-Khawlani told him that he had an uncle who sold wine, and he used to give charity. He said: So I forbade him from it, but he did not stop. So I went to Madinah and met Ibn Abbas and asked him about wine and its price. He said: It is forbidden, and its price is forbidden. Then Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: O people of the nation of Muhammad, if there were a book after your book, and a prophet after your prophet, it would have been revealed to you as it was revealed before you, but that has been delayed from your affair until the Day of Resurrection, and by my life it is more difficult for you. Thabit said: So I met Abdullah bin Umar and asked him about the price of wine. He said: I will tell you about wine. I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the mosque, and while he was sitting on his camel, he said: Whoever has any of this wine, let him bring it to us. So they began to come to him, and one of them would say: I have a water skin, and the other would say: I have a wineskin, or something like that. God willed that he should be with him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Gather him at such-and-such a place, then inform me. So they did, then they informed him, so he stood up and I stood up with him and walked to his right while he leaned on me. Then Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, caught up with us, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pushed me back, so he made me on his left and put Abu Bakr in my place. Then Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, caught up with us, so he pushed me back and made him on his left, so he walked between them until he stopped at the wine and said to the people, Do you recognize this? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God, this is wine. He said: You have spoken the truth. Then he said: God has cursed wine, the one who presses it, the one for whom it is pressed, the one who drinks it, the one who pours it, the one who carries it, the one to whom it is carried, the one who sells it, the one who buys it, and the one who eats its price. Then he called for a knife and said: Sharpen it. So they did. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it and cut open the wineskin with it. The people said: There is benefit in this wineskin. He said: Yes, but I only do that out of anger for God, the Almighty, because of what is in it of His wrath. So Umar said: I will suffice you, O Messenger of God. He said: No. Ibn Wahb said: Some of them add to the story of the hadith. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it. [Another Hadith] Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Al-Hussein bin Bishr informed us, Ismail bin Muhammad Al-Saffar informed us, Muhammad bin Ubaid God Al-Munadi informed us, Wahb bin Jarir informed us, Shu’bah informed us on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Mus’ab bin Sa’d, on the authority of Sa’d, who said: Four verses were revealed regarding wine, and he mentioned the hadith. He said: A man from the Ansar made food and invited us, so we drank wine before it was forbidden until we became intoxicated and then we boasted. The Ansar said: We are better, and the Quraysh said: We are better. So a man from the Ansar took a young camel’s tail and struck Sa’d’s nose with it, causing it to split, and Sa’d’s nose was split, so the verse was revealed: Indeed, wine and gambling until the Almighty’s saying: Will you then desist? Narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Shu’bah. [Another Hadith] - Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Nasr bin Qatada informed us, Abu Ali Al-Rafa’ informed us, Ali bin Abdul Aziz informed us, Hajjaj bin Munhal informed us, Rabia bin Kalthoum informed us, my father informed me on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He said: The prohibition of alcohol was revealed regarding two tribes of the Ansar. They drank, and when the people became drunk, some of them played with each other. When they sobered up, a man would see the marks on his face, head, and beard, and he would say, My brother so-and-so did this to me. They were brothers with no grudge in their hearts. He would say, By God, if He had been kind and merciful to me, He would not have done this to me. Until grudges entered their hearts, then God Almighty revealed this verse: O you who have believed, indeed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan. to His saying: Will you then desist? Some of the pretenders said: It is defilement and it is in the stomach of so-and-so, who was killed on the Day of Uhud. Then God Almighty revealed: It is not… For those who believe and do righteous deeds there is a sin for what they have eaten” to the end of the verse. Al-Nasa’i narrated it in the interpretation on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdul Rahim Sa’iqa, on the authority of Hajjaj bin Munhal. [Another hadith] - Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Khalaf told me, Saeed bin Muhammad al-Harami told us on the authority of Abu Numailah, on the authority of Salam, the freed slave of Hafs Abu al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Buraidah, on the authority of his father, who said: While we were sitting on a drink of ours, and we were on a sandy patch, and we were three or four, and we had a bowl of ours and we were drinking alcohol as it was lawful, then I got up to go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and greeted him, then the prohibition of alcohol was revealed: O you who believe, indeed, wine and gambling are but for the sake of God to the end of the two verses, So will you not desist? So I came to my companions and recited it to them until His saying: So will you not desist? He said: And some of the people had his drink in his hand, and he had drunk some of it and some remained in the vessel, so he said: With the vessel under his upper lip as a cupper does, then they poured out what was in their bowls, and they said: We have desisted, our Lord. [Another Hadith] - Al-Bukhari said: Sadaqah bin Al-Fadl told us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: Some people drank wine in the morning of the Battle of Uhud, and they were all killed as martyrs that day, and that was before it was forbidden. This is how Al-Bukhari narrated it in his interpretation of his Sahih. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad: Ahmad bin Abdah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, he heard Jabir bin Abdullah say: Some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, drank wine in the morning, and they were all killed as martyrs on the day of Uhud. The Jews said: Some of those who were killed died with it in their stomachs. So God revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten. Then he said: This is a sound chain of transmission, and it is as he said, but there is something strange in its context. [Another hadith] - Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu`bah told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Bara` ibn `Azib, who said: When the prohibition of alcohol was revealed, they said: What about those who used to drink it before it was prohibited? Then the verse was revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten al-Baqarah 2:17. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Bandar Ghandar on the authority of Shu`bah, with a similar wording, and he said: It is good and authentic. [Another Hadith] - Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la Al-Mawsili said: Ja`far bin Hamid Al-Kufi told us, Ya`qub Al-Qummi told us, on the authority of `Isa bin Jariyah, on the authority of Jabir bin `Abdullah, who said: There was a man who used to carry wine from Khaybar to Madinah and sell it to the Muslims. He carried some of it with money and brought it to Madinah. A Muslim man met him and said: O so-and-so, wine has been forbidden. So he put it down on a hill where it ended, and covered it with cloaks. Then he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, have I heard that wine has been forbidden? He said: Yes. He told me to return it to the one from whom I bought it. He said: It is not permissible to return it. He said: May I give it as a gift to someone who will reward me for it? He said: No. He said: There is money in it for orphans in my care. He said: When the money of Bahrain comes to us, come to us so that we may compensate your orphans from their money. Then he called out in Medina, and a man said: O Messenger of God, can we benefit from the vessels? He said: Then untie their ties. So it was erected until it settled in the valley. This is a strange hadith. [Another hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Waki` told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Hubayrah, who is Yahya ibn Abbad al-Ansari, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that Abu Talhah asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about orphans in his care who inherited wine, so he said, Pour it out. He said, Shall we not make it into vinegar? He said, No. Muslim, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri, with a similar wording. [Another hadith] Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abdullah bin Raja’ told us, Abdul Aziz bin Salamah told us, Hilal bin Abi Hilal told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Yasar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: This verse in the Qur’an, “O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful,” he said: It is in the Torah. God revealed the truth to remove falsehood, and to invalidate games, flutes, zithers, and kabarat, meaning the tambourine and flutes, meaning the tambourine and tambourines, poetry, and intoxicants are bitter to whoever tastes them. God swears by His right hand and His glory that whoever drinks it after I have forbidden it, I will make him thirsty on the Day of Resurrection, and whoever abandons it after I have forbidden it, I will make him drink it in the enclosure of Jerusalem. This is a sound chain of transmission. [Another hadith] - Abdullah bin Wahb said: Amr bin Al-Harith told me that Amr bin Shuaib told them on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whoever abandons prayer once out of intoxication, it is as if the world and everything in it were his and it was taken away from him. Whoever abandons prayer four times out of intoxication, it is a right upon God to make him drink from the mud of Khabal.” It was said: What is the mud of Khabal? He said: The juice of the people of Hell. Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib. [Another hadith] - Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Rafi` told us, Ibrahim ibn `Umar al-San`ani told us: I heard al-Nu`man, who is Ibn Abi Shaybah al-Jundi, say on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Everything that is intoxicating is alcohol, and every intoxicant is forbidden. Whoever drinks an intoxicant, his prayers will be diminished for forty mornings. If he repents, God will accept his repentance. If he does it a fourth time, God will have a right to make him drink from the mud of Khabal.” It was said: What is the mud of Khabal, O Messenger of God? He said: “The pus of the people of Hell. Whoever gives it to him when he is young, not knowing what is lawful from what is unlawful, God will have a right to make him drink from the mud of Khabal.” Abu Dawud alone transmitted it. [Another hadith] - Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: Malik informed us on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever drinks alcohol in this world and does not repent from it, will be forbidden from it in the Hereafter. Al-Bukhari and Muslim included it on the authority of Malik. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu al-Rabi’, on the authority of Hammad ibn Zayd, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Every intoxicant is alcohol, and every intoxicant is forbidden. Whoever drinks alcohol and dies while addicted to it and does not repent from it, will not drink it in the Hereafter.” [Another Hadith] - Ibn Wahb said: Umar ibn Muhammad informed me on the authority of Abdullah ibn Yasar that he heard Salim ibn Abdullah say: Abdullah ibn Umar said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three whom God will not look at on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:the one who disobeys his parents, the one who is addicted to alcohol, and the one who boasts about what he has given.” Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Amr ibn Ali, on the authority of Yazid ibn Zurai’, on the authority of Umar ibn Muhammad al-Amri, on his authority. Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Ghundar, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The one who boasts about what he has given will not enter Paradise, nor the one who is disobedient to his parents, nor the one who is addicted to alcohol. Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Samad, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, on his authority. Marwan ibn Shuja’, on the authority of Hasif, on the authority of Mujahid, on his authority. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Zakariya, on the authority of Husayn al-Ja’fi, on the authority of Za’idah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyadah, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d and Mujahid, both of them on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on his authority. [Another Hadith] - Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of Jaban, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No one who is disobedient to his parents, nor one who is addicted to alcohol, nor one who boasts, nor the child of fornication will enter Paradise. And he narrated it in the same way on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Jaban, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on his authority. And he also narrated it on the authority of Ghundar and others, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Nabit ibn Sharit, on the authority of Jaban, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No one who boasts, nor one who is disobedient to his parents, nor one who is addicted to alcohol will enter Paradise. And al-Nasa’i narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Shu`bah, then he said: We do not know of anyone who followed Shu`bah on the authority of Nabit ibn Sharit. Al-Bukhari said: Jabban is not known to have heard from Abdullah, nor is Salim from Jabban or Nabit. This hadith was narrated by way of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and also by way of his on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and God knows best. Al-Zuhri said: Abu Bakr bin Abdul Rahman bin Al-Harith bin Hisham told me that his father said: I heard Uthman bin Affan say: Avoid alcohol, for it is the mother of all evils. There was a man among those who came before you who used to worship and isolate himself from people, but a prodigal woman caught him. She sent her slave girl to him and said: We call you for a testimony. So he entered with her, and she began to close every door behind him until he came to a beautiful woman who had a boy and a bowl of wine. She said: By God, I did not call you for a testimony, but I called you to have intercourse with me or kill this boy or drink this wine. So she gave him a cup and he said: Increase it. But he did not throw anything until he had intercourse with her and killed a soul. So avoid alcohol, for it and faith can never come together except that one of them will soon drive the other out. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it with a sound chain of transmission. Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in his book Dhamm al-Musker on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Buzay’ on the authority of al-Fudayl ibn Sulayman al-Numayri on the authority of Umar ibn Sa’id on the authority of al-Zuhri with it as a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is more sound, and God knows best. It has a corroborating report in the two Saheehs on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer, nor does he steal while he is a believer, nor does he drink alcohol while he is a believer. Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Aswad ibn Amir told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When alcohol was forbidden, some people said: O Messenger of God, our companions who died while drinking it. So God revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten to the end of the verse. And when the qiblah was changed, some people said: O Messenger of God, our brothers who died while praying towards Jerusalem. So God revealed: And God would never let your faith go to waste. Imam Ahmad said: Dawud ibn Mihran al-Dabbagh told us, Dawud, meaning al-Attar, told us, on the authority of Abu Khathim, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Asma’ bint Yazid, that she heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever drinks alcohol, God will not be pleased with him for forty nights. If he dies, he dies as an unbeliever, and if he repents, God will accept his repentance, and if he returns, it is God’s right to make him drink from the mud of Khabal.” She said: I said: O Messenger of God, and what is the mud of Khabal? He said, The pus of the people of Hell. Al-A’mash said, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when the verse, There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten as long as they fear God and believe, was revealed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, It was said to me, ‘You are one of them.’ Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, and Al-Nasa’i narrated it in this way. Abdullah bin Al-Imam Ahmad said: I read on the authority of my father, Ali bin Asim told us, Ibrahim Al-Hijri told us on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Beware of these two branded Ka’bahs that are used to play, for they are the gambling of the Persians.
5:94: Al-Walibi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, God will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and spears may reach, he said: It is the weak and small game that God tests His servants with during their state of ihram, to the point that if they wanted to, they could reach it with their hands, but God forbade them from approaching it. Mujahid said, That your hands may reach, meaning the small and fledgling game, and your spears, meaning the large ones. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: This verse was revealed during the Umrah of Hudaybiyyah, when wild animals, birds and game would overtake them in their camps, something they had never seen before. So God forbade them from killing it while they were in a state of ihram, so that God may know who fears Him unseen. That is, God Almighty tests them with game, which would overtake them in their camps, so that they could seize it with their hands and spears, secretly and openly, so that the obedience of those who obey them in secret and openly would be apparent, as God Almighty said: Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward. And His statement here, But whoever transgresses after that, Al-Suddi and others said: meaning after this notification, warning and advance, he will have a painful punishment, that is, for disobeying God’s command and law. Then God the Almighty said: O you who believe! Do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram. This is a prohibition from God the Almighty to kill game while in a state of ihram, and a prohibition against engaging in it while in a state of ihram. This only includes, in terms of meaning, edible game and what is born from it and other things. As for non-edible land animals, according to al-Shafi’i, it is permissible for the person in a state of ihram to kill them, and the majority of scholars are of the opinion that it is also forbidden to kill them. No exception is made to this except what is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of al-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Five pests are to be killed in the sanctuary and outside of it: the crow, the kite, the scorpion, the mouse, and the rabid dog.” Malik said, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Five pests are to be killed in the sanctuary and outside of it: the crow, the kite, the scorpion, the mouse, and the rabid dog.” Narrated by both of them, and Ayoub narrated it on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar in a similar manner. Ayoub said: So I said to Nafi’: What about the snake? He said: There is no doubt about the snake. There is no disagreement about killing it. Some scholars, such as Malik and Ahmad, include the wolf, the wild beast, the tiger, and the cheetah with the rabid dog, because they are more harmful than it. And God knows best. Zayd ibn Aslam and Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: The rabid dog includes all of these wild beasts. Those who said this supported their argument with what was narrated that when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) supplicated against Utbah ibn Abi Lahab, he said: O God, let Your dog in Ash-Sham rule over him, and the wild beast ate him in Zarqa. They said: If he kills anything other than them, he must pay its ransom, such as the hyena, the fox, the wild cat, and the like. Malik said: The young ones of these five stipulated are also excluded from this, as well as the young ones of the wild beasts that are included in them.
