Abdul Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, and Abdul Karim on the authority of Ibn Abi Asiya, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he disliked eating game for the person in ihram, and he said: It is ambiguous, meaning his statement, And forbidden to you is the game of land as long as you are in ihram. He said: Muammar informed me on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that he disliked for the person in ihram to eat the meat of game under all circumstances. Muammar said: Ayoub informed me on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, something similar. Ibn Abd Al-Barr said: Tawus and Jabir bin Zaid said the same, and Al-Thawri and Ishaq bin Rahawayh agreed with it in one narration. Something similar was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, narrated by Ibn Jarir on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Arubah, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab that Ali disliked eating the meat of game for the person in ihram under all circumstances. Malik, Ash-Shafi’i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh in one narration, and the majority of scholars said: If the halal person intended to hunt it, the muhrim is not permitted to eat it, based on the hadith of As-Sa’ib ibn Jaththama, who gave the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) a wild donkey while he was in Abwa’ or Budan, so he returned it to him. When he saw the look on his face, he said, We did not return it to you except because we are forbidden. This hadith is narrated in the two Sahihs, and it has many different wordings. They said: The reason for it is that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) thought that he had hunted it for his own sake, so he returned it for that reason. However, if he did not intend to hunt it, then it is permissible for him to eat from it, based on the hadith of Abu Qatadah, who hunted a wild donkey, and it was halal, not forbidden, and his companions were in a state of ihram. They hesitated about eating it, then they asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said, Was there anyone among you who pointed to it or helped in killing it? They said, No. He said, Then eat from it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ate from it. This story is also proven in the two Sahihs with many different wordings. Imam Ahmad said: Saeed bin Mansour and Qutaybah bin Saeed told us: Yaqoub bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of Amr bin Abi Amr, on the authority of Al-Muttalib bin Abdullah bin Hantab, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and Qutaybah said in his hadith: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Game of the land is lawful for you. Saeed said - and you are in a state of ihram - as long as you do not hunt it or it is hunted for you. And this is how Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it, all on the authority of Qutaybah. Al-Tirmidhi said: We do not know of Al-Muttalib hearing it from Jabir. Imam Muhammad bin Idris Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Abi Amr, on the authority of his client Al-Muttalib, on the authority of Jabir, then he said: This is the best hadith narrated on this topic and the most reasonable. Malik, may God be pleased with him, said: on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Bakr. On the authority of Abdullah bin Aamer bin Rabia, he said: I saw Uthman bin Affan in Al-Arj while he was in the state of ihram on a summer day, and he had covered his face with a purple blanket. Then some game meat was brought to him and he said to his companions: Eat. They said: Will you not eat yourself? He said: I am not like you, it was hunted for my sake.
5:98: Ibn Abi Talha said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas in a narration on his authority, and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, and Saeed bin Jubair and others, in the words of God Almighty: Lawful to you is the game of the sea meaning what is caught from it fresh and its food what is provided from it sweet and dry, and Ibn Abbas said in the famous narration on his authority: Its game is what is taken from it alive and its food is what is thrown out dead, and thus it was narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, Zaid bin Thabit, Abdullah bin Amr, Abu Ayyub Al-Ansari, may God be pleased with them, and Ikrimah, Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri. Sufyan bin Uyaynah said, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq that he said its food is everything in it, narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Samak, who said: I was told on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Bakr addressed the people and said: Lawful to you is the game of the sea And its food is for your enjoyment.” And its food is what it throws up. He said: Ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Lawful to you is the game of the sea and its food, he said, its food is what it throws up. Akrima said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: His food is what he expels from dead animals, and Ibn Jarir also narrated it. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: His food is what he expels alive or rolls up and dies, narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, Ayoub told us on the authority of Nafi’ that Abdul Rahman bin Abi Hurairah asked Ibn Umar, saying: The sea has thrown up many dead whales, so can we eat them? He said: Do not eat them. When Abdullah returned to his family, he took the Qur’an and read Surat Al-Ma’idah and came to this verse: And his food is provision for you and for the travelers, and he said: Go and tell him: Let him eat it, for it is his food. Ibn Jarir chose this way, that what is meant by his food is what died in it. A report has been narrated on this matter, although some of them narrate it as a narration that ends with the Prophet. Hannad bin Al-Sarri told us: Abdah bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, Abu Salamah told us, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Lawful to you is the game of the sea and its food as provision for you. He said: Its food is that which it throws up dead. Then he said: Some of them stopped this hadith with Abu Hurayrah. Hannad told us, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, regarding his statement: Lawful to you is the game of the sea and its food, he said: Its food is that which it throws up dead. His saying, Provision for you and for the travelers, meaning benefit and sustenance for you, O you who are being addressed, and for the travelers, which is the plural of siyar. Ikrimah said: for those who are in the presence of the sea and traveling. Another said: the fresh part of it is for those who hunt it from the presence of the sea, and its food is what dies in it or is caught from it, salted and dried, as provisions for travelers and those far from the sea. Something similar was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Suddi and others. The majority have proven the permissibility of his death by this noble verse, and by what Imam Malik bin Anas narrated on the authority of Ibn Wahb and Ibn Kaysan, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent an expedition towards the coast, and he put Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah in charge of them, and they were three hundred, and I was among them. He said: So we set out until we were on the way, and the provisions ran out, so Abu Ubaidah ordered the provisions of that army, and he gathered all of it, and my provisions were dates. He said: Our sustenance was little by little every day until it ran out, and we were only getting one date at a time, so he said: We found its loss when it ran out. He said: Then we reached the sea and there was a fish like a humpback, and that army ate from it for eighteen nights, then Abu Ubaidah ordered two of its ribs to be set up, then he ordered a camel to be mounted and it passed under them, but it did not reach them. This hadith is reported in the two Sahihs and it has chains of transmission on the authority of Jabir. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, “There was something like a huge sand dune on the shore of the sea. We came to it and there was a beast called al-Anbar.” Abu Ubaidah said: It is dead. Then he said: “No, we are messengers of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and you are forced to eat.” He said: “So we stayed with him for a month, and we were three hundred until we became fat. I saw us scooping up fat from the hollows of his eyes with jugs, and he cut off from it the udder like a bull.” He said: “Abu Ubaidah took thirteen men from us and made them sit in the hollows of his eyes, and he took one of his ribs and made it stand up, then he saddled the largest camel with us, and it passed under it, and we took provisions from its meat and meat sha’iq. When we arrived in Madinah, we came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we mentioned that to him, and he said: “It is a provision that God has brought forth for you. Do you have any of its meat with you so that you can feed us?” He said: “So we sent some to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he ate it.” In some of the narrations of Muslim, they were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when they found this fish. Some of them said: It is another incident. Some of them said: Rather, it is one incident, but they were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, first, then he sent them on a raid with Abu Ubaidah and they found this in their raid with Abu Ubaidah. And God knows best. Malik said on the authority of Safwan bin Saleem on the authority of Saeed bin Salamah from the family of Ibn Al-Azraq: Al-Mughirah bin Abi Burdah, who was from Banu Abd Al-Dar, told him that he heard Abu Hurairah say: A man asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, we travel by sea and carry a little water with us, and if we perform ablution with it we become thirsty. Can we perform ablution with seawater? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Its water is pure and its dead are lawful. This hadith was narrated by the two Imams Al-Shafi’i and Ahmad bin Hanbal and the people of the four Sunans, and it was authenticated by Al-Bukhari, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Hibban and others. It was narrated on the authority of a group of the Companions on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, who said: Abu Al-Muhazzam - he is Yazid ibn Sufyan - told us: I heard Abu Hurairah say: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during Hajj or Umrah, and we encountered locusts, so we began to hit them with our sticks and whips, killing them. We lost hope, so we said: What should we do while we are in ihram? So we asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: There is nothing wrong with hunting at sea. Abu Al-Muhazzam is weak, and God knows best. Ibn Majah said: Harun bin Abdullah al-Jammal told us, Hashim bin al-Qasim told us, Ziyad bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Allam, on the authority of Musa bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jabir and Anas bin Malik that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate against locusts, he would say: O God, destroy their adults, kill their young, spoil their eggs, cut off their roots, and seize their mouths from our livelihoods and provisions, for You are the Hearer of supplications. Khalid said: O Messenger of God, how can you supplicate against one of God’s soldiers to cut off their roots? He said: The locusts are the scatter of the whale in the sea. Hashim said: Ziyad said: I was told by someone who saw the whale scatter them, and this is unique to Ibn Majah. Al-Shafi’i narrated on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he denounced those who hunt locusts in the Haram. This noble verse was used as evidence by those jurists who believed that sea creatures may be eaten, and they did not exclude anything from that. It was previously reported on the authority of As-Siddiq that he said: Its food is everything in it. Some of them excluded frogs and permitted everything else, based on what Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Khalid, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abdur-Rahman ibn Uthman At-Taymi, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the killing of frogs. An-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the killing of frogs, and said: Its croaking is glorification of God. Others said: Fish may be eaten from sea catch, but frogs may not be eaten. They differed concerning other than them. It was said: All of that may be eaten. It was said: It may not be eaten. It was said: Whatever is similar to it on land is similar to it in the sea. What is not eaten is similar to what is not eaten. These are all aspects of the Shafi’i school of thought, may God Almighty have mercy on him. Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said: What dies in the sea is not to be eaten, just as what dies on land is not to be eaten, due to the generality of the Almighty’s statement: Forbidden to you are dead animals. A similar hadith has been reported. Ibn Mardawayh said: Abd al-Baqi, who is Ibn Qani’, told us: Al-Husayn ibn Ishaq al-Tastari and Abdullah ibn Musa ibn Abi Uthman told us: Al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Tahan told us: Hafs ibn Ghiyath told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whatever you catch while it is alive and then dies, eat it, but whatever the sea throws up dead and floating, do not eat it. Then he narrated it through the path of Ismail ibn Umayya and Yahya ibn Abi Anisa, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, and it is rejected. The majority of the companions of Malik, al-Shafi’i, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal used as evidence the hadith of ambergris mentioned above, and the hadith: Its water is pure and its dead are permissible, which has also been mentioned. Imam Abu Abdullah Al-Shafi’i narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Two dead things and two types of blood have been made lawful for us. As for the two dead things, they are fish and locusts, and as for the two types of blood, they are the liver and the spleen.” It was narrated by Ahmad, Ibn Majah, Al-Darqutni, and Al-Bayhaqi, and it has corroborating evidence. It was narrated as a narration that ends with the Prophet, and God knows best. And his saying, And hunting on land is forbidden to you as long as you are in a state of ihram, meaning while you are in a state of ihram, hunting is forbidden to you. This indicates that this is forbidden. So if a person in a state of ihram hunts game intentionally, he has sinned and will pay, or by mistake, he will pay and it is forbidden for him to eat it, because in his case it is like a dead animal, and likewise in the case of others in a state of ihram or in a state of ihram, according to Malik and al-Shafi’i in one of his two opinions, and this is what ‘Ata’, al-Qasim, Salim, Abu Sayf, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and others say. If he eats it or part of it, is he required to pay a second penalty? There are two opinions of the scholars regarding this. One of them Yes, Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of ‘Ata’ who said: If he slaughters it and then eats it, then there are two expiations, and this is the opinion of a group. The second There is no penalty for eating it, as Malik ibn Anas stated. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said: This is the opinion of the jurists of the regions and the majority of scholars. Then Abu Omar directed him to the case of someone who had intercourse, then had intercourse, then had intercourse before he was punished, then he is only subject to one punishment. Abu Hanifa said: He is subject to the value of what he ate. Abu Thawr said: If the pilgrim kills game, he is liable for its punishment and it is permissible to eat that game, except that I dislike it for the one who killed it, based on the hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Game of the land is permissible for you, and you are in a state of ihram, unless you hunt it or it is hunted for you. This hadith will be explained, and his statement that it is permissible for the killer is strange. As for others, there is a difference of opinion about it, and we have mentioned the prohibition from those who came before. Others said that it is permissible for someone other than the killer, whether those in a state of ihram or those who are in a state of ihram, based on this hadith, and God knows best. If a lawful person hunts game and gives it to a person in ihram, some scholars have permitted it absolutely, and they did not question whether he hunted it for it or not. This statement was narrated by Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr, on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab, Abu Hurairah, Al-Zubayr bin Al-Awwam, Kaab Al-Ahbar, Mujahid, and Ata’ in one narration, and Saeed bin Jubair. The Kufians also said the same. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie’ told us, Bishr bin Al-Fadl told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatadah, that Saeed bin Al-Musayyab told him, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that he was asked about the meat of game hunted by a lawful person, can a person in ihram eat it? He said: So he gave them a fatwa to eat it, then he met Omar bin Al-Khattab and told him what had happened, and he said: If you had given them a fatwa other than this, I would have given you a headache. Others said: It is not permissible for a person in ihram to eat game at all, and they forbade it absolutely due to the generality of this noble verse. Abdul Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, and Abdul Karim on the authority of Ibn Abi Asiya, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he disliked eating game for the person in ihram, and he said: It is ambiguous, meaning his statement, And forbidden to you is the game of land as long as you are in ihram. He said: Muammar informed me on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that he disliked for the person in ihram to eat the meat of game under all circumstances. Muammar said: Ayoub informed me on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, something similar. Ibn Abd Al-Barr said: Tawus and Jabir bin Zaid said the same, and Al-Thawri and Ishaq bin Rahawayh agreed with it in one narration. Something similar was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, narrated by Ibn Jarir on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Arubah, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab that Ali disliked eating the meat of game for the person in ihram under all circumstances. Malik, Ash-Shafi’i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh in one narration, and the majority of scholars said: If the halal person intended to hunt it, the muhrim is not permitted to eat it, based on the hadith of As-Sa’ib ibn Jaththama, who gave the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) a wild donkey while he was in Abwa’ or Budan, so he returned it to him. When he saw the look on his face, he said, We did not return it to you except because we are forbidden. This hadith is narrated in the two Sahihs, and it has many different wordings. They said: The reason for it is that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) thought that he had hunted it for his own sake, so he returned it for that reason. However, if he did not intend to hunt it, then it is permissible for him to eat from it, based on the hadith of Abu Qatadah, who hunted a wild donkey, and it was halal, not forbidden, and his companions were in a state of ihram. They hesitated about eating it, then they asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said, Was there anyone among you who pointed to it or helped in killing it? They said, No. He said, Then eat from it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ate from it. This story is also proven in the two Sahihs with many different wordings. Imam Ahmad said: Saeed bin Mansour and Qutaybah bin Saeed told us: Yaqoub bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of Amr bin Abi Amr, on the authority of Al-Muttalib bin Abdullah bin Hantab, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and Qutaybah said in his hadith: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Game of the land is lawful for you. Saeed said - and you are in a state of ihram - as long as you do not hunt it or it is hunted for you. And this is how Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it, all on the authority of Qutaybah. Al-Tirmidhi said: We do not know of Al-Muttalib hearing it from Jabir. Imam Muhammad bin Idris Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Abi Amr, on the authority of his client Al-Muttalib, on the authority of Jabir, then he said: This is the best hadith narrated on this topic and the most reasonable. Malik, may God be pleased with him, said: on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Bakr. On the authority of Abdullah bin Aamer bin Rabia, he said: I saw Uthman bin Affan in Al-Arj while he was in the state of ihram on a summer day, and he had covered his face with a purple blanket. Then some game meat was brought to him and he said to his companions: Eat. They said: Will you not eat yourself? He said: I am not like you, it was hunted for my sake.

I saw us scooping up fat from the hollows of his eyes with jugs, and he cut off from it the udder like a bull.” He said: “Abu Ubaidah took thirteen men from us and made them sit in the hollows of his eyes, and he took one of his ribs and made it stand up, then he saddled the largest camel with us, and it passed under it, and we took provisions from its meat and meat sha’iq. When we arrived in Madinah, we came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we mentioned that to him, and he said: “It is a provision that God has brought forth for you. Do you have any of its meat with you so that you can feed us?” He said: “So we sent some to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he ate it.” In some of the narrations of Muslim, they were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when they found this fish. Some of them said: It is another incident. Some of them said: Rather, it is one incident, but they were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, first, then he sent them on a raid with Abu Ubaidah and they found this in their raid with Abu Ubaidah. And God knows best. Malik said on the authority of Safwan bin Saleem on the authority of Saeed bin Salamah from the family of Ibn Al-Azraq: Al-Mughirah bin Abi Burdah, who was from Banu Abd Al-Dar, told him that he heard Abu Hurairah say: A man asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, we travel by sea and carry a little water with us, and if we perform ablution with it we become thirsty. Can we perform ablution with seawater? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Its water is pure and its dead are lawful. This hadith was narrated by the two Imams Al-Shafi’i and Ahmad bin Hanbal and the people of the four Sunans, and it was authenticated by Al-Bukhari, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Hibban and others. It was narrated on the authority of a group of the Companions on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, who said: Abu Al-Muhazzam - he is Yazid ibn Sufyan - told us: I heard Abu Hurairah say: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during Hajj or Umrah, and we encountered locusts, so we began to hit them with our sticks and whips, killing them. We lost hope, so we said: What should we do while we are in ihram? So we asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: There is nothing wrong with hunting at sea. Abu Al-Muhazzam is weak, and God knows best. Ibn Majah said: Harun bin Abdullah al-Jammal told us, Hashim bin al-Qasim told us, Ziyad bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Allam, on the authority of Musa bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jabir and Anas bin Malik that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate against locusts, he would say: O God, destroy their adults, kill their young, spoil their eggs, cut off their roots, and seize their mouths from our livelihoods and provisions, for You are the Hearer of supplications. Khalid said: O Messenger of God, how can you supplicate against one of God’s soldiers to cut off their roots? He said: The locusts are the scatter of the whale in the sea. Hashim said: Ziyad said: I was told by someone who saw the whale scatter them, and this is unique to Ibn Majah. Al-Shafi’i narrated on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he denounced those who hunt locusts in the Haram. This noble verse was used as evidence by those jurists who believed that sea creatures may be eaten, and they did not exclude anything from that. It was previously reported on the authority of As-Siddiq that he said: Its food is everything in it. Some of them excluded frogs and permitted everything else, based on what Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Khalid, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abdur-Rahman ibn Uthman At-Taymi, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the killing of frogs. An-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the killing of frogs, and said: Its croaking is glorification of God. Others said: Fish may be eaten from sea catch, but frogs may not be eaten. They differed concerning other than them. It was said: All of that may be eaten. It was said: It may not be eaten. It was said: Whatever is similar to it on land is similar to it in the sea. What is not eaten is similar to what is not eaten. These are all aspects of the Shafi’i school of thought, may God Almighty have mercy on him. Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said: What dies in the sea is not to be eaten, just as what dies on land is not to be eaten, due to the generality of the Almighty’s statement: Forbidden to you are dead animals. A similar hadith has been reported. Ibn Mardawayh said: Abd al-Baqi, who is Ibn Qani’, told us: Al-Husayn ibn Ishaq al-Tastari and Abdullah ibn Musa ibn Abi Uthman told us: Al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Tahan told us: Hafs ibn Ghiyath told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whatever you catch while it is alive and then dies, eat it, but whatever the sea throws up dead and floating, do not eat it. Then he narrated it through the path of Ismail ibn Umayya and Yahya ibn Abi Anisa, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, and it is rejected. The majority of the companions of Malik, al-Shafi’i, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal used as evidence the hadith of ambergris mentioned above, and the hadith: Its water is pure and its dead are permissible, which has also been mentioned. Imam Abu Abdullah Al-Shafi’i narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Two dead things and two types of blood have been made lawful for us. As for the two dead things, they are fish and locusts, and as for the two types of blood, they are the liver and the spleen.” It was narrated by Ahmad, Ibn Majah, Al-Darqutni, and Al-Bayhaqi, and it has corroborating evidence. It was narrated as a narration that ends with the Prophet, and God knows best. And his saying, And hunting on land is forbidden to you as long as you are in a state of ihram, meaning while you are in a state of ihram, hunting is forbidden to you. This indicates that this is forbidden. So if a person in a state of ihram hunts game intentionally, he has sinned and will pay, or by mistake, he will pay and it is forbidden for him to eat it, because in his case it is like a dead animal, and likewise in the case of others in a state of ihram or in a state of ihram, according to Malik and al-Shafi’i in one of his two opinions, and this is what ‘Ata’, al-Qasim, Salim, Abu Sayf, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and others say. If he eats it or part of it, is he required to pay a second penalty? There are two opinions of the scholars regarding this. One of them Yes, Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of ‘Ata’ who said: If he slaughters it and then eats it, then there are two expiations, and this is the opinion of a group. The second There is no penalty for eating it, as Malik ibn Anas stated. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said: This is the opinion of the jurists of the regions and the majority of scholars. Then Abu Omar directed him to the case of someone who had intercourse, then had intercourse, then had intercourse before he was punished, then he is only subject to one punishment. Abu Hanifa said: He is subject to the value of what he ate. Abu Thawr said: If the pilgrim kills game, he is liable for its punishment and it is permissible to eat that game, except that I dislike it for the one who killed it, based on the hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Game of the land is permissible for you, and you are in a state of ihram, unless you hunt it or it is hunted for you. This hadith will be explained, and his statement that it is permissible for the killer is strange. As for others, there is a difference of opinion about it, and we have mentioned the prohibition from those who came before. Others said that it is permissible for someone other than the killer, whether those in a state of ihram or those who are in a state of ihram, based on this hadith, and God knows best. If a lawful person hunts game and gives it to a person in ihram, some scholars have permitted it absolutely, and they did not question whether he hunted it for it or not. This statement was narrated by Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr, on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab, Abu Hurairah, Al-Zubayr bin Al-Awwam, Kaab Al-Ahbar, Mujahid, and Ata’ in one narration, and Saeed bin Jubair. The Kufians also said the same. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie’ told us, Bishr bin Al-Fadl told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatadah, that Saeed bin Al-Musayyab told him, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that he was asked about the meat of game hunted by a lawful person, can a person in ihram eat it? He said: So he gave them a fatwa to eat it, then he met Omar bin Al-Khattab and told him what had happened, and he said: If you had given them a fatwa other than this, I would have given you a headache. Others said: It is not permissible for a person in ihram to eat game at all, and they forbade it absolutely due to the generality of this noble verse. Abdul Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, and Abdul Karim on the authority of Ibn Abi Asiya, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he disliked eating game for the person in ihram, and he said: It is ambiguous, meaning his statement, And forbidden to you is the game of land as long as you are in ihram. He said: Muammar informed me on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that he disliked for the person in ihram to eat the meat of game under all circumstances. Muammar said: Ayoub informed me on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, something similar. Ibn Abd Al-Barr said: Tawus and Jabir bin Zaid said the same, and Al-Thawri and Ishaq bin Rahawayh agreed with it in one narration. Something similar was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, narrated by Ibn Jarir on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Arubah, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab that Ali disliked eating the meat of game for the person in ihram under all circumstances. Malik, Ash-Shafi’i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh in one narration, and the majority of scholars said: If the halal person intended to hunt it, the muhrim is not permitted to eat it, based on the hadith of As-Sa’ib ibn Jaththama, who gave the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) a wild donkey while he was in Abwa’ or Budan, so he returned it to him. When he saw the look on his face, he said, We did not return it to you except because we are forbidden. This hadith is narrated in the two Sahihs, and it has many different wordings. They said: The reason for it is that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) thought that he had hunted it for his own sake, so he returned it for that reason. However, if he did not intend to hunt it, then it is permissible for him to eat from it, based on the hadith of Abu Qatadah, who hunted a wild donkey, and it was halal, not forbidden, and his companions were in a state of ihram. They hesitated about eating it, then they asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said, Was there anyone among you who pointed to it or helped in killing it? They said, No. He said, Then eat from it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ate from it. This story is also proven in the two Sahihs with many different wordings. Imam Ahmad said: Saeed bin Mansour and Qutaybah bin Saeed told us: Yaqoub bin Abdul Rahman told us, on the authority of Amr bin Abi Amr, on the authority of Al-Muttalib bin Abdullah bin Hantab, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and Qutaybah said in his hadith: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Game of the land is lawful for you. Saeed said - and you are in a state of ihram - as long as you do not hunt it or it is hunted for you. And this is how Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it, all on the authority of Qutaybah. Al-Tirmidhi said: We do not know of Al-Muttalib hearing it from Jabir. Imam Muhammad bin Idris Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Abi Amr, on the authority of his client Al-Muttalib, on the authority of Jabir, then he said: This is the best hadith narrated on this topic and the most reasonable. Malik, may God be pleased with him, said: on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Bakr. On the authority of Abdullah bin Aamer bin Rabia, he said: I saw Uthman bin Affan in Al-Arj while he was in the state of ihram on a summer day, and he had covered his face with a purple blanket. Then some game meat was brought to him and he said to his companions: Eat. They said: Will you not eat yourself? He said: I am not like you, it was hunted for my sake.
5:100: God Almighty says to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say O Muhammad, The bad and the good are not equal, even if it pleases you meaning O human being, The abundance of the bad means that a little lawful and beneficial is better than a lot of unlawful and harmful, as it came in the hadith, What is little and sufficient is better than what is much and distracts. Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi said in his dictionary: Ahmad ibn Zuhair told us, al-Hawti told us, Muhammad ibn Shu`ayb told us, Ma`an ibn Rafa`ah told us on the authority of Abu Abd al-Malik Ali ibn Yazid on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah that Tha`laba ibn Hatib al-Ansari said: O Messenger of God, ask God to grant me wealth, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, A little for which you can be grateful is better than a lot that you cannot bear. "So fear God, O you of understanding" meaning O you of sound and upright minds, and avoid the unlawful and leave it and be content with the lawful and be satisfied with it, so that you may succeed, meaning in this world and the hereafter. Then God the Almighty said: O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are made known to you, may distress you. This is a discipline from God the Almighty to His believing servants, and a prohibition for them from asking about things that are of no benefit to them in asking about and investigating, because if those matters are made known to them, they may distress them and be difficult for them to hear, as came in the hadith that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let no one tell me anything about anyone, for I like to come out to you with a pure heart. Al-Bukhari said: Mundhir bin Al-Walid bin Abd Al-Rahman Al-Jaroudi told us, my father told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Musa bin Anas, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon the like of which I have never heard before, and he said in it: If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much. He said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, covered their faces out of longing, and a man said: Who is my father? He said, So-and-so, and this verse was revealed: Do not ask about things. Narrated by Al-Nadr and Ruh bin Ubadah on the authority of Shu’bah. Al-Bukhari narrated it in a place other than this, and Muslim, Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, and Al-Nasa’i narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Shu’bah bin Al-Hajjaj. Ibn Jarir said: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are made clear to you, will distress you, the verse, he said: So he told us that Anas bin Malik told him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked him until they surrounded him with questions, so he came out to them one day and ascended the pulpit and said, Do not ask me about anything today except that I will explain it to you. So the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, feared that a matter was imminent before me, so I would not turn to the right or to the left except that I would find everyone with his head wrapped in his garment and weeping. Then a man who used to argue arose and was called to someone other than his father, so he said, O Prophet of God, who is my father? He said, Your father is Hudhafah. He said: Then Omar stood up - or he said: Omar began - and said: We are satisfied with God as our Lord, with Islam as our religion, and with Muhammad as our Messenger. We seek refuge in God - or he said: I seek refuge in God from the evil of trials - He said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have never seen in good and evil like today. Paradise and Hell were pictured to me until I saw them beyond the wall. They both narrated it on the authority of Saeed, and Muammar narrated it on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Anas, something similar or close to it. Al-Zuhri said: Then Umm Abdullah bin Hudhafah said: I have never seen a more disobedient son than you. Were you certain that your mother might have committed what the people of ignorance committed, so you would disgrace her in front of the people? He said: By God, if he were to make me join a black slave, I would join him. Ibn Jarir also said: Al-Harith told us, Abdul Aziz told us, Qais told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out angry, his face red, until he sat on the pulpit. A man stood up to him and said: Where is my father? He said: In the Fire. Another man stood up and said: Who is my father? He said: Your father is Hudhafah. Then Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up and said: We are satisfied with God as our Lord, Islam as our religion, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as our Prophet, and the Qur’an as our leader. O Messenger of God, we have recently left ignorance and polytheism, and God knows best who our fathers are. He said: So his anger subsided, and this verse was revealed: O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, may distress you. The verse has a good chain of transmission. This story was mentioned in a mursal form by more than one of the early Muslims, including Asbat on the authority of al-Suddi, who said about the words of God Almighty: O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, may distress you. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry one day, so he stood up to deliver a sermon and said: Ask me, for you do not ask me about anything except that I will inform you about it. A man from the Quraysh from Banu Sahm called Abdullah bin Hudhafah, who used to slander him, stood up and said: O Messenger of God, who is my father? He said: Your father is so-and-so. So he called him to his father, and Umar bin al-Khattab stood up and kissed his foot and said: O Messenger of God, we are pleased with God as our Lord, with you as our Prophet, with Islam as our religion, and with the Qur’an as our leader, so forgive us, may God forgive you. He kept on at him until he was pleased. On that day he said: The child belongs to the bed, and the adulterer gets stoned. Then Al-Bukhari said: Al-Fadl bin Sahl narrated to us, Abu Al-Nadr narrated to us, Abu Khaithama narrated to us, Abu Al-Juwayriyyah narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: There were people who used to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mockingly. A man would say: Who is my father? And a man whose camel had gone astray would say: Where is my camel? So God revealed this verse about them: O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are made known to you, may distress you. Until he finished the entire verse. Al-Bukhari is the only one who transmitted it. Imam Ahmad said: Mansur bin Wardan Al-Asadi narrated to us, Ali bin Abdul A’la narrated to us on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Al-Bukhtari, who is Saeed bin Fairuz, on the authority of Ali, who said: When this verse was revealed: And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to God by mankind, those who can afford the expenses for one’s expenses, they said: O Messenger of God, is it every year? He was silent. They said: Is it every year? He was silent. Then they said: Is it every year? He said, No. If I had said, Yes, it would have been obligatory, and if it were obligatory you would not have been able to do it. Then God revealed, O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are made known to you, will distress you. The verse was also narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah on the authority of Mansur bin Wardan, and Al-Tirmidhi said, It is strange from this aspect. I heard Al-Bukhari say, Abu Al-Bukhtari did not meet Ali. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hijri, on the authority of Abu Ayyad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has prescribed Hajj for you. A man said: Is it every year, O Messenger of God? He turned away from him until he came back two or three times, and he said: Who is the questioner? He said: So-and-so. He said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if I had said yes, it would have been obligatory. And if it had been obligatory for you, you would not have been able to do it, and if you left it, you would have disbelieved.” So God, the Almighty, revealed: O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are made known to you, will distress you, until he finished the verse. Then Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Waqid on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, and he said: Then Muhsin al-Asadi stood up, and in a narration on this authority, ‘Ukasha ibn Muhsin, and he is more likely, and Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hijri is weak. Ibn Jarir also said: Zakariya bin Yahya bin Aban Al-Masry told me, Abu Yazid Abdul Rahman Abi Al-Ghamr told us, Ibn Mut’i Mu’awiyah bin Yahya told us on the authority of Safwan bin Amr, Salim bin Aamer told me: I heard Abu Umamah Al-Bahili say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood among the people and said, Hajj has been prescribed for you. Then a Bedouin man stood up and said, Is it every year? He said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped talking, and was silent, and became angry and became angry, and remained for a long time, then he spoke and said, Who is the questioner? The Bedouin said: I am that one. He said: Woe to you, what assures you that I will not say yes? By God, if I had said yes, even if it were obligatory, you would have disbelieved. Indeed, those before you were destroyed by the leaders of hardship. By God, if I were to make lawful for you everything on earth and forbid you from it a small spot, you would fall into it. He said: Then God revealed at that time: O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were made known to you, would distress you to the end of the verse. Its chain of transmission is weak, and the apparent meaning of the verse is the prohibition of asking about things which, if a person knew about them, would distress him. It is better to turn away from them and leave them. How beautiful is the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, where he said: Hajjaj told us: I heard Isra’il ibn Yunus, on the authority of Al-Walid ibn Abi Hashim, the client of Al-Hamdani, on the authority of Zaid ibn Zaid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions: Let no one inform me of anything from anyone, for I love to come out to you with a sound heart. The hadith was narrated by Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Isra’il. Abu Dawud said on the authority of Al-Walid, and Al-Tirmidhi said on the authority of Israel on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Al-Walid bin Abi Hashim on his authority, then Al-Tirmidhi said: It is strange from this aspect. And the Almighty said: And if you ask about them when the Qur’an is being revealed, they will be made clear to you. That is, if you ask about these things that you were forbidden to ask about when the revelation is being sent down to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they will be made clear to you. And that is easy for God. Then He said, God has pardoned them, that is, what happened from you before that. And God is Forgiving and Forbearing. It was said: What is meant by His saying, And if you ask about it when the Qur’an is being revealed, it will be made clear to you, is that do not ask about things that you will ask about again, because perhaps a strict or restrictive ruling may be revealed because of your question. It was mentioned in the hadith, The greatest sinner among Muslims is he who asks about something that was not forbidden, and it is forbidden because of his question. But if the Qur’an is revealed with it in general terms and you ask about its explanation, it will be made clear to you at that time because you need it. God has pardoned it, meaning that whatever He did not mention in His Book is among what He has pardoned, so you should be silent about it as He was silent about it. In the Sahih, it is narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, Leave me as I have left you, for what destroyed those who came before you was their excessive questioning and their disagreement with their prophets. And in the Sahih hadith also, “God, the Most High, imposed obligations, so do not neglect them. He set limits, so do not transgress them. He prohibited things, so do not violate them. He was silent about things out of mercy for you, not forgetfulness, so do not ask about them.” Then the Almighty said: A people before you asked about it, then they became disbelievers because of it. That is, a people before you asked about these forbidden issues and they were answered, then they did not believe in them, so they became disbelievers because of them, that is, they were made clear to them but they did not benefit from them because they did not ask for guidance but rather out of mockery and stubbornness. Al-Awfi said: On the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the verse: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out to the people and said, O my people, Hajj has been prescribed for you. A man from Banu Asad stood up and said: O Messenger of God, is it every year? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became very angry and said, “By Him in Whose Hand is my soul, if I had said, ‘Yes,’ it would have been obligatory. If it were obligatory, you would not have been able to do it. In that case, you would have disbelieved. So leave me as I have left you. If I command you to do something, do it, and if I forbid you from something, refrain from it.” Then this verse was revealed. He forbade them from asking about something like what the Christians asked about from the table, and because of that they became disbelievers. So God forbade that and said, “Do not ask about things about which if the Qur’an were revealed with severity, it would upset you. But wait, for when the Qur’an is revealed, you will not ask about anything except that you will find its explanation.” Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are made known to you, will distress you. But if you ask about them when the Qur’an is being revealed, they will be made clear to you.” He said: When the verse about Hajj was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out to the people and said, O people, God has prescribed Hajj for you, so perform Hajj. They said, O Messenger of God, once a year or every year? He said, “No, one year. If I had said every year, it would have been obligatory, and if it were obligatory, you would have disbelieved.” Then God Almighty said, O you who have believed, do not ask about things until His saying, Then they became disbelievers in them. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Khasif said, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Do not ask about things. He said, “They are the bahīrah, the wasīlah, the sa’ibah, and the Ḥām. Do you not see that he said after that, “God has not made a bahīrah,” nor such and such? He said, “As for Ikrimah, he said, ‘They used to ask him about the signs, but they were forbidden from doing so.
